chapters.name: Chapter 91: Chapter 91: Fifth in the Fleet
chapters.content:
"Ric, what is wrong with you?"

 

Jitto came jogging after Fenric the moment they cleared the school gate, wearing the expression of a brother whose teammate just sold a purple drop for copper. "You really turned down that opportunity? Are you… not into girls?"

 

He even side‑stepped a few paces, theatrically putting space between them.

 1

"Get lost." Fenric gave him a side‑eye. "I just don't want to deal with that right now. The Samsara Tower is my real pursuit."

 

No outsiders were nearby, so he didn't bother pretending.

 

"…Alright then." Jitto believed him— mostly because the strength Fenric showed last time was way beyond 'safe-zone casual.' That wasn't an ordinary grind-run kid.

 

"By the way," Jitto lowered his voice, leaning in, "can you tell me how you cleared the First Stage of the Samsara Tower?"

 

"It's simple." Fenric kept his tone light. "You get half an hour of prep after entering, right? Use that window. Hit an archery club, grab the owner, strip the racks — bows, arrows, all of it. Then find a tall building, go to the roof, stay quiet, and pick zombies off from range. Don't make noise. They can climb stairs."

 5

He left it there.

 

He wasn't about to hand out the optimal route. Not because he was stingy, but because exposing his real strategy was dangerous. On top of that, his previous trade with Aurora was enforced under the Samsara System's fairness protocols; sharing a "best clear" elsewhere could risk system penalties.

 

What he'd given Jitto could clear the floor — just not with a great rating.

 

Jitto's eyes lit up. "So that's how you did it? What evaluation?"

 

"A‑grade. Took out a few hundred zombies." Fenric lied without blinking.

 2

"F**k! Brutal!"

 

But Jitto was visibly tempted.

 

Fenric added, "Think carefully before stepping into the Tower. Once you enter, there's no going back. Safe‑zone instance lock out after you clear the first stage. You can only push forward. And another thing: don't trust 'alliances' people shout about in the Tower. Nine out of ten are pits."

 

Jitto's expression turned serious. "Ric… thanks. No matter what happens later, you're my brother."

 

"Enough with the mother‑in‑law nonsense. Which way are you headed? Go already." Fenric swatted at him.

 

"One last thing! That beauty Isla really isn't bad. Not shallow, either. Don't waste it…"

 

With that parting bit of life advice, Jitto trotted off.

 

Arriving at his house, Fenric ate a simple supper, showered, and grabbed some sleep. At midnight sharp, he re‑entered the Samsara Space.

 

Aurora was already online — punctual as ever. Fenric sent a video request at once. She connected quickly.

 

"Shura?" Her tone held mild surprise. "Rare to see you reach out first. What's wrong?"

 

"Need to pick the old boss's brain." He smiled. "Drinks on me?"

 

She snorted. "Drop the 'boss'—or at least stop adding 'old.' Same teahouse as last night. Book a room and ping me."

 

Fenric reserved a private room for 100 points (rooms can't be number‑selected; his came up 1376, meaning 1,375 boxes had already been booked), then sent her the code.

 

The Samsara Space had become a second habitat for most Samsara players. Even on cooldown nights, people logged in out of habit.

 

Fenric was starting to do the same.

 

Private Room 1376

 

"Good evening," Aurora said as she entered.

 

"Please." Fenric gestured. "What'll you have?"

 

"Calm Tea."

 

She sat — composed but visibly tense. Her brows hadn't relaxed since she arrived.

 

Fenric ordered two cups, then studied her. "Your expression doesn't look great. Something happened?"

 

She nodded. "I'm pushing for the 28th floor tonight."

 

"..."

 

Fenric paused. No wonder.

 

For any Samsara, every Tower run was a walk across a knife edge. The higher you climbed, the thinner the blade.

 

"You confident?" he asked.

 

Aurora smiled wryly. "Who dares say they're confident in the Samsara Tower?"

 1

Fair point. No run was guaranteed. Unless you knew the plot in advance — like him.

 

She waved the topic aside. "Enough about me. What did you want to ask?"

 

"I'm going into the Third Stage dungeon tonight," Fenric said. "I wanted to confirm some things. If you're willing to share?"

 

"You got another dungeon cooldown refresh card?" she asked, surprised.

 

"Yeah."

 

"You're pushing too hard," she sighed. "There's a reason the Tower gives us a week between runs — physical recovery, mental reset. Going back in tired is how people die."

 1

"I'm fine," he said with a shrug.

 

"..."

 

She held his gaze a beat, then gave in. "Alright. Since you bought tea, ask."

 

He hesitated, then went straight to it. "Ms. Morwyn, how did you clear it?"

 

"I chose the Navy camp," she said. "Participated in the Headquarters assessment. Finished fifth overall."

 

Then, as if remembering something, she added, "Adam took Navy too. He placed third."

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed slightly. "What did fifth place pay out?"

 

"A‑grade evaluation," she said. "8,000 points. And one Zoan‑type Devil Fruit."a

 1

chapters.name: Chapter 92: Chapter 92: Don’t Provoke the Admiral (2/10)
chapters.content:
"Shura, there's something you need to keep in mind."

 

Aurora said with a serious tone.

 

"Devil Fruits—each person can only eat one. If you clear this trial, you'll be rewarded with a Devil Fruit, but it might not be a rare type. I suggest you avoid taking it recklessly… otherwise, you may end up regretting it, just like I did!"

 

Fenric nodded in agreement.

 

He was already aware of the rules from the storyline. Of course, he knew that eating a Devil Fruit indiscriminately could give you a useless or troublesome ability—and worse, ruin your life.

 

In fact, Fenric was quite curious.

 

What kind of Devil Fruit did Aurora eat for her to regret it so deeply?

 1

But that topic touched on Aurora's personal matters.

 

Their relationship wasn't close enough yet, and it would be unwise to pry—better to avoid creating any awkwardness.

 

"Ms. Morwyn, you ranked fifth in the military trial back then, right? Do you remember who the top four were?" Fenric asked.

 

"Hmm? That was a long time ago… let me think."

 

Aurora paused, then replied,

 

"The first was a blind man. His codename was 'Fujitora.'

 3

"Don't let his blindness fool you—he's terrifyingly strong.

 

I've seen him spar in close combat, and his swordsmanship is top-notch.

 

Plus, he has a powerful Devil Fruit ability."

 

Fenric remained calm on the surface—but his heart skipped a beat.

 

Fujitora?

 

Isn't that one of the future Admirals?

 

Of course Admirals are powerful—but…

 

Fenric knew the plot.

 

He clearly remembered Fujitora's story.

 

This man only joined the Navy after the war at Marineford.

 3

Following the war, Akainu was promoted to Fleet Admiral, and Aokiji left the Navy.

 

That left two Admiral positions open.

 

To fill them, the Navy launched a global draft—"World Military Conscription."

 

It was then that Fujitora joined the force.

 

In just two years, he rose to the position of Admiral thanks to his overwhelming strength, code-named "Fujitora" (Wisteria Tiger).

 

He, alongside Ryokugyu (Green Bull) and Kizaru (Yellow Monkey), became known as the New Three Admirals.

 

So… if the Third Stage "One Piece" dungeon really takes place two years after the Marineford War, then why did the 28th-floor dungeon already reach the Marineford timeline?

 

Wasn't the timeline of the large-scale dungeons supposed to progress in order?

 

And once an identity is assigned in a major dungeon, that identity continues into future dungeons—so why was there such a clear timeline inconsistency?

 

Aurora continued,

 

"Second place went to Momonga. Very tall, excellent in hand-to-hand combat, a sword master, and overall a formidable opponent."

 

"As for third place... I'm sorry, it's been too long—I can't remember."

 5

"But I clearly remember the fourth place. He beat me back then—his name was Smoker. He was still a recruit at the time. Always had two cigars hanging from his mouth."

 4

Hearing that, Fenric was stunned again.

 

Smoker?

 

Another notable figure in the One Piece universe.

 

Then the confusion truly began to set in.

 

Aurora just said that Smoker was a recruit during the third-level dungeon trial.

 

Combine that with the presence of Momonga, a future Vice Admiral, and the clues pointed to one thing:

 

The third-level dungeon's timeline must be set before Luffy set out to sea.

 

But then what about Fujitora?

 

Why was he in the Navy so early?

 

Was it an intentional move by the Samsara system to raise the difficulty?

 

Wanting to clarify the timeline, Fenric asked,

 

"Ms. Morwyn, when you were running the third-level dungeon, who were the Admirals? And who was the Fleet Admiral?"

 

"The Fleet Admiral was Sengoku. The Admirals were Akainu, Aokiji, and Kizaru," Aurora replied matter-of-factly.

 

Then, she warned seriously,

 

"Shura, if you're planning to choose the Pirate camp, don't provoke any of those guys—especially not the three Admirals. They're the highest combat force of the Navy HQ. Each one of them is terrifying in their own right!"

 

After hearing this, Fenric finally confirmed it—the third-level dungeon timeline was definitely before Luffy set out on his journey.

 

As for why Fujitora was already in the Navy… it must've been a deliberate tweak by the Samsara system to increase the challenge.

 1

"Thank you for the warning." Fenric said.

 

Only a fool would provoke the Admirals.

 2

His true target remained the Celestial Dragons.

 3

That said…

 

With this timeline, killing a Celestial Dragon wouldn't be easy.

 

The main story hadn't begun yet, which meant Fenric couldn't use canon plot points to set a trap.

 

The only place he knew for sure where the Celestial Dragons appeared was the Holy Land: Mary Geoise.

 2

And with his current power level?

 

Trying to invade Mary Geoise would be like… an old man eating birthday cake made of steel—it's just suicidal.

 1

"By the way, when you cleared the third-level dungeon, did you hear where the Celestial Dragons might show up?" Fenric asked.

 

"The Celestial Dragons? You mean the ones with bubbles on their heads?"

 

"Yeah."

 

"The Navy HQ, of course. After the assessment ends, a representative of the Celestial Dragons comes to crown the top three."

 2

Aurora paused, then looked at him suspiciously.

 

"Shura… don't tell me you're planning to pick the Pirate side and assassinate a Celestial Dragon at Navy HQ? Don't be crazy! That place is crawling with monsters. Even if you get inside, you'll never get close to a Celestial Dragon!"

 

"Those nobles may be weak themselves, but they're heavily guarded. Plus, Admiral Kizaru is there—and he's got the Light-Light Fruit. His speed is basically light-speed. If you make a move, you'll die before you even draw your weapon!"

 3

"..."

 

Fenric nodded. He agreed—it was practically suicide to attempt an assassination at Navy HQ.

 

But even so...

 

He hadn't given up on killing a Celestial Dragon.

 

Then he asked again,

 

"Do you remember how long it took between the end of the assessment and the arrival of the Celestial Dragon?"

 

"Of course. Six days." Aurora Morwyn answered without hesitation.

 

Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

Six days…?

 

That meant if he chose to assassinate a Celestial Dragon, and survived for just one day, he could escape before the Admirals even arrived!

 

"Ms. Morwyn, thank you for all this information. I owe you one." Fenric said earnestly.

 1

Aurora chuckled,

 

"Well, your favor must be worth a lot—I'll be sure to cash it in~"

chapters.name: Chapter 93: Chapter 93: The Dungeon Begins! (3/10)
chapters.content:
The information Aurora Morwyn had provided was incredibly helpful to Fenric.

 

After thinking for a moment, Fenric asked,

 

"By the way, Ms. Morwyn, you're heading to the 28th floor tonight, right? I heard that's another large-scale One Piece dungeon?"

 

He didn't want to owe a favor without giving something in return—if possible, he wanted to help.

 

"Yes," Aurora nodded, though when she mentioned the dungeon, a look of worry crossed her face.

 

"What's the mission for the 28th floor?" Fenric asked.

 

Aurora Morwyn shook her head.

 

"I don't know."

 

"So far, only one person has cleared this floor—Adam. He's our competitor, so of course he hasn't shared any information.

 

I only know that the 28th-floor dungeon is linked to a major event… the 'War on the Top.'

 3

It involves the strongest pirate in the world of One Piece—Whitebeard—launching a full-scale war against Navy Headquarters."

 2

"The strongest pirate, huh?" Fenric replied vaguely, trying not to sound alarmed.

 

"Then you'd better find a way to stay far away from him."

 

Whitebeard was terrifying. In one-on-one combat, few could match him.

 

Aurora nodded solemnly.

 

"I'm afraid the main mission is directly tied to Whitebeard."

 

That was... truly unfortunate.

 

Fenric silently wished her good luck.

 

Even Aurora didn't know the mission details, so there wasn't much he could do to help.

 

"Are you going into the dungeon alone tonight?" Fenric asked.

 

"Yes." Aurora nodded again.

 

"I'm the only one currently stuck on the 28th floor."

 

After a pause, she added,

 

"Shura, I suggest you don't rush through the floors after the 10th. Be well-prepared before moving forward. The higher the floor, the fewer the Samsara players—and the less reference material you'll find from those who came before you."

 

"You've probably checked the Samsara Forum, right? Strategy guides become rare above the 10th floor, and they're almost nonexistent above the 20th. Anything above the 25th floor? Completely classified.

 1

They're treated as state secrets—strictly forbidden to be leaked."

 

"Shura, once you reach the 25th floor, you'll start to feel very alone. You'll often find yourself clearing huge dungeon worlds all by yourself."

 1

Fenric nodded. He had already anticipated this.

 

The deeper into the Samsara Tower, the harder the challenges became. Fewer and fewer people could pass each stage.

 

People like Aurora and Adam were essentially clearing large-scale public dungeons solo now.

 

While there were benefits to not competing with other Samsara players, the drawbacks were obvious too:

 

No support, no allies, and no backup.

 

Then, Fenric voiced the doubt in his mind.

 

"Ms. Morwyn, I hope you won't take offense… but if you don't know what's waiting for you, why take the risk?

 

The Samsara System doesn't force anyone to clear a floor immediately. And if the mission fails..."

 

Aurora sighed softly, then said just one sentence:

 

"I've received word… Adam cleared the 30th floor last night."

 

That explained everything.

 

Fenric immediately understood why Aurora was suddenly pushing herself to challenge the dungeon.

 

Because if Adam reached the 33rd floor first and obtained partial authority over the Samsara Space, it would be a disaster for every Samsara in the country.

 

Right now, Aurora Morwyn was the only one in Jadeveil Nation who could still compete with Adam.

 

Clearly, she wasn't risking herself just for personal glory—she was carrying the hopes of the entire nation.

 

Fenric couldn't help but feel a deep sense of respect.

 

"Ms. Morwyn, I'll be hoping for your safe return… and your victory!" Fenric said seriously.

 

He rarely admired others—but he truly admired Aurora Morwyn.

 

She smiled faintly.

 

"Shura, I hope you keep getting great results too."

 

They chatted for about forty minutes before parting ways.

 

After they separated, Fenric gave a direct command:

 

"System, send me to the Samsara Tower."

 

In the next instant, he appeared at the base of the tower.

 

Without hesitation, he used a "Dungeon Cooldown Refresh Card" to reset his dungeon entry timer.

 

He never relied on others.

 

Fenric believed that, with his speed in clearing dungeons, he might still be able to catch up to Adam before Adam reached the 33rd floor.

 

Stepping forward, he ascended to the Third Stage.

 

The moment he arrived, the tower spirit appeared out of thin air before him.

 

"Hello, Dear Samsara Player Shura. How may I assist you?"

 

"I'm here to enter a dungeon," Fenric said directly.

 

"The next dungeon is the world of One Piece. Do you wish to enter now?"

 

"Yes."

 

As soon as he confirmed, Fenric was instantly teleported into a white preparation room.

 

To his surprise, the room was packed with hundreds of people.

 

The air buzzed with chatter, creating a noisy atmosphere.

 

Clearly, all these people were here for the One Piece dungeon.

 1

As expected of a large-scale dungeon—the number of participants was massive.

 

A countdown timer on the wall indicated there were 15 minutes left before the dungeon opened.

 

Fenric quietly found a corner and sat down to wait.

 

"Huh? Are you... the God—Shura?"

 2

Suddenly, someone nearby let out a loud gasp.

 

Instant silence.

 

In an instant, the entire room quieted down.

 

These days, anyone active in the Samsara Space knows of Shura.

 

His image—a masked assassin—had spread far and wide among Samsaras.

 

"It's really Shura!"

 

"Holy sh*t, the God himself is doing this dungeon too? Didn't he just clear the Second Stage yesterday?"

 

"You dummy! Ever heard of a 'Dungeon Cooldown Refresh Card'?"

 

"He just scored an SSS-level Super God evaluation yesterday—and he's already back today for another round? Insane!"

 

"That's what makes him God-like! His dedication puts us all to shame..."

 

Samsara players from all directions were now whispering about Fenric.

 

He said nothing, simply closed his eyes and ignored the crowd.

 

At that moment...

 

A young woman dressed like a princess walked up to him.

 

"Hello, Lord Shura! Would you consider forming an alliance with me? My family is very wealthy... and I'm also very beautiful."

 

The entire room: "..."

 

Damn, sis, could you be any less subtle?

 

Many male Samsara players looked at Fenric with open envy.

chapters.name: Chapter 94: Chapter 94: Pirate Mundo! (4/10)
chapters.content:
"No."

 2

Fenric rejected her without hesitation.

 

What kind of nonsense—trying to form an alliance with him?

 

"Don't be so quick to refuse! I really am beautiful. As long as you're willing to take me along, I can fly to your city anytime," she said flirtatiously.

 

Fenric: "..."

 

Faced with someone so shameless, Fenric simply closed his eyes and pretended not to see her.

 

The "princess" chattered a few more times, but seeing that Shura completely ignored her, she finally gave up—albeit reluctantly.

 1

Fenric had still underestimated how low some people could go.

 

Many were willing to do anything to become stronger, even abandoning their dignity and morals. For this "princess" to have made it to the Third Stage, she had clearly been carried the whole way. As for what she paid in return—only she knew.

 3

In the following minutes, more Samsara players arrived.

 

Ten minutes before the start of the mission, the Samsara system sealed the passage, stopping any further entries.

 

"Attention, all Samsara players. The mission world teleportation will commence in 10 minutes."

 

By then, nearly 150 people had gathered in the white room.

 

In these final ten minutes, people clustered into small groups, discussing their plans in hushed tones. Clearly, alliances had already formed.

 

Of course, there were still a number of lone wolves—like Fenric.

 

He noticed many eyes quietly sizing him up.

 

Fenric sneered inwardly. Whatever intentions these people had, if they dared make a move on him, he wouldn't hesitate to send them straight to hell.

 

Time passed.

 

Ten minutes slipped by quickly.

 

The system's voice echoed again:

 

"Teleportation countdown starting—10, 9, 8... 3, 2, 1!"

 

When the countdown ended, everyone in the white room was enveloped in red light and vanished.

 

"Please choose your faction!"

 

"Option 1: Pirate Camp"

 

"Option 2: Navy Camp"

 

Note: This is a major dungeon world. Faction selection is final and cannot be changed. Please choose carefully.

 3

In a burst of red light, all participants received the same prompt.

 

Fenric chose the pirate faction, according to his prior plan.

 

Right after choosing, a virtual interface appeared in front of him.

 

Displayed was a character model—a one-eyed pirate with a brutish build.

 

"Player 'Shura', this is your default image in this world. If unsatisfied, please make adjustments promptly."

 

Hearing the system's voice, Fenric immediately began to customize the appearance.

 

The first thing he removed was the Cyclops eye!

 4

It was far too conspicuous—and obviously villainous. That kind of appearance would only complicate his plans later on.

 

After some tweaking, Fenric transformed his avatar into a simple, honest-looking burly man. He was satisfied with the results.

 

He only altered his appearance—everything else remained default.

 

The system-generated name for his new identity was "Mundo," which Fenric accepted without modification.

 12

And just like that—

 

Fenric's new identity in the One Piece world was established.

 

"Identity confirmed. Good luck!"

 

With that, the red light faded from Fenric's vision.

 

When his surroundings became clear again, he found himself inside a dilapidated cabin.

 

The place was a mess. The air smelled foul. There were leaks everywhere, and the ship looked like it might sink at any moment.

 

"Oi! Mundo, get up! We've docked!"

 

A skinny man came over, sharp-faced with monkey-like features and squinty eyes. He didn't look like a decent fellow.

 

As Fenric got up, the man grinned and said, "You promised me, remember? After we land, you'll buy me a bottle of good rum! Let's go! I wanna sing today!"

 

Fenric, now appearing simple and honest, smiled warmly: "Sure, but first, tell me—where's the nearest navy base?"

 

The man's face changed. "Hey hey hey, Mundo, are you still half-asleep? You're a pirate, remember? Why are you looking for the navy?"

 

"Tell me where to find them and I'll get you your rum."

 

"Alright, alright! I don't know what kind of madness you're on, but if you head east, you should reach Marineford before nightfall. That's the navy headquarters—navy everywhere!"

 

Fenric nodded and disembarked.

 

"Hey, my rum! Don't forget!" the skinny man shouted behind him.

 

After coming ashore, Fenric headed east without pause. Before long, he could see the distant silhouette of Marineford Island.

 4

The skinny guy had been wrong—Fenric reached it in just three hours, not needing to wait until dark.

 

With his current agility, Fenric could run as fast as a speeding car.

 

He had now changed his clothes, appearing like a tall but unremarkable country bumpkin.

 

The area where he stood was a small port town.

 

From here, Marineford Island could be clearly seen.

 

That island—home of the Navy Headquarters—was Fenric's next target.

 

But first...

 

He needed to assume a new identity.

 

After wandering around town and quietly observing his surroundings, Fenric took everything in.

 

Due to the town's proximity to Marineford, it was crawling with navy personnel. And because of the navy's presence, the town remained peaceful and lively—completely untouched by pirate activity.

 

At this moment, Fenric's choice of a "kindly villager" appearance paid off.

 

The navy soldiers walking past didn't give him a second glance.

 

If he had kept the one-eye pirate look, there's no way he would've blended in so easily.

 

On several walls, he noticed navy recruitment posters.

 

Today just happened to be the last day!

 

Fenric made his way to the recruiting station—but didn't go in to apply.

 

Even a fool knew that navy recruitment involved basic identity checks. At minimum, they'd ask for registration records and documentation.

 

This was what Fenric lacked.

 

So, he wasn't there to apply...

 

He was there to steal someone's place.

 

Before long, Fenric had locked onto his target—a simple, honest-looking young man who bore a remarkable resemblance to him.

 

The man had just left the recruitment office, smiling brightly. He had clearly been accepted.

 

He walked briskly, eager to share the good news with his aunt.

 

But he didn't know...

 

Behind him, a devil was quietly watching.

chapters.name: Chapter 95: Chapter 95: Naval Hero — Garp! (5/10)
chapters.content:
"Notice: Task issued!"

 

"Main Mission: Raise your bounty to at least 30 million Berries within seven days!"

 1

"Time Limit: Seven days."

 1

"Failure Condition: Obliteration!"

 

"Warning: Do not disclose the existence of the Samsara Space to anyone. Violators will be obliterated!"

 

"Tip: The higher your bounty within the time limit, the better your task evaluation will be!"

 

As expected, the system's mission notification arrived right on schedule.

 

Fenric had already anticipated the content, so his expression remained composed.

 

He quietly followed the honest-looking man who had just completed enlistment and was led into a small room.

 

"Auntie, I joined the Navy... I can finally leave this godforsaken place!" the man said over a communication snail.

 

"No need to celebrate with a drink. I'll be shipping out with the main force tonight to Marine Headquarters—Marineford."

 

"Yes, I heard there's another assessment once we get there, so I won't be coming back for a while. Just send me some extra Berries if you can."

 

"Take care of yourself, don't worry about me."

 

"You're so naggy! I'm hanging up now!"

 

…

 

An hour later.

 

The man's body lay buried behind the mountains.

 12

When he died, his eyes were wide open — he couldn't rest in peace.

 

Fenric calmly buried the body, showing no emotion whatsoever.

 

Cold-blooded. Ruthless.

 

He took the man's identity card and naval trainee certificate issued by the recruitment office, then turned and walked away.

 

Based on the information the man let slip before his death, all new recruits were scheduled to leave town by ship tonight to reach Marineford and participate in the assessment at Navy Headquarters the following day.

 

Coincidentally, the man's name was also Mundo.

 14

In other words, Fenric didn't even need to change his name.

 

When he arrived at the recruitment station, he easily blended in with the group.

 

Thanks to his [Proficient Disguise] skill, he naturally assumed Mundo's identity. His expression, movements, and demeanor were so seamless that not even a hint of suspicion arose.

 2

In such circumstances, who could tell he was a fake?

 

In the backyard of the recruitment station, dozens of trainee marines had already gathered, chatting animatedly.

 

Excitement buzzed through the air—many young men proud and thrilled to be joining the Navy.

 

Fenric quietly found a corner where no one paid attention and rested, waiting in silence.

 

Nearby, the voices of recruits carried through the crowd:

 

"Hey, Yamamoto, why do you think the Navy's recruiting so many people this time?"

 

"I heard it's because of what the Pirate King Roger said before his execution. It inspired loads of people to become pirates, and now the Navy's short-handed."

 

"Then we should thank that guy. If not for him, we might never have gotten in!"

 

"Tch. He's just a pirate."

 

Hearing that, Fenric confirmed his theory—the main storyline hadn't officially started yet.

 

The man who would later become the Pirate King likely hadn't even set sail.

 5

As the sun dipped toward the horizon, a captain-level officer arrived and loudly announced:

 

"Line up! Collect your uniforms according to size, then assemble at the port!"

 

Fenric followed the other recruits to the uniform distribution point and received a medium-sized uniform.

 

Although he now stood at 1.85 meters tall—an imposing height by human standards—in the world of One Piece, humans reaching two to three meters were common, not to mention the existence of giants.

 

So naturally, a medium uniform was all he rated.

 

Putting on the crisp navy uniform, Fenric joined the group heading toward the port.

 

A naval warship had just docked.

 

From the bow, a booming laugh echoed out as the recruits came into view:

 

"Bwahahaha! These recruits look full of spirit!"

 

The speaker was an old man, tall and powerfully built, with a broad chest and a prominent scar across his left eye. His short hair was gray-white, and his piercing eyes radiated energy.

 

He wore the signature navy "Justice" cloak, shoulder pads marked in black and red, and two silver stars indicating his rank: Vice Admiral.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed sharply the moment he saw the man.

 

He recognized him instantly.

 

Monkey D. Garp.

 

The naval hero, a living legend known across the seas as "Iron Fist Garp."

 

And more importantly—the grandfather of Monkey D. Luffy, the future protagonist.

 

"That's Hero Garp!"

 

"It's really him—the legend himself!"

 

"Can't believe he's the one picking us up! What an honor!"

 

Excited voices rang out as the recruits recognized the old man.

 

Fenric immediately lowered his head, avoiding eye contact.

 

He had no chance of defeating Garp in his current state.

 

If this old monster realized he was actually a pirate, he might not survive the infamous Iron Fist of Love.

 

The excitement among the recruits grew unruly, prompting a captain to shout:

 

"Quiet! Line up and board the ship in order!"

 

Order quickly returned as the recruits obeyed and filed into the ship.

 

Once everyone had boarded, the warship set sail.

 

Throughout the journey, Fenric remained inconspicuous, avoiding attention and refraining from even the smallest actions that might raise suspicion.

 

Even when a nearby recruit grew seasick and vomited violently, Fenric didn't so much as flinch—completely unbothered.

 

An hour later.

 

Before full darkness fell, the warship docked at Marineford.

 

Upon arrival, Fenric noticed several other naval vessels approaching the island, each one filled with recruits like themselves.

 

It seemed this round of assessments was massive in scale.

 

The Navy truly must have been understaffed—so this was their way of quickly selecting promising new talents.

 

Under a captain's direction, the recruits were assigned dormitories.

 

Fenric was led to a six-person dorm, and appeared to be the first to arrive.

 

He placed his bedding on a bunk and was just about to sit when the door swung open.

 

A sturdy young man walked in—two cigars clenched in his mouth.

 

"Yo, senior! I'm Smoker. Pleased to meet you!"

 

Fenric blinked in surprise.

 

He stared at the polite, youthful version of Smoker and couldn't help but feel a sense of déjà vu.

 

What a coincidence.

 

"Hello, I'm Mundo. Just a new recruit like you, not a senior," Fenric replied with a smile.

chapters.name: Chapter 96: Chapter 96: The Three Navy Admirals, Grand Debut (6/10)
chapters.content:
Fenric's plan wasn't particularly complicated.

 

He intended to assassinate a Celestial Dragon — and his only opportunity was during the appearance of a Celestial Dragon representative at Navy Headquarters after the assessment concluded.

 2

Because the main storyline hadn't officially started yet, he couldn't rely on the plot to locate a Celestial Dragon.

 

The world of One Piece was vast — an enormous map filled with countless islands and oceans.

 

And the system had only given him seven days!

 2

Finding the whereabouts of a Celestial Dragon within that limited timeframe was nearly impossible.

 

So, Fenric disguised himself as a Navy recruit and infiltrated headquarters, biding his time for the right moment to strike.

 

However—

 

Navy Headquarters was teeming with elite combatants. In such a heavily guarded environment, assassinating a Celestial Dragon under strict protection was no simple task.

 

According to intel from Aurora, after the naval assessment, the top three candidates would be received and honored by a representative of the Celestial Dragons.

 

Fenric's goal, then, was to blend in as a fake recruit, earn a top ranking, and wait for the Celestial Dragon representative to appear.

 

Only under those conditions could he get close safely.

 

That was his plan.

 

Extremely dangerous.

 

Even a single mistake in any step could expose him — and once exposed, he'd be hunted down by an Admiral.

 

"Senior, can I sleep here? There's a window nearby — it helps disperse my smoke!"

 2

The young Smoker pointed at the bed next to Fenric, a look of excitement on his face.

 1

It had always been his dream to join the Navy.

 

"Of course," Fenric replied with a smile. "Just call me Mundo."

 

"Got it, Senior Mundo! Thank you for your generosity."

 

Smoker cheerfully laid down his bedding, then asked, "By the way, Senior Mundo, does my smoke bother you? It's from my Devil Fruit ability — it won't affect you."

 

"I don't mind," Fenric said, shaking his head with a faint smile.

 

"Senior Mundo, you're really kind and generous!" Smoker said sincerely.

 

At that moment—

 

The dormitory door creaked open again.

 

A burly man, nearly two meters tall, stepped inside.

 

Both Fenric and Smoker turned to look.

 

The man scanned the room, and when he noticed the best bed already occupied by the two, he marched over without hesitation.

 

He looked at Fenric first, then at Smoker. Judging by Smoker's younger appearance and the constant smoke irritating him, the man must've thought he could push him around.

 1

"Hey, smoker," the man growled. "You're on my bed. Move your stinkin' stuff before I lose my patience!"

 

Smoker might have still been young and somewhat inexperienced, but he wasn't a fool.

 

"The beds are first come, first served. I got here before you."

 

The man snorted. "I don't care when you got here. I said that bed is mine, so it's mine!"

 

Fenric stayed seated on the bed, watching the exchange calmly.

 

Smoker looked helpless. He had just joined the Navy and didn't want trouble—but this guy was clearly picking a fight. And Smoker wasn't going to just swallow his pride.

 

The next moment—

 

His body began to swell and transform, turning into a massive smoke giant, nearly brushing the ceiling.

 

He loomed over the brawny man, gazing down with cold eyes.

 

"A D-Devil Fruit user…!" the man stammered, pale with fear.

 1

"This is my bed. Any objections?" Smoker asked coolly.

 

"N-no… no objections…"

 

Satisfied, Smoker returned to normal size, deactivating his powers.

 

The brawny man no longer dared to look him in the eye. Instead, he turned his frustration toward Fenric.

 

"What the hell are you looking at—"

 

Boom!

 

Before he could finish his sentence, he was sent flying across the room.

 

Fenric sat calmly back down on the bed, as if nothing had happened.

 

"!!"

 

Smoker was stunned.

 

He had just said that Senior Mundo was kind and generous...

 

Now he wasn't so sure.

 1

The Next Day

 

Early morning.

 

Ding-ding-ding—!

 

A loud bell echoed through the recruits' dormitory, rousing many from their sleep.

 

"Recruits, up and out! Assemble in the square in ten minutes!"

 1

Veterans shouted from the corridors, their voices loud and stern.

 

Grumbling quietly, countless recruits got out of bed, washed up, threw on their uniforms, and rushed toward the square.

 

When Fenric and Smoker arrived, they saw ten massive broadcasting platforms arranged throughout the giant square.

 

At the front was a high platform lined with many chairs — clearly reserved for important guests.

 1

"Senior Mundo, I thought we were here to be assessed?" Smoker whispered. "What's all this?"

 

Fenric smiled. "This is probably the most important part of the assessment."

 

Smoker looked confused and was about to ask more when an excited shout came from nearby:

 

"Look! It's the Fleet Admiral Sengoku! He's here!"

 

"And the three Admirals too!"

 

All the recruits turned their eyes toward the platform.

 

Fenric did the same.

 

A group of high-ranking naval officers strode out slowly and purposefully.

 

Leading them was a man wearing frog-shaped glasses, with a long beard twisted like rope. His cap bore the Navy's iconic seagull insignia.

 1

Fleet Admiral Sengoku.

 

He looked calm and composed — but Fenric knew better. This man was incredibly powerful.

 

Behind him walked three towering men, each about three meters tall.

 

Fenric's eyes lit up instantly.

 

Aokiji. Akainu. Kizaru.

 2

The three Admirals of the Navy Headquarters — symbols of the Navy's ultimate power.

 

Trailing behind them were a dozen vice admirals.

 

Among them were notable figures like Garp, Tsuru, and Momousagi.

 

In truth—

 

Some of the vice admirals were as powerful as the admirals themselves. They simply preferred to stay low-key or had no interest in promotion.

 

The most famous among them was none other than the Hero of the Marines: Monkey D. Garp!

 

On paper, Garp's feats far surpassed those of the three Admirals.

 

Once all the distinguished guests had taken their seats on the high platform, Fleet Admiral Sengoku stepped forward. Looking down at the sea of recruits, he began to speak.

 

"I am Sengoku, Fleet Admiral of the Navy. On behalf of the Navy — I welcome you all!"

 

A wave of cheers and applause erupted from the square.

chapters.name: Chapter 97: Chapter 97: Smoker vs. Fenric (7/10)
chapters.content:
The Navy Fleet Admiral Sengoku stepped forward and gave a speech to inspire the recruits.

 

His oratory skills were impressive.

 

However, Fenric had heard more than enough motivational speeches in his life. To him, it all sounded like overused chicken soup for the soul—sleep-inducing at best.

 

In contrast, the fresh-faced recruits were full of fire and enthusiasm.

 

Even Smoker, standing beside Fenric, looked fired up and ready to give his life for the Navy.

 1

"Now—begin the assessment!"

 

With Sengokus' declaration, the evaluation officially commenced.

 

Due to the sheer number of recruits, the assessments had to be conducted in batches.

 

There were ten arenas in total.

 

Based on regional assignments, Fenric and Smoker were both assigned to Arena 7.

 

Once grouped, everyone began drawing lots to determine their opponents.

 

Half the participants drew numbers from a box, while the other half held matching numbered tags.

 

If someone drew a number, they would face the recruit who held the corresponding tag.

 

"Senior Mundo, I'll go up first!"

 

Smoker eagerly rushed forward to draw a number.

 

He pulled out number 30.

 

The officer overseeing the area immediately called out, "Who has tag number 30? Step forward!"

 

Fenric looked down at the label in his hand, dumbfounded.

 

What the hell…

 

What kind of luck is this?

 

With a sigh, Fenric stood up and silently made his way to the arena.

 

When Smoker saw that his opponent was none other than Mundo, his confident expression immediately fell.

 

If he had a choice, fighting Mundo was the last thing he'd want.

 

But the draw was binding. There was no backing out now. Like it or not, he had to fight.

 

"Senior Mundo, I didn't mean for this to happen…" Smoker said with a miserable expression.

 

Fenric was at a loss for words. Just as he was about to comfort the kid, Smoker added with a grave tone:

 

"Please don't take it personally, Senior Mundo. I didn't want to eliminate you so early."

 2

Fenric: "…"

 

What the hell?!

 

Where is this kid getting his confidence from?!

 1

And hey—those were supposed to be my lines!

 

"Have you two finished chatting?! Begin—now!!" barked the impatient officer.

 

All the other arenas were already underway, but these two were still dawdling.

 

Hearing that, Smoker quickly shut up and got into a combat stance.

 

But when he noticed that Fenric remained motionless, he couldn't help but remind him, "Senior Mundo, I won't hold back! Please be careful!"

 

"Go ahead," Fenric said calmly.

 

As soon as he spoke, Smoker charged toward him.

 

And so, the battle began.

 

Up on the observation platform—

 

"Zzz… snrk—"

 

The sound of snoring interrupted the serious atmosphere.

 

"!!"

 

Sengoku's face darkened.

 

He didn't need to look to know who it was. Only Garp would dare fall asleep on such an important occasion.

 

"Garp! Show some respect! This is a formal event!" Sengokus scolded.

 

Woken abruptly, Garp casually picked his nose, looking bored.

 

It wasn't that he disrespected the recruits. It's just that their performance was far too underwhelming.

 

Most of them were either slow and clueless or swinging their fists around like amateurs. He hadn't seen a single decent seedling yet.

 

Truthfully, many on the platform shared his sentiment.

 

Even Admiral Kizaru, lounging lazily, looked disinterested as he watched the ten simultaneous matches below.

 

"Hmm?"

 

Suddenly, Kizaru's eyes lit up.

 

The match in Arena 7 had caught his attention.

 2

"Senior Mundo, surrender! I really don't want to hurt you!"

 

Smoker's voice echoed from the ring.

 

Fenric: "…"

 

Alright, that's it.

 

Time to teach this overly confident brat a lesson about the real world.

 

He activated his Telekinesis power.

 1

Smoker, who had just lunged forward, suddenly lost control of his body and was flung directly into Fenric's waiting fist.

 

"Devil fruit user?!"

 

Smoker was stunned and instinctively transformed into smoke.

 

Poof!

 

Fenric's punch passed through harmlessly, hitting only air.

 

"Interesting…" Fenric smirked.

 

This was his first time facing a Devil Fruit user in combat.

 

In the next moment, Smoker's smoke condensed, and his form reappeared at the same spot.

 

Now fully alert, Smoker said seriously, "I didn't expect you to be a Devil Fruit user too, Senior Mundo!"

 

Fenric simply shrugged.

 

If Smoker mistook his Telekinesis powers for a Devil Fruit ability, there was no need to correct him.

 

"In that case, if you want to eliminate me, you'd better get serious," Fenric said calmly.

 

"I will! Please be careful!"

 

Smoker took a deep breath and shouted, "White Fist!"

 

His arms immediately turned into smoke, and his fists launched away like missiles, trailing long white smoke tails as they flew toward Fenric.

 

Of course, an attack of that level couldn't hit Fenric.

 

With a casual wave of his hand, Fenric subtly used his mind power. The smoke fists veered off course and missed completely.

 

But Smoker wasn't finished.

 

This move had a follow-up!

 

The drifting smoke fists suddenly spun around mid-air and redirected toward Fenric—like heat-seeking missiles.

 

The surrounding recruits were shocked at the technique.

 

Even the bigwigs on the platform showed interest and turned their attention to the seventh arena.

 

Fenric, however, remained composed.

 

As Smoker's fists neared the back of his head, he activated his Telekinesis power once again.

 

This time, he didn't interfere passively.

 

He stopped them directly in mid-air.

 

Smoker's fists froze on the spot, unable to move forward even an inch.

 

"If that's all you've got," Fenric said flatly, "then I'm afraid you're the one who's going to be eliminated."

chapters.name: Chapter 98: Chapter 98: I Am Very Optimistic About Him! (8/10)
chapters.content:
On the elevated platform—

 

"One has a Logia-type smoke ability, and the other… something strange."

 

Sengoku stared intently at Arena No. 7 and asked without turning his head,

 

"Garp, can you tell what that ability is?"

 

"It should be a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit. Quite a rare one at that," Garp replied.

 

At this moment, Garp was no longer dozing like before. He sat upright and focused on the battle playing out on the screen.

 

The same was true for the three Admirals and several Vice Admirals. All eyes were now on the seventh arena.

 

In Arena 7

 

Smoker's expression changed drastically as he realized his outstretched fist had been frozen in place—restrained by some invisible force.

 

Senior Mundo's ability was even more bizarre and overwhelming than his own!

 

"White Smoke Launcher!"

 

Smoker shouted. His legs instantly turned into smoke as he launched himself at Fenric like a cannonball.

 

This was his second technique.

 

Facing the charging Smoker, Fenric simply raised his hand—his fingers splayed open.

 

Telekinesis power—activated again.

 

Once more, Smoker's body was suspended in mid-air, immobilized by Fenric's will.

 

However, Smoker didn't panic. It was as if he had anticipated this.

 

"White Blast!!"

 

Smoker shouted again, and his body began to expand before dissolving entirely into smoke.

 

Thick white clouds surged outward, surrounding Fenric from all directions.

 

This was one of Smoker's ultimate moves!

 

In the original plot, he had once used this technique to trap an entire pirate crew—not exactly weak opponents either.

 

It wasn't just a trap. If used to its fullest, this technique could suffocate or kill.

 

"Senior Mundo! This is my strongest move! I advise you to surrender now!" Smoker yelled from within the fog.

 

Fenric couldn't help but chuckle inwardly.

 

This younger version of Smoker really gives off some serious chuuni energy… But he's not a bad kid.

 

"Since you've shown your strongest technique, Smoker, then I'll also get serious. You might get hurt, so don't say I didn't warn you."

 

As soon as the words left his mouth, Fenric clenched his fist.

 

Om—

 

Armament Haki surged forth, coating his hand.

 

His entire fist turned jet-black with a deep metallic sheen, shining faintly under the arena lights.

 

Fenric's current Armament Haki had already reached Grandmaster proficiency. Just in terms of Armament Haki mastery alone, even in the world of One Piece, he ranked mid-top.

 

Then—

 

He unleashed his full Telekinesis power, condensing all the surrounding smoke into a dense cluster.

 

Immediately after, Fenric launched a punch.

 

"Senior Mundo, it's useless! I'm a Logia-type Devil Fruit user! Your fists can't hurt me—"

 

BAM!

 

Before Smoker could even finish his sentence, Fenric's punch struck him head-on, instantly forcing him back into his solid form and sending him crashing to the ground.

 

Smoker nearly coughed up blood on impact.

 

And that was with Fenric holding back.

 

If Fenric had used his full strength, Smoker would've been eliminated instantly.

 

Smoker was still far too inexperienced. He hadn't even grasped Haki yet, so there was no way he could match Fenric.

 

"Smoker," Fenric said with a smirk, "What was that you were saying just now?"

 

"Cough… cough…" Smoker clutched his stomach, half-kneeling on the ground, his face pale. "Armament… Haki!"

 2

Clearly, he now understood what he had just been hit with.

 

"Want to keep going?" Fenric asked casually.

 

Smoker lowered his head and replied weakly, "Senior Mundo… I surrender."

 

He wasn't an idiot. It was obvious that Fenric had gone easy on him.

 

With Smoker conceding, the referee captain, who had finally recovered from shock, quickly stood up and announced:

 

"First match on Arena No. 7—Player 30, 'Mundo', wins!"

 1

Beneath the broadcasting platform, many recruits looked at Fenric with newfound fear and awe.

 

Standing in the center of the ring, Fenric scanned the area but didn't see the blind man he'd been wary of. He let out a quiet sigh of relief before stepping down.

 

According to Aurora's intel, that blind man was one of the few individuals who might actually threaten Fenric.

 

Even someone like the future Vice Admiral "Momonga" might not be much stronger at this point in time.

 

On the high platform—

 

Admiral Kizaru watched Fenric walk off the stage, his tone as lazy as ever but with a hint of surprise:

 

"He's so young, yet already has a Devil Fruit ability and mastered Haki? These rookies nowadays really can't be underestimated…"

 

Akainu and Aokiji remained silent, but their gazes were fixed firmly on Fenric.

 

Meanwhile, Garp suddenly burst out laughing.

 

"That kid's not bad. I'm very optimistic about him!"

 3

It wasn't just Fenric's strength that impressed Garp—but the fact that he had shown mercy to Smoker.

 

To Garp, strength alone wasn't what defined a great Navy officer. Character and judgment were just as important.

 

In fact, at this moment, Garp was even entertaining the idea of taking Fenric in as a disciple.

 

Sengoku nodded beside him, agreeing with Garp's assessment.

 

"He's a good seed, indeed," the Marshal said. "Someone who wields power yet knows how to restrain it—that's the kind of talent the Navy needs."

 

Unlike the red-hot Admiral Akainu standing next to them... Sengoku had never liked his overly aggressive nature.

 

But how will these two old veterans react when Fenric eventually shows his true colors?

 3

Back in the rest area—

 

Seeing Smoker sulking, Fenric chuckled and offered some words of comfort.

 

"Don't be discouraged. This whole assessment is about finding promising talent. Your performance was excellent, even if you were eliminated for now."

 

He wasn't just being polite.

 

In the original storyline, Smoker's strength kept improving, and he was promoted rapidly. Within a few years, he became a Vice Admiral of the G-5 Branch!

 

Smoker's eyes widened in surprise.

 

"Senior Mundo, are you serious?!"

 

"Of course," Fenric said with a smile. "Just wait—you'll go far."

 

For some reason, Smoker completely believed him. Encouraged by those words, his spirits lifted immediately.

 

He was about to ask more, but noticed Fenric's gaze had shifted—focused sharply on the fifth ring.

 

Smoker followed his line of sight, curiosity piqued.

 

At that moment…

 

A middle-aged man, over two meters tall and visibly muscular, stepped onto Arena 5.

 

Surprisingly—this man was blind.

 

(Author's Note: I saw some readers asking about the 35-year-old age limit. This ties into a future urban arc and is part of a major upcoming plot twist so don't mind the details.)

 3

chapters.name: Chapter 99: Chapter 99: A Great Character Arrives (9/10)
chapters.content:
"On Ring Five, Player No. 17—Markuri—will face off against Player No. 22—Issho. Both contestants, please take the stage!"

 

At the captain-referee's announcement, a towering figure—nearly two meters tall and rippling with muscles—leapt onto the stage with ease.

 

This was Player No. 17: Markuri.

 

Clack! Clack! Clack!

 

The distinct sound of a cane tapping the ground followed. Slowly, a blind man made his way onto the stage, relying on the cane in his hand to guide him.

 

As he stepped up onto the platform, many in the audience held their breath, worried he might stumble.

 

The man's features were rugged, with an "X"-shaped scar over the left side of his forehead. He had short, black hair, a rough beard, and wore a lavender bathrobe secured with a dark purple belt. Despite his tall frame, nothing about him appeared particularly threatening.

 1

Only Fenric understood how terrifying this blind man truly was.

 

This was the future Navy Admiral—Fujitora, currently known only by the name "Issho."

 

Right now, he appeared to be in his thirties or forties—his physical prime.

 

Fenric's expression grew solemn as he watched the man's back.

 

For the system to throw someone like this into the recruits' assessment... it could only be an intentional challenge for the Samsara players.

 

"Senior Mundo, is he strong?" Smoker whispered beside him.

 

Smoker wasn't dumb. Seeing Fenric's expression, he immediately sensed something was off about the blind man.

 

Fenric nodded. "Very strong."

 

Smoker's eyes lit up with interest as he turned his attention to Ring Five.

 

On Ring Five.

 

Markuri blinked at the sight of the blind man stepping onto the platform. After a brief pause, he chuckled.

 

"Hey, Uncle, did you walk into the wrong place?"

 

The blind man smiled calmly and scratched the back of his head. "I don't think I'm mistaken."

 

Markuri laughed. "I don't like bullying the disabled. How about you just forfeit now?"

 

The blind man said nothing, only shook his head gently.

 

"Fine then! Don't blame me for what happens. I won't go easy on you!"

 

With that, Markuri charged forward like a runaway tank, his enormous fist swinging straight for the blind man's face.

 

The spectators around the ring all winced, certain the old man was done for.

 

Boom!

 

A thud echoed as something heavy hit the ground.

 

To everyone's shock, it wasn't the blind man who had fallen—but Markuri. He had been sent flying out of the ring.

 

Gasps rippled through the crowd.

 

No one had seen what happened. How had the man who seemed certain to win been defeated in an instant?

 

Offstage.

 

Only Fenric had witnessed the full exchange.

 2

Thanks to his enhanced neural reflexes and vision, capable of tracking even bullets, he had seen it all.

 

The blind man had merely tapped the ground with his cane—and Markuri was launched from the ring.

 

The speed of the strike was too fast for ordinary eyes to follow. The match was already over before most had realized it had begun.

 

Fenric's gaze sharpened. He stared intently at the blind man, his expression unreadable.

 

Fujitora was indeed terrifying. But it didn't interfere with Fenric's larger plan.

 

Back on the ring.

 

The referee stood frozen, failing to announce the result. The blind man cleared his throat with a gentle cough.

 

"Ahem."

 

The referee snapped out of his daze and quickly shouted, "Player No. 22—Issho—wins!"

 

With a faint smile, the blind man turned and walked off the stage.

 

The crowd instinctively parted for him, no one daring to block his path.

 

They weren't fools. If anything, the fact they hadn't even seen how the man won made him all the more terrifying.

 

High above, on the observation platform.

 

The three admirals narrowed their eyes as they watched the blind man retreat.

 

While ordinary people couldn't see what had happened, the admirals certainly could.

 

True experts could always recognize another master.

 

The move he had used was deceptively simple—a straightforward thrust of the cane. But such a basic motion required impeccable mastery of fundamentals.

 

To the three admirals, one thing was clear: this man was no ordinary recruit.

 

"That one... is powerful," Aokiji remarked, breaking the silence.

 

Just being acknowledged by Aokiji was enough to prove Fujitora's terrifying strength.

 

"The newcomers these days are getting more and more ridiculous," Kizaru added, his tone as strangely aloof as always.

 

Akainu said nothing. His piercing gaze remained fixed on the blind man, unblinking.

 

Beside the admirals, Sengoku and Garp also wore grave expressions.

 

The average person might miss the details, but not veterans like them. They saw the technique behind the blind man's strike—and the strength.

 

The assessment continued.

 

With over 200,000 recruits, even dividing them among ten rings meant the trials would last for days.

 

Fenric and Fujitora became the center of attention for the high-ranking officials.

 

Each time Fenric fought, he effortlessly defeated his opponent. But he was careful—always stopping just short of doing real harm.

 

It was an image he was crafting on purpose: one of benevolence and righteousness.

 

He wanted to appear harmless. The idea was simple—if he seemed noble and principled, the higher-ups would lower their guard. That way, when the time came for him to approach the Celestial Dragons, no one would suspect his true intentions.

 

After all, who would ever think that such a "righteous" man would dare assassinate a Celestial Dragon?

 

But Fenric hadn't expected that his carefully cultivated image would attract attention from even higher up.

 

Both Sengoku and Garp had taken a liking to him.

 

In fact, Garp was seriously considering taking him as a disciple!

 

"Garp, have you made up your mind?"

 

On the observation deck, Sengoku asked quietly.

 

Garp let out a hearty laugh. "Yeah! It's not often you meet such an interesting kid. Sengoku, you wouldn't object, would you?"

 

"Of course not," Sengoku replied with a grin. "With your guidance, this kid—'Mundo,' was it?—is incredibly lucky."

 

"But Garp," he added, his voice becoming more serious, "you should hold off until the assessments are over. If he finds out your intentions too early, he might get cocky."

 

Sengoku couldn't help but remind him. Garp was great in many ways—but he had a habit of being reckless and unpredictable.
