chapters.name: Chapter 100: Chapter 100: The Top Three Masters (10/10)
chapters.content:
"The winner of the seventh ring, Contestant No. 30—Mundo!"

 

Following the referee's announcement, Fenric secured yet another victory.

 

However, instead of stepping down immediately, he walked over to the opponent he had just defeated and extended a hand.

 

"You alright?"

 

"Huh? Senior Mundo, I'm fine. Thank you for showing mercy," the young man replied, visibly moved by Fenric's gesture.

 

Although he had been eliminated, it was hard to resent someone like Mundo.

 

"That's good."

 

Fenric helped the man up before turning to leave the arena.

 

As soon as he stepped off the ring, Smoker rushed over excitedly.

 

"Senior Mundo, you're amazing! That's your nineteenth win today!"

 

Smoker now resembled a devoted fan, thoroughly impressed by Mundo's (Fenric's) image as the benevolent and righteous figure.

 5

Fenric simply smiled, unfazed by the praise.

 

Most of those nineteen wins had been against ordinary opponents—nothing to brag about.

 

"The next match: Contestant No. 76, Bray, versus Contestant No. 55, Kate!"

 

Two young men stepped into the arena. The match ended quickly.

 

Contestant No. 55, Kate, knew actual martial arts—Tai Chi.

 

He used a technique called "Tai Chi Push" and effortlessly sent Bray flying out of the ring.

 

Clearly, this wasn't something native to the One Piece world.

 

"That Kate guy is incredible—another clean win!"

 

"Yeah! That's two eliminations now!"

 

"His moves look slow, but they pack a serious punch. Really weird stuff."

 

The crowd buzzed with chatter.

 

Fenric's eyes gleamed. He was almost certain—this "Tai Chi" Kate was like him: a Samsara player.

 

Just like the few others he had already identified.

 

Still, he didn't concern himself with them.

 

As long as they didn't provoke him or interfere with his plan to hunt down the Celestial Dragons, he wouldn't bother.

 

Of course, if one of them ended up as his opponent by random draw—well, that couldn't be helped.

 

Sunset.

 

"Today's assessment ends here! Be back here tomorrow at 7:00 sharp!"

 

With a booming declaration from a vice admiral, the day's trials came to an end.

 

The recruits shuffled off toward the mess hall.

 

Those who had been eliminated looked dejected, appetite lost.

 

Even those still in the running were uneasy. The assessment would continue tomorrow, and no one felt truly safe.

 

Only the genuinely strong—or overconfident—remained unbothered.

 

Five days passed in a flash.

 

Over the course of those five days, several recruits managed to stand out and cause quite a stir.

 

The top three most popular figures were: the blind man "Issho," the gentle and kind "Senior Mundo," and the Navy captain known as "Momonga."

 2

The three of them had eliminated countless opponents—and still, none had shown their full strength.

 

Even after five days, no one knew for sure who among them was the strongest.

 

Some believed the blind man Issho had bottomless depths.

 

Others were convinced that Mundo, the kind senior, was truly unmatched.

 

Momonga had plenty of support too, especially since he was a disciple of the former admiral Zephyr. He'd entered the assessment to prove himself.

 

Besides those three, a few other notable names emerged.

 

There was the axe-wielding "Pillard," the mysterious expert "Kate," and the battle-hardened "Banamen," known as the King of Fights.

 

From over 200,000 participants, fewer than a hundred now remained.

 

Today was the final day of the assessment.

 

It was rumored that the top three candidates would be personally received by a true noble.

 

Day Six.

 

Early in the morning, the square was packed with recruits eager to witness the final outcome.

 

"Look! It's Senior Mundo!"

 

"Get out of the way! Don't block Senior Mundo's path, you idiots!"

 

As Fenric appeared, waves of chatter erupted all around him.

 

Fenric kept up his act of "benevolence and righteousness," smiling warmly and nodding politely to anyone who looked his way, friend or stranger alike.

 1

"Ah! He smiled at me!"

 

"As expected of the 'Gentle Senior'—so noble and kind."

 

"After this, he'll surely become a senior general!"

 

Fenric's face remained composed, but internally he was screaming curses!

 

Who the hell gave me that ridiculous nickname?!

 

And worse—it had actually caught on among the recruits!

 

Gentle Senior?

 

Just wait until the Celestial Dragons appear. Then you'll see just how 'gentle' I really am!

 3

"Senior Mundo, look! It's Vice Admiral Garp! He's coming this way!" Smoker suddenly exclaimed.

 

Fenric immediately snapped to attention along with the others.

 

As Garp approached, Fenric and all the nearby recruits saluted in unison.

 

"Vice Admiral Garp!"

 

It was standard protocol for low-ranking Navy members to salute high-ranking officers.

 

Garp ignored the others and walked straight up to Fenric. He looked him up and down, then grinned and patted him on the shoulder.

 

"Kid, do well today. I made a bet with Sengoku that if you take first place, I'll personally train you—ha ha ha!"

 

With that, Garp turned and walked away.

 

Watching his powerful figure retreat, Fenric let out a breath.

 

That old man...

 

For a moment, Fenric had worried that his cover was blown!

 

To his surprise, Garp had only come to encourage him—and hint that he was interested in taking him on as a disciple.

 

Fenric couldn't help but laugh wryly.

 

Would Garp still be so eager if he knew I planned to kill the Celestial Dragons?

 6

"Senior Mundo, Vice Admiral Garp wants to take you as his student!" Smoker exclaimed, both envious and excited.

 

The nearby recruits all stared in envy, wishing they were in Fenric's place.

 

Fenric sighed inwardly. Garp was far too unpredictable.

 

"It's not that easy. I have to win first place," he replied casually.

 

"Then go for it, Senior Mundo! I believe in you!"

chapters.name: Chapter 101: Chapter 101: Vs Navy Six Forms!
chapters.content:
With all the major figures in attendance, the sixth day's assessment officially began.

 

The remaining 92 participants were divided into two teams.

 

Once again, lots were drawn to determine opponents.

 

The first to step forward was the blind man known as "Issho."

 

He reached into the box and drew a small ball, handing it to the referee beside him. Unable to see the number himself, he relied on the official's announcement.

 

"Contestant No. 22, Issho—your opponent is Contestant No. 55, Kate!"

 

As the referee's voice rang out, Fenric clearly saw the man nicknamed "Kate" instantly turn pale.

 

Apparently, Kate knew all too well that he was no match for Issho.

 

And indeed, he wasn't.

 

The moment both contestants stepped onto the stage, Kate was quickly overwhelmed and defeated, leaving the ring with a look of despair.

 

Still, with his current reputation and accomplishments, he likely wouldn't have trouble completing his mission from the Samsara System.

 

After Issho's easy victory, the 27th person approached the box—a chubby young man wielding a massive axe.

 
 COMMENT

Despite his youthful appearance, his massive frame stood out—taller and broader than the average adult. Dressed in a bright red bellyband and carrying a giant axe slung over his shoulder, he radiated an imposing aura that made people hesitant to judge him by his age.

 

From the viewing platform above, Admiral Kizaru chuckled at the sight.

 

"This kid's pretty cute," he remarked.

 

"Contestant No. 11, Sentomaru—your opponent is Contestant No. 67, Banamen!"

 6

As the next pairing was announced...

 

Moments later, another Samsara was eliminated.

 

That's right—Banamen, known as the "King of Fighting," was a Samsara player like Fenric. His combat style? The "Yagami Ancient Martial Arts" from the King of Fighters universe!

 

He definitely had connections—there's no way a newcomer to the Third Stage of the Samsara Tower could afford to acquire such a legendary martial art without serious backing.

 

After Sentomaru's rather foul-smelling victory, the third contestant approached the box.

 

This man's uniform was noticeably different from the standard recruit's attire. Even the referee greeted him with visible respect.

 

His name was Yumo, a disciple of the former Admiral "Black Wrist" Zephyr. Currently serving as a Navy captain, Yumo was one of the Three Elite Masters everyone was eager to see in action.

 1

His appearance stirred interest among the higher-ups seated on the observation platform.

 

Zephyr had once trained many powerful disciples—including the current three Admirals.

 

In terms of seniority, that made Red Dog (Akainu), Green Pheasant (Aokiji), and Yellow Monkey (Kizaru) essentially Yumo's "senpais."

 4

Back in the arena...

 

Yumo silently drew a ball from the box.

 

The referee paled upon seeing the number.

 

"Contestant No. 85, Yumo, your opponent is Contestant No. 30—Mundo!"

 

The moment the names were called, gasps echoed through the crowd.

 

Two of the Three Elite Masters were about to face off!

 

As Fenric calmly walked toward the ring, excitement rippled through the audience. All eyes were glued to the stage, eager to witness a true showdown between two elites.

 

"Hey, who do you think is stronger? Senior Mundo or Senior Yumo?"

 

"I bet on Senior Yumo. His teacher was the famous Admiral Zephyr! That kind of background guarantees strength!"

 

"No way, I'm rooting for Mundo. So far, no one has even forced him to go all out!"

 

Even the high-ranking officers on the platform grew interested, their attention fixed on the unfolding match.

 

In the ring, Fenric and Yumo faced off from a distance.

 

In terms of size, Fenric was clearly at a disadvantage.

 

Though tall by normal standards, he looked downright petite next to Yumo's towering frame of over 2.5 meters.

 

Fenric sighed inwardly. In the original timeline, Yumo (Momonga) had already become a renowned figure during Roger's era. For someone like him to suddenly appear here as a contestant… there was no doubt—it was the Samsara System at work again.

 3

"Begin!"

 

The referee's voice rang out.

 

Whoosh!

 

Before the echo faded, Yumo vanished.

 

Navy Six Forms: Shave!

 

The Navy Six Forms was an advanced martial art, exclusive to high-ranking officers. It pushed the limits of the human body and consisted of six powerful techniques.

 

Yumo had clearly mastered both Shave and Moonwalk.

 

Shave—in just 0.36 seconds, by stomping the ground dozens of times in rapid succession, the user generates explosive reaction force and seemingly disappears from sight.

 3

As Yumo vanished, Fenric's eyes narrowed sharply.

 

He clenched his right fist, coating it instantly with Armament Haki.

 

Without hesitation, he punched the air to his left!

 

To bystanders, it looked like he was attacking thin air.

 

But the next second, a large figure materialized—Yumo—mid-kick, striking from Fenric's blind spot.

 

His foot, wrapped in Armament Haki, came crashing down—

 

BOOM!!!

 

Fist and foot collided with a deafening roar.

 

A shockwave exploded outward from the two fighters, the force cracking the broadcasting platform beneath Fenric's feet inch by inch.

 

Below the ring, the watching recruits were stunned.

 

No one expected the duel to erupt with such intensity from the very first move!

 

"Moonwalk!"

 1

Yumo shouted, withdrawing his leg as his body launched into the air. His feet tapped against the air itself, propelling him like a ghost above the battlefield.

 

Navy Six Forms: Moonwalk!

 

This technique resembled lightfoot-style martial arts, akin to "Cloud-Stepping."

 

By exerting powerful force with each step, users could walk on air as though climbing invisible stairs.

 

Watching Yumo dart through the sky, Fenric remained expressionless.

 

He raised one hand and pressed downward.

 

"Come down."

 

Telekinesis: Activated.

 

An invisible force surged upward, immediately binding Yumo's movements. Mid-air, he felt his limbs stiffen as the force disrupted his control over Moonwalk.

 

His towering form began plummeting toward the ground.

chapters.name: Chapter 102: Chapter 102: Too Strong!
chapters.content:
Bang!

 

Fenric stepped forward, and the stone slab beneath his foot exploded.

 

Using the recoil, he shot forward like a sharp sword, charging straight at Momonga!

 

At the same time, Yumo was pinned to the ground by Fenric's telekinetic force, and Fenric followed up with a powerful punch.

 

Simultaneously, his Telekinesis power began suppressing Momonga's movements.

 

Fenric's mental strength wasn't exceptionally high, and continuously using telekinesis in combat consumed a significant amount of his mental energy. That's why using his fists was his most effective method.

 

When dealing with someone like Smoker, it was fine to rely on mind power alone.

 

But using mental abilities recklessly against every opponent as if playing a game was nothing short of idiocy.

 

Once his mental energy was depleted, he'd end up dizzy and unable to fight at all.

 

Whoosh!

 

A sonic boom rang out. One could only imagine the sheer power behind Fenric's punch.

 

Yumo's expression shifted.

 

In that brief moment, he could only cross his arms and coat them in Armament Haki to block Fenric's strike.

 

Boom!!!

 

Another thunderous explosion echoed.

 

Skrrt! Skrrt! Skrrt!

 

The towering Yumo was sent skidding back repeatedly by Fenric's punch, nearly falling out of the ring.

 

When he finally stabilized himself, his expression darkened.

 

A sharp pain shot through his arms, and the impact site had already gone numb.

 

Clearly, the muscles and bones beneath had sustained serious internal damage!

 

The Mundo before him—was this guy even human?!

 

If not for his Armament Haki's strong defense, that punch might have shattered his arms and even killed him on the spot.

 

What was more terrifying, though, was Fenric's strange psychic ability—it was virtually impossible to guard against!

 

"You truly are strong, Mundo."

 

Momonga's tone was solemn.

 2

This was the first time he had spoken to an opponent during a match.

 

In previous fights, he hadn't even bothered talking—he'd simply crushed his enemies.

 

"Thinking of surrendering already?" Fenric smiled.

 

"No. From here on, I'll be fighting seriously!"

 

Yumo drew his saber from his waist as he spoke.

 7

Beneath the Ring

 

The audience of countless recruits was in an uproar after the brief but intense exchange.

 

"Damn! Senior Mundo and Senior Yumo are insane!"

 

"Are they even human?!"

 

"Senior Mundo is seriously incredible!"

 

"Yeah, Yumo's being suppressed so badly he has to use his weapon now!"

 

"Senior Mundo's my idol from now on!"

 

On the Viewing Platform

 

Garp burst out laughing. "Wahahaha! Sengoku, my disciple's not bad, right?"

 

Sengoku ignored the shameless boast.

 

He looked deeply at Fenric in the arena and sighed before turning to Garp. "He's a rare talent. Garp, I hope you teach him properly."

 

Garp beamed with pride. He had called dibs on Mundo early on, and now it was clear he had made the right choice.

 

"Of course! Any disciple I train will be top-class!"

 

Sengoku rolled his eyes and quipped, "Just don't raise another 'Dragon'."

 10

Dragon…

 

Full name: Monkey D. Dragon—Garp's son, the leader of the Revolutionary Army, and the World Government's most wanted enemy.

 

Hearing the name, Garp instantly exploded with rage. "SENGOKU! YOU WANNA FIGHT?!"

 

Back in the Arena

 

Momonga raised his sword and asked, "Mundo, aren't you going to use a weapon?"

 

Fenric shook his head.

 

Right now, Yumo aka Momonga was far weaker than the future vice admirals—hardly someone worth using a weapon on.

 1

His black blade, Shusui, was reserved for opponents like Issho.

 

"Then watch yourself!"

 

As soon as he finished speaking, Momonga vanished.

 

Soru. One of the Navy's Six Powers.

 

Whoosh!

 

In the next instant, he appeared directly above Fenric, saber raised high, aiming to stab downward.

 

Fast.

 

So fast that most people couldn't even react.

 

But—

 

With Fenric's current speed, he could have easily dodged.

 

But he didn't.

 

He no longer had any interest in playing around. After gauging Yumo's strength, Fenric was ready to end it.

 

Armament Haki instantly coated his entire body!

 

Clang!

 

The blade struck Fenric's body and produced a metallic clang, like a giant temple bell, reverberating through the square.

 

On the Viewing Platform

 

Sengoku, Garp, and the three admirals all changed expression.

 

"A new recruit… with full-body Armament Haki?" Admiral Kizaru spoke slowly, his tone full of disbelief.

 1

As masters of Haki themselves, they knew just how difficult that feat truly was.

 

Among the Crowd

 

Issho looked up, his white eyes focused on Fenric in the arena, a faint smile tugging at his lips.

 3

Back in the Arena

 

Yumo's expression turned grim when he saw that even his full-powered stab couldn't pierce Fenric's skin.

 

He tried to retreat—but it was too late.

 

Fenric had taken the hit head-on just to end things faster.

 

He reached out, grabbed Momonga's blade with one hand—completely ignoring the edge thanks to his Armament Haki—

 

Crack! Crack!

 

—and crushed it like paper.

 

The saber shattered into countless shards and scattered across the floor.

 

Fenric's Telekinesis power surged once more, locking down Yumo as he tried to flee.

 

Then—Boom!

 

Fenric threw a powerful punch, sending Momonga flying across the arena until he crashed against the broadcasting station wall.

 

Right now, Momonga was still young—far from the strength of a future vice admiral.

 

And his saber? Nothing special.

 

If it had been something like the black blade Shusui, Fenric wouldn't have dared block it even with Armament Haki.

 

"C-Contestant #30—Mundo—wins!!"

 

The referee shouted, his voice trembling. His eyes filled with awe as he stared at Fenric.

 

This recruit—was a monster!

 

As the announcement echoed across the square, an uproar erupted among the foreign soldiers in the crowd.

 

When Yumo had drawn his sword, everyone knew he was going all out.

 

But no one expected him to lose this quickly.

 

"Senior Mundo is just too strong...!" Smoker muttered in awe.

chapters.name: Chapter 103: Chapter 103: Mundo vs. Fujitora! (1)
chapters.content:
"Is this newcomer… a monster?!"

 

On the high platform, the vice admirals were visibly shaken.

 

One of them couldn't help but speak up, his voice laced with disbelief. Even through the broadcast, he could tell—if he were to face Mundo himself, he probably wouldn't stand a chance.

 

Many other vice admirals around him silently nodded in agreement.

 

And it wasn't just them.

 

Even the Three Admirals—Akainu, Aokiji, and Kizaru—were now staring intently at Fenric, visibly astonished.

 

In terms of Armament Haki cultivation, Fenric was already close to them!

 7

The assessment continued.

 

But now that everyone had witnessed the showdown between Mundo and Yumo, their standards had drastically changed. The rest of the battles now seemed dull in comparison.

 

The real reason no one left yet?

 

It was simple.

 

Everyone wanted to see Senior Mundo go head-to-head with that blind uncle!

 

That blind uncle—shrouded in mystery—had been finishing fights in a single move. His strength was obvious.

 

Now, it all came down to this: which of these two powerhouses would take first place?

 

As time passed, more and more contestants were eliminated.

 

A few hours later, fewer than ten participants remained.

 

"The next match: Contestant No. 30, Mundo, versus Contestant No. 11, Sentomaru! Will both contestants please come forward!" the referee called.

 

"I surrender!"

 1

Without a moment's hesitation, Sentomaru gave up.

 

He jumped off the platform casually and strolled away, utterly unconcerned.

 

The crowd: "...???"

 

"WHAT?!"

 

No one had expected that little fat man to forfeit without even putting up a fight.

 

Originally, Sentomaru was considered one of the top contenders. After Momonga was eliminated, many thought he'd have a shot at making the top three.

 

Now?

 

He just… quit.

 

That left the third-place candidate slot wide open again.

 

But as for who would take first or second?

 

Everyone agreed—it could only be between Senior Mundo and the blind uncle.

 

With Sentomaru out, only six people remained:

 

Senior Mundo, the blind uncle, and four others.

 

To Fenric's surprise, two of the remaining four were clearly Samsara players—one man, one woman.

 

The man went by the nickname "Beast", and the woman by "Sunflower."

 

It was obvious they weren't using techniques native to the One Piece world. That alone marked them as Samsara players.

 

For them to make it this far was already impressive.

 

Fenric recognized their nicknames, which meant their reputation in the Samsara Space must be significant.

 2

In truth, both Beast and Sunflower never imagined they'd get this far.

 

They chalked it up to luck—and above all, to the guidance of their revered boss: Shura.

 

That's right.

 

They had already guessed that Mundo was Shura's alternate identity.

 

Before entering the third-layer world, they had done plenty of research and learned that the two strongest NPCs in this Navy assessment were the blind swordsman and Yumo.

 

Mundo's name never came up.

 

So when he suddenly appeared and demonstrated overwhelming strength, there was only one explanation: he was a Samsara player—and not just any Samsara.

 

Only someone like Shura could pull this off.

 

Of course, due to system rules, Samsara players weren't allowed to reveal too much about the Samsara Space. So even though they knew who Mundo really was, they didn't dare say it aloud.

 

Still, when they looked at Fenric, their eyes were filled with awe and admiration.

 

Shura was just too powerful!

 

After all, since the Samsara Space began, the best anyone had done in the Third Stage was third place, achieved by someone named Adam.

 1

And now?

 

Their boss was going for first!

 1

"The next match: Contestant No. 13, Beast, versus Contestant No. 22, Issho! Please take the stage!"

 

The referee's words wiped the smile right off Beast's face.

 

Still, he forced a bitter smile and stepped into the ring.

 

He knew the blind man was incredibly strong—but as a Samsara player, this assessment was important. His final rewards would depend on his performance.

 

Beast didn't expect to win.

 

He just wanted to last longer than one move, to break the "instant defeat" streak the blind uncle had going.

 

But he was still too optimistic.

 

He didn't even see the strike.

 

One moment he stepped onto the platform, and the next—he was airborne, flung out of the ring.

 

…Same as everyone else.

 

"The next match: Contestant No. 66, Sunflower, versus Contestant No. 4, Samo!"

 

Surprisingly, Sunflower and this marine named Samo ended up in a back-and-forth brawl. They were evenly matched.

 

But…

 

To the audience, it was a snoozefest.

 

Two rookies pecking at each other.

 

The crowd just wanted to skip the warm-up acts and get to the main event!

 

Eventually, after more than ten minutes of grinding it out, Sunflower launched Samo out of the ring with a high kick.

 

According to the rules, falling off the platform meant instant loss.

 

Sunflower took the win.

 

Next, it was Fenric's turn to draw lots.

 

Unfortunately, he drew No. 66.

 

Sunflower.

 

"The next match: Contestant No. 30, Mundo, versus Contestant No. 66, Sunflower!"

 

Sunflower, still catching her breath from the last match, froze. Her face instantly fell.

 

She had just expended most of her energy… and now she had to face the Shura boss himself?

 

Yeah, no thanks.

 

She wasn't going to embarrass herself.

 

"I surrender!" she said immediately.

 

Now, only three contestants remained:

 

Senior Mundo, the blind uncle, and one extremely lucky recruit.

 

The final lottery draw belonged to that last marine.

 

"Hey rookie, your turn to draw!" the referee called out.

 

The marine stepped up nervously, glancing at Mundo and the blind swordsman before weakly asking:

 

"Uh… can I skip this part?"

 

Pffft!

 

The crowd burst into laughter.

 

"Haha! This guy's hilarious!"

 

"His luck's finally run out!"

 

"There's no way he can take on either of those monsters!"

 

"Still, for a rookie, he's done amazing just to make it this far."

 

"That's true. But next… it's the showdown we've all been waiting for!"

 

Mundo vs. the blind swordsman!

 

The arena buzzed with excitement as the tension built.

 

As for the rookie?

 

He stepped onto the stage, eyes closed, and randomly pulled a number ball.

 

No. 30.

 

He looked at the number, sighed, and didn't wait for the referee.

 

"I abstain!!"

chapters.name: Chapter 104: Chapter 104: Mundo vs. Fujitora! (2)
chapters.content:
"In the next match, Contestant No. 30—'Mundo'—will face Contestant No. 22—'Issho'!"

 

As the referee made the announcement, his expression turned unusually solemn.

 

The gathered recruits reacted the same way, all turning their attention to the ring with grave expressions. Even the high-ranking officials seated on the elevated platform became serious, gazing down at the stage in silence.

 

"Senior Mundo! Go for it!!"

 

Smoker, standing beside Fenric, cheered excitedly.

 

Fenric offered a faint smile and stepped onto the ring.

 

He wasn't concerned about winning or losing.

 

What truly mattered to him... was measuring the gap between himself and an admiral.

 

Clack. Clack. Clack.

 

The sound of a cane striking the ground echoed.

 

A blind man slowly approached the ring.

 

Though he looked like he might trip at any moment, not a single soul in the audience dared underestimate him.

 

"The match begins!"

 

With that formal announcement, the referee swiftly stepped out of the ring, leaving the arena to the two powerhouses.

 

Mundo vs. Issho!

 

Below the ring, over 200,000 spectators watched in breathless silence. Many even held their breath, staring fixedly at the two figures on stage.

 1

The entire square had gone deathly quiet.

 

Even the officials on the high platform remained silent.

 

On stage, the two contenders—under the watchful eyes of thousands—remained calm and composed.

 

Fenric wasn't concerned about his rank.

 

Issho was even more indifferent.

 

In fact, Issho had begun to wonder why he'd even joined the Navy recruits in the first place.

 

"Mr. Issho," Fenric suddenly said, "I already know you're stronger than I am."

 

"Oh?" Issho tilted his head slightly, surprised. "Then… are you surrendering now?"

 

"Of course not."

 

Fenric shook his head and continued, "Even though I know I'll lose, I still want to fight you. Because until now, I've never met anyone who could force me to go all out. I want to find out my upper limit. So please… don't hold back."

 

"I see."

 

Issho smiled faintly.

 

"Mundo-san… you're worthy of my full strength."

 

Fenric gave a nod and fell silent.

 

He closed his eyes and took a deep breath.

 

When he opened them again, a sharp battle spirit blazed in his gaze.

 

He wasn't just saying empty words—he genuinely wanted to test the limits of his current power.

 

The Black Blade—Shusui was already in his hand.

 

At the same time, five floating blades appeared around him, spinning slowly in the air.

 

Armament Haki quietly spread across his body like a second skin.

 

This was Fenric, going all out!

 

"Mr. Issho—I'm attacking!"

 

"Good."

 

With a serious expression, Issho drew the blade hidden inside his cane.

 

Everyone knew the blind man's cane was a sword—but until now, no one had ever seen him actually use it.

 

And just as shocking, it was the first time Fenric revealed his own weapon. No one even knew where he'd been hiding it!

 1

As the two fighters adopted their stances, the entire arena held its breath.

 

Swish!

 

Fenric struck first.

 

With a wave of his hand, the five flying blades shot forward from multiple angles, converging on Issho.

 

Though he couldn't see, Issho's Observation Haki was unmatched.

 

His ears twitched slightly, and then his sword moved with a flurry of shadows—

 

Clang!

 

Each blade was intercepted cleanly.

 

He was fast. Very fast.

 

So fast, in fact, that many of the spectators couldn't even see the motions of his sword.

 

But Fenric hadn't expected those blades to succeed. They were only meant to create an opening for him to close the distance.

 

Whoosh!

 

With a rush of wind, Fenric charged forward, slashing toward Issho's waist with Shusui.

 

Clang!

 

Issho reacted instantly, intercepting the slash with his own blade.

 2

Crack!

 

A stone tile beneath Issho's feet shattered under the pressure.

 

"Nice sword," Issho complimented with a calm smile.

 2

Fenric's pupils contracted. His expression turned grim.

 

With the strength he possessed now, a full-powered strike from Shusui could cut a tank in half.

 

Yet Issho blocked it without so much as budging.

 

Their blades remained locked for a moment—until...

 

The five flying blades that had been knocked aside rose once again and shot toward Issho from behind.

 

This was Fenric's Telekinesis at work.

 

He pressured Issho from the front while his telekinesis power launched a sneak attack from the rear.

 

"Impressive ability," Issho praised again.

 

Then, he opened his eyes.

 

Only the whites of his eyes were visible.

 

HUMMMM—!

 

Suddenly, the atmosphere around Fenric seemed to triple in weight.

 

The air pressed down on him like a collapsing mountain.

 

The five flying blades were crushed to the ground before they could reach Issho.

 

Fenric immediately understood.

 

Gravity Fruit!

 1

Issho's Devil Fruit ability was in play.

 

This technique—Gravity Suppression—dramatically increased the gravity in a localized area, pressing down on his opponent and the environment with crushing force.

 

Even the ring made of solid stone couldn't endure.

 

BOOM!!

 

The entire arena collapsed under the pressure.

 

Gasps rippled through the audience.

 

This was no ordinary clash.

 

This was devastation.

 

No other match in the tournament so far had caused something like this.

 

"What just happened?! Why did the ring collapse?!"

 

"It's the Devil Fruit! The blind man—he's a Devil Fruit user!"

 

"Unbelievable! That power is insane!"

 

"Whether it's Senior Mundo or that blind uncle… they're both monsters!"

 

On the high platform, even the three admirals—Akainu, Aokiji, and Kizaru—wore grim expressions as they watched Issho's ability unfold.

 

"Garp," Sengoku said solemnly, "Do you still think your 'disciple' can win?"

 

Garp's weathered face twitched.

 

"Where the hell did this guy come from?" he muttered. "He's terrifying..."

 

Back in the ruins of the ring...

 

Fenric's legs were buried in the ground up to his knees.

 

Crushed by the overwhelming gravity.

 

"Gravity Suppression" wasn't just heavy—it made the very air feel like a thousand-ton hammer smashing down.

 

In the original story, even monstrous fighters like Luffy, Zoro, and Trafalgar Law had been utterly suppressed by this move.

 

This is the power of a true Admiral!

 

Fenric's raw strength allowed him to stand.

 

But moving… was another matter entirely.

 

"It seems… you can't move anymore."

 

Issho's calm voice came from nearby.

 

"Do you wish to surrender?"

 

Fenric gritted his teeth.

 

"No."

 

He raised his head.

 

"I still have one more technique, Mr. Issho. Please—be careful."

chapters.name: Chapter 105: Chapter 105: One Move Determines the Outcome! (3)
chapters.content:
From the very beginning, Fenric knew he couldn't defeat the old blind man.

 

The reason he hadn't chosen the Navy camp was simple—his current strength was still far from that of an Admiral.

 

In other words, if he had chosen the Navy camp, he wouldn't have been able to earn the highest evaluation.

 

That's why Fenric resolutely chose the Pirate camp.

 

"Mr. Issho, I have one final move. Please be cautious."

 

Though unable to move, Fenric's voice remained calm and resolute.

 

"If I cannot win after this strike, I will admit defeat."

 

"Oh?"

 

Hearing this, Issho suddenly lifted the gravitational pressure.

 

"Your next attack must be formidable. To show my respect, I will respond with something appropriate."

 

With that, Issho waved his sword and slashed at the air.

 

Boom!

 

A powerful surge of violet gravitational energy erupted from him and shot into the sky.

 

Fenric's expression changed instantly.

 

He recognized it immediately—it was one of Issho's ultimate moves: Meteor Summoning!

 

"A parting gift. I hope we can spar again next time," Issho said calmly, sheathing his blade.

 

Below the ring, the crowd of onlookers hadn't yet grasped what was happening and began to murmur:

 

"Hey, what's going on? Are they done fighting?"

 

"I'm not sure…"

 

"Judging by Senior Mundo's posture, the battle doesn't seem over!"

 

"That blind uncle is ridiculously strong. It's the first time I've seen Senior Mundo at a disadvantage."

 

"Wait, look at the sky! What's that!?"

 

"A meteorite? Seriously!?"

 

"Dear god… why is there a meteorite falling from the sky!?"

 

"It has to be the blind uncle's Devil Fruit power… terrifying!"

 

"Hey, are you joking?! That thing will kill us all!"

 

"Run! Run!!"

 

A massive meteorite, dragged down by the gravitational surge, began plummeting toward the square. As it tore through the atmosphere, it ignited, trailing flames behind it. From below, it looked like a flaming planet descending from the heavens, blotting out the sun.

 

The moment it appeared, the recruits watching from the square panicked and screamed.

 

Many were too shocked to react at first.

 

What the hell?!

 

It's just an internal evaluation! Why the hell are we dealing with a meteorite?! That's insane!

 

Once reality hit, the crowd turned and bolted in all directions, scrambling to save themselves.

 

Panic gripped the square.

 

"This is a bit excessive, isn't it?" Admiral Aokiji muttered from the high platform.

 

Not far from him, Kizaru added in his usual lazy tone, "Scary... really scary."

 

Sengoku and Garp had already stood up from their chairs.

 

Sengoku was worried that an accident might harm the recruits.

 

Garp, on the other hand, was simply concerned for his "disciple."

 

"These guys are going too far!" Sengoku growled, glancing at the blind man. "Garp, go handle this!"

 

Garp nodded and stepped forward, preparing to crush the meteorite with his Iron Fist.

 

"Garp-san, wait a moment," Aokiji suddenly interjected, pointing toward the arena. "Don't underestimate your 'disciple.' He's still standing."

 

Everyone looked toward Mundo and saw him standing calmly in the ring, completely unshaken.

 

His entire body was clad in Armament Haki, including the black blade Shusui in his hand, which gleamed with a glossy sheen.

 

This was the mark of someone who had mastered Armament Haki—capable of covering not only their body, but their weapons as well.

 

Garp was stunned.

 

Then, slowly, he unclenched his fist, though he still looked at Mundo with worry.

 

To someone like him, Issho's meteorite was nothing—a single punch could destroy it.

 

But for Mundo, it was too dangerous.

 

He was still too young.

 

The old man believed that with Mundo's talent, if trained properly for ten years, he could surpass even him. At that point, defeating Issho would be inevitable.

 

But now… Garp couldn't see how Mundo could survive this.

 

Mundo's physical strength and mysterious devil fruit ability were still far from enough to stop a meteorite.

 

"Borsalino," Garp said through clenched teeth, "stop watching and get ready. If my disciple's in danger, you save him!"

 

Among everyone present, Kizaru was the fastest.

 

And as a Vice Admiral, Garp had the authority to order even a top-tier Admiral like Kizaru.

 

"No problem, Garp-san," Kizaru replied lazily. "I wouldn't want to see such a promising kid go to waste."

 

Only then did Garp feel reassured.

 

With Kizaru ready to step in, his "disciple" should be safe.

 

Back in the ring…

 

Fenric had no idea that an old man had already prepared a safety net for him.

 

Right now, his entire focus was on the falling meteorite summoned by Issho.

 

Huff… huff… huff…

 

Finally, the meteorite drew near, casting a massive shadow over the square.

 

Fenric could feel the searing heat radiating from it.

 

The recruits below were losing their minds, wishing they had a few extra legs just to escape faster.

 

Who would've thought watching a match could cost you your life?

 

When the meteorite was less than 100 meters from the arena, Fenric suddenly bent his legs and slowly crouched.

 

Then—

 

He kicked off with explosive force.

 

"Crack!!"

 

The ruined ring cracked further as Fenric's launch left a massive crater behind.

 

He rocketed upward like a bullet, directly toward the meteorite.

 

A brutal impact was coming.

 

That's right—Fenric's final move was Savage Charge. 

 

Savage Charge (Active): Launch a ferocious forward rush. For 5 seconds you are immune to all damage; your attack power ×3 during the charge.

 

He'd long wanted to test the true power of this move.

 

In the next instant, a five-second invincibility state enveloped him.

 

His entire body slammed into the meteorite—

 

—and his black blade Shusui cleaved through the air!

 

Buzz!

 

A brilliant sword light tore through the sky.

 

Fenric had never trained in advanced swordsmanship. The blade light that appeared now was purely a result of his speed and power.

 

Savage Charge had tripled his strength.

 

It was a sword light born of raw force—not technique.

 

Boom!!!

 

Fenric collided head-on with the meteorite.

 

The massive rock halted mid-air for a moment.

 

Then—

 

Crack!

 

Fractures spread across its surface.

 

BOOM!!

 

The meteorite shattered in midair, exploding into countless flaming fragments that scattered like flower petals across the sky.

Not to mention the weak main character.

chapters.name: Chapter 106: Chapter 106: Kizaru Strikes!
chapters.content:
"!!!"

 

The audience was stunned!

 

No one had expected that Mundo could take a meteorite head-on and shatter it with his own body.

 

What kind of physique was this?

 

Too tough!

 

Even Garp and the other high-ranking officers were caught off guard.

 

This Mundo was full of surprises!

 

"Huff… huff…"

 

Above them, shattered fragments of the meteorite filled the sky like falling stars.

 

Although Fenric had smashed the meteorite apart, the resulting debris would still cause massive casualties if it landed on the plaza.

 

"Borsalino!!"

 

Sengokus shouted toward Admiral Kizaru.

 

Kizaru understood instantly. Standing up, he casually muttered:

 

"Man… these rookies are really going overboard."

 

As his words fell, his body erupted in golden light. The next instant, he turned into countless motes of light and vanished from view.

 

In a flash!

 

The motes of light reappeared midair above the plaza, condensing into Kizaru's figure.

 

"Yasakani no Magatama!!"

 

His voice thundered across the square.

 

From his hands—like the barrels of a Gatling gun—countless beams of light burst forth!

 

Each beam shot out like a bullet, raining down upon the falling debris with terrifying precision.

 

Suddenly, the entire sky lit up with golden flashes.

 

One by one, the deadly meteorite fragments disintegrated in midair, reduced to dust.

 

Alone, Kizaru had neutralized the entire threat.

 

And to him, it looked effortless.

 

Down below, Fenric, who had just landed, watched solemnly.

 

In his upcoming plan—after assassinating the Celestial Dragon—the greatest obstacle during his escape would be Kizaru!

 1

This guy was fast. Deadly fast. With powerful attacks to match.

 

If Kizaru caught up, Fenric could very well lose his life…

 

"We're saved! We're saved!"

 

"It's Admiral Kizaru! He protected us!"

 

"Thank goodness! I thought we were done for!"

 

"That blind old man nearly got us all killed with his meteorite stunt!"

 

"Senior Mundo is the real MVP. At least he tried to block it beforehand!"

 

"They're both terrifying… not even human anymore…"

 

"I wonder who'll take first place?"

 

As the last of the meteorite dust scattered, order slowly returned to the plaza.

 

The survivors—still shaken—began to voice their anger at Issho.

 

Seriously? Couldn't he at least consider the lives of ordinary people before dropping space rocks on them?

 

Not like Senior Mundo—he actually cared!

 

In the arena.

 

Issho didn't seem to care what the crowd thought. He had known from the start that the meteorites wouldn't harm anyone.

 

Even if no one intercepted them, he could have made the meteorite float away again.

 

Seeing Mundo return, Issho smiled.

 

"That final move of yours was really something," he said warmly. "At your age, I've rarely seen someone as talented."

 

Fenric shook his head, ignoring the compliment.

 

"I lost," he replied flatly.

 

He was still far from the level of a Navy Admiral.

 

Maybe… a Samsara player who had reached A-rank overall might be able to stand toe-to-toe with them.

 

The nearby referee, who had been paralyzed with fear, finally snapped out of it upon hearing Fenric's words.

 

"Contestant No. 30, Mundo, has forfeited! Victory goes to Contestant No. 22, Issho!"

 

The crowd was shocked.

 

"Why would Senior Mundo give up? He was amazing!"

 

"Come on, it's not that surprising. That blind uncle is basically a monster."

 

"Yeah, imagine if he dropped more meteorites. He could destroy Marine Headquarters!"

 

"Honestly, it's probably safer if they don't fight at all. Too dangerous."

 

After conceding, Fenric leapt off the ring.

 

The surrounding recruits instinctively parted to make way.

 

"Step aside! Step aside! The boss is coming through!"

 

Fenric ignored them and found a place to sit and rest.

 

Smoker approached from the side, eyes filled with admiration.

 

"Senior Mundo, you were incredible!" he said, then added with concern, "Don't worry too much about not placing first. With your strength, I'm sure you'll become an Admiral one day!"

 

Fenric smiled at the words but didn't bother explaining that he had no interest in winning.

 

He simply patted Smoker on the shoulder.

 

"Thanks, kid. We'll probably be going separate ways soon. I just hope the next time we meet, we can still speak like this."

 

Smoker froze. "Wait… are you leaving?"

 

"Yeah," Fenric nodded. "I'm leaving tomorrow morning."

 

At first, Smoker looked confused. Then realization dawned on him.

 

"I get it now! You're going to train under Vice Admiral Garp, aren't you? That's amazing… I'm so jealous."

 

Fenric didn't respond. He just smiled silently.

 

With Fenric's forfeit, the assessment had officially concluded.

 

The next moment, Sengoku announced that the top ten recruits would attend an appointment ceremony.

 

It would begin the next morning.

 

This "appointment" was, of course, a formal granting of military ranks.

 

Even more astonishing was the Fleet Admiral's declaration:

 

The top three would receive their commissions personally from a Celestial Dragon.

 1

The moment he said that, envy exploded from the crowd.

 

Eyes turned green with jealousy as they looked toward the top ten.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed slightly at this.

 

If he remembered correctly, he would return to the Samsara Space tomorrow afternoon.

 

Which meant…

 

If he killed the Celestial Dragon in the morning and survived for just half a day—

 

He could vanish without a trace.

 

Perfect timing.

 

The next morning, 9:00 a.m.

 

The appointment ceremony began.

 

Countless recruits arrived to witness the grand event.

 

Fenric and the other nine finalists stood on the high platform, waiting for their names to be called.

 

Unsurprisingly, Issho was first.

 

He was appointed a Rear Admiral on the spot.

 

His new title: "Fujitora."

 

In truth, based on his strength, he could've easily been made a full Admiral.

 

But with the Navy still maintaining its internal balance, that promotion would have to wait.

 

Next was Fenric.

 

He was promoted to Colonel, a prestigious senior officer rank in the Navy.

 

Then, the rest of the top ten received their own appointments.

 

Just as the ceremony seemed to wind down…

 

A strange, bloated figure waddled onto the stage.

 

He had a large bubble on his head and an arrogant, grotesque expression on his face.

 

A Celestial Dragon had arrived.

 

(Side Note: One Leaf Autumn killing Zoro doesn't mean that's all he can do. Don't underestimate A-rank Samsara players—someone like Aurora is no weaker than an Admiral! She just messed up her Devil Fruit usage due to her flawed innate foundation. We'll cover this in a future update. The Samsara System doesn't allow god-tier creations, okay?) 

 2

chapters.name: Chapter 107: Chapter 107: Abnormal Change!
chapters.content:
The Celestial Dragons.

 7

Nobles of the world, they reside in the Holy Land of Mary Geoise. They are the direct descendants of the twenty kings who founded the World Government eight hundred years ago.

 

The Celestial Dragons, or Tenryūbito, often refer to themselves as "Descendants of the Creator." They consider themselves superior to ordinary people, so much so that they wear bubble hoods to avoid breathing the same air. To them, other races are mere slaves—tools to be used, owned, and discarded. They enjoy absolute privilege.

 

If one is offended, even slightly, the Navy Headquarters or CP0 must devote all their strength to exact punishment.

 

"Yes, a World Noble, a Celestial Dragon—"

 

"Stop! Don't say that cursed name out loud!"

 

"Kneel—quickly! If you don't, you'll die!"

 

The moment the Celestial Dragon appeared that day, chaos erupted in the plaza.

 

Countless naval soldiers fell to their knees automatically.

 

Even among the top ten recruits in the assessment, half dropped to the ground in submission.

 

The top brass—Fleet Admiral Sengoku, Garp, and the three Navy Admirals—stood motionless.

 

But if one looked closely, it was clear none of them harbored any fondness for the Celestial Dragons. Even Garp wore an expression of open disapproval.

 

After all, the Celestial Dragons treated the Navy like guard dogs. How could these proud warriors feel anything but contempt?

 

Fenric's eyes flickered as he glanced at the approaching Celestial Dragon. His expression soon turned cold, his face emotionless, gaze fixed forward.

 

Many high-ranking officers present had powerful Haki—particularly Observation Haki.

 

If he revealed even a trace of hostility, he risked being detected.

 

And while the Navy might dislike the Celestial Dragons, they absolutely wouldn't allow one to be killed under their watch.

 

If anything happened to a Celestial Dragon within Navy Headquarters, the consequences would be catastrophic.

 

The Celestial Dragon arrived in full showy fashion.

 

Not only did he have several strong-looking bodyguards, but he was followed by a group of young men and women—all of them slaves, collars around their necks like dogs.

 4

Some of them were even children.

 

To the Celestial Dragons, anyone outside their bloodline was no different from livestock.

 

This particular Celestial Dragon looked like he'd just woken up.

 

Yawning as he stepped onto the stage, he lazily commanded, "Hurry it up~!"

 

There was no sign of respect for Navy Headquarters.

 

Sengoku's expression darkened, but he still stepped forward helplessly and announced, "The top three will now present themselves before Lord Saint Jalmack to receive their medals."

 

The so-called "coronation" meant the Celestial Dragon would personally present rank medals to the top three recruits.

 

Issho—Fujitora—stepped forward first.

 

He leaned on his cane and walked slowly up to the Celestial Dragon, bowing slightly.

 

It wasn't an act of submission, but a deliberate move. Fujitora was tall, and by barely bowing, he made the pudgy Celestial Dragon struggle to reach his shoulders.

 

Saint Jalmack pinned the medal on him with clear reluctance, his eyes flashing with annoyance when he realized Fujitora hadn't knelt.

 

Still, this was Navy HQ. He had to maintain some dignity.

 

"Next!"

 

Fujitora stepped back, and Fenric slowly stepped forward.

 

As they passed each other, Fujitora seemed to pause.

 

Fenric's heart skipped a beat.

 

Issho's Observation Haki was terrifyingly sharp. It must've been Fenric's sudden spike in heart rate that tipped him off.

 

Fortunately, Issho didn't interfere. He only paused briefly before continuing back to his place.

 

Fenric forced himself to calm down, controlling his breathing as he approached the Celestial Dragon.

 3

He kept his head lowered, as though terrified of the man before him.

 

Satisfied with the display, the Celestial Dragon nodded and took out a medal, moving to pin it on Fenric's uniform.

 

And then—

 

A sudden change!

 

Just as he appeared to obediently accept the medal, Fenric bared his fangs like a tiger ready to pounce!

 

With lightning speed, he grabbed the Celestial Dragon's arm and yanked him close. The frail noble was dragged into Fenric's grasp, and in an instant, the black blade Shusui was pressed against his neck, its tip already piercing the skin.

 8

It all happened so fast—

 

No one had time to react!

 

Fenric's current agility stat was already ten times that of a normal person. In terms of reaction speed, only Admiral Kizaru could match him.

 

Even then, with the attack so sudden, not even Sengoku or the other Admirals could stop it in time.

 

"Mundo!!!"

 

Garp was stunned, staring at Fenric in disbelief.

 

Sengoku roared, "Colonel Mundo, what the hell are you doing?!"

 

The three Admirals, Vice Admirals, and every officer on the platform froze in shock.

 

"Alala~ Something terrible has happened." Aokiji muttered, expression grim as he locked eyes with Fenric.

 

Akainu's gaze turned to steel, filled with fury.

 

Kizaru's eyes widened behind his sunglasses, stunned into silence.

 

Even Fujitora stopped in his tracks.

 

It wasn't until this moment that the Celestial Dragon realized what had happened.

 

"AAAAHHHHH! What are you doing, you filthy peasant?! Don't touch me with your disgusting hands!"

 

"Shut up!"

 

Fenric pressed his blade harder, drawing a thin line of blood. The Celestial Dragon trembled in fear, instantly silenced.

 

"Admiral Kizaru," Fenric said coldly, "I'd advise you to stop. The light you're gathering behind me is way too obvious."

 

Indeed—

 

A shimmer of light and shadow had quietly formed behind Fenric, Kizaru preparing a sneak attack.

 1

But now, he froze in place.

 

At that moment—

 

All the recruits in the plaza below had realized what was happening.

 

"Wha—?! No way!"

 

"Did... did Senior Mundo just take a Celestial Dragon hostage?!"

 

"It's over. It's all over. Why would he do something like this?!"

 

Chaos broke out among the onlookers, their expressions filled with horror.

 

"Senior Mundo..." Smoker muttered in disbelief, the twin cigars in his mouth almost falling out.

 

Even the Samsara players among them were stunned.

 

They couldn't understand it. Why would their Shura-like boss do something like this?

 

Was this a death wish?

 

He was a naval officer, and yet he took a Celestial Dragon hostage in front of everyone?

 

The Fleet Admiral Sengoku. Navy Hero Garp. And the three Admirals, they are all here!

 

Even a god wouldn't be able to save him now!

chapters.name: Chapter 108: Chapter 108: Slaying the Celestial Dragon Dog!
chapters.content:
A drastic turn of events!

 

The entire square was engulfed in a strange, suffocating atmosphere.

 

No one could comprehend why the promising rising star, Mundo, would do something so outrageous.

 

Was he insane?

 

Even Vice Admiral Garp couldn't make sense of it.

 

"Mundo, are you out of your mind?!" Garp cursed loudly.

 

He had never placed so much hope in a young man before. He had even considered taking Mundo in as a disciple. But now, this same young man had played him for a fool.

 

Thankfully, Sengoku had advised him to wait before officially taking Mundo under his wing. Otherwise, the title of "master and disciple" would have been sealed, and now Mundo had pulled this stunt in public.

 

"Garp-san, I'm sorry," Fenric said quietly. "I failed your expectations."

 

"Colonel Mundo, do you even realize what you're doing?!"

 

Sengoku's voice thundered across the square.

 

Of everyone present, Sengoku undoubtedly wore the ugliest expression.

 

As the Fleet Admiral, this sort of catastrophe had unfolded under his command, right at Marine Headquarters. He couldn't possibly avoid responsibility for it.

 

"Colonel?" Fenric sneered. "Fleet Admiral Sengoku, I am no longer a Marine!"

 

He turned to face the crowd, his voice echoing across the plaza:

 

"I! Mundo! Am a pirate! Remember my name, all of you—because from this day forward, I will kill every last one of the Celestial Dragons!"

 1

As soon as he finished speaking—

 

Fenric moved!

 

Sengoku's face darkened in an instant. "Stop—!"

 

He tried to intervene, but it was too late.

 

With a swift motion, Fenric raised his blade and beheaded the Celestial Dragon standing before him.

 

Splurt!!

 

Blood sprayed across his body.

 

The severed head rolled across the ground and stopped at Sengoku's feet, its eyes wide open in disbelief, forever locked in a death stare.

 

"Om—!"

 

Sengoku's fury boiled over.

 

His body began to swell like an inflating balloon, radiating a blinding golden light.

 

Within seconds, he had transformed into a towering Golden Buddha—his Devil Fruit ability in full effect!

 

This was the Mythical Zoan: Human-Human Fruit, Model: Great Buddha.

 

This form was why he was often called "Sengoku the Buddha."

 

Without hesitation, Sengoku struck.

 

A golden fist the size of a building hurtled toward Fenric, no words, only raw fury.

 

Facing the mountainous attack, Fenric simply smiled—and raised a strange bracelet in his hand.

 

It was a special item he had obtained in the "The Mountain Village Old Corpse" dungeon world.

 

This bracelet didn't just dispel ghosts—it had another, much more critical function:

 

Random Teleportation.

 

Once activated, it could instantly teleport the user up to 5,000 meters away in a random direction.

 9

Naturally, such a powerful ability came with restrictions—it could only be used once every 24 hours.

 

Without this bracelet, Fenric would never have dared to carry out such a reckless plan.

 1

Kill a Celestial Dragon and try to escape?

 

Not with the Admirals around.

 

Who did he think he was?

 

Suddenly, a deafening sound ripped through the air—

 

"Whoosh!! Whoosh!!"

 

Sengoku's golden fist, glowing with white light, came crashing down like a locomotive.

 

It wasn't just brute force—it carried a shockwave!

 

Sengoku had poured everything into this punch.

 

But he hit nothing.

 

The next moment—

 

Fenric vanished.

 

Truly vanished.

 

This was no illusion, no high-speed movement.

 

Even Issho and the other Admirals couldn't sense his presence.

 

BOOM!!!

 4

Sengoku's fist slammed into the platform, obliterating a large section of it.

 

Under normal circumstances, the sheer destruction would have shocked the recruits.

 

But today, no one cared about the damage.

 

Because something much, much worse had just happened.

 

A representative of the Celestial Dragons, visiting to bestow honor, had been beheaded by a pirate impersonating a Marine—right in Marineford!?

 

And that same pirate had escaped!

 

If they hadn't witnessed it with their own eyes, no one would've believed such a thing could happen.

 

Mundo hadn't just slapped the face of the Navy.

 

He'd taken a dump on it—then shoved it in their mouths.

 

Everyone stood frozen, too stunned to speak.

 

All eyes turned to the high platform.

 

To Fleet Admiral Sengoku.

 

What would he do?

 

Sengoku stood, breathing heavily.

 

"Huff... Huff... Huff..."

 

He slowly dispelled his Devil Fruit powers, his golden glow fading, and shrunk back to his normal form.

 

"EVERYONE—PURSUE MUNDO IMMEDIATELY!"

 

His voice was thunderous.

 

"And issue a bounty—2 billion Berries! Report this to the World Government and circulate it across every sea. Mundo must not be allowed to escape!!"

 

A collective gasp echoed among the soldiers.

 

Two billion Berries?!

 

It was unprecedented. Since the founding of the World Government, no one had ever received such a massive bounty so quickly.

 

This was the kind of figure reserved for the Four Emperors of the New World.

 

Even the Admirals and Garp stared at Sengoku in surprise.

 

"Sengokus, calm down!" Garp said sternly. "A 2 billion bounty—for a rookie?"

 

Sengoku shook his head. "Two billion is already too little."

 

"Mundo didn't just kill anyone. He murdered a Celestial Dragon. And what he declared was a direct challenge to the entire Celestial Dragon bloodline."

 2

"For someone that dangerous, a 2 billion bounty is justified—and the Celestial Dragons will approve."

 

"But more importantly—what he said at the end."

 

At those words, realization dawned across the officers' faces.

 

The bounty wasn't merely punishment—it was a statement to the Celestial Dragons.

 

Anything less than a billion would be an insult.

 

Mundo had struck a fatal blow to their pride. If his bounty had been too low, the World Government would be seen as weak.

 

Now, no one objected to Sengoku's bounty announcement.

 

In fact, many silently admired his political instincts.

 

This... this is why Sengoku was Fleet Admiral.

 

"Garp," Sengoku said quietly, "are you interested in taking my position?"

 

"What? At a time like this, you're joking?" Garp frowned.

 

Sengoku sighed. "Someone has to take the fall for this incident. As Fleet Admiral, I bear responsibility. After I step down... I haven't decided on a successor."

 

Garp fell silent, his expression grim.

 

A Celestial Dragon had been murdered—at Marine Headquarters.

 4

This wasn't just an incident.

 

It was a world-shaking catastrophe.

 

Only a change in leadership could begin to pacify the Celestial Dragons' wrath.

chapters.name: Chapter 109: Chapter 109: The Mission Ends!
chapters.content:
Clang! Clang!

 

With the order issued by the Fleet Admiral, the alarm bells of Marineford rang urgently.

 

All naval forces were mobilized. Soldiers assembled in full gear, weapons in hand, and were organized into search teams. Each team carried a Den Den Mushi and was immediately dispatched to hunt down Mundo!

 

Eve Admirals Aokiji and Akainu split up and led their forces to sea in pursuit of Mundo.

 

Only Admiral Kizaru remained at headquarters.

 

Because of his speed and mobility, Kizaru was tasked with immediate support should anyone locate Mundo's whereabouts.

 

"Remember! The enemy is a powerful Devil Fruit user. If you find him, do not engage—report to a superior officer immediately. Do you hear me?" a lieutenant colonel barked at the assembled soldiers.

 

"Sir, yes, sir!!" the soldiers shouted in unison.

 

"Move out!"

 

The massive search force launched in full force.

 

The same tense situation unfolded across Marineford.

 

For a time, the atmosphere at headquarters was suffocating with pressure.

 

Up on the high platform overlooking the square, Sengoku and Garp stood still, their expressions dark and grim.

 

In addition to the two old veterans, several guards and attendants belonging to the Celestial Dragons were also present on the platform.

 

But now that their master was dead, they stood frozen in confusion, not knowing what to do.

 

Among the crowd of enslaved people stood a young girl with her head bowed.

 

A faint smile curved on her lips.

 

Her name—Boa Hancock.

 15

In her mind, one name echoed over and over again: Mundo.

 

"Thank you, Mundo…" she whispered softly.

 

No one heard her voice.

 

Meanwhile, the Samsara players known as "Beast" and "Sunflower" were aboard a warship, sailing west in search of Mundo.

 

They both now understood the truth—Mundo was none other than the reincarnated Shura.

 

And now, everything made sense.

 

He had chosen the Pirate faction from the beginning, infiltrated the navy as an undercover agent just to get close to the Celestial Dragons.

 

While other Samsara were still focused on completing the mission and climbing the rankings, the Shura boss had treated the assessment like a game.

 

His real goal was to assassinate the world's so-called nobles—the Celestial Dragons!

 

The scale of his plan, his audacity, his strength—it all left Beast and Sunflower in awe.

 

They admired him from the bottom of their hearts.

 

Because such a plan was unimaginably dangerous.

 

To assassinate a Celestial Dragon at the heavily fortified Marineford… the mere thought sent shivers down one's spine.

 

And yet, the boss known as Shura not only pulled it off—he escaped without a trace.

 

If that's not a true boss, then what is?

 

On another warship, Smoker stood in silence.

 

His expression was somber, his spirit dulled.

 

Ever since meeting Mundo, he had looked up to him—respected him as a leader, even idolized him.

 

But now, that man had turned into a pirate.

 

Smoker felt as if his faith had shattered. He was at a loss.

 

What made things worse was the way the other soldiers were looking at him—suspicious, wary.

 

And he understood why.

 

Since their deployment, he had been the one closest to Mundo.

 

Of course, suspicion would fall on him.

 

This operation by Fenric—this entire stunt—had changed the fates of many.

 

Because of Mundo, Sengoku might be forced to resign early.

 

Because of Mundo, the selection for the next Fleet Admiral had become both simplified and complicated.

 

Because of Mundo, Marineford would now face severe repercussions.

 

Because of Mundo, the future Empress of Amazon Lily had broken free from captivity.

 4

Because of Mundo, Smoker had lost his guiding light.

 

Because of Mundo...

 

And as for the culprit behind all of this?

 

He was currently swimming in the open sea.

 

Yes—Fenric had been randomly teleported by the system bracelet to the waters south of Marineford, near a small coastal town.

 

But he didn't dare swim toward it.

 1

He was certain the town would already be crawling with Marines.

 

He had already used the bracelet's random teleportation function, and it wouldn't be available again for 24 hours.

 

And Fenric had no desire to die.

 

Regular Marines didn't scare him—but if he drew the attention of a Marine Admiral...

 

That would be a different story.

 

To play it safe, Fenric swam further out to sea.

 

With his enhanced physique and mental reinforcement abilities, he was swimming faster than a fish.

 

He kept swimming—for over an hour!

 

Eventually, he made landfall on a deserted shore.

 

Without wasting time, he disappeared into the mountains, preparing to ride out the remainder of the mission time in hiding.

 

The next few hours passed without incident.

 

Everything went smoothly.

 

Then, in the afternoon, a system notification echoed in every Samsara players's mind:

 

Ding!

 

"Mission time is over. Those who failed to complete the objective—will be executed!"

 

Onboard a Marine warship, one Samsara player's face paled in horror. Moments later, his body was wracked with pain as he let out a scream.

 

Before the stunned eyes of nearby Marines, his body began to disintegrate, slowly turning to dust and vanishing entirely.

 

"Ding! The seven-day countdown has ended. You have successfully completed the mission. Preparing to teleport to the Samsara Space…"

 

In a distant forest—

 

Fenric, hiding deep in the underbrush, let out a long sigh of relief when he heard the system message.

 

The next moment, his figure vanished into thin air.

 

The 28th Floor of the Samsara Tower

 

Inside the grand simulation world of One Piece, the third timeline phase—The Paramount War—had begun.

 

On a battlefield, Admiral Aurora was coughing up blood!

 

Moments ago, she had taken a full-force Thunder Bagua strike to the back from Kaido of the Four Emperors, and her body had been launched across the field.

 4

"Admiral Aurora!!"

 

Naval officers nearby cried out in panic.

 

But Aurora couldn't hear them clearly.

 

Earlier, she had already taken a devastating Air Shock from Whitebeard. Now, with Kaido's follow-up blow, even her remarkable physical resilience had reached its limit.

 

Her body was broken. Her life force was fading.

 

Lying motionless on the ground, she murmured:

 

"Am I going to die…?"

 

A look of peace—of release—spread across her bloodstained face.

 

Maybe this was for the best.

 

She had carried too much for too long.

 

But just then, a system message rang in her ears:

 

Ding!

 

"Dear Samsara player Aurora, please take note! The major simulation world 'One Piece' has undergone drastic changes due to the actions of Samsara player 'Shura.'

 8

This mission is currently under judgment.

 

Judgment passed.

 

Teleportation to the Samsara Space will begin in 30 minutes."

 1

Aurora: "…???"

chapters.content:
(Note: Regarding the setting being affected by the protagonist in the large dungeon world, there will be a reasonable explanation later.)

 1

"Congratulations! Samsara Player 'Shura' has performed exceptionally in the 'One Piece' dungeon world of the Samsara Tower!"

 

"Within 168 hours, he obtained a bounty of two billion Baileys, heavily impacted the dungeon world, overfulfilled the dungeon mission, and has been awarded a perfect evaluation — SSS!"

 6

Super God Evaluation — SSS!!

 

The announcement echoed across Samsara Plaza, the Dungeon Hall, and even within the dungeons themselves.

 

Every corner of the Samsara Space heard the broadcast.

 

SSS rating — Super God!

 

It was back. Once again, the double "S" most people could only dream of.

 1

And the one to claim this impossible feat?

 

"Shura!"

 

Shock? No—

 

Numbness.

 

Most Samsara players didn't even react anymore. Their expressions had long since turned blank.

 

Because they were numb!

 

This was Shura's fourth SSS Super God evaluation!

 

Four perfect ratings in eleven days!

 

[Chat screen messages flooded in rapidly:]

 

"It's him again. The Great God's breaking the system!"

 1

"No surprise. I heard someone saw Shura enter a dungeon recently. Of course, he's gonna flood the feed again!"

 

"Four SSS-rated clears in a row!? Damn, is Shura the secret lovechild of the Samsara System?"

 

"Forget lovechild — he is the Samsara System's real father!"

 

"Is Shura going for the top floor of the Samsara Tower?"

 

"C'mon now, there's no way even Shura can do that—"

 

"Don't be so sure. With four SSS evaluations, his power must be insane by now. And the higher you go, the more foundation matters. The stronger you are, the easier it gets!"

 

"Sh*t… hearing you break it down, it actually makes sense!!"

 

"By the way, where's he getting all those dungeon refresh cards?"

 

"Need you ask? Obviously it's a reward from the SSS rating!"

 

Most of those feeling overwhelmed were in Safe Zones.

 

They had never challenged the Samsara Tower, and had no idea how terrifying those dungeon floors really were.

 

But for the ones inside the tower? Especially those who had cleared the Third Stage "One Piece" dungeon — the shock hit much deeper.

 

"Two billion Baileys? What the hell did Shura do!?"

 

"Wait—did the system glitch? Or did I mishear? Two billion?? That's more than what most top pirates get!"

 

"There's no way! He must've hacked the game or something. No one can earn 2 billion Baileys in a week!"

 

"Did he kill a Marine Admiral or something!?"

 

"No way! The Admirals are crazy strong. Who the hell could kill one on the Third Stage?"

 

Inside a bar in the Samsara Space, a group of Samsara players gathered to discuss the news, all wearing expressions of disbelief.

 

Just then, a Samsara player who had recently cleared the Third Stage dungeon walked in, grinning ear to ear.

 

"I can tell you how Shura got that 2 billion bounty!"

 1

One of the seated Samsara turned and shouted, "Yo, Beast! Judging by that stupid happy face, did you score big in the Third Stage dungeon?"

 

Beast replied with exaggerated humility, "It wasn't much. Thanks to Shura's blessing, I only managed to get an 'A' grade evaluation."

 

"!!"

 

Gasps erupted from the table.

 

"Holy sh*t! An A rating?!"

 

"Beast, quit pretending you're humble. You know damn well that's nuts!"

 

"Tch, liar."

 

Beast chuckled and showed off the evaluation mark on his arm.

 

C!

 

The moment everyone saw the glowing "C", their eyes turned red with envy.

 

Even C-level strength was enough to qualify for a leadership role in the government departments post-dungeon. Beast had a bright future ahead of him.

 

"How the hell did you pull that off, Beast?" someone asked.

 

Beast smirked, "Nothing much. I ranked fifth in the Navy recruitment assessment. Got rewarded with a Zoan-type Devil Fruit. After eating it, my power jumped straight to C-level."

 

Everyone inhaled sharply at the brag — because he wasn't lying.

 

Then Beast added, his tone sincere for once, "Really though, I gotta thank Shura. Without him, I wouldn't have even cracked the top ten. And it's not just me — anyone who picked the Navy camp for that dungeon should be grateful."

 1

"What do you mean?"

 

"Yeah, how did Shura rack up a bounty of 2 billion Baileys?"

 

Beast smiled mysteriously. "You want the SSS strategy for free?"

 

"Come on, bro! Share the goods!"

 

"Brother Beast, please! My next run is in the Third Stage too!"

 

"Don't be a jerk! Just tell us already!"

 

Seeing their desperation, Beast snickered. "Fine. But I want three glasses of Bloody Mary in return!"

 2

A Bloody Mary cost 150 points per glass. Painfully expensive. But still, three players grit their teeth and ordered the drinks.

 

After a satisfying sip, Beast leaned in.

 

"Here's the deal. Shura also took part in the Navy recruitment assessment — but he joined as a pirate. That's right, he went undercover in the Navy."

 

"Wait, what?!"

 

"Let me finish," Beast said smugly. "He aced the recruitment exam and ranked second. But when a big shot showed up to personally award him honors…"

 

"He revealed his true identity — and killed the big shot on the spot!"

 

"Killed?! What big shot?" someone asked quickly.

 

Beast dropped the bomb: "A Celestial Dragon — a World Noble!"

 

"!!!"

 

The whole table went dead silent.

 

Gasps filled the bar.

 

"No f**king way! In Navy HQ? A Celestial Dragon?! How did Shura even get close!?"

 

"And how did he escape afterward? The Admirals would've obliterated him!"

 

"Yeah, don't tell me Shura's stronger than an Admiral!"

 

Beast laughed. "Of course not. After the Celestial Dragon was killed, the Fleet Admiral himself — Sengoku — tried to take Shura down. But Shura had prepared in advance. He either had a teleportation skill or a special item. He vanished instantly!"

 

"He what?! Teleported out from under Fleet Admiral Sengoku's nose?!"

 

"Holy sh*t, I never would've thought of that!"

 

"Yeah, but do you have teleportation gear? Can you rank top three in the assessment?"

 

"Damn it, Beast, your so-called 'strategy' is useless to us! You just scammed us out of our drinks!"

 

Similar conversations were erupting all over the Samsara Space.

 

With over a hundred Samsara players joining the Third Stage dungeon this time, most had chosen the safer Navy camp — and now they all bore witness to Shura's terrifying presence.

 

Everyone saw how Fenric, the Samsara known as Shura, dominated the entire battlefield with terrifying precision.

 

And now, with his fourth SSS rating, his legend only grew more untouchable.

 

______

 

P.S. Advanced chapters are now available on my Patreon!

 

Depending on your chosen tier, you can read 1–3 arcs ahead of the Webnovel schedule.

 

Daily updates will still follow the same pace as on Webnovel.

 

What are the perks of joining?

 

Well, aside from getting access to advanced chapters and other ongoing stories, you'll also get to see illustrations — like the images placed alongside the text to help visualize scenes from the story.

 

That's about it — nothing fancy, just more stories and a bit of visual flair.

 1
