chapters.name: Chapter 111: Chapter 111: Mr. Shura, This Operation is So Showy!
chapters.content:
Those lucky enough to participate in the dungeon with Boss Shura couldn't help but brag to their friends as soon as they returned.

 

Before long, the entire Samsara Space was abuzz with talk of how to achieve the elusive Third Stage "SSS" rating, following Shura's strategy.

 

This was also the first-ever "SSS"-level Super God strategy to circulate in the Samsara Space!

 

Everyone was amazed by Shura's brilliantly executed operation.

 

But as they soon realized…

 

It was utterly impossible to replicate!!

 

First of all, to be acknowledged by the Celestial Dragons, you had to place in the top three during the Marine assessment!

 

That requirement alone eliminated nearly all Samsara players.

 

After all, the Marine Recruit assessment included many powerful native characters—Fujitora (Issho), Sentomaru, Yumo(Momonga), Smoker, and more.

 

Most Samsara players who reached the Third Stage barely ranked D or C. Expecting them to defeat these native monsters in the One Piece world? It was a joke.

 

Since the Samsara Space opened, only two people had ever placed in the top three:

 

Shura, and Adam.

 

Not every Samsara player could go head-to-head with Fujitora like Shura did!

 

Even if, by sheer luck, you did get into the top three, another impossible hurdle awaited you—

 

How do you escape after killing a Celestial Dragon?!

 

The three Marine Admirals weren't just for show!

 3

Without teleportation abilities or special items, thinking you could walk away after the hit?

 

You might as well say goodbye to your life!

 

"High-paying offer for any item that grants instant teleportation! Cash ready! Even one-time-use items starting at 5 billion!"

 

"Holy hell, what a tyrant! But hey—has anyone even seen those so-called teleportation items?"

 

"Of course not. I'm just pretending to flex. You think I really have 5 billion?"

 6

"If God Shura doesn't have innate teleportation skills, then he must own some sort of rare item. Wonder if he's willing to sell..."

 

"You're dreaming. Why would Boss Shura sell a life-saving artifact like that?"

 

"No need to sell—just lend it! I'm willing to pay 1 billion just to borrow it once! I'll even sign a Samsara Space justice contract!"

 1

"Haha! You think Boss Shura is that naive? What if you die with the item still in the dungeon?"

 

"So basically, this 'SSS'-level strategy can only be completed by Shura himself, huh?"

 

"No kidding. The Samsara System is smarter than any of us. You think it'll hand out 'SSS' ratings like candy? Without real skill, exploiting loopholes gets you nowhere!"

 

"Newbie here. I heard the Cindralock Dominion once tried a 'God-Making Plan'—gathering 100,000 people to farm dungeons in the safe zone, mass-producing points, then transferring them all to a single Samsara player through item sales. Is that real?"

 

"Yep, totally real."

 

"So… did it work?"

 

"Sure did. But every newbie who participated? Their graves are covered in weeds by now."

 1

"As someone who lived through it, let me give you some advice—stop dreaming about gaming the system."

 

"This Samsara System runs on top-tier intelligence."

 

"It'll show you real quick—every 'shortcut' you find is actually a trap."

 

"Thanks for the warning, boss. I get it now!"

 

When Aurora Morwyn returned to Samsara Square, she was stunned.

 

All anyone could talk about was Shura.

 

"Shura... I can't believe you actually pulled it off!"

 

Aurora was in awe.

 

More than that—she had faced certain death in the 28th-floor dungeon, but at the critical moment, Shura's influence had brought her back to life!

 

Even the system, based on her altered performance, judged the task as complete!

 5

She only received a 'B' rating, but that was better than dying in the dungeon.

 

There's a saying: "Better a live dog than a dead lion."

 

Aurora had family, friends, and things she couldn't let go of. As Jadeveil Nation's top Samsara player, the pressure on her was immense. But if there was a chance to live, who would choose to die?

 

Shura saved her life!

 

You have a new message.

 

"Belle Morwyn" invites you to a video call. Please respond promptly.

 

The system prompt appeared.

 

Aurora hesitated for a moment, then accepted.

 

A cheerful elf like girl image popped up on the screen:

 

"Cousin! You passed the 28th floor? That's amazing!"

 

Aurora shook her head at first, then smiled softly. "I got lucky this time."

 

Belle didn't really understand what that meant, but it didn't dampen her excitement.

 

Aurora was the pillar of their family. Everyone had been worried ever since they heard she was attempting the 28th-floor dungeon.

 

After all, no one thought she could survive.

 

Now that she had returned safely, it was a clear sign that she had passed the test—and grown stronger.

 

For the family, this was a cause for celebration.

 

"Cousin, are you coming home now?" the elf girl asked.

 

Aurora shook her head. "Not yet. I'll log off later."

 

She had too many questions for Shura.

 

"Okay then! I'll tell Grandma, Grandpa, and Uncle right away! They've been so worried! They'll be thrilled when they hear the news!"

 

Hearing about her family made Aurora's heart warm.

 

She smiled and nodded. "Tell the elders not to wait up. I'll go offline later. Let them rest first."

 

"Got it! Bye-bye, Cousin!"

 

As soon as the call ended, another message came in—another communication request.

 

As a high-profile figure, every move Aurora made attracted attention.

 

She had planned a major dungeon run tonight. Not only her family but also the bigshots at the center were paying close attention.

 

But family concern?

 

That was genuine love.

 

Others?

 

They just didn't want her failure to shake the international balance of power.

chapters.name: Chapter 112: Chapter 112: Super-Large Dungeon!
chapters.content:
Samsara Space — Entertainment City.

 

Inside a large private room in a teahouse, more than a dozen Samsara players had gathered.

 

At a glance, most of them were clearly Cindralockers.

 

Judging from their seating arrangement and the underlying tension, it was obvious—they weren't from a single group, but rather two factions cautiously observing each other.

 

Careful inspection revealed that many of them were renowned experts within the Samsara Space.

 

"Adam hasn't arrived yet?" asked a towering man over two meters tall.

 

Upon hearing this, a bald man sitting across from him sneered.

 

"You think someone like you is worthy of meeting our god?"

 

The tall man's expression darkened. "Arrogant bastard. Is this the attitude you bring to a potential alliance?"

 

Disdain flickered in the bald man's eyes, but he adjusted his posture and replied with mock sincerity, "We are absolutely serious about cooperation."

 

"Funny. I'm not seeing any sincerity," the large man retorted.

 

"Regardless, you don't want to see Shura rise, do you? He's already received his fourth 'SSS' rating tonight."

 

The bald man leaned forward slightly, lowering his voice.

 

"According to our intel, he just cleared the Third Stage of the Sacred Tower… with at least a B-rank combat evaluation. He was able to fight Fujitora head-on in the One Piece world."

 2

As soon as the words left his mouth, the room fell silent. Shock spread across the faces of those present.

 

Going toe-to-toe with Fujitora?

 

Even among these elites, few could boast the same.

 

After a long pause, the muscular man muttered, "Still… Shura's momentum can't be stopped now. In dungeons of the same level, he has no equal."

 

"That's true," the bald man agreed, "but we'll have another chance soon."

 

"Oh?" The strong man narrowed his eyes. "Let's hear it."

 

"The annual 'super-large dungeon' for PUBG World Battle is coming up in Samsara Space. When that happens, our two regions can join forces—

 8

—and take Shura down together."

 

By the time he finished, the bald man's expression had turned cold and grim.

 

The large man's eyes lit up at the idea, but he voiced a concern.

 

"That woman—Aurora Morwyn—what if she intervenes?"

 

"Relax," the bald man said confidently. "Mr. Adam will personally take care of her."

 

Meanwhile…

 

Aurora had just ended a video call with an intelligence agent.

 

Her brows were furrowed.

 

According to the latest report, Samsara players from the Cindralock Dominion and the Land of Dawn Jewels were in close communication.

 

Not only those two countries, but even players from the Willowland country and the Anklebrook had become involved.

 

It didn't take a genius to guess—they were plotting something.

 

"Shura… you've risen too fast," she murmured. "You've become a thorn in too many sides."

 

The intelligence agent had mentioned that these factions wanted Shura to join their organization in exchange for protection and resources.

 

Aurora, however, didn't bother to pass the message along.

 

She already knew Shura's stance—he wouldn't play that game.

 3

And she didn't want to be the one to bring it up anyway.

 

With her current status, whether she cooperated or not wouldn't change much.

 

Opening her messages, she saw that Shura still hadn't responded, so she left a brief note for him.

 

She had many questions—especially now.

 

Shura had somehow influenced the One Piece dungeon world… and even she had felt it!

 

As far as she knew, the missions for each batch of Samsara players in large-scale dungeons were locked within isolated timelines.

 

No player should be able to interfere with another batch's scenario.

 

Every time a new group entered, the dungeon would reset back to the starting point.

 

What happened today?

 

It was unprecedented.

 

Inside Fenric's Personal Warehouse

 

Fenric was reviewing his rewards from the latest dungeon run.

 

Samsara Points: 40,000

 2

Strength Attribute +30 (automatically added)

 

Personal Dungeon Card x1 (stored in personal warehouse)

 

Golden Treasure Chest x1 (stored in personal warehouse)

 

Only 40,000 points this time—less than the 50,000 he earned in The Mountain Village Old Corpse.

 

And yet, this mission felt far more dangerous!

 

"This damned system… how the hell does it calculate difficulty anyway?"

 

Fenric complained inwardly.

 

He quickly began spending his points to enhance his potential.

 

However, just after exchanging dozens of potential attributes, a sudden system message popped up:

 

"Dear Samsara player Shura. You've accumulated over 500 potential exchanges, exceeding the novice threshold. From now on, each potential point costs 500 Samsara Points."

 2

"Damn it!" Fenric swore. "They raised the price!?"

 

He had hoped to supercharge his stats again this time.

 

Now, it was clear—he wouldn't be leveling up nearly as much.

 

Still, there was no choice. Power was everything.

 

By the end of it, Fenric had redeemed just 76 attribute points, keeping 5,000 points in reserve.

 

After distributing his potential, he turned to the rest of his loot.

 

Strength +30 — already added, no need to touch it.

 

Personal Dungeon Card — always a great item. He loved these!

 

Personal dungeons were rare, and his last one had yielded huge gains with very little danger.

 5

Now came the main prize:

 

The Golden Treasure Chest

 

According to online guides, chests from the Third Stage of the One Piece dungeon contained loot from the One Piece universe.

 

Most likely reward? A Devil Fruit!

 2

Rumor had it that the top-ranked player, Adam, had drawn a Superhuman Devil Fruit from just a bronze chest.

 3

And here Fenric was… with a gold chest—two grades higher!

 

(Treasure Chest Tiers: Black Iron < Bronze < Silver < Gold)

 

He wasn't asking for much—just give him a Goro Goro no Mi or a Gura Gura no Mi!

 1

Was that too much to ask!?

 

Grinning in anticipation, Fenric slowly opened the treasure chest.

 

A brilliant golden light burst out.

 

No Devil Fruit.

 

Only a scroll lay quietly inside.

 5

"Thw Hell!? Where's the damn Quake-Quake Fruit I ordered!?"

 

Fenric almost exploded with frustration, face turning blue from rage.

 

But the moment he picked up the scroll…

 

All his anger vanished.

 

A stunned smile crept across his face—

 

Because what he held in his hands might just be better than a Devil Fruit!

 2

chapters.name: Chapter 113: Chapter 113: The Fourth Super God Reward!
chapters.content:
"Special Item: Conqueror's Haki (Scroll)!"

 5

"Conqueror's Haki: The rarest and most powerful of the three types of Haki.

 16

Only those with the spirit of a king are born with this potential.

 

With Conqueror's Haki, one can overwhelm and intimidate enemies without lifting a finger.

 1

Weaker foes may collapse simply from the pressure."

 

Hearing the system prompt, Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

Conqueror's Haki!

 

Among all abilities in the One Piece world, this was undoubtedly one of the rarest and most sought-after powers.

 1

It was comparable—even rivaling—the might of a top-tier Logia Devil Fruit.

 1

Unlike Logia fruits that immediately transform the user into a formidable force upon consumption, Conqueror's Haki was weak at first, able to subdue only ordinary people. But its potential was limitless. Its ceiling? Sky high.

 

A perfect example was the Red-Haired Shanks—one of the Four Emperors.

 1

When he unleashed his Conqueror Haki, even opponents at his level could be suppressed.

 

Fenric was more than satisfied with this Golden Treasure Chest reward.

 

Very satisfied!

 

Based on online guides, the rewards for the third level of the One Piece large-scale dungeon weren't supposed to be this generous. Truly valuable Devil Fruits could only be acquired in the second phase—deep within the multi-floor Tower of Samsara.

 

Without hesitation, Fenric tore open the scroll.

 

"Notice: You have learned Conqueror's Haki. Proficiency: 500."

 

BOOM!!

 

Something in Fenric changed instantly.

 

His aura, already confident and powerful, took a leap to something even more formidable.

 

Before, people who met him for the first time would see him as charismatic and strong.

 

Now? He radiated an oppressive, kingly presence. He stood silently, yet resembled a lion at rest—quiet, but exuding an overwhelming force.

 3

The aura of a king!

 

Fortunately, Fenric could suppress his Conqueror Haki to a manageable level. Otherwise, just walking down the main street would draw far too much attention.

 

Next, he attempted to upgrade his newly acquired Conqueror's Haki.

 

To his surprise, a casual upgrade required 3,000 Samsara points—twice as much as for Armament Haki.

 

To push it to Proficient would cost a staggering 30,000 points.

 2

Insane.

 

Status:

 

Name: Shura

 

Samsara Number: Area C-90086

 

Physique: 100 → 120

 

Spirit: 200 → 230

 

Strength: 114 → 155

 

Agility: 100 → 115

 

Available Potential Points: 0

 

Skills:

 1

English (Proficient)

 

Driving (Beginner)

 

Shooting (Proficient)

 

Camouflage (Master)

 

Basic Swordsmanship (Proficient)

 

Special Skills:

 

Conqueror's Haki (Proficient)

 3

Armament Haki (Master)

 6

Combat Techniques:

 

Savage Charge

 

Abilities:

 

Telekinesis

 

Samsara Points: 2,672

 

Overall Evaluation: B

 3

Fenric reviewed his updated stats. His overall evaluation remained at B, which meant he still had a ways to go before reaching A-rank.

 

Still, he was pleased.

 

Among Samsara players of his level, he stood at the top—far above the rest.

 

As he exited the Personal Warehouse, a message came in from Aurora Morwyn.

 

His eyes brightened.

 

She was still alive!

 

Fenric vividly recalled their parting—Aurora had also entered the Tower of Samsara, intending to clear a dungeon.

 

If she was messaging him now, it meant she'd survived her run!

 

Excited, he immediately initiated a video call.

 

"Shura!!"

 

Aurora picked up almost instantly—as if she'd been waiting.

 

"Finally done hiding in your warehouse, huh? Got quite the haul this time? Your name's all over the Samsara Space!"

 

"Oh?" Fenric was surprised. "It was just a Super God rating. It's not even my first."

 

"This time's different," she said. "Lots of people saw your performance firsthand during the dungeon run. Word's spread fast. Your fame has skyrocketed—there are even some 'cheaters' calling you their idol."

 

Fenric chuckled.

 

Let them talk.

 

He knew no one could replicate what he did anyway.

 

"Shura, I honestly didn't expect you to actually assassinate a Celestial Dragon and make it out alive!" Aurora exclaimed.

 

Smart as ever, she didn't ask whether Fenric had a teleportation item or ability.

 

It was clearly a secret, and if Fenric didn't bring it up himself, she wouldn't pry.

 

"Just luck, really," Fenric replied humbly. "But congratulations to you as well! You cleared 28 floors—that's incredible!"

 

Aurora smiled softly. "Shura, I should be the one thanking you."

 

"Me? I didn't help you at all."

 

"Oh, but you did. Your actions in the One Piece dungeon altered the original timeline. Because of your influence, the Marine Fleet Admiral was replaced mid-arc. I should've died—but thanks to that shift, I survived. The system judged my mission complete."

 2

Fenric blinked.

 

Was that really possible?

 

"Shura, if you're free, let's meet up. I'd rather explain everything in person. Come to Box 3637 at the teahouse. My treat."

 

"Sounds good."

 

Fenric agreed readily—he was curious to hear what exactly had happened to her during the dungeon.

 

Entertainment City – Teahouse – Box 3637

 

Aurora Morwyn began by recounting her experience.

 

When she mentioned that Whitebeard and Kaido had joined forces to assault Marine Headquarters, Fenric looked completely stunned.

 4

The Four Emperors attacking the Marines together?

 

This wasn't just a "Marineford War." This was complete chaos!

 

"You're saying the Marine Fleet Admiral changed because of my actions? It wasn't Sengoku anymore?"

 

Aurora Morwyn nodded. "Right."

 

"Then who was it?"

 

"Akainu."

 

She continued, "And not just that. Admiral Aokiji vanished, replaced by a fearsome new figure nicknamed 'Green Bull.'"

 

Fenric asked quickly, "So who were the Admirals under Akainu's leadership?"

 

"Me, Fujitora, Green Bull, and Kizaru."

 

Fenric felt dizzy for a moment.

 

The entire storyline had been derailed.

 

Aurora added seriously, "I just found out that you didn't just affect my dungeon. Other Samsara players who entered the second stage of the One Piece world also reported strange developments."

 

"All of this because you assassinated a Celestial Dragon inside Marine Headquarters. It forced Sengoku to resign—and everything else spiraled from there."

chapters.name: Chapter 114: Chapter 114: Someone Wants to Block Shura After School?
chapters.content:
"How can this be?"

 

Fenric frowned. "If the entire 'One Piece' instance is affected by me, does that mean those who cleared it earlier in Stage One will automatically be upgraded to Stage Two the next time? Does that also mean those who've already completed a higher stage—like Adam, who passed the Third Stage—have changed in some way?"

 1

"This is too chaotic... it's a paradox!"

 

Aurora nodded. "I've considered that possibility. But based on the intel I've gathered so far, no abnormalities have been reported by those who previously cleared the 'One Piece' instance. At least not those who cleared it before your impact on the system."

 1

She continued, "My personal speculation is that the effects you triggered only apply to Samsara players who run the 'One Piece' world at the same time as you. Like me, for example. After all, no one has ever done anything as bold as what you did."

 

"We'll know for sure once more people go through the instance again. If they experience changes, my theory is wrong. Otherwise, it holds."

 

Fenric nodded in understanding.

 

Aurora's logic was clear. She believed the effects of Fenric's actions were localized, only impacting those who entered the instance concurrently with him. The majority of Samsara players, at least for now, were unaffected.

 

If her assumption was correct, then in future 'One Piece' runs, this small group—including herself—might have a different experience from others.

 

"If the enemy comes, I'll block them. If water floods in, I'll build a dam. No matter what changes come, I'll clear my instances in peace," Fenric muttered calmly.

 

Aurora smiled at his response.

 

Fenric might not be worried, but she was. Due to her current position, she couldn't afford to think only of herself.

 

She needed to fully understand the extent of the impact caused by Shura—by Fenric. Was it something the country could weaponize?

 

"Either way, you've saved my life today. I honestly thought I was going to die. Thank you, Shura."

 

"Ms. Morwyn, don't be so formal. You've helped me a lot too," Fenric replied with a grin.

 

"Oh, one more thing—"

 

Aurora suddenly became serious. "Shura, your rise has been too fast. According to my intel, several foreign factions already see you as a threat. Some are even plotting to eliminate you."

 

A cold glint flickered in Fenric's eyes. "Let them come. If it's a same-level instance, no matter how many they send—they'll all die."

 

Aurora nodded, agreeing with his confident, yet unpretentious tone.

 

"I've heard about your performance. Anyone who can go head-to-head with Fujitora has the right to talk big."

 

"However," she added, "they may still have other ways to deal with you. You need to stay alert."

 

"Oh?" Fenric asked. "What kind of ways?"

 

"The most direct would be to uncover your real-world identity and assassinate you. From what I've heard, even Adam now sees you as a threat. If your identity gets exposed… be prepared. Right now, even we can't determine where you're from."

 5

She paused, then continued, "But their main strategy is to wait for the annual super-dungeon: PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds. They're planning to gang up on you there."

 

Fenric was taken aback. "PUBG? Can you tell me more about that instance?"

 

In his memories, PUBG was an online game from his previous life.

 

Aurora explained, "PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds is a global event held every September. It's a confrontation-style instance organized by the Samsara System itself. Every Samsara player who has cleared a Samsara Tower instance must participate in a regional team."

 

"Winners get massive rewards. The rest get penalized—points will be deducted. You'd better start saving points now, just in case."

 1

"In that instance, Samsara players can fight each other freely. The system enforces combat through gas zones and bombing areas, pushing everyone to compete head-on."

 

"Right now, Zone E wins every year... because they have Adam."

 5

As she finished, Aurora's expression turned cold. Clearly, she'd suffered at Adam's hands before.

 

Fenric nodded thoughtfully. He planned to research this PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds instance in depth.

 

From what Aurora described, it sounded like a real-life version of the battle royale game he used to play.

 

...For now, Fenric stayed vigilant.

 

If he didn't want to end up as a corpse, he had to be fully prepared.

 

After parting with Aurora, Fenric didn't use his personal instance card right away.

 

Instead, he visited the world of The Great Wall, spent a day there (equivalent to an hour in the real world) with Lin Mei, then logged out and returned to reality.

 

Back in the real world.

 

He turned on his computer and searched for information about the PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds instance.

 

Airdrops. Poison zones. Bombing areas. Shrinking safe zones...

 

After reading, Fenric shut off the computer, expressionless.

 

There was no doubt—this was the very same game from his past life, only reworked by the Samsara System into a deadly, real-life version.

 

In this massive PUBG instance, if you got killed by another Samsara… you'd die for real.

 12

And the worst part?

 

It was mandatory.

 

Any Samsara who had cleared a tower dungeon had to participate.

 

There was no way to opt out.

 

The next morning.

 

Fenric washed up and headed straight to school.

 

Tonight, he would refresh a new personal instance to strengthen himself even further.

 

Although he was confident that Aurora would help him during the PUBG event...

 

Fenric had never relied on others.

 

He only trusted one thing: his own strength.

 2

At school.

 

The moment Fenric sat down, a fat classmate leaned over from behind with a grin. It's Jitto.

 

"Fenric, you missed a good show today!"

 

Fenric sighed. "If you've got something to say, just say it."

 

"Haha! Tazhan from the next class made an announcement. He said you'd better go apologize to him before school ends today. Promise to stay away from Wen, the school beauty—otherwise, he's going to block you after school!"

 6

Fenric's expression darkened.

 

Are high schoolers these brain-dead these days?

 1

He was starting to feel more and more that campus life just wasn't worth the trouble.

chapters.name: Chapter 115: Chapter 115: Scared-to-Cry Genius!
chapters.content:
Fenric ignored Jitto words.

 

He also ignored the so-called "genius" and his empty threats.

 

Instead, he took out his phone and started browsing the web.

 

As expected, his Shura identity had exploded online once again.

 

At this point, even Fenric himself was starting to feel numb to it.

 

Online Comments Section:

 

"He's f**king amazing! That's the fourth time God Shura has received a Super God rating, right?"

 

"Insane! Ever since the name 'Shura' appeared, it's been nothing but Super God evaluations!"

 

"All hail Shura! He's gonna surpass Adam in no time and dominate the leaderboard!"

 

"Ever since I learned how he killed the Celestial Dragon and got an 'SSS' rating, I've been so hyped. He's just too damn fierce!"

 

"Exactly! Most people wouldn't even dare to try that!"

 

"So jealous of the Great God Shura. I hope he shares all his strategies!"

 

"Heh, here comes another moral-kidnapping dog. Didn't Shura already share his entire strategy for the Third Stage? If you've got the guts, go replicate it yourself."

 

"Yeah right. Only Shura can pull off Shura's strategy. You think some mutt can do it?"

 

"I heard the Great God Shura went head-to-head with an Admiral. That's terrifying!"

 

"Seriously terrifying. And he's only just cleared the Third Stage? How is he this strong already?"

 

"You guys are exaggerating. I watched the whole run last night when he got the Super God evaluation. Shura really did face off against that old blind man, but it was only for two rounds. Based on their fight, Shura's still got a long way to go before he matches an Admiral… A long way! Still, I totally idolize him!"

 

"Regardless, just reaching the Third Stage and putting on that kind of performance—he's a monster!"

 

"Exactly. With that kind of talent, it's only a matter of time before Shura surpasses Adam!"

 

"Foreign players must be panicking, watching the rise of the Great God Shura."

 

"Adam be like: Damn… I'm panicking right now."

 

The internet was ablaze.

 

This was the first time an "SSS"-ranked dungeon strategy had been revealed to the public.

 

Now, countless netizens knew exactly how Shura achieved the coveted "SSS" rating.

 

There wasn't a single person who didn't admire his bold and strategic performance in the Third Stage One Piece dungeon.

 

Fearless. Decisive. Meticulous. Overwhelming. Brave and brilliant.

 

These were the impressions the world now had of the Great God Shura.

 

Two words summed it all up:

 

"Absolute Legend!"

 

Fenric scrolled through the comments and smiled faintly.

 

Behind him came the voice of Jitto, the ever-loud fat guy.

 

"Ric, why do you look so calm? That Tazhan guy—ugh—I've hated him for a while now! I hope you humiliate him so badly today he won't dare show his face again!"

 

Fenric replied flatly, "I'm not interested in your little high school rivalries."

 

"Oh? So you're saying you're not a young man anymore?"

 

It was class time, but with the college entrance exams fast approaching, most teachers had stopped lecturing. Students were left to self-study.

 

Today, no teacher showed up.

 

Idle students whispered among themselves, and quite a few kept sneaking glances at Fenric, smirking or snickering.

 

Clearly, Tazhan's little stunt had already spread throughout the school.

 

The day passed like that.

 

When the final bell rang in the afternoon, the usual slackers—normally faster than rabbits when fleeing school—didn't leave.

 

They were waiting.

 

All eyes were on Fenric, watching his every move, eager for drama.

 

Fenric ignored the stares. He packed up his things, shoved the books he hadn't touched back into his desk, then casually walked out of the classroom and headed toward the school gate.

 

The moment he stepped out, the others quickly followed.

 

However, they kept their distance, not wanting to be mistaken as part of Fenric's group and risk getting caught in any crossfire.

 

"Ric! Wait for me!"

 

Jitto jogged to catch up.

 

Fenric gave him a sideways glance. "Aren't you afraid of being dragged into this?"

 

"Afraid? Hell no! Others might be scared of Tazhan, but I'm not!"

 

Outside the school gate, a crowd had already gathered—eager to watch the drama unfold.

 

When Fenric appeared, a buzz ran through the students. Excitement rose.

 

"Damn, this guy's got guts!"

 

"Yeah! I thought he'd sneak out the back. Didn't expect him to just walk straight out the front!"

 

"No wonder the school beauty has her eye on him. Just for his courage alone, I have to respect him!"

 

"Heh. That's dumb. Tazhan has a relative in the Education Bureau. Even the principal doesn't dare touch him. Does this guy really think Tazhan won't retaliate?"

 

"Exactly! Doesn't he understand it's better to live and fight another day? Blind courage is just stupidity. I don't see what Wen sees in him."

 

"Hey, quiet down."

 

Meanwhile, Fenric calmly continued walking toward the gate.

 

There, a row of luxury sports cars was parked in full view.

 

A dozen stylish but clearly arrogant young men were waiting.

 1

The one at the center, dressed in a tight little suit with a greasy face that made it hard to tell if he was a guy or girl, stepped forward.

 

Tazhan Tao.

 

As soon as he saw Fenric, Tazhan flicked away his cigarette, raised a hand, and led his cronies over to block Fenric's path.

 

"You're Fenric?"

 

Tazhan craned his neck to look up at the taller boy.

 

"You've got guts, huh? Ignoring my warnings? Did I not tell you to apologize before school ended?"

 

As Tazhan droned on, he didn't notice Fenric's expression gradually turning cold.

 

This guy and his endless "labor and management" crap had officially crossed the line.

 

Fenric's voice rang out, sharp and deep—

 

"Scram."

 

Om—

 

Conqueror Haki— Activated!

 9

An invisible force exploded from Fenric.

 

In an instant, the onlooking students behind him felt it—an overwhelming kingly presence radiated from Fenric's tall frame.

 

As if a monarch had descended.

 

Some students' legs buckled from the pressure. A few nearly dropped to their knees in instinctive submission.

 

As for Tazhan and his fancy crew, they were hit directly by the full force of Fenric's Conqueror's Haki.

 

Several of them immediately passed out with eyes rolled back.

 

Tazhan himself, though still conscious, dropped to the ground in a heap.

 

In that moment—he had truly felt it.

 

The threat of death.

 

It was as if the boy standing before him was no longer a classmate…

 

…but an ancient, unstoppable king.

 

With just a thought—he could decide whether Tazhan lived or died!

chapters.name: Chapter 116: Chapter 116: Psychological Shadow!
chapters.content:
"..."

 

"..."

 

"...."

 

At the school gate, silence reigned.

 

The crowd of students who had gathered to watch the commotion never expected that a single word—"Scram"—could hold such terrifying power.

 

More than a dozen people had been scared stiff.

 

Even Tazhan—the so-called "genius" of the school—was so terrified that he wet his pants!

 

Looking at Tazhan's horrified expression, it was clear this moment would leave a deep psychological scar.

 

Even more shocking was the overwhelming aura that Fenric had just released.

 

It was so majestic, even ancient emperors would pale in comparison!

 

In the stunned silence, Fenric had already withdrawn his aura. Without sparing Tazhan a single glance, he turned and calmly walked away.

 

As he strolled down the street, Fenric allowed a smile to tug at his lips.

 

That was just him deliberately releasing a trace of Conqueror's Haki.

 

And it worked perfectly.

 

Fenric wasn't worried about exposing his identity as Shura.

 

Because so far, no one in the Samsara Space had ever awakened Conqueror's Haki—not a single person!

 6

Plus, according to Aurora, there was no Luffy in the "Paramount War" instance on the 28th floor. It seemed Luffy had been delayed somewhere else due to the ripple effects of Samsara players.

 3

In other words, almost no one on the 27th floor even knew what Conqueror's Haki looked like.

 

"It's boring to keep hiding like this. I should just get stronger as fast as possible! When I become powerful enough, even if the whole world knows I'm Shura, what can they do?"

 9

With that thought, Fenric picked up his pace and hurried home.

 

He was planning to tackle a personal dungeon tonight.

 1

Hopefully, this time it would offer an unexpected surprise.

 

Only after Fenric disappeared did the students at the school gate slowly begin to scatter.

 

Before leaving, each one cast a look of contempt at Tazhan.

 

They already hated Fenric for "stealing" Isla Wynn, but they hated Tazhan even more—for his constant bullying.

 

No one expected things to end like this.

 

The pressure Fenric had exuded left a lasting impression on everyone present.

 

A long while later...

 

Tazhan finally regained some strength.

 

Ashamed and trembling, he staggered to his feet.

 

His legs still shaky, he clambered into his car and started the engine, speeding off without a second thought.

 

As for the friends he had brought with him? Tazhan didn't even bother to look at them—leaving them unconscious on the ground.

 

How embarrassing...

 

Frightened just by someone yelling at him?

 

He had even lost control of his bladder!

 

As the car sped along the road, Tazhan gritted his teeth and slammed the accelerator.

 

He would be lying if he said he didn't resent Fenric for humiliating him in front of everyone.

 

But...

 

The sheer fear he had felt when facing Fenric came flooding back at the thought of revenge.

 

He was terrified.

 

Truly terrified.

 

The moment Fenric had released that aura, Tazhan felt as though fear had gripped him from the very depths of his soul.

 

(Ordinary people with weak wills can't withstand the pressure of Conqueror's Haki.)

 

"Damn it! Damn it!!"

 

At a red light, Tazhan furiously pounded the steering wheel to vent his frustration.

 

By the time he got home, a new thought surfaced in his mind—

 

"I don't want to go back to school..."

 

He had been utterly humiliated, couldn't muster the courage to retaliate, and was even scared of facing that person again...

 

So what was the point of going back?

 

Midnight.

 

"Jingle Bell..."

 3

The alarm rang.

 

Fenric, who had been resting with his eyes closed, immediately stood up.

 

In the next moment, he appeared in the Samsara Space.

 

From his personal inventory, he pulled out a Personal Dungeon Card.

 

"System, I want to use this card to open a personal dungeon!"

 

As soon as the command was given, the system responded:

 

"Personal dungeon opening."

 

"Initiating teleportation countdown: 10, 9, 8... 3, 2, 1."

 3

As the countdown ended, Fenric vanished from the square.

 

There was no white transition room, no preparation time.

 

Just like last time, he was directly teleported into the dungeon world.

 

When Fenric opened his eyes again, he found himself standing in a narrow alleyway.

 

Dirty water trickled along the ground, emitting a foul stench.

 

Fenric frowned slightly, but didn't move just yet.

 

Instead, he watched the people walking in and out of the alley.

 

All of them had Asian faces, dressed in long gowns from the Republic era. Occasionally, men in tuxedos were seen riding in rickshaws.

 2

"Long Robe? Tuxedos? Rickshaws? This feels like the People's Republic period..."

 7

Whether that was accurate remained to be seen.

 

For now, his priority was to figure out what kind of world this was.

 

Fenric had experience with personal dungeons. He knew the Samsara system wouldn't provide tasks or hints. Everything depended on his own initiative.

 

Soon, Fenric stepped out of the alley.

 

He found himself on a busy street bustling with life.

 

Most of the buildings were no more than three or four stories tall, and both sides of the street were lined with shops and vendors.

 

Merchants shouted, vendors hollered—the whole place was lively.

 

Looking at the retro scenery, Fenric narrowed his eyes.

 

There was no doubt about it—this was some period in the People Republic in the past.

 

As he looked around, many people on the street began sneaking glances at him.

 

And for good reason.

 

Fenric's current appearance was nothing short of striking.

 

Tall and muscular, wearing a crisp white shirt, gleaming leather shoes, and carrying an aura of confidence and strength...

 

(In personal dungeons, the real body enters the world.)

 

To everyone watching, Fenric looked like the young master of a wealthy family.

 

Countless women—both maidens and married—couldn't take their eyes off him.

 

As for the local thugs? None dared approach, unable to gauge his background.

 

Fenric ignored the attention and approached a roadside vendor.

 

The stall sold porcelain—bowls, vases, all neatly arranged.

 

The vendor, an elderly man in his fifties, smiled warmly as he saw Fenric approach.

 

"Welcome, sir! What would you like to buy?"

 

Of course, Fenric had no intention of buying anything.

 

"Old Man, where is this place?"

 

The vendor looked slightly disappointed but didn't dare be rude. Fenric clearly wasn't ordinary.

 

"You must be from out of town, sir. This is Renjia Town."

 

"Renjia Town?"

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed.

 

That name... sounded strangely familiar?

 

—---

chapters.name: Chapter 117: Chapter 117: Hammers Zombies Online (1/10)
chapters.content:
"Renjia Town?"

 

Fenric found the name vaguely familiar.

 

But no matter how hard he tried, he couldn't recall where he'd heard it before.

 

After thinking for a moment, Fenric asked, "Are there any well-known figures from this town? Or who's in charge around here?"

 

The old man smiled kindly and replied without hesitation,

 

"The Ren family, of course. The elder of the Ren household practically runs the town. Even the captain of the patrol unit reports to him.

 

But when it comes to someone truly famous, that would be Master Nine of Spirit Hall. He lives a few dozen miles away from here.

 

No matter what happens—whether it's ghosts or disturbances—people always turn to Master Nine!"

 

Fenric's expression shifted slightly.

 

Ren Family? Master Nine?

 

Isn't this the world of Mr. Vampire?

 12

A grin spread across his face.

 

He had already dealt with zombies and vengeful spirits before. And now, more zombies? Was he collecting every supernatural creature like Pokémon?

 

Since he had entered this world, the objective was likely simple: defeat zombies and earn points.

 

"Excuse me, old man," Fenric asked again, "how do I get to Spirit Hall?"

 

The old man pointed down the road.

 

"Just head out of town and keep going straight. But if you're going now, you might not find Master Nine."

 

"Oh? Why's that?"

 

"Today is the day the Ren family is relocating their ancestor's grave. Master Nine's been invited by Master Ren himself."

 

Ancestor's grave being moved?

 

That means the story has just begun.

 

If Fenric remembered correctly, the moment the old lady's corpse was unearthed, it would only take a few days for it to transform into a zombie.

 

"Then, where exactly is this grave?"

 

"Just head straight out of town. Once you're past the gates, turn right. There's a hill over there. Master Ren and the others are at the top."

 

"Thank you, old man."

 

After bidding the old man farewell, Fenric didn't rush to meet Master Nine.

 

Since this was the world of Mr. Vampire, things were already lining up.

 

He had watched the movie before. The plot wasn't complicated: the wealthy Ren family moved the grave of their ancestor, who had been dead for over twenty years. But instead of peace, they unearthed a powerful zombie that went on to terrorize Renjia Town.

 

Eventually, Master Nine joined forces with others to put the creature down.

 

As he walked, Fenric organized his thoughts.

 

The plot had only just started, and it would still take another two or three days for the corpse to transform into a zombie.

 

Looking for one now would be pointless.

 

There was no need to rush—he would take things step by step.

 

First, he'd find a place to stay in town.

 

Then, if possible, he wanted to see if he could learn a few techniques from Master Nine.

 

Now that he was in this world, he might as well take the opportunity to earn points and expand his skill set.

 

After all, as far as he knew, the trials in the Tower of Samsara often involved ghosts and demons.

 

It wouldn't hurt to learn how to deal with them properly.

 

But Fenric was also aware that earning Master Nine's favor wouldn't be easy. The old man had a rigid personality and didn't easily accept disciples. Bribery wouldn't work either—Master Nine was a man of principle.

 

Still, whether he could learn from him or not, it didn't matter much. Personal instances were mainly for scoring points.

 

Fenric strolled down the street, deep in thought.

 

Not long after, he noticed a long procession coming his way.

 

In the middle of the group were two people seated in modest sedan chairs carried by porters—clearly of higher status than the rest.

 1

One was a middle-aged man, not particularly striking in appearance, but his clothing screamed wealth.

 

The other was a young woman—slim, elegant, and breathtakingly beautiful.

 2

When the townsfolk saw them, they greeted respectfully:

 

"Hello, Master Ren! Hello, Miss Ren~!"

 

Fenric's eyes flashed.

 

Master Ren? Miss Ren?

 

Of course! Major figures in the story. No wonder they looked familiar.

 

Judging by the direction they were coming from, they must be returning from the tomb relocation.

 

Fenric's mind began to turn.

 

As Ren Tingting passed by, Fenric subtly moved his finger—activating his telekinetic powers.

 

Suddenly, the two porters stumbled as if tripping on something. The sedan chair tilted sharply.

 

"Ahh!"

 

Miss Ren and the porters cried out in alarm.

 

But as ordinary people, they had no way to resist the unseen force Fenric had unleashed.

 

Just before the sedan was about to topple completely, Fenric acted.

 

He stepped forward swiftly, caught Ren Tingting in his arms, and gently brought her down to safety.

 

"Careful."

 

Fenric's voice was calm and reassuring as he held her.

 

A textbook case of "hero saves beauty."

 

Shameless? A bit. But effective.

 

People in this era were straightforward and easy to read.

 

To Ren Tingting, she had nearly fallen—and this handsome man had come to her rescue.

 

When she looked up at Fenric's face, she was momentarily stunned.

 

So handsome…!

 

She gazed up at him dazedly, forgetting to move from his arms.

 

It wasn't that Ren Tingting was easily impressed—Fenric's appearance at this moment was simply too dazzling.

 

He had height, a well-sculpted figure, piercing eyes, and carried the aura of someone strong and capable.

 

If he didn't want to work another day in his life, some women would line up to support him.

 

Tingting, a young woman just beginning to understand love, was naturally drawn to someone like Fenric—confident, powerful, and attractive.

 

Besides, he had saved her.

 

"Miss, are you hurt?" Fenric asked gently.

 

After she steadied herself, he let go, playing the role of a proper gentleman.

 

It was all part of the plan—to get close to Ren Tingting.

 

As the female lead in this world, she was bound to have an important role. In the original plot, once the zombie awakened, it relentlessly targeted Ren Tingting, its closest blood relative.

 1

"Huh? I-I'm fine."

 

Ren Tingting finally snapped out of her daze, her cheeks flushed red.

 

She stole a glance at Fenric, feeling her heart flutter at the thought of being in his arms.

 

He's so graceful…

 

Embarrassed, she quickly looked away.

 

Truthfully, this was a face-based society.

 1

If her savior had been unattractive, her reaction would've been very different.

 3

"Miss, I'm sorry! We're so sorry!"

 

The two porters hurriedly apologized.

 

"I don't know what happened—our feet just slipped all of a sudden!"

 

_____

chapters.name: Chapter 118: Chapter 118: Courageous, Careful, and Thick-Skinned! (2/10)
chapters.content:
"It's okay, I'm fine."

 

Just like in the original plot, Ren Tingting was kind-hearted at her core.

 

Although she was generous by nature, some men were still extremely petty.

 

"What are you good for? You can't even lift a sedan chair properly! Useless!"

 

It wasn't Master Ren who reprimanded the bearer, but a well-fed man with a slicked-back hairstyle and sharp eyes—he looked every bit the classic sycophant.

 

His name was Weiha, the captain of the town's security team, and Ren Tingting's cousin. He had long harbored feelings for her and wanted to marry her.

 8

Although he was scolding the sedan chair bearer, Weiha's eyes remained fixed warily on Fenric.

 

Fenric's appearance and demeanor were exceptional. This immediately made Weiha feel threatened.

 

"Weiha, that's enough!"

 

Master Ren finally spoke up, clearly dissatisfied with Weiha's conduct.

 

Publicly berating someone in the street only reflected poorly on the Ren family's upbringing.

 

Master Ren then approached Fenric with a warm smile. "Thank you for saving my daughter, Tingting. You must come to our home so she can personally thank you."

 10

Master Ren's courteous tone made it clear he had noticed Fenric's unusual aura. Coupled with Fenric's neat and modern clothing—actually casual modern wear—Master Ren easily mistook him for the scion of a prestigious family.

 

Upon hearing her father's words, Ren Tingting shyly stepped forward, her cheeks flushed.

 

"Thank you… Thank you for helping me," she said, bowing.

 

"It was nothing, really. Don't worry about it," Fenric replied with a smile.

 

Master Ren then extended an invitation. "This isn't the place to talk. Why don't we head back to my house and continue the conversation there?"

 

"Alright! I'd be honored." Fenric responded with a gracious nod.

 

Of course, this was all part of Fenric's act—a staged hero-saves-damsel routine to get his foot into the Ren household.

 

"Please, young friend, after you."

 

"You're the elder, sir—please go first."

 

"Haha, then let's walk together."

 

Watching his uncle prepare to bring this unfamiliar man into their home, Weiha grew visibly agitated.

 

But this was Master Ren's town, and he wielded real power here. No matter how upset Weiha felt, he didn't dare speak out. He could only glare at Fenric with obvious hostility.

 

Fenric returned his threatening gaze with a calm smile, completely unfazed.

 

If he truly wanted to, Fenric could crush someone like Weiha as easily as stepping on an ant.

 

—

 

Once they arrived at the Ren residence, Fenric and Master Ren sat down in the parlor, sipping tea and chatting.

 

Ren Tingting, for some reason, also joined them. Since he had feelings for his cousin, Weiha of course wouldn't miss this scene.

 

So, what began as a conversation between two people soon became one between four.

 

Weiha, of course, tagged along uninvited.

 

"By the way, young friend," Master Ren asked with a smile, "may I ask your name?"

 

"My surname's Fen, given name Ric," he answered casually.

 1

Since this was a solo instance and no other Samsara had joined, Fenric had the freedom to say whatever he liked—even using his real name didn't matter.

 

"Ric isn't a local, is he?" Master Ren probed further.

 

Fenric smiled and nodded. "That's right. I've been living overseas. I came back this time to admire the motherland's scenery and—hopefully—contribute to her future."

 

Thanks to his [Disguise] skill, Fenric could lie through his teeth without the slightest change in expression.

 2

Ren Tingting's eyes immediately lit up. She leaned forward eagerly and asked, "Then… Can you speak a foreign language?"

 

"If it's English, sure," Fenric replied.

 1

That wasn't a bluff—his English skill had already reached "Proficient." Daily communication was no problem at all.

 

"Amazing!"

 

With a sparkle in her large, expressive eyes, Ren Tingting glanced at Fenric admiringly. Then she turned to her father and said, "Father, I've always wanted to study abroad, but I couldn't find anyone who could teach me a foreign language."

 

As soon as she said it, her cheeks turned pink again.

 

Her implication was obvious.

 

Fenric smiled knowingly.

 

He was well aware of the original plot—Ren Tingting was infatuated with the idea of foreigners. That was why she deliberately fashioned the persona of an overseas native.

 

It was hard to blame her. In this era, foreign nations were strong and represented progress, while their country still struggled to rise above poverty.

 7

Master Ren gave his daughter a quick, subtle glance.

 

Still, for the sake of her happiness, he was willing to give in.

 

"Ric," he said with a smile, "my daughter is eager to learn a foreign language. Would you be willing to teach her? As for your salary, rest assured—I won't treat you unfairly."

 

He spoke so readily because he could tell Fenric was refined, well-mannered, and clearly not ordinary.

 

If he were just some no-name vagabond, Master Ren wouldn't have even considered it.

 

Master Ren's proposal was exactly what Fenric had hoped for.

 

Fenric nodded. "Since Master Ren has extended the offer personally, I'll gladly accept. I only hope Miss Tingting won't find my teaching inadequate."

 

Just as Ren Tingting was about to respond, Weiha—unable to contain himself—burst out, "Uncle! This guy's background is unclear. How can you let him teach Tingting!?"

 

He spoke without a shred of courtesy.

 

Fenric remained silent, but Ren Tingting jumped up like a cat whose tail had been stepped on.

 

"Cousin, how can you be so rude to my teacher? Apologize to him, right now!"

 2

"T-teacher…?"

 

Weiha felt a sharp pain in his chest.

 1

He hadn't even managed to become her teacher, and now his cousin was calling that pretty boy teacher—and demanding he apologize?

 

"Enough, Weiha. Don't make trouble," Master Ren said coldly.

 

Weiha was thoroughly humiliated, but he didn't dare defy Master Ren.

 

After all, it was Master Ren's money that had secured his position as the town's security captain. He couldn't afford to offend him.

 

Just then, Master Ren glanced up at the sky and said, "It's almost lunchtime. Mr. Fen, let me host you today. I know of a Western-style restaurant with very authentic dishes—I believe you'll enjoy it."

 

Now that Fenric had become his daughter's teacher, Master Ren respectfully referred to him as Mr. Fen.

 1

Upon hearing this, Fenric's eyes narrowed slightly.

 

He understood immediately—this lunch was a test.

 

It seemed that Master Ren was far more calculating than he let on.

 

Then again, someone who could maintain a household of this size had to be cunning.

 

Compared to Weiha's impulsiveness, Master Ren was truly shrewd.

 

"In that case, I'll graciously accept Master Ren's hospitality," Fenric said with a calm smile.

 

______

chapters.name: Chapter 119: Chapter 119: Test? (3/10)
chapters.content:
Soon after—

 

Master Ren took Fenric and Ren Tingting to a Western restaurant outside of Ren Mansion.

 

As for Weiha, Master Ren disliked his lack of discretion and decisively left him behind.

 

Ten minutes later—

 

"Here we are."

 

Master Ren was the first to get out of the car. He turned to Fenric and said, "The owner of this Western restaurant is an old acquaintance of mine. He studied abroad and opened this place after coming back. I heard his chef is a real foreigner, imported straight from overseas!"

 1

As he spoke, Master Ren kept a close eye on Fenric's expression, trying to catch any flicker of unease.

 

If Fenric flinched now, it would be proof that he was hiding something!

 

But Fenric's face remained calm and composed.

 

He already understood that this meal wouldn't be so simple.

 

But so what?

 

Even if he got exposed, it wasn't like Master Ren could do anything about it.

 

What, did Master Ren think he could take him down? If pushed, Fenric could raze Renjia Town to the ground.

 

Besides, it wasn't like he couldn't speak English.

 

The three entered the restaurant, and a waiter quickly approached, politely guiding them to a window seat on the second floor.

 

As a regular guest, Master Ren was always given a good spot.

 

Once seated, the waiter handed them menus.

 

Master Ren chuckled. "Mr. Fen, feel free to order anything you like. You're a top student who studied abroad, right? While you're at it, help me judge whether this chef my friend brought back is the real deal or not!"

 

Fenric smiled and opened the menu.

 

The selections were few, and all written in English.

 

Still, Fenric showed no hesitation.

 

"I'll have a steak and a coffee," he said fluently.

 12

The waiter, clearly trained to understand basic English, nodded. "Okay, sir. It'll be out shortly."

 2

Master Ren continued to smile, but deep down, he remained cautious.

 

If Fenric could only spit out a few basic phrases, that wouldn't pass his test.

 

Soon, Master Ren and Ren Tingting ordered as well—both speaking in their mother tongue.

 

Since it was lunchtime and the restaurant wasn't crowded, their food arrived quickly.

 

The three chatted as they ate.

 

Just as they were nearly done, a fat, middle-aged man—around Master Ren's age—approached their table with a tall foreigner beside him, whose deep-set eyes marked him as a foreigner.

 

"Haha! Master Ren! What brings you to my place today?"

 

Fenric, sensing the real show was about to begin, calmly picked up his napkin and wiped his mouth with practiced grace.

 

"We came to support your business, of course," Master Ren said with a friendly smile.

 

"Haha, thank you, thank you!"

 

The portly man gave Master Ren a grateful nod before turning to Fenric. Noticing his refined appearance, he asked curiously, "Master Ren, is this your son-in-law? What a distinguished young man!"

 

Hearing this, Ren Tingting immediately blushed. Yet, she didn't deny it—not even a single word!

 

"Don't talk nonsense," Master Ren scolded, casting the fat man a glare. "This is the foreign language tutor my daughter invited. He's a top student who just returned from studying abroad."

 

The restaurant owner scratched his head, a little embarrassed. "Ah, I see! A high-achiever from overseas. My apologies, that was rude of me." Then he turned to Fenric again. "May I ask which country you studied in?"

 

Fenric replied casually, "I spent most of my time in the States Nation."

 

The man's eyes lit up. "What a coincidence! The chef behind me was recruited from the S.N Why don't you two have a chat? Maybe you could even give me some suggestions for improving the restaurant."

 1

Fenric turned to the foreigner behind him.

 

His gaze sharpened slightly, and then he initiated the conversation in English.

 

"Cana?"

 1

The white man nodded. "Yes, from North Angeles."

 2

"Oh? N.A.'s a beautiful place. I love the scenery—and especially the Bollywood movies."

 10

"Really? Dude, I love movies too!" The white man grinned, clearly enjoying the common ground.

 

"I'm a big fan of Xavier—he's a master of comedy."

 

"Haha, that guy cracks me up! But honestly, I prefer the actresses."

 

Fenric laughed, then smoothly shifted topics again. "By the way, I didn't catch your name."

 

He deliberately kept the conversation flowing so the foreigner wouldn't get a chance to ask any tricky questions—after all, his own knowledge of foreign countries was limited.

 2

"Jason Downey. You can just call me Jason."

 

"Nice to meet you, Jason. I'm Fen Ric. You can call me Ric. I used to live in Past York's Town. Only recently came back to the country."

 

"Really? I've heard of Past York's Town! People say there are lots of fighting masters there."

 

Fenric chuckled. "That's right."

 

Then he asked, "Jason, what brought you to the People's Republic?"

 

Jason shrugged. "I got into trouble. Beat up a rich guy's son. If I didn't skip town, I'd be behind bars right now."

 1

The entire exchange was conducted in fluent English.

 

The three people at the table were utterly dumbfounded, as if they were listening to some heavenly scripture.

 

Ren Tingting's eyes sparkled as she looked at Fenric. Her face was filled with admiration.

 

She wished she could converse with foreigners as effortlessly as her teacher.

 

Having grown up in the provincial capital, she often encountered foreigners—but she frequently found herself in awkward situations due to the language barrier.

 

At this point, Master Ren had no more doubts about Fenric's background.

 

Being able to chat so naturally with a foreigner—that said it all.

 

As the conversation wrapped up, Master Ren burst into hearty laughter.

 

"Hahaha! Looks like Mr. Fen found a kindred spirit today!"

 

Kindred spirit your ass...

 

Fenric cursed silently, but still kept up a polite smile. "We just exchanged a few words. I hope Master Ren didn't mind."

 

Right then, the restaurant owner chimed in.

 

"Mr. Fen, since you come back from overseas, you must have seen a lot. My restaurant's business hasn't been great lately. Do you have any advice or suggestions?"

 

Fenric smiled faintly.

 

As someone from modern times, he'd seen countless restaurants with all kinds of innovative themes and styles.

 

Trying to stump him with something like this?

 

Impossible.

 

"Then I'll just speak casually."

 

Fenric stood up and began offering his suggestions.

 

"First point—lighting. Boss, the lights you installed are indeed beautiful. Clearly, you put a lot of thought into them. Unfortunately, they're not suitable for this space.

 1

"These lights have limited diffusion. The seats directly under them are bright enough, but the surrounding tables, especially those in the corners, are left in shadow. I assume those seats rarely get occupied? After all, who wants to eat in a dark corner?"

 

The restaurant owner's eyes widened. Clearly, Fenric had struck a nerve.

 

Fenric continued calmly, "I recommend installing a few smaller lights around the edges. They won't cost much in electricity, but they'll make the space feel warmer and more inviting."

 

He paused briefly, then went on, "Now, about the decor—it's another issue. Frankly, your seating style is very generic. People don't come to a Western restaurant just to eat. There's usually a sense of vanity involved—a desire to highlight their status."

 

His words were blunt, and they made both the restaurant owner and Master Ren feel embarrassed.

 

Especially Master Ren—he often invited others to dine at Western restaurants or offered imported coffee during meetings, just as Fenric had described. A matter of face, of image.

 

However, Ren Tingting, listening quietly nearby, looked at Fenric with sparkling eyes. She was completely captivated. In her heart, her teacher was both handsome and brilliant.

 

"The current decor of your restaurant isn't much different from an average local spot. It fails to create a special atmosphere or experience. That's a major shortcoming. I suggest you turn the area by the windows into private booths or alcoves."

 

The restaurant owner quickly asked, "What do you mean by booths or alcoves?"

 

"It's simple," Fenric explained. "Use some wooden boards to create semi-private sections—small enclosed areas with curtains at the entrances. Each one can have a different theme: history, culture, cityscapes, nature, fairy tales—you name it.

 

"For instance, create a booth themed around the story 'Blessings of Love'. Use dim lighting, add a few flower baskets, and set a romantic mood. It's cheap to implement, but young couples will flock to it."

 

'Blessings of Love' was one of the most popular love stories in Jadeveil.

 1

The restaurant owner's eyes lit up as if he'd discovered gold. He looked at Fenric with admiration, clearly recognizing a man of true talent.

 

To think a simple restaurant could be transformed like this...

 

As for Ren Tingting? Well, her gaze was locked on Fenric, and her eyes were practically glowing.

 

Fenric continued sharing layout ideas inspired by modern restaurant design—carefully picking what would fit the current era—and finally said, "The key is to give guests a feeling of luxury and sophistication. Make them feel like they're gaining something—an experience worth talking about. If you can do that, your restaurant won't stay small for long. Word will spread. Even people from the provincial capital might come just to see it."

 

"OOHH—"

 

"What does 'sophisticated' mean?" someone asked.

 

Fenric sipped his coffee, smiling. "High-end. Elegant. Classy."

 

The restaurant owner closed his eyes, processing everything he had just heard.

 

Fenric's insights—drawn from modern-day knowledge—had opened a whole new door for him. He'd never imagined a restaurant could be played like this. Compared to Fenric, he now felt like a clueless country bumpkin.

 

After a long moment, the restaurant owner opened his eyes and looked at Fenric with admiration. Then, unexpectedly, he bent down and bowed deeply.

 

"Sir, your words today have truly enlightened me. I have an earnest request.

 

"Renjia Town is too small. I plan to open a Western restaurant in the provincial capital. I'd like to invite you to become the manager. You'll get half the profits. Would you be willing?"

 

Fenric was stunned.

 

Before he could respond, Master Ren's voice rang out, furious. "Old Lao, have you lost your mind? Mr. Fen is my guest and my daughter's teacher! How dare you try to poach him right in front of me?"

 

Fenric's performance today had left a deep impression on Master Ren. In his eyes, Fenric was no ordinary man—he was a true gem.

 

Although the Ren family still held some local prestige, their influence and wealth had been fading. Master Ren had long hoped to reverse their decline. That's why he'd called on Master Nine before, hoping to change the feng shui of the Ren ancestral grave.

 

But after seeing Fenric today, Master Ren began to realize something else—perhaps the family could enter the restaurant business instead.

 

With ideas like Fenric's, it might not even be difficult to restore the Ren family's glory.

 

"Of course, of course! I meant no offense!" the restaurant owner quickly apologized. "I was simply moved by Mr. Fen's talent and spoke out of turn. Please forgive me, Master Ren."

 

Master Ren's expression softened.

 

But Ren Tingting still gave the restaurant owner a wide-eyed glare—adorably fierce.

 2

Trying to steal her dashing, brilliant teacher?

 

Not a chance!

 

She'd never support his business again!

 1

______

chapters.name: Chapter 120: Chapter 120: Mr. Fen with a Human Face and a Beastly Heart! (4/10)
chapters.content:
Back in Ren Manor.

 

Master Ren's attitude toward Fenric had become noticeably more respectful.

 

"Nephew, make yourself at home. If you need anything, just ask one of the servants!"

 

He used to call him Mr.—now it was nephew.

 

"Thank you, Master Ren," Fenric replied with a polite smile. But inwardly, he sneered:

 

This old man dares to test me? Just wait till I "educate" your daughter later...

 5

Master Ren added, "Then I'll leave Tingting to you. Don't tire her out too much—make sure she gets some rest after her studies."

 

"I know, Father," Ren Tingting replied dutifully.

 

With that, Master Ren left.

 

The moment her father was gone, Ren Tingting turned to Fenric with sparkling eyes. "Teacher, you know so much. Can you teach me how to open a restaurant?"

 

Fenric smiled. "Oh? Done with learning foreign languages already?"

 

Ren Tingting shook her head quickly. "No, I still want to learn! But my family only relies on my father to support everything. I want to help him however I can."

 

She admired Fenric, and wanted to be as knowledgeable and capable as he was.

 

"If that's your wish, then I'll teach you," Fenric said. Then, with a subtle shift in tone, he added, "By the way, Tingting, I wanted to ask you something."

 

Hearing her name spoken so casually, Ren Tingting's cheeks flushed red. She looked down shyly and murmured, "What do you want to ask, Teacher?"

 

"I heard there's a very skilled Taoist in this town—goes by the name Master Nine?"

 

"Yes! Master Nine is amazing. He's great at feng shui, hunting ghosts, exorcisms—you name it," Ren Tingting replied proudly.

 

"I had a run-in with something evil before, and it piqued my interest. I wonder if Master Nine would be willing to teach me a few things?" Fenric asked deliberately.

 

Truly, this guy was shameless—he'd even use someone's innocent daughter to get what he wanted.

 1

Ren Tingting's eyes lit up. "Teacher, you really want to learn Taoism from Master Nine? I can ask my father to speak to him. They're on good terms—he might be able to convince Master Nine."

 

Fenric was secretly pleased, but kept his expression hesitant. "Wouldn't that trouble Master Ren too much?"

 

"It's no trouble. My father has a lot of influence in Renjia Town."

 

However, she hesitated slightly and added, "But Master Nine is quite stubborn. He might not be willing to take on a disciple..."

 

"We'll see how it goes," Fenric said with a smile. "Anyway, today I'll teach you something about foreigners. If you ever open a Western-style restaurant, you'll need to know more than just the language—you'll need to understand the culture too."

 

His sharp hearing picked up on it—someone was eavesdropping outside the door.

 

It wasn't Master Ren.

 

It was that nosy cousin, Weiha!

 

Ren Tingting tilted her head curiously. "What are you going to teach me, Teacher?"

 

"It's a type of foreign dance—called social dance. Want to learn?"

 

"Yes! Teach me!"

 

Fenric smiled and walked over to her, gently taking her into his arms.

 

"Ah!" Ren Tingting gasped, startled by the sudden contact.

 

She had never been this close to a man before. Flustered, she stammered, "T-T-Teacher, what are you doing?"

 

"Teaching you how to dance," Fenric replied with a perfectly serious expression.

 

Outside the room.

 

Hearing voices inside, Weiha's blood boiled. He immediately tried to barge in.

 

But just as he stepped forward, Master Ren happened to pass by.

 

"Weiha, what are you doing here?"

 

"Uncle!" Weiha said urgently. "That guy Fen is a fraud—he's trying to take advantage of cousin Tingting!"

 

"What?!"

 

Master Ren was startled.

 

While he didn't object to his daughter spending time with Fenric, things had to progress gradually. If Fenric was rushing things, that was unacceptable!

 

Determined to protect his daughter's innocence, Master Ren immediately stormed into the room, with Weiha right behind him.

 

But what they saw inside left them speechless.

 

Fenric was standing at the front of the room, speaking seriously. "Good morning means 'good morning'—a common greeting used by foreigners."

 2

Ren Tingting was sitting upright, listening intently.

 

None of the indecency Weiha had imagined was happening.

 

"Master Ren?" Fenric looked up with a surprised and confused expression. "Is something the matter?"

 

Embarrassed, Master Ren shot a glare at Weiha and quickly said, "Oh, it's nothing. I was just wondering if Nephew Fen needed anything from outside."

 

"No need, thank you," Fenric replied with a gentle smile. "The Ren residence has everything I need."

 

"Then I won't disturb you any longer," Master Ren said with a chuckle before closing the door.

 

Once he was gone, Ren Tingting stuck out her tongue playfully and snuck a glance at Fenric before quickly looking away, her cheeks red.

 

That hug from earlier... almost made me pass out from lack of oxygen!

 

It was… a wonderful feeling.

 

Outside.

 

Master Ren scolded Weiha harshly. "What the hell were you doing?!"

 

"Uncle, I swear I heard him trying to seduce cousin!"

 

"Shut up!" Master Ren snapped. "As the security captain of the patrol room, you've been skipping your duties every day. What are you doing, sneaking around here?"

 

He waved his hand impatiently. "Go back to work. Right now."

 

"But Uncle, I'm telling the truth!"

 

"Are you defying me now?!"

 

"N-No..."

 

"Then get back to the patrol room!"

 

With tears in his eyes, Weiha left the Ren residence.

 

That night.

 

Ren Tingting brought up Fenric's interest in studying under Master Nine. Master Ren agreed to speak to the Taoist priest about it the next day.

 

The following day.

 

Master Nine arrived at the Ren household with his two apprentices to discuss the relocation of the family tomb.

 

Inside the study—

 

"Master Ren, I still recommend cremating your father's body," Master Nine said solemnly.

 

He could sense something was wrong with the corpse—change was coming.

 

"No! Absolutely not! My father feared fire his whole life. Cremation is out of the question."

 

Master Nine sighed. "Then… very well."

 

Master Ren changed the subject cautiously. "Master Nine, have you considered taking on a new disciple lately?"

 

"Taking a disciple?"

 

______
