chapters.name: Chapter 121: Chapter 121 – Corpse! Zombies Are Coming! (5/10)
chapters.content:
In the living room.

 

Fenric sat quietly, pretending to read a book.

 

Nearby, Ren Tingting was arranging flowers—or at least pretending to. In truth, she was constantly stealing glances at her teacher, captivated by how elegant and handsome he looked, even while simply reading.

 

He really is so charming, she thought, her gaze lingering. Why is he so attractive even when he's just flipping through a book?

 

At this point, Ren Tingting had fully transformed into Fenric's little fangirl.

 

Elsewhere, the two apprentices brought by Master Nine—Chong and Monmoi—were huddled together, whispering like scheming ghosts. 

 

[TL/n: On the Left is Monmoi (Coward guy) in middle is Master Nine and on the right is Chong(Brave guy)]

 2

"Hey, Chong," Monmoi muttered. "What's the story with that pretty boy? Even Master Ren seems to respect him!"

 

"How should I know?" Chong replied. "But it's not just Master Ren. Didn't you see how Miss Ren was practically glued to him with her eyes?"

 

"Hmph! He's just a pretty face. What's so special about him?"

 

"What? You wanna mess with him?"

 

"Is that really a good idea? If Master finds out, we'll get scolded."

 

"Can you really sit back and watch Miss Ren be taken away?"

 

"…Tsk! Fine, let's deal with him!"

 

Fenric, with his advanced senses, heard every word they said.

 

If this had been the old Fenric, he might have gone up to greet them out of politeness—after all, they were important plot characters.

 

But now?

 

Now, they were just small fries in his eyes. Not worth his time.

 

Still, hearing their scheme brought a plotline to mind.

 

In that particular scene, Chong and Monmoi had used a puppet talisman to control Weiha's body. They made him do all kinds of ridiculous things—slapping himself, stripping in front of Ren Tingting, and acting like a complete lunatic.

 

The memory made Fenric smile.

 

Let's see if such a petty trick could work on me now…

 

A few moments later, Chong and Monmoi crept toward Fenric with the subtlety of mischievous spirits.

 

Ren Tingting noticed them immediately and called out, "Hey! What are you two sneaking up to my teacher for?!"

 

She moved protectively between them.

 

"Teacher, be careful around those two. They're always up to no good."

 

Chong and Monmoi looked deeply offended—especially Monmoi, who had a crush on the lovely Miss Ren.

 

"It's okay, Tingting," Fenric said with a gentle smile. "Besides, they're guests. You shouldn't treat guests like that."

 

Chastised by her teacher, Ren Tingting lowered her head. "Sorry, Teacher. I understand."

 

"..."

 

Chong and Monmoi were both stunned. What kind of magic did he use to make Ren Tingting so obedient?

 

Fenric turned to them. "Is there something I can help you two with?"

 

"Oh, no. We just noticed your extraordinary presence and wanted to introduce ourselves," Chong said while secretly signaling Monmoi with a wink.

 

Monmoi nodded and casually moved behind Fenric, pretending to look around—then quickly plucked a single strand of his hair.

 

"Oh!" he said with a fake laugh. "Mr. Fen, I spotted a white hair and thought I'd help you pull it out. Hope you don't mind?"

 

"Not at all," Fenric replied with a calm smile.

 

Of course he knew exactly what they were up to.

 

Without his cooperation, they wouldn't have been able to touch even a single strand.

 

Seeing that Monmoi had succeeded, Chong quickly said, "We'll stop bothering you now, Mr. Fen. Come on, Monmoi, let's wait for Master outside."

 

"Got it, Brother."

 

The two of them hurried out of the room.

 

Fenric, unbothered, resumed reading—his expression as serene as ever.

 

Outside.

 

Chong pulled out a puppet talisman and carefully wrapped the hair in talisman paper.

 

"Monmoi, you eat it."

 

"Me?! Why me?" Monmoi frowned.

 

"You're the one who pulled the hair!" Chong reasoned. "Come on! Once you swallow it, you'll be able to control that pretty boy's body. Imagine what Miss Ren will think when he humiliates himself!"

 

Monmoi hesitated for only a moment before falling for it. He swallowed the hair in the talisman.

 

Then, he began chanting, fingers forming hand seals.

 

"Is it working?" Chong asked eagerly.

 

"It's done!" Monmoi said, excited.

 

"Alright! Make him slap himself. Let's see how effective it is!"

 

Without another word, Monmoi slapped himself—hard.

 

Inside the living room.

 

Fenric felt a sudden twitch in his right hand.

 

His eyes flickered.

 

But with a single thought, his powerful will instantly suppressed the impulse. His body calmed once again.

 

Interesting…

 

He chuckled softly.

 

With his current level of spiritual strength, it was impressive that the puppet talisman could influence him at all. For an ordinary person, control would've been absolute.

 

"Teacher, is something wrong?" Ren Tingting asked.

 

"It's nothing," Fenric said with a warm smile. Then he teased, "Tingting, that potted flower's about to be massacred by you."

 

"Huh?!"

 

Flustered, Ren Tingting's cheeks flushed. "Hmp! Ignore you!"

 

With that, she scurried off, too embarrassed to stay.

 

Outside, Chong and Monmoi continued watching through the window.

 

"…Why isn't anything happening?" Chong muttered. "Monmoi, did you screw up?"

 

"No way!" Monmoi insisted. "This worked last time! There's no mistake!"

 

"Then what gives?"

 

Just then, Master Ren and Master Nine exited the study.

 

"Master's coming. Let's go meet him," Chong said quickly.

 

"Wait, wait!" Monmoi said, gagging himself and finally spitting out the talisman.

 

Master Nine immediately noticed the suspicious behavior and glared at them.

 

"What are you two up to now?"

 

"N-nothing, Master!" they chorused.

 

Seeing that nothing seemed out of place in the living room, Master Nine frowned but let it go. "Fine. Come on, let's go back."

 

He didn't even spare a glance at Fenric.

 

Fenric sighed quietly. Looks like Master Ren failed to convince him.

 

As expected, once Master Nine left, Master Ren approached Fenric with an apologetic expression.

 

"Nephew Fen, I spoke to Master Nine for you, but… he's not planning to take in any disciples at the moment."

 

"I understand," Fenric replied with a calm smile. "Thank you for going through the trouble."

 

He was a little disappointed, but not overly so.

 

After all, he remembered that in the Samsara Tower, other Samsara players were selling Taoist skills—and they weren't that expensive. Worst case, he could just buy what he needed with some points.

 

Night fell.

 

Spirit Hall grew quiet and still.

 

In the dead silence, beneath the coffin containing an old man's body…

 

A deep crack echoed.

 

From within, a blackened hand covered in sharp claws emerged—slowly pushing the coffin lid open.

 

[TL/n: Spirit Hall is the name of the morgue.]

chapters.name: Chapter 122: Chapter 122: Still Dare to Bite? (6/10)
chapters.content:
The old man's corpse had changed!

 

In the original plot, after the transformation, the first person the old man killed was his own son, Master Ren.

 

That was because once a corpse is transformed into a zombie, it retains fragmented memories and instinctively seeks out people it once knew.

 

Tonight, the plot was unfolding in the same way.

 

Boom! Boom! Boom!

 

In the dead of night, a dark figure dashed rapidly toward Renjia Town.

 

Late Night.

 

Ren Mansion.

 

Lying in bed, Fenric's eyes snapped open.

 

"…You've arrived."

 

Thanks to his extraordinary hearing, he had heard the faint thud of footsteps—heavy, unnatural steps that landed like thunder inside the Ren household.

 

Each step was deliberate and powerful.

 

Clearly, these were not human footsteps.

 

Fenric immediately got out of bed.

 

From a distance, he saw a zombie in a Qing Dynasty official uniform, hopping toward the inner courtyard.

 

Its direction—Ren Tingting's room.

 

Fenric's expression changed slightly.

 

In the original timeline, didn't the zombie target Master Ren first? Why was it after Ren Tingting now?

 

Had his appearance caused a change in the sequence?

 

Actually...

 

That wasn't the case.

 

What Fenric didn't know was that Ren Tingting had recently moved her room closer to the back of the inner courtyard—just to be nearer to her handsome teacher.

 

And zombies, driven by their instincts, seek out relatives first. Since Ren Tingting was closer…

 

She became the first target.

 

Crash!

 

The window burst open, jolting Ren Tingting awake.

 

"Who's there?!"

 

She quickly got dressed and stood up.

 

Suddenly, a large shadow lunged at her.

 

"Roar!"

 

The figure let out a low, guttural growl that clearly didn't belong to a human.

 

Under the pale moonlight, Ren Tingting could see its face—a grotesque monster with green skin and protruding fangs.

 

"AHHH!!"

 

Her scream pierced the night, echoing through the entire Ren residence.

 

Just as Ren Tingting fell into despair, a tall figure descended from the sky—shattering the rooftop as he landed directly in front of her.

 

Like a divine guardian, he shielded her from the monster.

 

Ren Tingting blinked, stunned by the familiar silhouette.

 

It was the very man who'd been occupying her dreams lately.

 

Her handsome teacher—Fenric!

 

Boom!!

 

A heavy impact followed. The zombie was sent flying, smashing through a wall and out the window.

 

Fenric retracted his fist casually.

 

"…Huh. Might've used too much strength. Hopefully I didn't beat him to death. If I did, the plan's going to need a delay…"

 

His current strength attribute was 155 points—

 

Fifteen times stronger than a regular human.

 

A single punch from him could unleash impact forces measured in tons.

 6

"Teacher!"

 

Ren Tingting's panicked voice pulled him back. He turned and asked gently, "Tingting, are you alright?"

 

After two days of interaction, Fenric had grown quite fond of her. She was sweet, polite, breathtakingly beautiful, and had a stunning figure. He wasn't made of stone—of course he felt something.

 5

So, that concern he showed? It was genuine.

 

"Mhm… Teacher, I was so scared…"

 

Without hesitation, Ren Tingting threw herself into his arms.

 

At that moment, a strange warmth washed over her.

 

Pressed against Fenric's firm chest, she felt something she could only describe as… happiness.

 

Just moments ago, that monstrous figure nearly claimed her life. But now, in his arms, she felt utterly safe. Her teacher had descended like a god of war and blown the creature away with a single punch.

 

Fenric smiled, gently patting her back. "Don't worry. As long as I'm here, no one can hurt you."

 

And that wasn't bragging.

 

With his current strength, even if a legion of zombies appeared, he could take them on without breaking a sweat.

 

"Tingting! Tingting! What happened?!"

 

Master Ren's voice echoed from afar.

 

Fenric said softly, "Alright, your father's coming. Get dressed quickly."

 

Reluctantly, Ren Tingting pulled away from his embrace and began putting her clothes back on.

 

But before Master Ren could arrive—

 

"AHHH! G-GHOST!"

 

Another terrified scream rang out.

 

Fenric sighed. "Tingting, don't worry. I'll go save your father."

 

Leaving those words behind, he turned and left.

 

"Be careful, teacher!" Ren Tingting shouted after him.

 

Outside.

 

Master Ren had fallen to the ground, too terrified to move.

 

The transformed corpse—now a zombie—was hopping toward him.

 

Fenric rushed forward.

 

Bang!

 

Another clean hit. The zombie flew again.

 

"Master Ren, are you alright?"

 

Master Ren, still shaking from fear, looked up and saw the powerful figure who saved him.

 

"Nephew! Nephew! Help me!"

 

"Don't worry, Master Ren. I'm here."

 

While reassuring him, Fenric subtly pushed Master Ren back to safety.

 

By now, the household servants had also rushed in—only to scream and scatter again upon seeing the zombie.

 

"Stop yelling! Go get the thickest iron chain you can find!"

 

Fenric barked the order.

 

Hearing his command, the servants seemed to regain composure. One of them quickly ran off toward the warehouse.

 

Fenric approached the zombie.

 

Surprisingly, instead of attacking, the zombie shrank back in fear—curling into a trembling ball.

 

After all, Fenric had already punched it twice. The creature now understood: this human was terrifying.

 

In the original plot, the zombies transformed by the old man's corpse retained a sliver of intelligence. When the Four-Eyed Daoist later subdued one using a spirit-hanging talisman, it showed the same fear.

 

[TL/n: Four-Eyed Daoist and Master Nine. He's a fellow Taoist priest and an old friend of Master Nine.]

 

Fenric narrowed his eyes.

 

"Scared already? So this is the legendary zombie? Hmph."

 2

Of course, he could talk big—his power now far exceeded normal limits. To him, a newly awakened zombie was like a punching bag.

 

As he got closer, the zombie suddenly turned and attempted to flee.

 

Fenric snorted.

 

No words—just fists.

 

Boom! Boom!

 

A series of iron-fist beatings followed.

 

"Stay down!"

 

He activated Armament Haki just to be sure—not that he needed it against this level of threat.

 

Finally, a servant arrived with the chain.

 

Without hesitation, Fenric bound the zombie's upper body tightly with one end and held the other end in his hand.

 

It looked like he was walking a particularly hideous dog.

 

"Master Ren, I'll take this monster outside. No need to let it dirty the place."

 

Master Ren nodded frantically. "Yes, yes! Thank you, nephew. Please—take it away!"

 

In his blind panic, Master Ren hadn't even realized the truth—

 

The "monster" being dragged off like a dog…

 

…was his own father.

 

What a filial father and son indeed.

 

_____

chapters.name: Chapter 123: Chapter 123: This Human Is So Cruel! (7/10)
chapters.content:
Night fell, and silence blanketed the land.

 

On an empty street, two figures suddenly appeared—one was a human dragging a bound zombie.

 

Watching the zombie stumble slowly along, Fenric frowned and snapped,

 

"Move it! What are you dawdling for? Believe it or not, I'll smash you right here!"

 

The zombie trembled in fright, letting out a low, muffled groan.

 

Its intelligence was limited. It didn't understand a word Fenric said—just a pitiful, mindless creature.

 

Fenric ignored it and began contemplating his next move.

 

A single zombie wasn't enough to earn significant points.

 

Fortunately, zombies could infect humans. If enough humans were bitten, Fenric was confident a whole horde of zombies could be produced in no time.

 

His plan was simple—capture a large number of humans and feed them to his zombie.

 9

Once they turned and he finished them off, the points would start rolling in.

 

Don't tell Fenric that zombies are hard to kill.

 

That might apply to ordinary people—but not to him.

 

He possessed overwhelming strength and wielded the black blade Shusui, sharp enough to cleave flesh and bone like paper.

 

If he wanted to, he could turn a zombie into minced meat on the spot.

 

Even the mutated zombie from the original plot, the evolved "Old Man," would be nothing more than a ragdoll for him now.

 

However, Fenric's plan was undeniably vicious, even inhumane.

 

All for the sake of earning points, he disregarded the lives of others.

 

But this is a dungeon. Just like in a game, he never sees them as real people—only as Non-Playable Characters (NPCs). The only ones he sees as living people are those he knows and holds dear. And he's not a good guy in the first place.

 3

Half an hour later.

 

Fenric and the zombie arrived at a mountain not far from Renjia Town.

 

It took him more than an hour to find a well-hidden cave. After driving out a family of wild boars, he claimed it for himself.

 

With Fenric's current strength, the wild boars didn't dare put up a fight—they fled with their piglets without a sound.

 

Inside the cave, Fenric drew Shusui and dug a large pit.

 3

Then he tossed the bound zombie into it.

 

"Until I say otherwise, don't you dare come out and bite anyone. If I catch you sneaking around—believe it or not—I'll hammer you to death!"

 

The threat was laced with Conqueror Haki.

 

Om—

 

The pressure sent shudders through the air.

 

The zombie let out a terrified howl and shrank back. Resistance? Not even a thought crossed its mind.

 

The raw aura of dominance from Fenric made its undead instincts tremble in fear.

 

Next, Fenric rolled over a massive boulder—easily weighing a thousand catties—and used it to seal the pit.

 

He clapped the dust from his hands, satisfied.

 

With his power, moving a boulder like that was child's play.

 

As he made his way back…

 

Suddenly, Fenric halted.

 

He turned to glance at the nearby woods, his eyes narrowing.

 

With his heightened senses, he felt it—something, or someone, was watching him.

 

But the woods appeared empty. Not a single trace of life.

 

Fenric snorted coldly and raised his voice:

 

"Mind your own damn business. Don't you dare mess with what I've hidden. I know where your grave is. If you stick your nose in where it doesn't belong—believe it or not—I'll make sure you vanish for good. Not even your soul will remain!"

 

Leaving those domineering words hanging in the air, Fenric turned and walked away.

 

In this world, zombies weren't the only threat.

 

There were also female ghosts.

 

In the original plot, one even held a deadly grudge against Master Nine's eldest disciple Chong.

 

After Fenric left…

 

A crimson figure appeared in the woods.

 

Staring in the direction he had gone, the woman in red whispered anxiously,

 

"That man… is terrifying."

 

Fenric's body radiated a powerful, masculine energy. His physique was strong, his blood vibrant, and his yang energy overwhelming.

 2

Moreover, with human blood in his hand— a deadly aura clinging to him.

 

Spirits like her instinctively feared people like Fenric.

 

Back at the Ren residence.

 

Master Ren and Ren Tingting were still awake.

 

The events of the day had left them both shaken.

 

"Teacher!"

 

Ren Tingting's eyes lit up the moment she saw Fenric return, and she rushed to his side.

 

It was as if his presence alone gave her peace of mind.

 

Master Ren quickly approached as well. "Nephew, what about that monster?"

 

"Don't worry, Master Ren. It's been handled."

 

Master Ren breathed a sigh of relief.

 

"If it weren't for you, my daughter and I… we wouldn't have made it. Nephew, you saved our lives."

 

"Master Ren, you're too kind."

 

Actually, Master Ren had recognized something strange about the monster—it resembled his late father.

 

He wanted to ask Fenric how he had "handled" it, but the words caught in his throat. Instead, he forced a smile and said,

 

"Nephew, it's getting late. I won't keep you from resting."

 

"Tingting, go to sleep as well."

 

Ren Tingting clung to Fenric's arm and said softly,

 

"Father, I… I'm too scared."

 

Master Ren was at a loss.

 

He couldn't blame her. Truthfully, he was still a little shaken himself.

 

But he couldn't very well ask Fenric to sleep with his daughter, could he?

 

Seeing Master Ren hesitate, Fenric smiled.

 

"Tingting, go rest. I'll stand guard at your door tonight."

 

Master Ren was stunned, then chuckled.

 

"That's very kind of you, nephew."

 

As for Ren Tingting—her heart melted. Fenric's words were sweeter than honey.

 

The next morning.

 

The sun rose.

 

Ren Tingting woke up unusually late—unsurprising, considering how late she fell asleep.

 

As soon as she got up, she ran to the door.

 

Seeing Fenric reading a book on a chair on her door, she couldn't help but smile brightly.

 

"Teacher really stayed up all night to keep watch..."

 

Her heart swelled with joy.

 

"Teacher, are you tired? Do you want to rest?"

 

Fenric shook his head.

 

With his current strength and endurance, he could go three days and nights without sleep if he had to.

 

"Tingting, I want to ask you something."

 

"Teacher, if it's something I know, I'll tell you everything."

 

Fenric smiled.

 

"It's not that serious. I just want to know—who's the worst person in Renjia Town? Someone truly notorious."

 

Before launching his plan, he needed to run an experiment.

 

He had to confirm that killing zombies would actually earn him points.

 

So…

 

Fenric intended to round up some human scum—and offer them up to the zombie in the pit.

 

But just as Ren Tingting was about to respond, Master Nine arrived at the Ren residence with his two disciples, looking anxious.

chapters.name: Chapter 124: Chapter 124: The Shock of Master Nine (8/10)
chapters.content:
"Master Nine?"

 

Master Ren greeted him with a warm smile.

 

"Why are you here so early today?"

 

Master Nine's face was tense with concern.

 

"Master Ren, I came to ask if anything unusual happened at your house last night?"

 

"Something happened? No, nothing at all."

 

Master Ren instinctively denied it—after all, family matters were best kept private.

 

"Really?"

 

Master Nine looked inside suspiciously and spotted Ren Tingting and Fenric standing together.

 

Seeing that both Master Ren and his daughter were perfectly fine, Master Nine frowned in confusion.

 

"That doesn't make sense... Where did that thing go?" he muttered to himself.

 

Master Ren raised a brow.

 

"Master Nine, what exactly is going on?"

 

Master Nine no longer kept it a secret.

 

"I won't hide it. The corpse of Old Master Ren was kept in Spirit Hall. But last night, it transformed."

 

"What?!"

 

Master Ren was shocked.

 

Master Nine continued, "By all logic, a newly risen corpse would return to the place it remembers best—its home. It should've come here first."

 

Then he looked seriously at Master Ren.

 

"Are you sure nothing strange happened last night?"

 

Master Ren hesitated for a moment before sighing.

 

"Well... since you've asked so many times, I won't hide it anymore. Yes, a zombie did show up at my house last night."

 

"What?! Where is it now?" Master Nine asked anxiously.

 

At that moment, Master Ren glanced at Fenric, who stepped forward casually.

 

"I drove it away," Fenric said with a faint smile.

 

Master Nine looked at him in surprise.

 

"And you are…?"

 

Master Ren quickly introduced him, "This is my brilliant nephew I mentioned to you before. He's been wanting to become your disciple and learn the Taoist arts."

 

"Huh?"

 

Master Nine examined Fenric carefully.

 

"With skills like yours, why do you want to learn Daoism from me?"

 

"I'm just genuinely interested," Fenric replied lightly.

 

Master Nine fell silent for a moment, then shook his head.

 

"My teachings aren't something I can pass on so easily."

 

Fenric didn't mind.

 

"No need to explain, Master Nine. I won't force it."

 

In truth, Fenric didn't care too much about becoming a disciple. If he could learn something useful, great. If not, it wasn't a loss. He wasn't about to spend three to five years in this world studying Taoism.

 

He had more important goals—like becoming a god in the Samsara Tower!

 

Master Nine changed the subject.

 

"Mr. Fen, can you tell me where the zombie went?"

 

He was genuinely worried that the creature might still be roaming, posing a threat to others. Zombies like that, once awakened, had tremendous potential for growth—especially after feeding on human blood.

 

Fenric shrugged.

 

"I don't know exactly. I tried to destroy it last night outside Renjia Town, but it was harder to kill than expected. It couldn't beat me, so it ran off."

 

Of course, Fenric couldn't say he was keeping Old Man Ren like a pet.

 

Nor could he claim he'd killed it—there was no body to show for it. If Master Nine asked about the remains, what would he say? Burned it? Then where were the ashes?

 

So saying it fled was the safest option.

 

Monmoi, standing nearby, couldn't help but mutter, "You sure like to brag... You beat a zombie?"

 

Though his voice wasn't loud, they were all close enough to hear.

 

Master Nine scolded immediately, "Monmoi! Shut up!"

 

Fenric didn't even bother responding to someone like him.

 

But Ren Tingting wasn't having it.

 

"Why are you talking like that about my teacher? He saved me last night! I saw it with my own eyes—he punched the zombie and sent it flying!"

 

Hearing this, even Master Nine found it hard to believe.

 

In their experience, zombies had thick skin and were incredibly hard to injure—let alone knock into the air with a single punch.

 

"..?."

 

Monmoi looked utterly heartbroken as he watched Ren Tingting cling to Fenric's arm.

 

His first love was crushed before it even began.

 

Master Nine sighed.

 

"Master Ren, I have to go. I need to track that zombie before it hurts anyone else."

 

"Alright, alright. Master Nine, take care," Master Ren said, seeing him off.

 

After Master Nine left, Master Ren turned to Fenric and asked quietly,

 

"Nephew… did the zombie really run away?"

 

Fenric shook his head.

 

"No, Uncle. That was just a story I told to brush off Master Nine. I buried the zombie deep underground. It won't be harming anyone."

 

He didn't explain further, but Master Ren understood immediately.

 

He gave Fenric a grateful look.

 

"You're very thoughtful, nephew. Thank you."

 

"You're too kind, Uncle."

 

Then Master Ren smiled and said,

 

"You know, calling me 'Master Ren' all the time feels distant. If you don't mind… why not just call me Uncle?"

 

"Sure, Uncle," Fenric replied.

 

The bond between them grew even closer.

 

Master Ren laughed heartily.

 

"Good! From now on, this is your home too. What happened last night—my family owes you everything."

 

"Uncle, you don't have to say that. We're all family now—no need for thanks."

 

"Haha! Well said!"

 

Then Master Ren's expression changed subtly, and he asked,

 

"By the way, nephew… are you married?"

 

"I'm not," Fenric replied without hesitation—conveniently forgetting about his engagement to Commander Lin Mei.

 19

Master Ren let out a sigh of relief.

 

He had been a bit worried about how close Fenric and his daughter had become. But now that he knew Fenric was still single, he had no objections.

 

"!!"

 

Ren Tingting's eyes sparkled with joy, her pretty face lighting up with a bright smile.

 

"By the way, Dad," she suddenly asked, "are there any really wicked people in the poor areas of Renjia Town? Like people who only do bad things?"

 

Fenric had clearly asked her to inquire on his behalf.

 

Master Ren blinked.

 

"Why do you want to know?"

 

"Ahh, don't ask so many questions! Just tell me, please?" Ren Tingting said, tugging at his arm like a spoiled child.

 

Unable to resist her charms, Master Ren gave in.

 

"Alright, alright! If I had to name the worst scumbag in town, it'd be Old Wu. He runs both a casino and a brothel. Ruined countless families."

 

He answered honestly—unaware that his words would seal Old Wu's fate.

 

Tonight, Old Wu would unknowingly become a sacrifice... for a certain zombie old man's appetite.

chapters.name: Chapter 125: Chapter 125: Zombies Who Don’t Know the Meaning of Limits (9/10)
chapters.content:
Night.

 

Wu Laosan had just returned from the casino, swaggering down the street with a few of his lackeys. He was in high spirits, heading off to spend the night with his sixth mistress.

 

But as they passed through a dimly lit alley, a shadowy figure suddenly appeared ahead of them.

 

"Who's there?"

 

Wu Laosan was instantly alert and barked a warning.

 

"Delivery's here," came a voice from the darkness.

 

Wu Laosan was about to ask what the hell kind of courier service delivered at night, but before he could react, a heavy blow struck the back of his head. He collapsed to the ground like a sack of potatoes.

 

The same fate met all his henchmen—taken out in an instant.

 

Once their entire group had been neutralized, a black brick that had been hovering in the air lost its balance and dropped to the ground with a thud.

 

The figure stepped out from the shadows.

 

Bathed in moonlight, he was revealed to be a young man—well-built, graceful, and brimming with quiet menace.

 

"Five…" he murmured.

 

The man—Fenric—walked up to the unconscious gang, tied them all together with a thick rope, and slung them over his shoulder like a delivery package.

 

Five people in total.

 

Even if each one weighed 150 kilograms, that was still 750 kilograms altogether.

 5

But...

 

Fenric carried them effortlessly with just one arm.

 

Soon, he arrived at the cave where he had hidden the zombies.

 

Noticing that the massive boulder blocking the entrance remained undisturbed, Fenric nodded with satisfaction.

 

He had carved a discreet mark into it—if anyone had tampered with the stone, he'd know instantly.

 

Then again, maybe he was overthinking.

 

After all, who could even move a boulder weighing over a thousand pounds?

 

Removing the rock, Fenric slipped into the cave and dumped the five unconscious men onto the ground. He then dug up Old Man Ren, unchained him, and pointed at the pile of bodies.

 

"Here's your dinner. Eat."

 

Fenric had done his homework—Wu Laosan and his crew were complete scum. Feeding them to zombies wasn't just practical, it was justice.

 

However, the zombies still showed fear. Even after being freed, it didn't move.

 

Smack!

 

Fenric slapped its head, startling it.

 

With his strength, even a casual slap could shatter bone.

 

"I said, drink the blood. You understand me?"

 

The zombie stared at him blankly, clearly not following.

 

Fenric sighed and drew his black blade—Shusui. With a swift motion, he nicked Wu Laosan's neck, allowing blood to trickle out.

 

The scent of blood immediately stirred something in Old Man Ren. His face twisted with hunger—but he still hesitated.

 

The psychological trauma Fenric had inflicted was clearly immense. Even now, the zombie didn't dare to act recklessly.

 

Fenric grunted in annoyance and shoved Wu Laosan's limp body directly into Old Man Ren's arms.

 

Only then did the zombie snap, sinking its fangs into Wu Laosan's neck.

 2

"Aaaagh!"

 

Wu Laosan jolted awake, screaming in agony. His eyes widened in horror before rolling back as he passed out again.

 

Zombies feed fast. In mere moments, the blood was drained completely.

 

"You're welcome. Four more to go—have at it."

 

Fenric gestured toward the remaining men.

 

He had noticed two of them were faking unconsciousness.

 

Pretenders, huh? Then sleep... forever.

 

Now understanding what Fenric wanted, Old Man Ren lunged at the other four bodies.

 

"Aaagh!!"

 

"No, please! Help! Someone—!"

 

Ten minutes later...

 

All five had been completely drained.

 

It was obvious that after consuming that much blood, something in Old Man Ren had changed.

 

Her body darkened, skin hardening into a tougher shell. His limbs moved more naturally now, and he walked like a normal person—not with the erratic jumps typical of zombies. Intelligence flickered in his eyes.

 1

He had evolved.

 

What Fenric didn't expect was the look he gave him afterward—cold, feral, almost as if he was considering turning on him.

 

His expression darkened.

 

"Oh? Got a little boost and now you're getting cocky?"

 

His tone was ice-cold.

 

"You dare look at me like that?"

 

Fenric cracked his knuckles.

 

"Let me remind you with my fists—your master will always be your master."

 

OOOOWWWWW!!!

 

A monstrous howl echoed throughout the cave.

 

Ten minutes later...

 

Old Man Ren lay motionless on the ground, looking like a beaten dog.

 

Now he was staring at Fenric again—only this time, with pure terror.

 

"Haven't even warmed up, and you're already done?" Fenric scoffed.

 

"And you dared bare your teeth at me?"

 

Grumbling, he re-chained him and tossed him back into the pit.

 

He didn't resist at all.

 

Once he was buried, Fenric paid no more attention to the five corpses.

 

This cave was well-hidden. As long as he covered it with the boulder again, even if the others turned into zombies, they wouldn't be able to escape.

 

From what he remembered, it took a while for someone to become a full zombie after being bitten.

 

So, he left and resealed the cave, planning to return the next night.

 

The Following Night

 

Fenric arrived at the cave on schedule.

 

As soon as he moved the boulder aside and stepped in, five little figures leapt at him, teeth bared and claws extended.

 

Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

He drew Shusui and slashed the first one cleanly in two—head to waist.

 

"You killed a zombie (Beginner). Gained 100 points!"

 

Hearing the system prompt, Fenric burst into laughter.

 

"It works!"

 

Without hesitation, he cut down the remaining four beginner-level zombies.

 

Against Fenric's raw power and Shusui's legendary edge, these so-called high-defense zombies were no different from regular humans.

 

Unless a high-level zombie showed up—maybe a Level 4—none of them could even challenge him now.

 

All five were killed.

 

Fenric earned another 500 points.

 

Even better, his plan had proven viable.

 

He could already see a flood of points coming his way.

 

As for whether zombies were immortal? Nonsense.

 

Split one from head to toe, and it still dies!

 

In the original story, Master Nine had countless methods to kill zombies. Immortality was just a myth.

 

In the Days That Followed...

 

The townspeople of Renjia began noticing something strange.

 

All the local thugs and bullies—the ones who'd been making life miserable—had suddenly vanished.

 1

Literally gone. As if they'd never existed.

 

The mysterious disappearances quickly attracted attention—even from Master Nine himself...

chapters.name: Chapter 126: Chapter 126: You Want to Stop Me? (10/10)
chapters.content:
Lately, Master Nine had been feeling incredibly annoyed!

 

There were two main reasons.

 

First, a number of people had mysteriously disappeared in town. No one had seen them alive, and no bodies had been found either.

 

Though those who vanished were known scoundrels who preyed on common folk—people whose deaths wouldn't be mourned—Master Nine still felt something was very wrong.

 

Second, he noticed his eldest disciple, Chong, had been acting strangely. The young man wandered about in a daze, with heavy dark circles under his eyes, his energy clearly drained, and his Yang Qi(*masculine life force) dangerously depleted.

 1

From experience, Master Nine could tell—Chong had definitely encountered something unclean.

 

After some thought, Master Nine decided the situation with Chong took precedence. He could investigate the town's missing people later.

 

And so…

 

That night, when Chong headed home, Master Nine secretly followed him. Eventually, he discovered the truth—Chong had fallen under the spell of a female ghost and was spending all his time with her.

 

Furious, Master Nine immediately moved to exorcise her on the spot—but Chong intervened.

 

"Master, please!" Chong pleaded, shielding the ghost.

 

Master Nine let out a long sigh. In the end, he relented, agreeing to spare the ghost—but firmly forbade them from seeing each other again.

 

"Humans and ghosts walk different paths," he said solemnly. "If you keep consorting with her, you'll lose all your Yang Qi and die before long."

 

As the female ghost prepared to leave, she left Master Nine with one chilling remark:

 

"Taoist Master, you're so keen on killing demons, yet someone's using human lives to raise a corpse nearby. Why don't you deal with that?"

 

Master Nine's eyes widened. "What did you say? Don't leave—explain! Who's raising corpses with human lives?"

 

The female ghost hesitated. "That person is terrifying. I didn't dare get too close. But from his appearance and clothing… he seems to be someone quite well-known in town."

 

"What does he look like?" Master Nine asked immediately.

 

"Young. Handsome. Tall. And his eyes… sharp."

 

Chong turned pale. "Master! I think it might be the teacher Master Ren recently hired from her description!"

 

"..."

 

Master Nine didn't answer. Instead, he asked the ghost, "Are all the lives used for the corpse-raising from the town?"

 

She nodded at once. "Yes, all of them. All scum, to be honest. I'm not even sure if he's good or evil! Taking lives to raise corpses, yet he only targets wicked people... It's like fighting poison with poison."

 

Master Nine snorted coldly. "Do you know where he's keeping this corpse?"

 

"I do!"

 

"Then take me there," Master Nine said seriously.

 

He didn't care about evil men being punished—but raising a corpse? That couldn't be allowed.

 

If someone were cultivating a powerful corpse demon, it could endanger the whole world!

 

The full moon hung high in the night sky.

 

Bathed in moonlight, a lone young man left Renjia Town and arrived at a hidden cave in the mountains. With ease, he removed the boulder blocking the entrance.

 

Facing the darkness of the cave, Fenric showed no fear as he stepped inside.

 

Almost instantly, several shadowy figures lunged at him.

 

Without hesitation, he swung his blade.

 

Slice!

 

The shadows were shredded instantly, collapsing to the ground in pieces.

 

Seeing the system prompt flash before him, Fenric gave a satisfied smile and began clearing the remains.

 

This place was no ancient ruin. Right beside the cave, he had dug numerous deep pits, tossing the mangled corpses of low-level zombies into them before covering them up.

 

While he worked, a pale-white, terrifying zombie stood silently nearby, watching him.

 

It was none other than Old Man Ren.

 

But this wasn't the same zombie as before.

 

The last time it tried to escape, Fenric had seen it fly with his own eyes—leaping through the air like it had wings. By traditional zombie classifications, Old Man Ren had reached the "Flying Zombie" level!

 

As Old Man Ren's power increased, so too did its intelligence.

 

It didn't understand what Fenric was doing, but some instinct told it—this human was no benevolent soul. The zombie knew it couldn't win in a fight right now and resolved to keep a low profile, biding its time and growing stronger.

 

One day, when it was strong enough, it would suck Fenric's blood and undergo a true transformation!

 

Eventually, Fenric finished the cleanup and turned to look at Old Man Ren, whose face remained eerily calm.

 

"A fattened pig," Fenric muttered with a faint smirk. "Once fattened, it's ready for slaughter."

 

He knew very well that Old Man Ren was growing stronger by the day.

 

Right now, he could still overpower it. But if this continued unchecked, the day would come when the zombie might surpass him.

 

Fenric wasn't foolish—he wouldn't raise a tiger that could one day devour him.

 

To prevent being betrayed, he planned to begin cultivating a second zombie starting tomorrow. Once that was done, he'd kill Old Man Ren and harvest the benefits.

 

As long as he maintained absolute dominance over these undead, he didn't need to fear rebellion.

 

Yes…

 

If anyone here was a true demon, it was Fenric!

 

Though Old Man Ren couldn't understand human speech, it could feel Fenric's gaze—like that of a butcher eyeing a prize pig. Instinctively, it trembled in fear.

 

"Hm?"

 

Suddenly, Fenric frowned and turned to look behind him.

 

In the distance, four figures were approaching—three men and a female ghost.

 

If Fenric wanted to avoid confrontation, his speed was more than enough to disappear before they arrived.

 

But he didn't move.

 

In this world, no one could make him retreat.

 

Even if Master Ren came, he wouldn't flinch!

 

As a great devil… he had the pride of a great devil!

 2

A few moments later, Master Nine and his group arrived.

 

Monmoi caught sight of the pale-white zombie and exclaimed in horror, "Master! There really is a zombie!"

 

Master Nine's face turned grim.

 

His vision was far sharper than Monmoi's. He immediately recognized that the white-haired zombie was no ordinary creature—it was terrifyingly strong, possibly beyond even his ability to suppress.

 

What confused him, though, was why the zombie hadn't attacked Fenric.

 

In fact… it seemed a little afraid of him?

 

"Mr. Fen," Master Nine said, his voice stern, "so you are raising a corpse here!"

 

"Do you have any idea how dangerous this is? That zombie has already reached the stage of transformation. If it turns violent, no one may be able to stop it!"

 

Fenric didn't answer.

 

Instead, he turned his gaze to the female ghost, his eyes ice-cold.

 

"I warned you not to meddle, didn't I?" he said quietly. "Did you really think I have no way to deal with you?"

 

The female ghost shrank back in terror, her body trembling as she hid behind Chong.

 

"FEN RIC!!" Master Nine roared. "What you're doing is no different from the demonic path! I won't let you harm the living!"

 

"Oh?" Fenric brushed some dirt off his fingers and smiled. "Master Nine, you want to stop me?"

 

He raised his head, eyes gleaming.

 

"Do you really think… you can?"

 

_____

chapters.name: Chapter 127: Chapter 127: He Is the Real Devil!
chapters.content:
Upon hearing what Fenric said, both Chong and Monmoi were instantly enraged.

 

"Master, there's no need to waste words with him! Let's subdue him now!" Chong barked.

 

He was still fuming over how Fenric had frightened Rain earlier.

 

[TL/n: The female ghost name. She's also called the Seductive Spirit. Here's what she looks like.

 16

]

 

Master Nine's face turned grave. He looked at Fenric and asked, "Do you realize how many people will die because of what you're doing?"

 

"Die?" Fenric sneered. "Master Nine, which of these people don't deserve to die?"

 

"Even if they're evil, you can't sacrifice their lives just to feed corpses!" Master Nine retorted.

 

"Master, there's no point reasoning with him! Let's just take him down!" Chong urged again.

 

Master Nine shot him a sharp glare and snapped, "Shut up!"

 

If they could actually defeat that white-haired zombie, did Chong really think Master Nine wouldn't have acted already?

 

Fenric chuckled. "Your apprentice's got the right idea, Master Nine. If you're going to stop me, then hurry up. I'm on a tight schedule—still need to find more sinners to feed my zombies."

 

Hearing this, Master Nine's expression darkened. He could no longer hold back.

 

He shouted to his two apprentices, "I'll handle the zombie—you two, go take care of him!"

 

"Got it!" Chong and Monmoi responded in unison, charging forward.

 

They already found Fenric unbearable.

 

But Rain, the seductive spirit, knew all too well how terrifying Fenric truly was. She quickly grabbed Chong's arm.

 

"Chong, don't go! You can't beat him!"

 

"Rain, don't underestimate me! Trust me, I can handle this!" Chong said confidently, shaking her off.

 

Together with Monmoi, he rushed at Fenric.

 

Fenric simply smiled faintly. With a casual wave of his hand, an invisible force surged toward them—sending both flying back even faster than they came.

 

Midair, the two began vomiting blood.

 1

What Fenric used just now was Mind Impact—a mental shockwave-like force that acted just like a real physical blast.

 5

"!!?"

 

Master Nine was stunned. He immediately shifted to catch Monmoi midair, while Rain flew up to catch Chong.

 

Suspicion flickered in Master Nine's eyes.

 

His apprentices might not be powerful, but they weren't so weak they'd be thrown like ragdolls without even getting close. What kind of technique was that?

 

"What kind of sorcery is this?" he asked in shock.

 

Fenric didn't bother to answer. Instead, he turned to the white-haired zombie and slapped it on the back head.

 

"What are you spacing out for? Didn't you see these two disrespect your master? Go teach them a lesson!"

 

The scene left Master Nine shaken.

 

This wasn't just any zombie—it was a terrifying Flying Zombie! And yet this young man treated it like a dog?!

 

[TL/n: Zombie Ranking: Fresh Corpse → Stiff Corpse → Flying Zombie → Spirit-Bound Zombie → King Zombie.]

 

If the zombie got angry, no one here would escape alive.

 

With their speed, none of them could outrun it.

 

But what Master Nine feared didn't happen.

 

The zombie only growled softly, obediently rising and walking toward his apprentices—not jumping, but walking… with long strides.

 

Yes—walking. Not hopping.

 

Seeing the white-haired zombie approach, Master Nine shouted, "Get back! Now!!"

 

He knew full well he couldn't handle a zombie of this level.

 

"Master, what about you?" Chong asked, panicking.

 

"No time! Go!"

 

Before they could say more, the white-haired zombie lunged at Master Nine with a low roar.

 

Master Nine quickly drew his wooden sword, bit his finger, and smeared his own blood on the blade.

 

In an instant, golden light flared from the sword.

 

With a shout, Master Nine thrust the blade at the zombie. This was one of his most powerful techniques.

 

He dared not hold back against a creature like this.

 

Boom!

 

The sword struck as if hitting solid iron. It failed to pierce the zombie's skin, and the spell on the blade had no effect.

 

Crack!

 

The wooden sword shattered—snapped clean in two by the zombie.

 

Don't be fooled by how obedient the zombie acted around Fenric—it was only because Fenric was terrifying.

 

In truth, this "Old Man Ren" was powerful. A Taoist priest like Master Nine was no match at all.

 

"!!"

 

Master Nine stumbled back in shock.

 

Seeing that even their master's strongest strike was useless, the two apprentices finally grasped how serious things had become.

 

That pretty boy really had raised a monster!

 

"Run! Now!!" Master Nine shouted desperately.

 

He was preparing to sacrifice himself so the apprentices could escape when suddenly—

 

The zombie swerved mid-rush, leaped high into the sky… and tried to flee.

 

Master Nine froze in confusion.

 

Fenric's face darkened. "Ungrateful mutt."

 

With a flick of his hand and a clench of his fingers, he pulled.

 

An invisible force seized the zombie, yanking it from the sky and slamming it back to the ground.

 

The zombie thrashed, trying to claw the earth in desperation.

 

When Fenric began walking over, the zombie whimpered in terror—its mouth letting out a low "Wuuuuu~" sound.

 

Master Nine and the others stared, dumbfounded.

 

How could such a powerful zombie be so terrified… of a human?

 

Finally, Fenric stood over the struggling creature, looking down coldly.

 

"It seems I haven't beaten you in a while. Forgotten how it feels, huh? You ungrateful beast."

 

He rolled up his sleeves, revealing his massive fists.

 

Then—

 

Boom!!

 

One punch.

 

The ground shook with the impact.

 

Fenric hadn't held back. He was furious. That zombie trying to run had embarrassed him in front of Master Nine.

 

"Aghhh!" the zombie howled in agony.

 

Everyone around gasped in horror.

 

Was this really… human strength?

 

Boom!

 

Another punch. The ground trembled again.

 

The white-haired zombie wailed miserably and lashed out with its claws in desperation.

 

"Watch out!" Master Nine warned instinctively.

 

A scratch from this level of zombie wasn't something to take lightly.

 

Rip! Rip!

 

Its claws tore through Fenric's clothes—but couldn't even scratch his skin.

 

Fenric had already activated his Armament Haki.

 

Even if he stood there and let the zombie bite him, it wouldn't break the surface.

 

"Oh? You actually dare to resist? If you ruin my clothes, can you even afford to pay for them?" he said coldly.

 

Then he resumed punching.

 

Boom! Boom! Boom!

 

The repeated impacts made the entire earth tremble like a localized earthquake.

 

Under the merciless onslaught, the white-haired zombie could only howl in pain—its cries eventually growing faint.

 

Master Nine and the others stared, pale-faced, unable to utter a word.

 

This wasn't a man.

 

THIS WAS THE REAL DEVIL!

chapters.name: Chapter 128: Chapter 128: The Demon King Descends, the Dark Age!
chapters.content:
At last, Master Nine and the others finally understood why that zombie had been so terrified of Fenric.

 

Ten minutes later, Fenric finally stopped.

 

Old Man Ren had once again collapsed like a dead dog, lying motionless on the ground.

 

Fenric took a deep breath, feeling inexplicably refreshed.

 

After ten full minutes of venting, his mind had cleared, and his breathing had steadied.

 

Seeing the stunned looks on Master Nine and the others, Fenric chuckled.

 

"Master Nine, sorry about that. I didn't handle this thing properly—let you guys see a bit of a joke."

 

Master Nine looked at him speechlessly.

 

He truly didn't know what to say.

 

The man standing before him was someone who could keep a flying zombie as a pet.

 

"Master Nine, I know what you're worried about. You're afraid this thing will end up harming the world, right? Don't worry. I'll deal with it later. I promise it won't get the chance to hurt anyone."

 

Master Nine couldn't help but respond, "Flying zombies have bodies like iron—invulnerable to swords and bullets. They're almost impossible to kill."

 

"Is that so?"

 

A black blade suddenly appeared in Fenric's hand—out of thin air.

 

Then, with a few swift swipes of the blade—shhk, shhk!—the white-haired zombie's limbs were cleanly severed. In mere moments, it had been chopped into a "+".

 

In truth, the white-haired zombie's defenses were incredibly strong. Its entire body was like steel—true iron skin and copper bones!

 

But in front of the Black Blade, Shusui, it was still laughably weak.

 

Besides, with Fenric's power level sitting at 510, cutting through the zombie's limbs was effortless.

 

"The so-called flying zombie? That's all it is," Fenric said casually, smiling. "Master Nine, can you rest easy now?"

 

Master Nine: "..."

 

…Pretend I didn't say anything!!

 

Even so, zombies really were terrifyingly durable.

 

Even after being chopped up by Fenric, the zombie was still "alive and kicking"—as if nothing had happened at all.

 

In other words, unless the torso or brain was severely damaged, this thing wouldn't die. It had no concept of "vitality" in the human sense.

 

Master Nine asked again, "You're this strong—why are you raising this zombie? What exactly are you trying to do?"

 

Fenric smiled faintly.

 

"I've heard that many foreign invaders have occupied our land, while our government is mired in civil strife, allowing outsiders to trample on the heads of our descendants.

 

As a patriotic man, I feel I should step forward and do something. But, being lazy by nature," he grinned, "I decided to raise a zombie and unleash it upon that aggressor country."

 5

"Let them taste the pain."

 1

"You… really think like that?"

 

Master Nine was stunned.

 

He hadn't expected Fenric to be a patriot?!

 

"Of course. I love this land, Master Nine! This place belongs to us. How can we allow outsiders to run amok here?"

 

After a pause, Fenric added with a smile,

 

"Don't believe me? I'm leaving tonight—taking the zombie with me."

 

Even if Old Man Ren had been reduced to a near-human state, he could still bite. Worst case, Fenric could just catch someone and hand-deliver them to him.

 

"..."

 

Master Nine was convinced.

 1

He had to be.

 

With Fenric's strength, no matter what he intended to do, no one in this world could stop him.

 

The world's current technology was far too primitive. The most powerful weapons were tanks and artillery—nothing that could truly threaten someone like Fenric.

 

Too strong!

 

When you're that powerful… you really can do whatever you want.

 

"Mr. Fen," Master Nine said gravely, "I admire your intentions. But have you considered… if you let zombies loose overseas, what if they eventually make their way back here?"

 

Fenric reassured him, "Don't worry, Master Nine. My first stop is the country who's eyeing our land the most. It's far from here, with an ocean in between. Zombies won't be able to cross easily. And any powerful ones, I'll handle myself."

 1

He clapped his hands.

 

"Alright, Master Nine. I've said all I need to say. No one can stop what I'm about to do. Till next time."

 

With that, Fenric picked up the zombie one-handed, turned, and walked away—without a trace of hesitation.

 

Before heading out tonight, he had already told Ren Tingting he was going abroad to pick up his "sister," and afterward, they'd settle permanently in Renjia Town.

 

Ren Tingting, though reluctant, had agreed for the sake of their future happiness.

 

As for where Fenric would find this "sister"?

 

Heh.

 

In this chaotic world, human life is like grass.

 

It wouldn't be hard for him to find an orphaned little girl to adopt.

 

The two disciples + ghost of Master Nine watched Fenric's retreating figure in silence.

 

After a long pause, Monmoi asked,

 

"Master… is Mr. Fen a good person or a bad one?"

 

Master Nine sighed.

 

"Not a bad person… but his heart is too radical. He does as he pleases—he could easily bring disaster."

 

"Then what should we do, Master?" Chong asked.

 

At that, Master Nine glared at his disciples.

 

"What else? Of course, we train harder! We have to be ready for whatever's coming. I don't know what you two lazy brats are doing all day… Mr. Fen is younger than both of you—look at how capable he is!"

 

Monmoi mumbled,

 

"But Master… even you can't beat Mr. Fen, can you?"

 

Master Nine exploded:

 

"You little brat! What did you just say?!"

 

Three Months Later

 

In Pyong, the capital of the Zion Country, the situation had completely collapsed.

 4

The city had become a zombie paradise.

 

Every night after sunset, zombies could be seen hopping through the streets—utterly terrifying.

 

Countless citizens had fled in panic.

 

Among the religious fanatics, a prophecy spread like wildfire:

 

"The dark age has arrived! Satan walks among us! The extinction of mankind is at hand!"

 1

That night, once again, Fenric roamed the streets of Pyong—hunting for "leeks."

 

He ignored the low-level zombies.

 

After killing over 300 of them, the system had informed him:

 

"Samsara player reward saturation reached. Further kills will yield no rewards."

 

So now, his targets were intermediate and high-level zombies.

 

Intermediate zombie: 300 points.

 

Advanced zombie: 1,000 points.

 

As for anything beyond that… it seemed extremely rare. Fenric hadn't encountered one yet.

 

You ask about Old Man Ren?

 

He'd long been retired, sent off to the "Hell Nursing Home" by Fenric. Whether the "Ren" family accepted him was anyone's guess.

 

After some searching, Fenric found an intermediate zombie in a mansion, sucking the blood of a plump lady.

 

Over the past month, Fenric had discovered something strange.

 

Other than Old Man Ren, who evolved quickly, most twice-infected zombies evolved very slowly.

 

A basic zombie would need to feed on hundreds of people just to reach intermediate level.

 

Fenric was about to harvest his "leek" when suddenly—

 

Ding!

 

"Player Shura, please be advised: the zombie you released has killed the Queen of the Zion Country and caused a major disturbance."

 3

"Notice: Your current world is about to be frozen. You will be forcibly removed in 60 seconds."

 

"Ah?"

 

Fenric blinked.

 

World freeze?

chapters.name: Chapter 129: Chapter 129: One Hundred Thousand Points
chapters.content:
One minute later.

 

Fenric was teleported back to the Samsara Space.

 

The first thing he did was question the system:

 

"System, what does it mean that my personal copy world is frozen?"

 

The mechanical voice of the system echoed in his mind:

 

"Hello, Samsara player'Shura'. When a major negative impact occurs within your personal dungeon world, causing significant disruption to the world's progression, the system will freeze that world temporarily."

 

Fenric was speechless.

 

"All because a queen in name died? How is that considered a major negative impact?"

 

"To the Zion Country in that world, the queen is a spiritual symbol," the system replied calmly.

 

Tch. Fine!

 

It made sense.

 

To Fenric, the queen was just an old hag he slaughtered without a second thought. But to the citizens of the Zion Country, that woman—their monarch—meant everything.

 

In fact, when Fenric wreaked havoc in Pyong, the political ripples had already begun. Rumor had it the Zion Country's government pulled all its troops from other countries just to quell the domestic unrest.

 4

Peace?

 

With Fenric around, peace was a luxury that no one could afford.

 

By that logic, the turmoil he caused really had disrupted the world's narrative flow.

 

"What happens to a frozen personal copy world? When can I unseal it?" he asked again.

 

The system explained:

 

"Once frozen, the flow of time in that world is completely halted. To unseal it, you must obtain partial authority over the Samsara Tower."

 4

So it can be unsealed.

 

Fenric finally felt some relief.

 

After all, personal copy cards were rare and precious. To him, personal dungeons were like private gardens. Losing even one would be a painful blow.

 

He shifted gears and began checking the earnings from this latest dungeon run.

 

Samsara Points: 102,336!!

 1

That was Fenric's current point balance.

 

Seeing those six digits, he couldn't help but grin.

 

Three months!

 

It had taken three long months to amass that kind of wealth!

 

This was, by far, the most lucrative run he'd ever done.

 

It was a massive improvement over the last personal copy.

 

Still, Fenric wasn't in a rush to spend the points. First, he planned to check out the available dungeons on the Fourth Stage of the Samsara Tower.

 

Ding!

 

"You have a new communication message. Aurora Morwyn invites you to a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

Seeing the message, Fenric raised an eyebrow in mild surprise.

 

Without thinking too much of it, he accepted.

 

Aurora Morwyn's figure appeared on the screen.

 

"Ms. Morwyn, is something the matter?"

 

"Shura, stop calling me 'Ms. Morwyn'. At the rate you're growing, you'll surpass me soon enough. What then—should I start calling you Mr?"

 1

Aurora smiled, then added, "If you really see me as a friend, just call me Aurora."

 

Fenric chuckled.

 

"Alright then, Aurora."

 

"Shura, about the 'One Piece' copy from last time—you know, the one you... heavily impacted—I've looked into it."

 

"Turns out, only the players who were running that copy alongside you were affected. Meaning, future instances of the 'One Piece' dungeon might diverge for each user."

 

"Oh?"

 

Fenric was intrigued. Then another thought struck him.

 

"Wait—that doesn't make sense. What happens if I enter the second phase of the 'One Piece' dungeon and run into a player whose story hasn't diverged from the original?"

 

"That's a valid paradox. There's no clear answer yet," Aurora admitted. "My personal guess is the system will default to one timeline, probably the one that's dominant. After all, two conflicting storylines can't exist in a single world."

 

Fenric frowned.

 

He didn't like uncertainty.

 

Still, even if he could go back and do it again, he would still kill the Celestial Dragon.

 

He didn't regret anything.

 

"Shura, are you free right now? Want to meet up and chat?" Aurora suddenly asked.

 

Fenric paused, instantly sensing there was more to this.

 

But he was free, so he replied:

 

"Sure. Where to?"

 

"Let's meet at the teahouse. Bars are too noisy for proper conversation. I booked Box 2779—come straight there."

 

"Alright, see you soon."

 

After ending the call, Fenric made his way to the teahouse.

 

There, in the private box, he met Aurora Morwyn.

 

"Shura, take a seat. What do you want to drink?" Aurora asked.

 

"Same as you."

 

"Got it."

 

Aurora ordered two cups of Calming tea.

 

Then silence fell between them.

 

It was obvious Aurora had something important to discuss, but she seemed hesitant.

 

Fenric broke the tension with a smile.

 

"Aurora, I'm not a fan of beating around the bush. If you've got something to ask, just say it."

 

Aurora exhaled.

 

"Alright then. Shura, once the cooldown ends, you plan to challenge another dungeon, right?"

 

"That's the plan." Fenric nodded.

 

"Do you know which dungeon you'll take on next? Specifically, which one on the Fourth Stage?"

 

Fenric scratched his head.

 

"Actually, I don't even know what options are available on the Fourth Stage yet."

 

Aurora filled him in.

 

"There are two dungeons on the Fourth Stage. One is harder: 'Venom: Deadly Guardian'. The other's considered easier: 'Strange Forms'."

 8

She quickly added, "Although 'Strange Forms' seems easier, it's not simple. The monsters in there are terrifying. They multiply rapidly and can only be effectively dealt with using fire."

 2

Hearing those names, Fenric's eyes gleamed.

 

He was familiar with both.

 

"Aurora, which one did you pick?"

 

"Venom: Deadly Guardian," Aurora replied.

 

"What's the main task?"

 

"Kill a symbiote," Aurora said. "It's hard to get a high evaluation in that dungeon. There aren't many symbiotes, and they're strong—but they do have weaknesses: they're vulnerable to loud noise and fire."

 4

Fenric's expression sharpened slightly.

 

After thinking for a moment, he said,

 

"I haven't made a decision yet. I'll have to consider it carefully."

 

"You definitely should."

 

Aurora took a sip of tea and finally got to the real reason for their meeting.

 

"Shura... I actually wanted to ask you for a favor."

 2

________

 

The Mr. Vampire Arc is finally complete!

 2

Now, let's talk about what's coming next — the Venom Arc, which will span 13 chapters in total!
