chapters.name: Chapter 130: Chapter 130: Venom – Deadly Guardian!
chapters.content:
"Aurora, just say it outright."

 1

Fenric smiled and added, "If it's something I can help with, I definitely will."

 

Then, silently in his heart, he added: If I can't help… I definitely won't lift a finger.

 

Aurora said seriously, "Over the years, I've made a lot of enemies. They can't touch me directly, but they might retaliate through my family. I have a cousin I'm close with. She's also in the Samsara Space and will soon reach the Fourth Stage."

 

Fenric frowned slightly at that.

 

Is she going to ask me to carry someone through a dungeon?

 

If that was the request, then sorry—he'd refuse without hesitation.

 2

Fortunately, Aurora wasn't so shameless. She didn't make any unreasonable demands.

 

"It's actually not a big favor," she continued. "Entering the Samsara Tower is dangerous—that's something everyone accepts. Shura, if you happen to meet my cousin in a dungeon, could you look after her a little?"

 

"If it's just lending a hand when possible, that's no problem," Fenric replied. "But... what kind of help are you talking about? Don't tell me you want me to form an alliance with her?"

 

"Of course not!" Aurora Morwyn laughed. "Her name is Belle Morwyn. If you see her in danger, just help her out."

 1

"Oh, that's no big deal."

 

Since it was just a favor based on convenience, Fenric had no issue agreeing.

 

Aurora added, "Shura, don't feel obligated just because it's me. If the situation is too risky, you don't need to get involved. Your life is more important than hers. A lot of people see you as a once-in-a-generation genius—they have high hopes for your future."

 

Fenric nodded, but thought to himself: Girl, you don't need to tell me twice. If your cousin ends up in a situation that even I can't handle... trust me, I'll run faster than anyone else!

 7

"By the way, Aurora," Fenric suddenly asked, "do you know if anyone's selling dungeon cooldown refresh cards?"

 

Aurora Morwyn was momentarily stunned, then let out a wry laugh. "Shura, you're really relentless. You must want the refresh card so you can clear more dungeons, right?"

 

She went on, "Actually, a lot of people have cooldown refresh cards. I have two myself."

 

Fenric was surprised. "Then why haven't I seen any for sale at the consignment center?"

 

"Because no one buys them!"

 

Aurora explained, "You think everyone's like you? So eager to clear dungeon after dungeon? People like us sometimes avoid dungeons for months if we're not fully prepared. The Samsara Tower is lethal. Fail a mission, and you die. Who's in a rush to throw their life away?"

 

Fenric: "…"

 

Fair point.

 

Others weren't like him. He had knowledge of the plot—a cheat-level advantage—so he could approach dungeons with confidence.

 

But other people? They didn't have that luxury. Naturally, they'd be more cautious.

 

"But couldn't people sell them to players in the Safe Zone? Missions there don't kill you. Someone would buy them, right?"

 

"The Safe Zone?" Aurora sighed. "That place is full of broke newbies. If they earn 1,000 points from a dungeon, it's a huge windfall. Do you think they can afford to pay good money for a cooldown card?"

 

"If they're only selling for a few hundred points, might as well keep it," she added.

 

"In short, we usually use these cards for favors—giving them to juniors or new recruits so they can advance more quickly in the Safe Zone. If we ever sell them, it's usually for cash. But most people who own cooldown cards are already rich, so they don't need to sell."

 

Fenric finally understood.

 

He had assumed the cooldown refresh card was a rare and valuable item.

 

Turns out, the reality was completely different.

 

"If you really want one, I'll give you mine," Aurora offered without hesitation.

 

Fenric's eyes lit up, though he quickly put on an embarrassed expression. "Wouldn't that be too much?"

 

"It's fine. I'm not using them anyway."

 

Despite her words, Aurora couldn't help but sigh inwardly.

 

Her next dungeon was on the 29th floor—Avengers 3. Rumor had it that a terrifying purple-skinned monster appeared in that one, and she wasn't confident she could clear it.

 6

Fenric smiled. "Well, if you insist, I won't say no."

 

"The tea's done. Shura, let's head to the trading center."

 

That made Fenric blink. "Wait... even gifts have to go through the trading center?"

 

"Of course!" Aurora looked at him strangely. "Didn't you know? Whether it's a gift or a trade, any special item has to go through the trading center. Once it's transferred, it can't be given to anyone else for three years."

 

"That's a rule of the Samsara Space. It's meant to prevent people from extorting items out of others—or abusing trade loopholes to rack up a ton of Samsara points and ascend to 'godhood' in a short time."

 

Fenric suddenly understood.

 

After that, the two of them went to the trading center. Under the system's supervision, Aurora officially transferred two cooldown refresh cards to Fenric.

 

Two cards, absolutely free. Which made Fenric thrilled.

 

To most players, the cooldown cards weren't that useful.

 

But to Fenric, they were extremely valuable.

 

If he wanted to get stronger fast, he had to keep grinding dungeons.

 

The next day.

 

Fenric went back to school.

 

He hadn't planned to attend anymore, but with only six days left before the college entrance exam, he figured he should show up—at least to avoid a lecture from his father.

 

When he entered the classroom, he noticed something strange: many students were looking at him with a mix of awe and fear.

 

"Ric! Ric!" Fatty Jitto called out as soon as he sat down. "After school yesterday, how did you scare Tazhan so badly he peed himself?!"

 

"They said your aura was terrifying! How did you get so scary, man?"

 1

Hearing this, the nearby students pricked up their ears in curiosity.

 

"It's called 'killing aura,'" Fenric replied casually, raising his voice on purpose. "You get it by killing enough people in the dungeons."

 2

"Holy sh*t! Big bro, you're amazing!" Jitto gasped, momentarily speechless.

chapters.name: Chapter 131: Chapter 131: The Boldest Plan Is Born!
chapters.content:
"So the aura around him… was actually cultivated through killing?"

 

"I didn't expect it. Fenric actually has that kind of nerve? He dares to kill?"

 

"Practicing aura through murder? That's insane!"

 1

"Seriously. People in the dungeons are still living beings."

 

"Better stay away from him from now on. Don't provoke him either. I heard that if someone kills too much, they start accumulating a heavy evil aura... makes them bloodthirsty."

 

"Is it really that scary?"

 

Fenric chuckled faintly as he listened to the whispers around him.

 

He had said those things on purpose.

 

And the results were excellent.

 

These students were clearly afraid of him now.

 

Good.

 

The next few days should be... nice and quiet.

 

Just then, a familiar voice called out behind him.

 

"Ric, did you hear? Tazhan filed his withdrawal this morning. He's going to study at home for the next few days."

 

A plump student walked up, grinning smugly. "You must've scared the hell out of him yesterday. After losing face like that, the guy doesn't even dare come back to school!"

 

Fenric paused at the news, then laughed.

 

Not because he had frightened Tazhan—but because the effect of his Conqueror's Haki was simply too satisfying.

 

Dominance is dominance, after all. And it worked like a charm.

 

In the early stages, Conqueror's Haki was particularly effective at clearing out the small fry.

 

Back in his personal instance of "Mr. Vampire", Fenric had released zombies in Pyong and ended up surrounded by military forces.

 

But then—

 

He just stared.

 

And all those soldiers collapsed.

 

People were horrified on the spot.

 

Some even started calling him "Satan," the Demon Lord himself!

 

If he had enough points to upgrade his Conqueror Haki to the later stages—just like Red-Haired Shanks—even enemies on the same level as him would find themselves overwhelmed by its pressure. Their combat strength would plummet in his presence.

 

Ignoring the buzzing around him, Fenric took out his phone and opened the Samsara Forum.

 

He started browsing information related to the Fourth Stage of the Samsara Tower.

 

After his conversation with Aurora last night, Fenric had learned that, like the Second Stage, the Fourth Stage also had two dungeon options:

 

One was the "Easy" difficulty: Strange Forms.

 

The other was the "Hard" difficulty: Venom.

 

He pulled up the official guide and began reading.

 

[Guide: Samsara Tower – Fourth Stage Dungeons]

 

Just like the Second Stage, the Fourth Stage offers two dungeons for Samsara to choose from.

 

Easy-Level Dungeon: "Strange Forms"

 2

This instance features a terrifying, highly contagious monster.

 

A single touch is enough to infect someone.

 

After being infected, the person can still blend into crowds like a normal human—making it incredibly hard to detect.

 

The mission objective is to eliminate at least one of these creatures.

 

But beware: These monsters can divide infinitely. Even if you slice one into a pulp, it can regenerate from the smallest scrap—creating countless smaller versions of itself.

 6

The only truly effective method of eradication? Burn it. Monsters in this dungeon are terrified of fire.

 

Note from the editor:

 

Based on gathered intel, this dungeon is surprisingly dangerous despite being labeled "easy." Prepare accordingly—especially with protective gear to avoid infection.

 

Hard-Level Dungeon: "Venom: Deadly Guardian"

 1

Set in a technologically advanced modern world, this instance's mission is to kill at least one symbiote within 30 days.

 

Be advised: There are only four symbiotes in total.

 2

This means that if more than four people enter the instance at the same time, someone will fail their mission. Time your entry strategically!

 

After entering, you'll be allowed to customize your appearance and background, but the identity must be plausible within the instance's world. No making up fantasy roles like a fairy queen or divine guardian.

 

Ideally, players should create a persona that can get close to Carlton Drake—the head of the Life Foundation and lead scientist overseeing most of the symbiote experiments.

 2

Additional intel:

 

Symbiotes are alien organisms resembling black slime.

 

They require a host to survive and grant immense power.

 

Carlton Drake will eventually become host to a powerful symbiote.

 

Symbiotes are weak to high-decibel sound and fire. Loud noise can force them to separate from their host, while fire can kill them outright.

 

Important tip:

 

Have at least one sound-based or fire-based item ready before entering!

 

The real challenge in this dungeon isn't completing the task—it's getting a high evaluation.

 

With only four symbiotes available, competing players will struggle to score high.

 

For example, killing just one symbiote will net a C-rank result.

 

One top-tier player once killed all four and received an A-rank reward.

 1

How you approach this… is up to you!

 

After reading the entire guide, Fenric suddenly smiled.

 

Very soon…

 

He made up his mind:

 

Tonight, he would enter the "Venom" instance!

 1

Even with all the details in the guide, one crucial piece was still missing—

 

The plot.

 

But Fenric had watched the original movie.

 

He knew every twist and turn, including the most critical events.

 1

In his mind, a plan slowly began to take shape…

 

A bold plan. So bold, it could easily get him killed.

 3

And yet—Fenric decided to go through with it!

 1

For the rest of the day, Fenric was deep in thought, refining his strategy.

 

Even with his current strength, this plan was risky.

 

Very risky.

 

But if he wanted a high evaluation—and maybe more—he needed to be prepared…

 

And he would be.

chapters.name: Chapter 132: Chapter 132: He Is Your Idol! (1/8)
chapters.content:
Midnight.

 

Fenric appeared in the Samsara Space on time.

 

After checking his contact list and confirming that Aurora hadn't arrived yet, he headed straight for the Samsara Tower Mall.

 

He needed to prepare for a bold plan in the upcoming "Venom" dungeon.

 

As he walked into the center of the mall, a series of holographic projection screens flickered to life around him.

 

Opening the item catalog, Fenric searched for specific types of equipment—items capable of producing flames or generating high-decibel noise.

 

To his surprise, he actually found something.

 

Special Item: Enchant Whistle

 

Emits a high-decibel sound that causes auditory hallucinations in enemies. Highly effective against sound-sensitive targets.

 

Price: 8,300 Samsara Points

 

Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

This item would be extremely effective against symbiotes.

 

However... the price was outrageous!

 

"Seriously? A whistle costs this much? The Samsara Tower Mall really knows how to rob people blind!"

 

There was no way he'd burn that many points just to clear a single dungeon.

 1

Fortunately, the mall always offered a compromise. For every permanent item, there was usually a cheaper, disposable version available.

 

Sure enough, Fenric soon found it.

 

Special Item: Enchant Whistle (One-Time Use)

 

Emits a high-decibel sound that causes auditory hallucinations in enemies. Highly effective against sound-sensitive targets.

 

Price: 1,150 Samsara Points

 

Note: After use, the whistle loses its enchantment and becomes a regular whistle within ten days.

 4

Ten days?

 

More than enough.

 1

Fenric chuckled and clicked Buy.

 

A moment later, the whistle appeared in his personal inventory.

 

Next, he searched for items that could produce flames—but the results were disappointing.

 

All he could find was something labeled:

 

Special Item: Infinite Energy Ignition Machine

 

...That sounded like a fancy name for a lighter.

 

An unlimited-use lighter. It never needed fuel and could ignite endlessly.

 

But what good would a tiny flame do against a symbiote?

 

"What am I going to do, poke it to death with a lighter?" Fenric scoffed. "That thing would laugh itself into a coma."

 2

Leaving the Samsara Tower Mall, Fenric noticed Aurora was finally online.

 

He immediately initiated a video call.

 

"Shura? You're the one calling me? That's rare," Aurora said, appearing in the video feed. "What's going on?"

 

Fenric smiled. "I do need something. Are you free right now?"

 

"I just log in every day to check things out. Of course I'm free."

 

"Then come meet me at the tea house, Room 2217. I want to discuss something with you."

 

Tea House – Room 2217

 1

"Take a seat. I've already ordered your favorite, Calming tea," said Fenric, gesturing toward the table.

 

Aurora entered with a smile. "So, what's the matter? Just tell me~"

 

Fenric nodded. "Alright. I called you here because I want to propose a collaboration."

 

"Oh?" Aurora Morwyn perked up immediately.

 

The man in front of her—Shura—was a top-tier player recognized by all the major factions.

 

Every time he entered a dungeon, it was either a crushing victory or a brutal slaughter.

 

If someone like him wanted to cooperate, it must be something big.

 

"Shura, what kind of cooperation? Don't tell me... you've finally decided to join us?" she asked excitedly.

 

Fenric chuckled and shook his head. "I prefer my freedom. I don't like being bound by organizations. More precisely, I want to collaborate with your cousin this time."

 

He leaned forward slightly.

 

"Tonight, I'm heading into the fourth-level dungeon, Venom. If your cousin joins me, I can't promise a top-tier evaluation, but she'll definitely complete the mission without a hitch."

 

Aurora's eyes sparkled.

 

A smart girl like her immediately cut to the chase.

 

"Shura, what's the price?"

 

Talking to intelligent people always saved time.

 

Fenric grinned. "You know that symbiotes are afraid of fire, right? I'm currently short on an item that can unleash large-scale flames. Do you think your cousin can provide something like that?"

 

Of course, while he said "your cousin," this request was clearly aimed at Aurora herself.

 

After all, what kind of newbie on the Fourth Stage would have access to rare items?

 

Aurora paused for a moment, thinking.

 

"I'm not sure about permanent fire-breathing props," she admitted, "but I can definitely get you a one-time-use version. Will that work?"

 

"Oh? What kind of item?" Fenric asked with interest.

 

She thought for a bit before replying, "It's called the Enchanted Flamethrower. It has limited magic fuel inside and can last a few days."

 

That was nearly identical to the whistle he had just purchased.

 

"Its what I want!" Fenric grinned.

 

A permanent fire-breathing item would've been akin to having a fire-based ability—far too valuable to ask for. He didn't expect to get one anyway.

 

Aurora smiled. "Give me an hour. I'll get it."

 

"No problem."

 

Once she left, Fenric remained seated in the tea room, waiting patiently.

 

Real World – Capital City

 

In a dimly lit antique room, a woman appeared out of thin air.

 

She stood over 1.7 meters tall, with long legs that seemed to go on forever. Her features were sharp, with sword-shaped eyebrows and bright, star-like eyes.

 1

Most notably, she exuded the aura of a dominant Onee-san—powerful and composed.

 1

This was the true form of Aurora Morwyn, real name Vivienne.

 

After materializing in the real world, she immediately picked up her phone and dialed her cousin.

 

"Hello? Cousin?" came a sleepy, feminine voice on the other end.

 

"Yuhan, you're still sleeping? Get up and log into the Samsara Space!"

 

"Ugh... Cousin, can't I have five more minutes? I gamed all day. I'm exhausted…"

 

Aurora chuckled and scolded, "Lazy girl. Haven't you always wanted to clear the fourth-level dungeon? Well, I found someone to take you through it tonight!"

 

"What?!!" The voice immediately sharpened, suddenly wide awake. "Really? Who?"

 

"It's your idol—Shura."

 

As soon as she said it, a loud, excited scream nearly broke the speaker:

 

"WAAAAAHHH!!!"

 

"Cousin, you're the best!!"

 

Aurora rolled her eyes. "I'll give you one minute to get dressed. Move it."

 

"No need! I'll be ready in 30 seconds!! Bye!"

 3

After hanging up, Aurora shook her head in exasperation, then smiled.

 

She had practically raised her cousin. The two had shared many hardships, even life-and-death moments, and their bond was unshakable.

chapters.name: Chapter 133: Chapter 133: Shura Boss Has Started! (2/8)
chapters.content:
Shura!

 

In the Samsara Space, this name has become synonymous with the "Super God" rating.

 

Countless players dream of joining the Shura Boss in a dungeon run—just being on the same team guarantees success.

 

But...

 

The Shura Boss is notoriously cold and has blocked all stranger communications, making it almost impossible to get in touch with him.

 

Now, for the first time, Shura is actually willing to take someone into a dungeon run—and that someone is her! Yuhan was so excited she could hardly contain herself.

 

She had no idea how her cousin managed to get Shura to agree, but she didn't care—this was incredible news.

 

Getting personally guided by Shura was like eating scraps from a king's feast. If the boss gets the meat, she's more than happy with the soup!

 

Within just ten seconds, Yuhan had thrown on some clothes—no makeup, no prep—and logged directly into the Samsara Space.

 

After all, your real appearance didn't matter here. Everyone's look was virtual anyway.

 

"Cousin!"

 

Belle Morwyn—Yuhan's in-game name—immediately called her cousin, Aurora Morwyn, via video chat.

 1

"Come to Private Room 2217 at the teahouse. Shura and I are waiting for you," Aurora replied calmly in the video.

 

Belle ended the call and hurried excitedly to the teahouse.

 

There, in the box, she saw her cousin—and her idol.

 

God Shura!

 

In reality, Shura had only just broken through the fourth level of the Samsara Tower. Technically, he'd just stepped out of the rookie bracket.

 1

But!

 

That didn't matter—not when he repeatedly earned SSS (Super God) ratings while running dungeons.

 

Everyone with half a brain could tell—it was only a matter of time before this guy became a true top-tier boss.

 

At this rate, it wouldn't even be a surprise if he eventually became the No. 1 player in the entire world.

 

How could anyone else even compare?

 

"Cousin, Lord Shura! Hello, it's an honor to meet you!"

 

The moment she stepped into the box and saw Shura—masked like an assassin—Belle was overwhelmed with excitement and bowed deeply.

 

Aurora introduced her with a smile.

 

"Shura, this is my cousin, Belle Morwyn."

 

"Hello."

 

For Aurora's sake, Fenric—Shura's real identity—responded politely.

 

"It's an honor to see you, Lord Shura!" Belle repeated, glowing with admiration.

 

"She's been idolizing you forever," Aurora added with a soft laugh.

 

Fenric merely smiled in return.

 

The two then added each other as friends.

 

Just then, Aurora stood up.

 

"Shura, take your time chatting with Belle. I'll go get the fire-breathing props you asked for."

 

"Thanks. I appreciate it."

 

After she left, only Fenric and Belle remained in the box.

 

"Want something to drink?" Fenric offered.

 

"No need, Lord Shura. I'm not thirsty at the moment," Belle replied politely, like a refined mage.

 1

Fenric chuckled and ordered her a cup of Calming Mind Tea anyway.

 

When the tea arrived, he got down to business.

 

"The dungeon this time is 'Venom.' Do you have any questions?"

 

"None!"

 

How could she question anything the great Shura said?

 

"I can't guarantee what kind of rating you'll get from this dungeon, but I'm confident you'll be able to complete it smoothly. Think it over first."

 

"Great God Shura, I'll follow your lead. I have no objections at all!"

 

Belle was fully prepared to go along for the ride.

 

Fenric shook his head inwardly.

 

This girl trusts me way too much...

 

"By the way, what's your current strength rating?" he asked.

 

"Just C-rank," she replied, lifting her fair arm to show him her interface.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed slightly with interest.

 

"Your last dungeon was 'One Piece,' right? You got a Devil Fruit?"

 

"Yes!" Belle Morwyn nodded. "It's not a particularly strong Zoan type. I didn't really understand anything at the time, so I just ate it. My cousin even scolded me for it."

 

Now Fenric was really intrigued.

 

"Which fruit was it?"

 

"Zoan-Type: Cat-Cat Fruit, Leopard Form!"

 2

Fenric's interest sharpened.

 

He recalled that in the original One Piece story, Rob Lucci from CP9 had that same fruit—and he was no joke.

 

The fruit itself wasn't weak at all—it just needed a strong body to unlock its full potential.

 

"Can you show me your ability?"

 

Belle hesitated, clearly flustered.

 

Fenric remained composed on the surface.

 

"I need a clear reference point to assess your strength before we enter the dungeon."

 

"A-alright then..."

 

She closed her eyes.

 

The transformation began.

 

Cat ears sprouted atop her head, leopard-like markings bloomed on her shoulders like tattoos, and her nails grew long and razor-sharp.

 

The biggest change was at the base of her spine—she now had a long, slender tail.

 

Rip!

 

Her tail tore right through her pants.

 

The transformation was complete.

 

A sleek and seductive "catwoman" now stood before Fenric.

 

Despite himself, even Fenric's heart skipped a beat at the sight.

 

Her tail in particular stirred a strange urge within him...

 8

"Ahem! Okay, that's enough."

 

Fenric quickly composed himself and tried to act calm.

 

Belle let out a sigh of relief and promptly returned to her normal form. Her torn clothes automatically repaired themselves—one of the many perks of the Samsara Space.

 

Fenric remembered something else and casually asked,

 

"By the way, do you know which Devil Fruit your cousin ate? I got the feeling she kind of regretted it."

 

Belle shrank back slightly.

 

"I... I don't dare say. If she finds out I spilled it, she'll kill me..."

 7

Meanwhile…

 

After leaving the box, Aurora immediately initiated a call.

 

A man dressed like an ancient swordsman appeared in the video.

 

"Yo! Miss Aurora? What made you reach out to me today?"

 

Aurora's voice was calm and commanding.

 

"One Leaf Knows Autumn, if I remember correctly, you still owe me a favor... or am I wrong?"

 2

"That's right! What do you need? Just say the word, I won't hesitate," One Leaf Knows Autumn replied with a grin.

 

"No need to jump into fire or climb a blade. I just need your enchanted flamethrower—the one-time-use special item."

chapters.name: Chapter 134: Chapter 134: Only Shura Dared to Play Like This! (3/8)
chapters.content:
"Alright! No problem!"

 

One Leaf Knows Autumn replied with a somewhat shy smile. "As long as Miss Aurora asks, even if it's not a disposable item but a permanent one, I'll still give it without hesitation!"

 

Of course, Aurora merely listened to his words casually.

 

What a fool.

 

"Okay, are you free right now?" Aurora asked.

 

"I'm at a bar, having a drink. Want to join me, Miss Aurora?"

 

Aurora ignored the invitation. "I'll meet you at the Trading Center—make it quick."

 

"So eager? Miss Aurora, is this for your cousin?" One Leaf Knows Autumn asked with a smile.

 

He assumed Aurora had no use for the item himself.

 

"No."

 

"Oh?" One Leaf Knows Autumn was surprised. "Then who is it for?"

 

"For Shura," Aurora replied flatly.

 

"...What?"

 

One Leaf Knows Autumn's expression visibly shifted. "Him? Why him?"

 

"Why not?"

 

"Miss Aurora, surely you know… I've had a bit of a history with that guy, right?"

 

Aurora frowned. "Didn't you rescind the bounty on Shura?"

 1

One Leaf Knows Autumn's face twitched, his expression turning grim.

 1

He had indeed withdrawn the bounty on Shura—not because he wanted to, but because he couldn't deal with him. Shura had become invincible among his peers. Who could kill him? The withdrawal was nothing short of swallowing his pride.

 

Because of that incident, One Leaf Knows Autumn had been mocked by his peers for a long time.

 

His prestige in the Samsara Space had also taken a serious hit.

 

Many people accused him of being afraid of Shura, a humiliation he couldn't live down.

 

"...Miss Aurora, has that guy joined the organization too?"

 

As he asked, his face grew even more sullen.

 

If Aurora Morwyn was stepping in and requesting a flamethrower, it meant Shura had agreed to cooperate.

 

And if Shura joined the organization, that made him one of their own. One Leaf Knows Autumn would no longer be allowed to move against him—not with central command so protective of talented newcomers.

 

One Leaf Knows Autumn was considered a high-ranking member himself, and he knew just how much value was placed on Shura.

 

"Meet me at the Trading Center and hand over the flamethrower to Shura," Aurora Morwyn said coldly. "Your debt to me will be considered paid. Leave everything else alone."

 

One Leaf Knows Autumn owed Aurora a favor from a previous joint mission.

 

If it weren't for Aurora saving him during a crucial moment, he would have been erased by the system for failing the mission.

 

More than a year had passed since then. Aurora had already climbed to the 29th floor, while One Leaf Knows Autumn was still stuck on the 26th, too scared to attempt another run.

 

That was the difference between them.

 

Although Aurora's words irritated him, One Leaf Knows Autumn swallowed his pride and forced a nod.

 

Aurora didn't just outrank him by three stages.

 

In the real world, in both influence and strength, Aurora Morwyn could easily crush him.

 

And then there was the Song family—more than enough to suppress his Armand Family.

 

"...I understand," One Leaf Knows Autumn replied, sounding somewhat aggrieved.

 

In a private room.

 

Fenric was reviewing the plan with Belle Morwyn.

 

"Your dungeon cooldown should've reset by now, right?" he asked.

 

Belle responded a bit sheepishly. "It reset a while ago… but I wasn't confident I'd get a good result, so I didn't go in."

 

Fenric said nothing in response.

 

Samsara player like Belle were more or less the norm within Samsara Space.

 

Dungeon maniacs like Fenric were the rare exceptions.

 

"Alright then. Meet me at the staging room for the Fourth Stage dungeon 'Venom' at 3:30 AM tonight."

 

Belle blinked in surprise. Was Shura really that eager?

 

Still, she nodded quickly. "Okay, sure!"

 

She was inwardly amazed— So this is what a true powerhouse looks like...

 

Fenric said seriously, "Once inside, try to choose a role that can access weapons of mass destruction. Something like a job at an arms manufacturing company."

 

"Don't bother with regular weapons. We're talking about personal missiles or heavier."

 1

"The more explosive, the better."

 

"These weapons will be used to kill symbiotes. The more weapons you acquire, the more symbiotes you'll be able to eliminate."

 

He continued, "Also, once you're inside, contact me immediately. I'll be joining the Life Foundation under the name Ronan Anderson as part of their security team. Remember that name—it'll help you locate me."

 1

"Then, just wait for my signal and follow my instructions. Got it?"

 

Belle didn't ask further and quickly nodded. "Yes, I understand!"

 

She came from a large, influential family and had been trained in etiquette and social roles since childhood. Playing the part of a corporate executive—especially at an arms company—shouldn't be a problem.

 

Fenric thought for a moment, then added, "That's all for now. If the plan changes, I'll let you know."

 

"Okay."

 

As they were wrapping up their conversation, the door opened, and Aurora walked in.

 

"Shura, Belle, done talking?"

 

"Just finished," Fenric replied.

 

"Perfect. Come with me to the Trading Center," Aurora said with a smile. "I've got your flamethrower."

 

Fenric's eyes lit up. "Thank you!"

 

Bringing Belle into the dungeon would help him run it smoothly, and now Aurora was helping him further.

 

This cooperation truly was mutually beneficial.

 

As for whether Belle might leak his strategy?

 

Fenric wasn't worried.

 

His current strategy—just like the one for One Piece—was reckless to the extreme.

 

No one else could pull it off.

 

Even for him, a single misstep could mean death. He takes such dangerous risks only because he has the strength to support his plans.

 5

Anyone else trying to replicate it? They'd be gambling with their lives.

 

"Don't mention it," Aurora smiled. "Helping Belle means helping me too."

 

She added, "Shura, the person handing over the flamethrower is One Leaf Knows Autumn. Don't worry, he's just delivering the item. There won't be any issues."

 

Fenric raised an eyebrow, then chuckled.

 

What a coincidence.

 

Due to the rules of Samsara Space, once a special item is traded, its ownership can't be changed again for three years.

 

So the item had to go directly from One Leaf Knows Autumn to Fenric.

 

If Aurora took it first and then transferred it, the system wouldn't allow it.

 

And so, the three of them headed for the Trading Center.

 

______

 

[Tl/n: Next Arc Deal

 

1,000 Power Stones + 5 Reviews OR RANK 1 = Full Release of the Entire Next Arc!

 1

P.S. Advanced chapters are now available on my Patreon!

 

Depending on your chosen tier, you can read 1–3 arcs ahead of the Webnovel schedule.

 

Daily updates will still follow the same pace as on Webnovel.]

chapters.name: Chapter 135: Chapter 135: Contract Symbiote! (4/8)
chapters.content:
Trading Center.

 

One Leaf Knows Autumn wore a gloomy expression and remained silent as he completed the handover with Fenric.

 

The man who killed his nephew!

 

And now, he was giving something to Fenric for free.

 

Even with Aurora's persuasion, One Leaf Knows Autumn still felt bitter and upset every day.

 

If tonight's events reached the ears of his elder brother and sister-in-law, who knew what they would think of him?

 

The moment the transaction ended, One Leaf Knows Autumn vanished without saying another word, unwilling to linger even a second longer.

 

Watching One Leaf Knows Autumn's retreating figure in the distance, Fenric remained expressionless—but inwardly, he sneered.

 

He would never change his view of One Leaf Knows Autumn, even if the man had withdrawn the reward.

 

To Fenric, this man would always be a mortal enemy.

 

"Shura, according to Belle, are you heading into a dungeon tonight?" Aurora asked.

 

"Yes," Fenric replied with a nod.

 

"Aren't you being a little too hasty?"

 

Fenric smiled faintly. "I know what I'm doing."

 

Aurora sighed. "Alright then. Belle, I'm counting on you."

 

After that, the three of them parted ways.

 

There was still more than an hour before 3:30 a.m.

 

Fenric needed time to assign attribute points, while Belle Morwyn had preparations of her own.

 

Entering a dungeon in the Samsara Tower was no joke. Failing to complete the mission meant death. Proper preparation was essential.

 

Personal Warehouse.

 

With 100,000 points, Fenric converted them all into potential points—earning 200 in total.

 

Originally, he had intended to enhance his Conqueror's Haki. But unsure if it would be effective against the symbiote, he decided instead to use the points to increase his attributes.

 

Attributes were raw power!

 

Even if it wasn't the most optimal choice, it was certainly not the wrong one.

 

He distributed the 200 points according to the best ratio.

 

After allocation, Fenric's attributes were:

 

Name: Shura

 

Samsara Number: (Zone C) 90086

 

Physique: 120 → 155

 

Spirit: 230 → 310

 

Strength: 155 → 203

 

Agility: 115 → 155

 

Potential Points Available: 0

 

Skills:

 

English (Proficient)

 

Driving (Beginner)

 

Shooting (Proficient)

 

Camouflage (Master)

 

Basic Blade Techniques (Proficient)

 

Special Skills:

 

Conqueror's Haki (Proficient)

 

Armament Haki (Master)

 

Combat Skills:

 

Savage Charge

 

Abilities:

 

Telekinesis

 

Samsara Points: 22

 

Overall Rating: B

 

This was Fenric's current state!

 

His Strength attribute had surpassed 200.

 1

A punch from him now would be comparable to getting hit by a speeding truck—deadly and devastating.

 3

His Spirit attribute had broken past 300, heightening all five senses (and even a sixth), and giving him far more control over his telekinesis.

 

Suddenly, Fenric's thoughts stirred. He poured all his energy into a single command.

 

His body slowly lifted off the ground.

 

Although he could only float for a few seconds before he lost control and landed again, Fenric laughed.

 

He had seen the possibility of flight!

 

It wouldn't be long before he could fly freely using only his mind.

 

In fact, with his current mental strength, Fenric could already move objects weighing five to six hundred catties with ease. Throwing enemies with telekinesis? No problem.

 2

But using that same power to make himself fly was another matter entirely.

 

Force is reciprocal.

 

It's like trying to lift yourself off the ground by pulling your own hair—impossible.

 1

To fly using telekinesis, he'd need his mental strength to be so overwhelming that it could influence the air around him and create lift.

 1

He was close—but not quite there yet.

 

While Fenric was preparing, Belle was also making her own arrangements.

 

"Bell, do you still have the healing potion I gave you last time?" Aurora asked.

 

"Yes!" Belle replied. "I haven't used it yet."

 

"Good. By the way, is Shura forming an alliance with you?"

 

"No."

 

"No?" Aurora looked puzzled. "Then what does he want you to do?"

 

"Great God Shura asked me to gather weapons with wide-area destruction capabilities. Then I'm supposed to wait for further instructions."

 

"Oh?"

 

Aurora Morwyn was momentarily stunned by the answer.

 

She had also cleared the Fourth Stage and knew the dungeon was Venom. According to online guides, there were no more than four symbiotes in the entire scenario.

 

Clearly, Shura was preparing for a mass extermination of symbiotes.

 

Suddenly, her eyes gleamed with realization. "It seems Shura has discovered something others missed… Maybe he's found the location of the symbiote nest?"

 

"Belle, just follow his lead. Don't get distracted. For my sake, he won't let you fail the mission."

 

Belle nodded eagerly. "Don't worry, Cousin. I'm not that dumb. With such a thick thigh to cling to, why would I try to act on my own? I'll just follow him obediently!"

 3

Aurora chuckled. "That's the right attitude. Go on then. Be careful. I'll be waiting for your safe return."

 

"Wait, Sister—one more thing. Shura asked me earlier… He wants to know what Devil Fruit you ate."

 

Aurora's expression darkened instantly. She glared at her cousin. "Did you tell him?"

 

Startled by her cousin's sudden intensity, Belle shook her head frantically. "No, no! Absolutely not! I really didn't say anything!"

 

"You'd better not! If you dare spill that secret—I'll slice open the part of you with the most meat!"

 24

3:30 AM.

 

Fenric appeared at the entrance of the Samsara Tower.

 

Without hesitation, he used a cooldown reset card to refresh his dungeon access.

 

He stepped forward—and was instantly transported to the Fourth Stage.

 

A system spirit materialized before him.

 

"Greetings, Dear Samsara Player Shura. How may I assist you?"

 

"I want to enter a dungeon," Fenric replied.

 

"Very well. Please choose the dungeon world you wish to enter."

 

With a wave of her hand, a holographic screen appeared before him.

 

Two dungeon options were displayed:

 

Strange Shapes (Easy)

 2

Venom: Deadly Guardian (Difficult)

 

Fenric had already made up his mind.

 

Without hesitation, he selected the difficult dungeon: Venom.

 

In the next instant, he was teleported into a white preparation room.

 

To his surprise, there were already over a dozen people present.

 

Not far away, Belle spotted him and waved with a bright smile.

 

Fenric nodded in acknowledgment, then swept his gaze over the other Samsara.

 

There were many competitors tonight.

 

Not wanting them to interfere with his plan, Fenric suddenly raised his voice:

 

"Listen up, everyone. I'm Shura! In tonight's dungeon, I hold all four symbiotes! If you want to back out, now's your chance. Otherwise, you can try your luck—see if you can beat me!"

 

His words were thunderous—absolutely domineering.

chapters.name: Chapter 136: Chapter 136: Sorry, Strength Is Just That Overwhelming! (5/8)
chapters.content:
In the white room.

 

All the Samsara were stunned!

 

They had been in the Samsara space for a long time, but they had never encountered someone so domineering!

 

And yet—

 

They were truly scared!

 

Many of them had already hesitated upon seeing the instance scheduled for 4:00 a.m., especially with such a large number of participants. Their desire to retreat had already begun to stir.

 

But now, upon hearing that Boss Shura was planning to monopolize all symbiotic contracts, panic erupted.

 

After all, the story of Shura going toe-to-toe with Admiral-level Fujitora had already spread throughout the Samsara space. Everyone knew just how terrifying Shura's strength was.

 

Sure, his behavior might seem arrogant and overbearing...

 2

But so what?

 

He had the strength to back it up!

 

Sorry, but overwhelming strength is its own justification!!

 

In an instant—

 

Many people chose to quit the preparation room, deciding to try again another time.

 

Waiting another day was nothing compared to risking their lives going up against a monster like that.

 

Of course, there were still a few who were either hot-headed or confident in their abilities and chose to stay.

 

Not long after...

 

In White Room 27, including Fenric and Belle Morwyn, only five people remained.

 

Among the other three, one looked hesitant, one was disdainful, and one remained expressionless.

 

Fenric smiled faintly. As long as no one interfered with his plan, he didn't care what others thought.

 

Next to him, Belle stared at Fenric with shining eyes, admiration written all over her face.

 

Big shots really are different—so bold and commanding!

 

As the countdown ticked on, the hesitant Samsara players eventually made the wise choice and left the room.

 

In the preparation phase, Samsara could choose to exit freely.

 

However, once the countdown entered its final ten minutes, the Samsara system would lock the entrance and prevent any further entry and exits.

 

Soon—

 

Only ten minutes remained.

 

A system notification rang out:

 

"Attention, Samsara Players. In 10 minutes, you will be teleported to the mission world."

 

At that moment, only four people remained in the white room.

 

Aside from Fenric (Shura) and Belle Morwyn, there was one male and one female Samsara players left.

 

This was probably the first time Fenric's presence alone had scared away so many people in the Samsara space.

 

Time passed swiftly.

 

Ten minutes flew by.

 

Then, the system prompt echoed once more:

 

"Initiating teleport countdown: 10, 9, 8… 3, 2, 1!"

 

As the countdown ended—

 

All four remaining Samsara were enveloped in red light and disappeared.

 

After teleportation, Fenric and the other three didn't immediately appear in the dungeon world. Instead, they were suspended in a red glow.

 

Then, a virtual interface appeared in front of Fenric.

 

On it was the image of a young man who shared some resemblance to Fenric.

 

"Samsara 'Shura', this is your default appearance in this world. If you're not satisfied, please modify it now."

 

Hearing the system's prompt, Fenric immediately began making adjustments.

 

First, he altered his appearance, transforming himself into a Caucasian. 

 1

It wasn't out of curiosity to experience another race, but rather to carry out the mission more effectively

 1

After all, the world of Venom took place in the United States, where racial discrimination still existed. Being a foreigner could attract unnecessary complications.

 14

After a few swift adjustments, Fenric transformed into a white man.

 

His facial features were designed to be average and unremarkable. He didn't want to attract attention during the mission.

 

However, he gave himself a strong, imposing physique—the kind that looked like it could take a bullet.

 

In the early stages of his plan, he intended to pose as a bodyguard, so having a strong frame would help build trust with his target.

 

Everything—from appearance to build—was designed with the mission in mind.

 

Once satisfied with his image, the system prompted again:

 

"Samsara Player 'Shura', please edit your identity!"

 

"Note: You may not assign yourself as a high-ranking official, politician, or any identity that would not exist in this world. If the identity fails authentication, you will appear in the dungeon as a blacklisted user."

 1

Fenric smiled and typed into the input fields:

 

"Name: Ronan Anderson"

 

"Age: 30"

 

"Identity: Personal bodyguard of Carlton Drake, owner of the Life Foundation"

 

[TL/n: It's OG character.]

 2

Once done, he clicked "Finish."

 

The system responded immediately:

 

"Identity approved. Transmitting to the dungeon world."

 

The next moment—

 

A red light flashed before Fenric's eyes.

 

When he regained focus, he found himself sitting in the passenger seat of a moving car.

 

The vehicle was speeding down the road.

 

Fenric remained calm, casually glancing at the driver, then using the rearview mirror to observe the back seat.

 

It was a luxurious Maybach. In the back sat a man and a woman.

 

The man was none other than Carlton Drake, the founder of the Life Foundation.

 

The future host of the Riot symbiote.

 

And now, the boss of his current identity.

 

The woman beside him looked like his assistant.

 

"Boss, an elementary school class will be visiting the company this afternoon. Also, you're scheduled for an exclusive interview," the assistant reported.

 

Drake, brimming with energy, nodded and asked,

 

"Who's the reporter?"

 

"Eddie Brock. He's one of the most popular reporters around. You've already confirmed the interview."

 

"Ah, yes, I remember now." Drake smiled. "Eddie Brock, huh? I like that guy."

 

Fenric's expression didn't change, but inside, his mind stirred.

 

Eddie Brock?

 

That was the protagonist of this dungeon world—the host of Venom!

 

In his past life, Eddie Brock was often mocked online as "the most pitiful protagonist ever created by Stan."

 11

And today, he was set to interview Drake?

 

This meant the plot was about to begin.

 1

If Fenric remembered correctly, from this point on, things would start to spiral for Eddie Brock.

 

It didn't take long.

 

The car pulled up to a building.

 

The sign outside read: "Life Foundation."

 

Drake's company.

 

As the car came to a halt, Fenric immediately got out and opened the door for Drake.

 2

After all, he was now playing the role of a bodyguard.

 

And as a bodyguard, he had to act the part—professionally and precisely.

 

Drake stepped out, shot a look of appreciation at Fenric, and strode confidently into the building.

chapters.name: Chapter 137: Chapter 137: God of Symbiosis (6/8)
chapters.content:
"Boss, the last rocket crash left a terrible impression. Today's interview is critical. Please do your best!"

 

The assistant hurried after Drake, earnestly reminding him.

 

Drake's expression darkened slightly at those words. He asked coldly, "Where are my things? When will they be delivered to the company?"

 

"Probably tonight!"

 

"Good."

 

Drake's face relaxed into a smile as he stepped into the exhibition hall.

 

Inside, a group of elementary school students were touring the Life Foundation's latest displays.

 

Fenric followed quietly behind Drake, his gaze sharp.

 

He remembered clearly—the rocket crash marked the beginning of Venom.

 

The plot of Venom wasn't complicated. The Life Foundation discovered four symbiotes in outer space and brought them back to Earth for research. However, the rocket crash scattered them, and one symbiote escaped.

 

That one... was Riot.

 

In the comics, Riot was Venom's "offspring."

 1

But in this cinematic universe, Riot was the leader of the symbiotes.

 

Its purpose? To bring an army from the symbiote homeworld and invade Earth—completely overtaking it.

 2

Later, Riot would bond with Carlton Drake, the head of the Life Foundation, and convince him to launch a shuttle back to the symbiote planet—to bring the rest of them.

 

The only reason this plot failed in the original story was because Venom fell in love with Earth and chose to betray his kind.

 

Fenric's plan was simple: let Riot live and follow it back to the symbiote homeworld.

 5

The true threat wasn't the symbiotes themselves.

 

With Fenric's current power, symbiotes posed little danger. The real risk was a being named—Knull.

 

A god—not just any god, but one powerful enough to slay members of the Celestials.

 5

Knull... the creator of the symbiotes.

 

The God of Symbiosis!

 

"System Notification: New Task Released!"

 

Main Task: Kill at least one symbiote within 30 days.

 

Time Limit: 30 days.

 

Failure Consequence: Obliteration.

 

Fenric kept silent and played the role of an observer, staying close to Drake like a shadow.

 

By afternoon, it was time for the highly anticipated interview.

 

Fenric spotted a disheveled-looking man enter the room—Eddie Brock.

 

As in the original story, Eddie had long despised the Life Foundation. He wasn't here to interview—he was here to stir trouble.

 

The beginning of the interview went relatively smoothly. But things quickly escalated when Eddie abruptly asked:

 

"Mr. Drake, some say the Life Foundation experiments on living people. That it's more like the Death Foundation. What's your response to that?"

 

Drake's face instantly turned grim.

 

The interview ended in complete disarray.

 

Later that night.

 

A long-distance freight truck quietly arrived at the company's back entrance.

 

Drake and several others were already waiting.

 

As the truck came to a stop, company security unloaded three large metal containers. Each was opened in front of Drake.

 

Inside each was a glass capsule—filled with viscous, foul-smelling slime.

 1

One black.

 

One yellow.

 

One blue.

 

Even more disturbing, the slime inside was... alive—squirming aggressively within their containers.

 

Drake's eyes gleamed with fanaticism as he gazed at the symbiotes.

 

"So beautiful," he murmured.

 

In the original plot, Drake was a madman who believed the human body was incomplete. He pursued the limits of evolution, and believed symbiosis could push humanity to the next level.

 

It was that very obsession that made Riot choose him as a host.

 

Then... chaos erupted.

 

A female assistant suddenly lunged forward and tackled Drake, pushing him aside and making a beeline for the containers.

 

"Stop her!" Drake roared in panic.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed.

 

She's a Samsara player.

 

Ahead, several security guards moved to intercept her—but they never stood a chance.

 

She had eaten the Paramecia-type Devil Fruit. Her arms transformed into sharp blades, effortlessly slicing through the guards.

 

Blood sprayed.

 

None survived.

 

Fenric quickly stepped forward and helped Drake up.

 

"Boss, are you okay?"

 

"Forget me—stop that crazy woman!"

 

"Yes, Boss!"

 

Before the words left his mouth, Fenric vanished from where he stood.

 

In a blink, he appeared behind the female assistant.

 

But by then, she had already reached the symbiote containers. With a sudden motion, she produced a can of gasoline—pouring its contents over the glass capsules.

 

Then, a windproof lighter appeared in her hand.

 

Seeing Fenric approaching, she sneered—and tossed the lit lighter toward the containers.

 

At that moment, gasoline covered the entire setup.

 

One spark would ignite a firestorm.

 

And no one could stop it.

 

She was certain of her victory.

 

"So much for the feared Shura," she thought smugly.

 

Nearby, Drake looked horrified. He reached out instinctively, trying to stop the lighter—but it was far beyond his grasp.

 

Panic spread across everyone's faces.

 

Everyone—except Fenric.

 

The next moment, something miraculous happened.

 

The flame on the lighter extinguished mid-air.

 

The female assistant froze.

 

Windproof lighter. Impossible to blow out... unless—

 

Fenric had used his Telekinesis to snuff the flame.

 

Ding!

 

The lighter landed harmlessly on the container with a metallic clang.

 

No flame.

 

No fire.

 

"!!"

 

The female assistant's expression twisted.

 

She rushed forward to relight the lighter—

 

But she never made it.

 

Fenric was already behind her.

 

He seized her by the nape of the neck with one hand, halting her completely.

 

She snarled, slashing backward with a hand-knife—but it was laughable.

 

With a Grandmaster-level Armament Haki? You think a hand blade can hurt him?

 

With one punch, Fenric shattered her arm.

 

With another twist, he grabbed her chin and—SNAP!

 

A sickening crack echoed.

 

The female assistant's eyes widened in disbelief before she collapsed, lifeless.

 

Her neck spine—crushed.

 

Fenric stood over her corpse, face blank.

 

Anyone who dares disrupt his plan...

 

Whether man or woman—no mercy.

 6

chapters.name: Chapter 138: Chapter 138: Riot Appears (7/8)
chapters.content:
In truth, the strength of the female Samsara wasn't weak—her overall combat evaluation was at least C-level.

 

Just moments ago, the heavily armed security personnel had been completely overwhelmed. The ground was littered with their dismembered corpses—each one the handiwork of that female Samsara.

 

Against ordinary humans, she was overwhelmingly powerful.

 

However…

 

Against Fenric, she was the one utterly outclassed.

 

In every aspect—speed, strength, technique—Fenric surpassed her. Taking her down in a single second was well within his ability.

 

"Well done!"

 

Seeing the symbiote successfully secured, Drake was overjoyed and couldn't help but express his admiration for Fenric.

 2

"Quick! Send it to my lab immediately!" Drake urged anxiously, fearful that another accident might occur.

 

After personally witnessing the three symbiotes delivered safely into the research lab, Drake finally let out a sigh of relief.

 

He walked over to Fenric, gave him a hearty slap on the shoulder, and said with a grin, "Excellent work. You've earned double your bonus this month!"

 

"Thank you, sir," Fenric replied calmly.

 

His performance just now was calculated—he had done just enough to showcase his strength without going overboard.

 1

Had he displayed his true power—say, stopping the lighter mid-air or instantly killing the female Samsara using telekinesis—Drake might've still been grateful, but also wary. It would've made him see Fenric as a monster, not a man.

 

"Your name is Ronan, right? Former Delta Force? Retired?" Drake asked, narrowing his eyes slightly.

 1

"Yes, sir."

 

"Good. From now on, you'll stay by my side and protect me. Don't worry—I take good care of my people."

 1

"Understood."

 

Fenric responded with stoic professionalism, like a quiet, reliable soldier.

 

Drake, seeing this, was even more satisfied.

 

What's the use of a bodyguard who's all talk? Loyalty and strength—that's what mattered.

 

His gaze then shifted to the female Samsara's corpse lying on the floor.

 

His eyes gleamed with interest.

 

He had been observing her during the earlier confrontation—those transforming arms that turned into blades had deeply intrigued him.

 2

"Don't touch the body. Bring it into my lab," Drake ordered, clearly planning to dissect and study the unique physiology of the female Samsara.

 

Fenric remained unmoved.

 

This was the cruel law of the Samsara world—the weak die, the strong survive. He felt no pity.

 

At that moment, Fenric's calm gaze swept across the area.

 

He remembered there were four Samsara who entered this dungeon.

 

Including himself and Belle Morwyn, there should be two others—one male, one female.

 

The female was already dead by his hands.

 

But where was the male?

 

Fenric speculated that the other Samsara player had likely infiltrated the Life Foundation as well.

 

Online strategy forums had made it clear: the only way to get close to the symbiotes was to embed yourself within the Life Foundation.

 

The next day.

 

Fenric continued to follow Drake closely.

 

The plot progressed in line with the original storyline. Drake began researching the symbiotes and used live human test subjects in hopes of discovering a safe method of symbiotic integration.

 

Unfortunately, all attempts ended in failure—and many test subjects died.

 

A female doctor, unable to bear the horrors any longer, secretly contacted a reporter named Eddie, hoping to expose Drake's atrocities.

 

Soon, Eddie sneaked into the facility and was infected by Venom, becoming its host.

 

Fenric observed everything silently, showing no intention of interfering.

 

Whether it was Venom or the other symbiotes, he wasn't particularly interested.

 

His goal was simple: protect Drake, let him finish building the spacecraft, and catch a ride to the symbiotes' home planet.

 

Once there… that was where Fenric would truly begin to shine.

 

As for the remaining Samsara player, he still hadn't shown himself. His whereabouts remained unknown.

 

A few days later.

 

While accompanying Drake to the research facility, a security guard stopped Fenric at the entrance.

 

"Mr. Anderson, this package is for you."

 

"Oh? Thanks."

 

Fenric opened it. Inside was a simple mobile phone.

 

Only one number was saved on it.

 

Seeing this, Fenric smiled faintly.

 

He knew who sent it.

 

Belle Morwyn.

 

While Drake entered the lab, Fenric stood outside and dialed the number.

 

"Hello?"

 

"Great Shura, it's me." Belle Morwyn's voice came from the other end.

 

"Mm. I figured. Did you complete the task I gave you?"

 

"Done!"

 

Fenric didn't ask how she managed it and simply followed up, "Good. Where are you now?"

 

"Los Angeles."

 

"You have one week. Bring the weapons and come to San Francisco."

 

Without another word, Fenric ended the call.

 

The Life Foundation was based in San Francisco.

 

During this time, Fenric had kept a low profile, quietly monitoring Drake's activities.

 

At the very least, he knew Drake had spent a fortune constructing a spacecraft—preparations for another trip to space.

 

Based on his understanding of the timeline, the launch would happen within a week.

 

Just as he ended the call, Fenric noticed something unusual.

 

A small, blonde-haired girl walked alone into the research facility.

 

His eyes gleamed sharply.

 

He recognized her instantly.

 

According to the plot, this little girl was the temporary host of Riot. She had come to the facility to merge with Drake.

 

The symbiotes were intelligent. Riot must've learned through various channels that Drake was the ideal candidate to help execute its plan.

 

That's why it had traveled all this way to possess him.

 

When the girl saw Fenric, he also locked eyes with her.

 

Fenric immediately stepped aside, making way.

 

Not because he feared Riot.

 

In fact, he had already learned the symbiotes' weaknesses. Taking down Riot wouldn't be hard.

 

But now wasn't the time.

 

He needed Riot to bond with Drake.

 

So, he let it pass.

 

The little girl entered the research room without resistance.

 

Two hours later.

 

Drake emerged.

 

No one else came out with him.

 

With his keen senses, Fenric immediately noticed something had changed.

 

Drake was no longer the same.

 

Clearly, Riot had taken over.

 

"Ronan, let's go."

 

"Yes, sir."

 

Fenric responded as usual, his face calm and composed.

chapters.name: Chapter 139: Chapter 139: The Most Dangerous Is You! (8/8)
chapters.content:
Ever since Riot possessed Drake, his behavior had become increasingly erratic—ruthless and utterly unrestrained.

 

Short-tempered. No hesitation in killing.

 

In just a few days, Fenric had personally witnessed Drake kill six or seven people without remorse.

 2

Drake's deep connections with the government, and the powerful corporate backers behind the Life Foundation, meant no one dared confront him.

 

Often, Fenric overheard Drake "talking to himself" alone in the office.

 

But Fenric knew better.

 

Drake wasn't talking to himself—he was conversing with Riot.

 

Under Riot's manipulation, Drake was now rushing to launch the spacecraft and head to the symbiote's homeworld.

 

Yes, the Life Foundation had its own launch base and space-worthy rockets.

 

From that point on, Drake focused entirely on the spacecraft's construction and lost interest in everything else.

 

He even abandoned efforts to retrieve Venom from Eddie, despite previously deploying people to hunt him down.

 

Fenric welcomed this behavior.

 

It was all unfolding as he'd hoped.

 

The only unexpected variable was the male Samsara, who still hadn't revealed himself.

 

The next day.

 

Drake suddenly left the company in a hurry, instructing Fenric to drive to the launch site on the coast.

 

He could no longer wait.

 

Upon arrival, Drake entered the spacecraft control room. Fenric remained at the door and immediately called Belle Morwyn.

 

"Great God?"

 1

"Where are you?" Fenric asked.

 

"Just reached downtown San Francisco. I'm heading toward the Life Foundation lab now."

 

"Turn around. I'll send you a location. Get here in ten minutes—no delays."

 

Fenric ended the call and sent the coordinates.

 

Then, he turned and walked straight toward the control room.

 

"No more testing. Launch prep begins now!"

 

As he approached, Fenric heard Drake's furious voice from inside.

 

"But boss, the flight team isn't ready yet!" a staff member protested.

 

"We don't need a flight team. I'll fly it myself!" Drake snapped.

 

Just as the staff member was about to argue again, a sudden sharp pain shot through his abdomen.

 

A long blade had pierced straight through him—emerging from Drake's transformed arm.

 

"Ahhh!"

 

The remaining staff screamed at the horrific scene and fled the control room in terror.

 

In seconds, only Drake remained.

 

He sneered coldly and walked to the control console, ready to launch the spacecraft.

 

"Boss, mind waiting a moment?"

 

Startled, Drake looked up and saw Fenric entering.

 

"Ronan? I told you to stay outside!" Drake frowned.

 

Fenric smiled. "I was outside, and I overheard your plan to launch immediately. As your bodyguard, I should follow you at all times. Can I come along?"

 

"Oh?" Drake looked surprised. "You don't even know where I'm going, and you still want to come?"

 

Fenric shrugged. "It's in the contract. As your personal bodyguard, I'm obligated to accompany you 24/7."

 

Drake stared at him, slightly dazed.

 

Is this guy just overly loyal? he wondered.

 

But the more he thought about it, the more it made sense. Ronan was strong—he could potentially serve as a perfect symbiote host.

 

"Very well. You'll come with me. Don't worry—I'll take care of you."

 

With that, Drake turned back to prepare the launch sequence.

 

"Wait, boss!"

 

"What now?" Drake's patience wore thin.

 

Fenric smiled again. "I have a friend on the way."

 

That sentence instantly set off alarms.

 

Even if Riot wasn't the brightest creature, it realized something was wrong.

 

Without another word, Drake's right arm morphed into a razor-sharp blade and lunged at Fenric.

 

Swoosh!

 

The air cracked.

 

But Fenric didn't flinch. Instead, he sank his weight, raised his palm—and caught Riot's blade bare-handed!

 

His palm gleamed with a metallic black sheen.

 

"!!"

 

Riot's expression twisted into surprise.

 

At first, it mistook Fenric for another symbiote host. But upon closer inspection… no, this wasn't one of them.

 

"Careful, boss. If you break the console, we won't be launching anything," Fenric warned calmly.

 

Riot hesitated. His expression darkened. A toothy grin appeared on Drake's twisted face.

 

"Who… are you?" Riot asked coldly.

 

Just now, Fenric had caught its blade bare-handed and hadn't lost in terms of strength. His skin was like reinforced steel.

 

Riot wasn't afraid of fighting—but destroying the control system would doom their plan.

 

"Me?" Fenric grinned. "Just a human, boss. I'm not here to stop you. I want to go to the symbiote homeworld with you."

 

"You… know about the symbiote planet?" Riot was stunned. Then it narrowed its eyes. "Why do you want to go there?"

 

"To find a symbiote that matches me. I want to get stronger."

 

Fenric spoke without hesitation, spinning a lie as easily as breathing.

 

Riot thought it over and decided—for now—it was better to keep him close.

 

In the next moment, Riot retracted into Drake's body like a receding tide, revealing Drake's face once more.

 

"I didn't expect the most dangerous person… to be by my side all along," Drake muttered, eyes narrowing.

 

Now that his identity was exposed, he had no choice but to leave Earth immediately.

 

He couldn't risk damaging the control systems with a fight.

 

"Boss, you're mistaken. I'm not your enemy. I'm not dangerous."

 

Drake didn't press the issue. "When's your friend arriving? I don't have much time."

 

"Ten minutes."

 

"Fine."

 

Ten minutes passed quickly.

 

A large transport truck rumbled toward the dock.

 

"Boss, my friend's here. And it looks like your friend is, too."

 

Fenric pointed toward a distant coastal ridge.

 

A massive black figure thundered down the slope.

 

Venom!

 

"Boss, start the launch sequence."

 

Without hesitation, Drake turned to the console and entered the launch code.

 

"Five-minute countdown to spacecraft launch initiated."

 

_________

chapters.name: Chapter 140: Chapter 140: Kill!
chapters.content:
Once the spacecraft started moving, Drake's expression immediately changed.

 

His Riot form erupted, transforming his arms into long, deadly blades that slashed straight at Fenric's neck.

 

Clang!

 

A metallic crash rang out.

 

The sharp Riot blades shattered in mid-air and fell uselessly to the ground.

 

Startled, Riot quickly looked at Fenric—only to see a black-bladed sword had somehow appeared in Fenric's hand without warning. The blade was ink-black, etched with intricate patterns, its edge gleaming coldly. It radiated a lethal sharpness.

 

The weapons Riot conjured were comparable to high-grade steel, yet they had been easily broken by this sword. The blade hadn't even dulled.

 

In that moment, Riot's evaluation of Fenric's threat level soared again.

 

Fenric sheathed the sword calmly and said, "Boss, I told you—I have no hostile intent. The real threat today is Venom. He's on his way here right now, planning to betray you and destroy the ship."

 

Hearing that, Riot turned and looked outside. Sure enough, Venom was charging toward the spacecraft at full speed.

 

"Traitor!!" Riot growled with fury.

 

Without hesitation, he smashed through the control room wall and dashed toward Venom.

 

He wanted off this planet—and he'd make sure Venom didn't stop that.

 

Fenric smirked and left the control room casually.

 

He didn't chase after Venom. In his opinion, Riot was strong enough to handle the threat on his own.

 

In the original story, Venom was thoroughly beaten by Riot.

 

If it hadn't been for the trick that blew up the ship, Venom would never have won.

 

A moment later, Fenric arrived at the truck.

 

"Great God??"

 

A blonde woman looked at him warily.

 

"It's me," Fenric replied, then glanced at the truck's cargo.

 

The truck bed was packed full of missile warheads. Fenric nodded approvingly.

 

"Nice work. Let's move this stuff into the ship, fast."

 

Weapons of mass destruction like missiles were banned in most countries, and yet Belle had managed to gather so many of them in such a short time. Her resourcefulness was impressive.

 2

Even better—she had also brought incendiary bombs.

 

Soon after, with Fenric's help, all the weapons were loaded onto the spacecraft in under a minute, including a large missile launcher and several smaller portable units.

 2

Seeing Riot still locked in combat with Venom, Fenric grabbed an incendiary bomb and turned to Belle.

 

"You get on board and wait for me. I'll be right behind you."

 

Without another word, he rushed toward the battling symbiotes.

 

He had no intention of letting the original story repeat itself. This time, he'd personally eliminate Venom.

 

"Boss, need a hand?" Fenric asked as he arrived.

 

At that moment, Riot was completely dominating the fight. Venom, bruised and battered, sneered as Fenric appeared.

 

"Oh? Riot, this your backup? What a joke!"

 

Riot growled and snapped, "Stay out of it!"

 

Fenric shook his head and unsheathed his black blade, Shusui.

 

"Boss, we don't have time. Let me finish this."

 

Without waiting for a response, Fenric charged straight at Venom, swinging his blade in a clean arc.

 

Riot, knowing just how powerful the blade was, immediately leaped back in alarm.

 

Venom, however, underestimated Fenric. He laughed and threw a punch at Fenric's face, not even bothering to dodge.

 

Splat!

 

The next moment, Venom's body was cleaved in two. His upper half flew through the air, cleanly sliced at the waist.

 

"W-What the hell?! Who is this guy?!"

 

Despite the blow, Venom wasn't dead. Symbiotes had incredible vitality, and few things could kill them outright—except fire.

 

Venom's upper half began crawling toward the lower half, desperate to reattach. Eddie, the host, wouldn't last long without him.

 

Fenric calmly activated the incendiary bomb in his hand—and tossed it right onto Venom.

 

BOOM!

 

The explosion lit the area in flames.

 

"ARGHHH!"

 

Venom's pained screams echoed as his black mass writhed and shifted grotesquely in the fire.

 

Eventually, he detached from Eddie entirely, becoming a ball of flaming goo that hurled itself at Fenric in one last suicidal attack.

 

But Fenric simply smiled.

 

He activated his psychic power—and stopped Venom's charge midair with ease.

 

Honestly, if Fenric had used the enchanted whistle or the flamethrower he possessed, the battle would've ended even faster. But both were one-time, time-limited tools—and he preferred to save them for emergencies.

 

"Boss, we're done here. Let's go."

 

Without looking back, Fenric turned and walked away. He was sure Venom was dead—because just then, the system prompt appeared:

 

You killed a symbiote and completed the main mission.

 1

You may choose to return immediately or stay in this world.

 

Note: Maximum remaining time is 30 days.

 2

Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

Thirty days?

 

The system was clearly allowing the Samsara player time to continue exploring.

 

Fenric smiled at the opportunity.

 

Behind him, Riot stared in awe and fear.

 1

Once aboard the spacecraft, Riot retracted his transformation, returning to Drake's human form.

 

Fenric waved to Belle Morwyn and introduced them with a grin.

 

"This is my boss—Drake."

 

Then he glanced at her. "And this is my friend. Wait… what's your current name again?"

 

"Jessica!" Belle Morwyn replied with a smile.

 

BOOM!

 

Right then, the countdown reached zero.

 

The spacecraft launched, rocketing into space.

 

Fenric suddenly thought of something and turned to Drake.

 

"Boss, do you know how to get to the symbiote homeworld? Don't tell me this is some long-haul trip that'll take decades."

 4

"!!"

 

Belle's eyes widened in shock.

 

He wants to go slaughter an entire symbiote planet?!

 

This man really was a monster!

 

Drake, however, answered coldly, "There's a space node ahead. We can use it to warp there instantly."

 4

Fenric relaxed. "Perfect."

 

He didn't mind Drake's aloofness.

 

Now that they were in space, Drake wouldn't dare act against him.

 

After all, if the ship was damaged… none of them would survive.
