chapters.name: Chapter 141: Chapter 141: The Moment of Landing, The Moment of Betrayal!
chapters.content:
In the early days of the Venom universe—when all was still void—there existed ancient life.

 

Among them slept "Knull," the god of symbiosis, hidden deep within the darkness.

 

One day, a blinding light pierced the void and awakened Knull.

 

That light came from the Celestials—they were forging stars, creating life and order across the cosmos.

 1

Knull, enraged by this intrusion, rejected the Celestials' creations. A battle broke out. From the shadows, Knull drew the All-Black Necrosword—a blade of death—and slew a Celestial.

 3

That very sword would become the origin of all symbiotes.

 

But Knull's defiance came at a cost. He was exiled from the void by the rest of the Celestials. In exile, he used their blood, flames, and divine hammers to further refine his weapon. During the forging, the intense heat and ultrasonic vibrations left a lasting impact—becoming the fatal weaknesses of all symbiotes that followed.

 1

This is why symbiotes fear sound and fire.

 

From there, Knull's story twisted further.

 

He created the first symbiotes using the All-Black sword. With them, he assembled a fearsome force—the 27th Symbiote Legion—and began conquering planets, spreading chaos across the universe.

 

But betrayal came swiftly.

 

On a nameless planet, the symbiotes turned against their god, imprisoning him deep within the world he sought to rule.

 

To ensure he never escaped, the symbiotes fused into a planetary mass, becoming Klyntar, their so-called homeworld. Ironically, "Klyntar" meant "cage."

 

Although they had overthrown Knull, the symbiotes still bore his dark legacy—an innate thirst for conquest. So, when Riot discovered Earth, he immediately set out to summon the symbiote army and conquer it.

 

Silent space.

 

A lone spaceship drifted through the void.

 

Riot, now a mass of writhing tentacles, was operating the ship's control system.

 

In the cockpit, Fenric and Belle sat side by side, watching Riot work.

 

"This is a symbiote, huh?" Belle muttered. "Kinda ugly, but... I have to admit, pretty damn strong."

 

Fenric gave a slight smile, but his eyes soon narrowed.

 

Traveling to the symbiote homeworld to slaughter its inhabitants was an incredibly dangerous plan.

 

And the danger didn't lie in the symbiotes themselves—but in the one sealed beneath them...

 

Knull—the god of the symbiotes.

 

An ancient deity, terrifyingly powerful.

 

If Knull sensed him, Fenric could be wiped out in an instant.

 1

This entire mission was a gamble.

 

As he mulled over the risks, Riot suddenly turned his head and growled, "Buckle up. I don't want you puking all over my ship."

 

The moment the words fell, the spacecraft dove into the void and vanished from normal space.

 

Silence. Absolute silence.

 

All sound disappeared from Fenric's ears. It was as if they had entered a realm where time itself stood still.

 

All around them, dazzling streams of color stretched and warped, distorting their vision.

 

Fenric glanced toward Belle Morwyn—and his eyes widened.

 

Her body looked stretched, aged, grotesquely twisted. Her face deformed into something inhuman.

 

But it didn't last.

 

Seconds later, the spacecraft burst free from the warped dimension and returned to stable reality.

 

Their bodies snapped back to normal.

 

Belle gasped, clutching her chest. "What the hell was that? A wormhole? That was... terrifying."

 

Even Fenric had been uneasy. For a moment, he genuinely wondered if they'd survive.

 

"We're home!" Riot shouted from the front, excitement in his voice.

 

Fenric and Belle Morwyn looked through the glass.

 

A massive red planet loomed ahead.

 

Its atmosphere was thin and unstable. Even from orbit, they could tell—the world was dead, desolate, and unwelcoming.

 

Suddenly, Riot turned to them. His eyes gleamed with menace.

 

"I don't care why you came here," he growled. "But once you step on this planet, you'd better behave. Otherwise, the entire universe will pay the price."

 

Fenric's gaze sharpened.

 

From Riot's reaction, one thing became certain—

 

The god of symbiosis was real.

 

But so what?

 1

Even if Knull truly existed, Fenric would not abandon his plan.

 

If unleashing Knull was the price... so be it.

 

What did the fate of the universe matter to Fenric?

 

Besides, this was still the Marvel Universe—filled with cosmic entities and gods. Knull might be terrifying, but he wasn't the strongest.

 7

The spacecraft descended.

 

Fenric and Belle had already donned oxygen masks.

 

This planet's atmosphere was deadly to humans. Even someone as powerful as Fenric couldn't survive long without support.

 

As the ship landed...

 

And just as Riot was about to disembark and summon his kind—

 

A sudden disruption.

 

A lone human stood at the exit of the spacecraft.

 

Riot squinted. Recognition flashed across his face.

 

It was Drake's former driver.

 

Belle Morwyn's eyes widened. She instantly realized—this man must be a fellow Samsara.

 

She glanced at Fenric.

 

Still calm. Still collected. The Shura Boss showed no hint of fear.

 

Reassured, Belle breathed easier.

 

"Shura is here," she thought. "Everything will be fine."

 

"Step aside!"

 

Riot marched toward the hatch.

 

But the man raised his voice. "Stop right there, you ugly freak! Look at what I've got on me! You take one more step, and we all go down together!"

 

Fenric's eyes flicked to the man's chest.

 

Bombs. Dozens of them. All strapped to his body.

 

And in his hand—the trigger.

 

If he let go, they'd all be vaporized.

 

Riot froze mid-step. He glared at the driver, rage barely contained.

 

The driver smirked and turned to Fenric.

 

"Shura," he said loudly, "I'm here to propose an alliance."

 

"Don't give me that 'everyone mind their own business' crap. I won't accept it. I know how powerful you are. So, either we join forces... or we all die right here!"

 

Riot looked from one to the other, fuming with frustration.

 

"What the hell are these humans saying?" he muttered. "I don't understand a single word!"

chapters.name: Chapter 142: Chapter 142: Spare My Life!
chapters.content:
"Boss Shura, I've actually been planning this ever since I found out you were tackling this dungeon!"

 1

"Because I know you—unless you can secure an SSS-tier evaluation—you wouldn't bother making a move."

 

"The four symbiotes alone aren't enough for an SSS rating. So I figured—you must know where to find a large number of them. That's why I decided to follow you in secret!"

 

"Once you killed that foolish woman and still remained calm, it confirmed my theory. You'd rather let two symbiotes die in the lab than intervene... which means you knew where more symbiotes were hiding!"

 

"And I was right all along!"

 

"I never expected you to discover the Symbiote Planet!"

 

"Boss Shura, I have to say, I'm in awe. I respect you to the core!"

 

Hearing all this, Fenric was speechless.

 

I guess this counts as being famous... right?

 

Then he asked coldly, "You must have some kind of aura-concealing ability, don't you?"

 

The spaceship wasn't that big. With Fenric's current level of spiritual awareness, even the slightest movement inside couldn't escape him. For this guy to sneak aboard unnoticed... it had to be some breath-hiding technique.

 

"Sharp as ever, Boss Shura!" the male Samsara player grinned. "I've mastered the 'Lurking' skill to the Grandmaster level. Otherwise, I'd never have gotten past you!"

 

"So now the question is—will you form an alliance with me... or shall we die together?"

 

The man smirked at Fenric, clearly thinking he had the upper hand.

 

What can the most talented man in the Samsara Space do?

 

Even he's been outwitted by me!

 1

"Shura, don't try to sweet-talk your way out of this. If we don't form an alliance, you'll definitely kill me. That leaves you with only one option."

 

"Don't take it personally—scheming against each other is the norm in Samsara Space. You help me get the SSS-tier reward, and I'll hand over all the points and rare items to you! I only want the rating. I'll even give you another item when we return to Samsara Space!"

 2

The symbiote Riot, who had been standing nearby, looked completely baffled.

 

Samsara Space? SSS-tier rewards?

 

It had no idea what any of that meant.

 

(Note: In this world, revealing information about the Samsara Space isn't restricted. There's a reason for that.)

 3

Clap! Clap! Clap!

 

Fenric suddenly began clapping, a smile spreading across his face.

 

"Simple plan... but not bad. Still, next time—learn more about your target before you try to scheme against me."

 

"What do you mean?" the Samsara player frowned. "Shura, I know you're powerful, but you'd better think this through. You think I'm bluffing? I swear I'll take everyone down with me!"

 

But Fenric only smiled faintly.

 

Even if this fool triggered a self-destruct, Fenric wouldn't die. With his Grandmaster-level Armament Haki, he could easily shield himself from an explosion of that magnitude.

 

The only real danger was to Belle, who stood nearby.

 

Suddenly, Belle Morwyn stepped forward. "I'll form an alliance with you," she said. "I'm already allied with the Shura God. So if you team up with me, you automatically become our ally."

 

"Alliance with you? Do I look stupid?"

 

The Samsara player clearly wasn't that easy to fool. He turned to Fenric, impatient.

 

"Shura! Make your choice. Don't waste my time!"

 1

Fenric chuckled. "Sorry. I'm not interested in alliances today. Maybe in your next life, I'll carry you through a dungeon."

 

As soon as he finished speaking, the Samsara player's expression changed.

 

He opened his mouth to retort—only for his eyes to go wide in shock.

 

A sharp iron shard—origin unknown—shot clean through the back of his head, exiting through his forehead in a spray of blood.

 

The shard had been launched by Fenric's psychokinesis.

 

This overly confident Samsara clearly had no idea about Fenric's abilities. His power of thought could manipulate reality in unpredictable ways—and the fool had let his guard down completely.

 

"Crap! It's going to explode!" Riot yelled, preparing to flee.

 

But to his surprise, the dead man's body was still standing, his hand clutching the detonator motionless.

 

That, too, was the work of Fenric's psychokinesis—locking the man's posture and hand in place to prevent detonation.

 

Fenric then opened the ship's hatch and casually hurled the body out into space.

 1

BOOM!!

 

A distant explosion echoed.

 2

Fenric turned back to Riot with a calm expression.

 

"Did you bring me here to kill my kind?" Riot asked darkly.

 

Even though he hadn't fully understood the earlier conversation, it wasn't hard to guess the truth from the context—Fenric had come to exterminate the symbiotes.

 

"That's right," Fenric replied without hesitation.

 

There was no point pretending now—he might as well be direct.

 

Riot was instantly furious. He wanted nothing more than to devour Fenric on the spot.

 

After all, he was the one who had brought Fenric to the Symbiote Planet!

 

"You'll pay for this treachery. You'll die here!" Riot roared—but he didn't dare make a move.

 

They were still inside the spaceship.

 

Riot needed this ship to carry his army of millions of symbiotes to Earth. He couldn't risk damaging it in a fight.

 

Fenric ignored him and turned to Belle Morwyn.

 

"Belle, bring out all the weapons. Arm them."

 

"Yes, my Lord!"

 

Belle responded immediately and headed to the storage room to start assembling missiles.

 

With her enhanced strength, she could easily carry them. And thanks to recent training, she was no longer clueless about how to use them.

 

Once she left, Fenric turned back to Riot and smiled.

 

"Riot... you must have a way to contact your kind, right? Go ahead. Summon them. As long as you bring out enough symbiotes... maybe I'll let you live."

 

"Let me live? You ignorant human, you have no idea how powerful I truly am!"

 

Before Riot could finish his sentence, Fenric suddenly pulled out a whistle and brought it to his lips.

 1

Sound Enchantment Whistle—

 

When blown, it emits a high-frequency sound that causes auditory hallucinations and severely affects enemies who are sensitive to sound.

 

A moment later—

 

FWEEEEET!!

 

The piercing noise filled the air.

 

And just like that—

 

Riot dropped to his knees, trembling violently, almost blurting out:

 

"D-Daddy! Please spare me!!"

 13

chapters.name: Chapter 143: Chapter 143: Massacre of the Million Symbiote Army
chapters.content:
Fenric blew a piercing whistle—shrill and high-decibel.

 

A sound that was the bane of all symbiotes.

 

Suddenly, the massive body of Riot began to tremble violently. It let out an agonized roar, unable to maintain its form. Within moments, its body split apart, revealing the host—Drake—inside.

 

"You have used the Enchanted Whistle."

 

"Reminder: The Enchanted Whistle is a one-time-use item. Its magic effect will expire in ten days."

 

Fenric remained expressionless as the system prompt echoed in his mind.

 

As the symbiote Riot could no longer hold on and withdrew from Drake's body, Fenric stopped whistling.

 

"How's that, Riot? Can you endure it?" Fenric asked with a smirk.

 

The Riot symbiote had already retreated deep into Drake's body, too afraid to show itself. For now, Drake was in full control.

 1

Drake was drenched in sweat, panting heavily, half-kneeling on the ground, looking utterly drained. He looked up at Fenric, dazed.

 

"Ronan... there's no clause in the contract about the employer getting hurt," he said weakly.

 

Fenric didn't bother replying. Instead, he drew a flamethrower and aimed it coldly at Drake's face.

 

"Riot, I'll say this one more time: Call your kind here. Now. Or I'll burn you to death."

 

Whoosh! Whoosh!

 

Flames burst from the nozzle.

 

Like sound, fire was also a fatal weakness of the symbiotes.

 

Seeing this, Drake quickly raised his hands. "Alright, alright! Calm down, man—I'll do it, okay?!"

 

Symbiotes had no real unity.

 

Even Riot had its own agenda—willing to sacrifice its kind as cannon fodder, using sheer numbers to eliminate Fenric.

 

With no other choice, Drake transformed back into Riot, walked to the spacecraft's exit (Number 540), and let out an ear-splitting roar to the sky.

 

"ROOAAARR!!"

 

The howl shook the heavens.

 

The sound carried far, echoing through the wild expanse.

 

Moments later, dark clouds of slime began forming on the distant horizon, converging on the spacecraft.

 

Densely packed. Endless.

 

Seeing this, Fenric shouted, "Belle! Are you ready?!"

 

"Ready, Great God!" Belle Morwyn replied, her voice trembling with excitement and nervousness.

 

Her heart was pounding as she watched the swarms of symbiotes flood in from every direction.

 

As expected—following the boss really does bring rewards!

 

"Fire at will!"

 

At Fenric's command, Belle immediately hit the launch switch.

 2

Swish! Swish! Swish!

 

Over a dozen missiles shot out in an instant.

 1

There was no need to aim.

 

With Riot's summons, the symbiotes were flooding in uncontrollably, blanketing the ground.

 

Boom! Boom! Boom!

 

Explosions roared, and system notifications flooded Belle's mind.

 

"You have killed a symbiote. Main mission completed."

 

"You may return to the Samsara Space or remain in this world."

 

"Note: Maximum stay time is 30 days."

 

"You killed a symbiote. Current mission progress: 2/1."

 

"You killed a symbiote. Current mission progress: 3/1."

 

"You killed a symbiote. Current mission progress: 4/1."

 

"You killed a symbiote. Current mission progress: 4837/1."

 

After the first wave of missiles, Belle Morwyn's mission progress had skyrocketed—she had killed 4,837 symbiotes in seconds!

 

"Great God... this...!" she stammered, overwhelmed with joy.

 

Fenric barked, "Stop gawking! Keep firing!"

 

Snapped back to her senses, Belle nodded vigorously, reloaded, and launched another barrage.

 

Boom! Boom! Boom!

 

"You killed a symbiote. Current progress: 12,219/1."

 

This harvest was even greater than the last.

 

The symbiote army was still growing.

 

In the original story, Riot claimed to have a million-strong army—and it wasn't an exaggeration!

 

Although Belle Morwyn's missiles had wiped out many, compared to the tidal wave of symbiotes still surging forward, it was only a drop in the ocean.

 

Down below, the symbiotes kept crawling forward, endless and overwhelming.

 

Belle Morwyn was flushed with excitement.

 

She never imagined she'd get to slaughter symbiotes like this!

 

But then—

 

A blob of black slime suddenly burst from the spacecraft's hull, heading straight for her.

 

"Om!"

 

Fenric activated his mind power.

 

The symbiote froze mid-air, struggling madly but unable to advance.

 

Belle Morwyn turned pale with fright.

 

Being possessed by a symbiote usually meant death.

 

Because not everyone could handle a bond with one of the "Symbiote Four."

 

Aside from physical compatibility, the symbiote also had to accept you.

 

So even if symbiote fusion promised power, no Samsara player dared to risk it.

 

Those who did—died.

 

Fwoosh!

 

A jet of flame appeared. The struggling creature was quickly incinerated.

 

"Thank you, thank you, Lord Shura!" Belle said earnestly, her face pale.

 

Fenric retracted the flamethrower and calmly turned his gaze toward the endless symbiote army.

 

Belle Morwyn, however, looked terrified.

 

"You should go," Fenric said. "Return to the Samsara Space. The rest of this battle isn't something you can be part of."

 

The system had already notified her—she could leave anytime or stay for up to thirty days.

 

Belle Morwyn nodded obediently. "Okay. Be careful, Lord Shura."

 

She knew that staying would only hold him back.

 

"I will." Fenric smiled faintly.

 

Belle Morwyn gave him one last look before vanishing from the spot.

 

Now alone, Fenric began his massacre in earnest.

 

He grabbed the rest of the incendiary bombs Belle had brought and threw them into the horde.

 

Boom! Boom! Boom!

 

Though incendiary bombs weren't as explosive as missiles, their damage lingered.

 

The planet's atmosphere had more oxygen than Earth's, so flames burned even hotter.

 

Sometimes, a single burning symbiote would flee, spreading fire to others in the crowd.

 

"You killed a symbiote. Progress: 3/1."

 

"You killed a symbiote. Progress: 4/1."

 

"You killed a symbiote. Progress: 336/1."

 

Before the bombs were used up, Fenric found the pace too slow.

 

So he leapt off the spacecraft—straight into the enemy ranks.

 

Seeing this, Riot let out a furious scream and commanded the army to swarm him.

 

Fenric just laughed.

 

"Perfect."

 

Fweeeet—!

 

The enchanted whistle blew again.

 7

All around him, symbiotes froze in place, paralyzed.

 

Fenric fired up the flamethrower and reaped them like weeds.

 

The slaughter lasted three days and two nights.

 

The battlefield was a sea of fire and charred symbiote corpses.

 

If not for the system's constant updates, Fenric would've lost count of his kills.

 

Riot stood atop the spacecraft, trembling with rage as it watched its kind perish.

 

But it never dared approach.

 

Because Fenric wielded two ultimate weapons: the enchanted whistle and the flamethrower.

 

Both were symbiote killers.

 

Even Riot, as powerful as it was, didn't dare face him directly.

 

Suddenly, Riot's expression changed. Its monstrous face twisted in fear.

 

Without a sound, it turned and fled.

 

Fenric, mid-massacre, paused—not from exhaustion. His body could fight for days without rest.

 

It was the symbiotes—they were retreating.

 

Fenric froze, eyes narrowing.

 

Then, realization struck.

 

"System, return me to the Samsara Space—now!"

 

The words had barely left his lips before he vanished.

 

BOOM!

 

A massive, inhuman hand slammed down where Fenric had just been standing—missing him by inches.

 

A second later, from deep underground, a monstrous roar echoed—inhuman, guttural, and filled with a terrifying presence that shook the air.

 2

chapters.name: Chapter 144: Chapter 144: Can a Person Become Super God?
chapters.content:
"Congratulations! Samsara Player Shura performed exceptionally well in the dungeon world of Samsara Tower: Venom – Deadly Guardian. During the mission, he eliminated 121,577 symbiotes, far exceeding the mission requirements, and earned the highest rating: SSS!"

 

Super God!

 

At that moment, in the Samsara Plaza, inside the Dungeon Hall, and even within the dungeon worlds where missions were still ongoing—every Samsara player across the entire Samsara Space heard the broadcast!

 

Super God Evaluation: SSS!

 

Once again, it appeared.

 

When Shura's name flashed across the system interface, most people had grown somewhat numb. But when they realized the dungeon world was Venom, shock followed.

 

Over 120,000 symbiotes killed?

 

Was that even possible?

 

Wasn't Venom supposed to only have four known symbiotes?

 

Where did the hundreds of thousands come from?

 

"F**k me! Did the great Shura wipe out the entire symbiote race?"

 

"One hundred twenty thousand?! Even if he destroyed the symbiote's home planet, that number's insane!"

 

"My god, how did Shura do that? Even if they lined up to die, it would take forever to kill that many!"

 

"Must be something like what happened in the World War Z dungeon. Shura must've used some kind of trick."

 

"Has to be fire. Everyone knows symbiotes fear fire!"

 

"Yeah, but that many? Where the hell did all those symbiotes come from?!"

 

"Same question. I hope the great Shura himself can explain!"

 

"Isn't this the fifth time Shura has scored an SSS? Damn, is he actually going to reach the top of the tower?"

 

The Samsara Space buzzed with speculation. Shock, admiration, and disbelief mingled into chaos.

 

Just as the chatter peaked, another system broadcast echoed across the entire space:

 

"Congratulations! Samsara Player Belle Morwyn performed admirably in the dungeon world of Samsara Tower: Venom – Deadly Guardian. During the mission, she eliminated 12,219 symbiotes, far exceeding mission requirements, and earned a top-tier rating: SS!"

 

Just like Shura's earlier announcement, this new one rang through the Samsara Space.

 

Silence.

 

And then—

 

Boom!

 

The entire space erupted like a pot of boiling oil thrown with raw meat!

 

This was the first time anyone had ever seen the system publicly announce an SS evaluation. Up until now, only SSS seemed worthy of that spotlight.

 

But that wasn't what shocked everyone the most.

 

The real shock was: Who the hell is Belle Morwyn?

 

And how did she get the same high rating from the same dungeon as Shura?

 

Anyone with half a brain could connect the dots—this newcomer must be connected to Shura!

 

"Same dungeon. One got SSS. The other SS. F**k, what's going on?"

 

"Who is this Belle Morwyn? Never heard of her before, yet she scores an SS?"

 

"No doubt about it—Shura carried her through the dungeon!"

 

"Exactly! Without Shura, how could she kill over ten thousand symbiotes?"

 

"Holy sh*t, can Shura even carry people like that? Next time, count me in—I'll do anything!"

 

"Shura is too awesome! Not only does he get a super god evaluation, he even brings others along for a high rating!"

 

"From today on, I bet the higher-ups won't be able to sit still. Shura's value is off the charts. He can raise people like he's nurturing future legends!"

 

"Right? With someone like Shura, even trash can rise to power. Just stick close and soak up the benefits!"

 

"F**k, I have a PhD and still can't find the words to describe how godlike Shura is!"

 1

"Ahhhhh, I want Shura to carry me too!"

 

"I'm almost at the Fifth Stage! Master Shura, please bring me once—just once!"

 

"Great God Shura, pick me! I'm a girl, a beautiful girl! If you take me, I'll be your loyal puppy!"

 1

The entire Samsara Space was on fire with hype and envy.

 

It didn't take a genius to realize that Belle Morwyn's sudden success was thanks to Shura. She had reaped rewards just by tagging along.

 

Belle Morwyn had been silent all this time, completely unknown. Then tonight, out of nowhere, she scored an SS rating in the Venom dungeon.

 

Could anyone seriously believe she pulled it off alone?

 

No—everyone knew she was carried.

 

The phrase echoing through everyone's mind now was:

 

"Follow Shura to eat meat!"

 

Shura wasn't just a god-tier solo player now—he was a one-man power-leveling factory. The kind of man who could casually flick a few crumbs and still change someone's destiny.

 

Belle Morwyn was the living proof.

 

Shura's value had skyrocketed again.

 

People were fantasizing about kneeling to Shura, just to become one of his followers.

 

Let's not exaggerate, but if Shura were to suddenly declare the formation of a faction, the signup lines would stretch across the entire Samsara Plaza.

 

Even the average Samsara were stunned.

 

But for those who actually knew Belle Morwyn, their reactions were on a whole different level.

 

Inside a bar—

 

One Leaf Knows Autumn hadn't logged off yet. He was still drinking alone, drowning his sorrows.

 

When the two broadcasts hit, he abruptly stood from his seat.

 

Bang!

 

The heavy wine glass in his hand shattered in an instant.

 

This alone proved One Leaf Knows Autumn's strength stat wasn't low.

 

"Shura..."

 

His voice was low, a mix of disbelief and acceptance. His face twisted through a dozen expressions before settling into a long sigh as he sank back into his seat.

 

Now he finally understood—why Aurora Morwyn had asked him for a flamethrower on Shura's behalf.

 

It was all to boost Belle Morwyn under Shura's guidance.

 

And once again, Shura had proven his terrifying value.

 

Not only could he earn SSS ratings himself, but he could lead others to top ratings as well.

 

With news like this, those old, powerful forces lurking behind the scenes—surely, they'd start paying very close attention to Shura now.

 

As for One Leaf Knows Autumn's personal grudge over his nephew... well, any thoughts of revenge were now a fantasy.

 1

That path was closing fast.

 1

He sighed again.

 

After tossing a few credits onto the counter to pay for the broken glass, he quietly logged off and returned to the real world.

 3

chapters.name: Chapter 145: Chapter 145: Aurora Morwyn’s Surprise
chapters.content:
Inside a private box at the teahouse,

 

Aurora remained online.

 

She had always shared a close bond with Belle. Since Belle was currently tackling a dungeon tonight, as her older sister naturally couldn't rest easy.

 

Even if Shura was a so-called genius who could clear content by simply lying down, Aurora still harbored some concern.

 

It was perfectly reasonable—after all, the Samsara Tower's dungeons were infamously dangerous.

 

That's why she waited.

 

When the broadcast suddenly announced that Shura had once again achieved a Super God rating, Aurora's lips curved slightly into a smile. She muttered under her breath:

 

"Shura… you've done it again."

 

At the same time, she exhaled a breath of relief.

 

If Shura succeeded, then surely that girl Belle had also completed the mission, right?

 

"I wonder what kind of rating Belle got? If she managed to score an A, that would already be impressive."

 

Just as she was thinking this, another system-wide announcement rang out in the Samsara Plaza:

 

"Congratulations! Samsara player Belle Morwyn performed outstandingly in the 'Venom: Deadly Guardian' dungeon within the Samsara Tower. During the mission, she eliminated 12,219 symbiotes, far surpassing the dungeon requirements, and achieved the highest rating: SS!"

 

"!!!"

 

Aurora's expression changed instantly. She sat up straight, eyes widening.

 

"Double S rating?!"

 

She repeated it to herself, shock written all over her delicate face.

 

Even she had never achieved an SS rating!

 1

But moments later, her surprise gave way to joy, and she laughed freely.

 

"That girl Belle must be over the moon right now."

 

Just then, the system prompted her:

 

"You have a new communication request. 'Adam' is inviting you to a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

Hearing this, Aurora's eyes flashed, and then she calmly accepted the call.

 

The screen lit up.

 

A middle-aged white man with deep-set eyes appeared on the screen. His appearance was plain—even slightly bald—making him look like any average person.

 

If someone saw him on the street, they would never suspect that this was Adam, the world's number-one expert and the only player to ever achieve a comprehensive S rating in strength.

 

Of course, this was just a disguise—a persona Adam had created when he first entered the Samsara space.

 

"Good evening, madam," Adam greeted with a polite smile.

 

Aurora Morwyn returned the smile. "Mr. Adam, what brings you to contact me so suddenly?"

 

"I want to propose a cooperation."

 

Adam got straight to the point—time was short, and the Samsara space would be closing soon. There was no time for pleasantries.

 

"Cooperation?" Aurora asked, still smiling. "What kind?"

 

"I know that Belle Morwyn is your younger sister. That genius—Shura—helped her achieve an SS rating. Given that, your relationship with him must be quite… special. I'm hoping you can persuade him to bring one of my friends along for a dungeon run."

 

Without waiting for her reply, Adam added, "Aurora, I heard you just cleared the 28th floor? As a sign of good faith, I'm willing to share key information about the 29th-floor dungeon—Avengers 3."

 1

Aurora's smile faded into a cold smirk.

 

The arrogance of this guy—it ran deep in his bones.

 

He thought that offering a mere dungeon tip would be enough to get her to convince Shura to carry someone through a mission?

 

It wasn't even a question of whether she could convince Shura. Even if she could, she wouldn't do something so foolish.

 

"I'm sorry, Mr. Adam. I'm afraid I can't help you. You'll have to contact Shura yourself."

 

As she said this, Aurora couldn't help but sigh softly.

 

Shura truly was remarkable.

 

Even a man like Adam had to beg him for help!

 

She had heard the rumors—that Adam viewed Shura as a dangerous rival and had long sought to eliminate him.

 

Adam didn't appear surprised by her refusal. He gazed at her through the screen and calmly upped the offer:

 

"Aurora, if it's a matter of sincerity, I can give you something else—an exclusive item. It can erase the Devil Fruit ability in your body and let you obtain a new one."

 

"..."

 

Aurora's eyes flickered with emotion.

 

In her younger days, she had foolishly consumed a highly embarrassing Devil Fruit. It had severely limited her growth ever since.

 2

Such things weren't uncommon in the Samsara space.

 

The Third Stage of the One Piece dungeon rarely awarded powerful Devil Fruits—players often got stuck with subpar ones.

 

To get a strong Devil Fruit, one had to challenge the second stage of the One Piece dungeon.

 

But how many people could resist the temptation of superpowers and survive long enough to reach it?

 

She never imagined Adam had an item that could erase a Devil Fruit ability.

 

She had to admit… she was tempted.

 

This was exactly what she needed most right now.

 

But.

 

Aurora still shook her head.

 

"I'm sorry, Mr. Adam. I appreciate your sincerity… but I must decline."

 

Adam's brows finally furrowed. He asked directly:

 

"Aurora, let's not dance around it. What do you want?"

 

This request—to have Shura carry someone—was extremely important. Far more critical than just "helping a friend."

 

"Adam, you misunderstand. Shura is his own person. No one can force him to do anything. Besides… I've heard that you've been plotting against him in secret. Do you really think he'd agree to your request?"

 

"Hostility is hostility. Cooperation is cooperation," Adam replied calmly. "That genius is smart—he knows how to distinguish between the two."

 1

"I'm powerless here," Aurora said flatly. "You'll have to try your own luck."

 

With that, she hung up.

 

She wasn't afraid of Adam causing trouble. Nor was she worried about him threatening Belle.

 

Belle was her younger sister, and her identity was no secret in the Samsara space.

 

Everyone knew who the top 100 players were.

 

The unspoken rule was simple: resolve personal grudges in private, but don't involve family.

 

Endangering someone's loved ones would shatter that balance.

 

And if anyone broke that rule…

 

Everyone would unite to strike them down.

 6

"You have a new communication request. 'Sventovite' is inviting you to a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

She had just ended her call with Adam when another request came in.

 

Sventovite—ranked third in the global leaderboard.

 

Aurora declined it without hesitation. She already knew what he wanted—the same thing Adam did.

 

She opened her friend list and clicked on Belle's account, sending her a video request.

 

Moments later, the screen lit up.

 

"Sis! You're still online? I was just about to look for you!"

 

Belle Morwyn beamed. Her beautiful face glowed with joy, clearly having just received her mission rewards. 

 

[TL/n: Changing how Belle calls Aurora from Cousin to Sis. The first one was done to make it easier to remember that she's her cousin. Now that everyone knows who she is, I'm changing it back to normal.]

 1

chapters.name: Chapter 146: Chapter 146: We Want to Hug Your Thighs Too!
chapters.content:
Belle Morwyn's beautiful face was lit up with excitement.

 

"You look really happy this time, don't you?" Aurora asked with a smile.

 

Belle Morwyn nodded eagerly.

 

"Yes, sister! I got an SS rating! Just from Samsara points alone, I earned 24,000! And there were other rewards too!"

 

Even Aurora couldn't help but feel a tinge of envy.

 

24,000 Samsara points!

 

With her current strength, she might not earn that much even after completing an entire dungeon run.

 

And that wasn't counting the item rewards!

 

"We'll talk about the details later," Aurora said. "Tell me first—how did Shura help you clear the dungeon? How did you two manage to kill that many symbiotes?"

 

"Sis, you won't believe how strong Shura is!"

 

Belle Morwyn's eyes sparkled as she mentioned his name.

 

"You'd never guess where he took me after—we actually went straight to the symbiote planet! He found their home base and took me there to farm them!"

 

"What!?"

 

Aurora was stunned.

 

She'd had a vague suspicion, but hearing her sister confirm it made her truly realize just how terrifying Shura's abilities were.

 

He actually wiped out the symbiote's nest?

 

Too savage!

 

Just then, the system announcement echoed in the air:

 

"Attention all Samsara players: The Samsara Space will close in 5 minutes."

 

Both Aurora and Belle heard it clearly.

 

"You're free tomorrow, right, Belle? Come see me."

 

"Okay, sis, got it!"

 

"Alright. We'll talk more when we meet."

 

Dear Samsara "Shura", you have completed the task. Your rewards are as follows:

 

Samsara Points: 40,000

 

Oxygen Mask x1 (Special item – stored in your personal warehouse)

 4

Riot Gloves x1 (Special item – stored in your personal warehouse)

 

Golden Treasure Box x1 (Stored in your personal warehouse)

 

Fenric was quite satisfied with the system rewards.

 

Two special items!

 

Now the only question was—what would the Golden Treasure Box contain this time?

 

"Attention all Samsara: The Samsara Space will close in 5 minutes."

 

Hearing the countdown from the system, Fenric decided to check his rewards later and logged off first.

 5

Back in the real world.

 

Fenric calmly reviewed the mission in his mind.

 

All in all, the results were excellent—after all, he received a Super God rating.

 

But...

 

There were a few loose ends.

 

For example, Riot was still alive, and the spaceship hadn't been destroyed.

 

The Earth in that world would likely suffer later, wouldn't it?

 5

Of course, that wasn't Fenric's problem.

 

Maybe after he left, the Samsara system reset that world.

 6

Smiling to himself, Fenric dismissed the thought and drifted off to sleep.

 

The dungeon had been relaxing in the beginning, but the final stretch was truly exhausting.

 

At least for now, the "Venom" dungeon had nothing more to do with him.

 

Morning.

 

He only slept for two hours before waking up at dawn.

 

At 7:00 AM, his biological clock woke him up naturally.

 

After getting washed up, he rushed off to school.

 

When he entered the classroom, a few students' chatter caught his attention.

 

"Hey, did you hear? The goddess Yuhan from Class 1 got an SS rating in the 'Venom' dungeon last night. I heard the rewards were crazy!"

 2

"No way? When did that happen? I was in the Samsara Space too and didn't hear anything."

 

"You probably logged off early. It happened around five in the morning."

 

"Damn! And didn't she just get a Devil Fruit in the 'One Piece' dungeon recently? Now she's got an SS rating too? That's insane!"

 

"Heh, what's so impressive?"

 

"Oh come on, Fuxen, don't tell me you're jealous of Goddess Yuhan?"

 

"Jealous? Of course I am! But I'm more jealous of her luck. Do you really think she earned that SS rating on her own? Shura carried her!"

 

"Wait, seriously? Shura helped her clear the dungeon?"

 

"Why would I lie? Check your phone—it's all over the internet. Last night, Shura got an SSS-level Super God rating, and Yuhan got SS by tagging along!"

 

"Damn, Goddess Yuhan actually managed to cling to Shura's thigh? Isn't this the first time he's ever brought someone with him? So lucky!"

 

"Tch! What's there to envy? Yuhan probably offered herself to get him to take her along. Why else would Shura help her?"

 

"Fuxen, don't say that kind of thing. It's bad to spread rumors. Besides, Goddess Yuhan has powerful connections—maybe someone influential offered her to Shura!"

 

"Either way, Shura is insane. Getting a Super God evaluation is one thing, but he even managed to carry someone else to an SS rank? Unreal!"

 

"Sigh… if only Shura would take me on a run!"

 

Fenric was speechless as he listened.

 

Belle Morwyn… was actually Yuhan Song?

 

That goddess all the boys were obsessed with?

 

Well, damn.

 

But now that her identity was public, wouldn't she be in danger?

 

Then again, Fenric chuckled at the thought.

 

With that kind of background, there was nothing to worry about.

 

As long as Aurora Morwyn was around, who would dare touch Belle in the real world?

 

That said…

 

If it were him, even with a powerful backer, he'd never reveal his true identity.

 

There were too many threats in the Samsara Space—even someone like Aurora Morwyn couldn't guarantee her own safety forever.

 

If she ever failed in a dungeon, Belle Morwyn would become a prime target for vengeance and endless pursuit.

 

But whatever. That's their business—not his.

 

"Ric! Goddess Yuhan got an SS rating last night—how awesome is that!" Jitto called out from behind.

 

Fenric nodded absently. "Mm, yeah."

 

Jitto's voice took on a pervy tone.

 

"But hey, a lot of people think she must be close with Shura. I mean, he never takes anyone with him. Suddenly bringing a girl? Kinda sus, right? What do you think, Ric?"

 

Fenric: "…"

 

"Ohh, I'm so jealous of Shura. If I could just talk to Goddess Yuhan, I'd be satisfied. Never mind carrying her through a dungeon—I'd carry her for the rest of my life!" Jitto groaned with envy.

 

Fenric: "…"

chapters.name: Chapter 147: Chapter 147: The End of the World!
chapters.content:
Fenric was completely speechless.

 

All around him, students were whispering and speculating that Yuhan was in some sort of relationship with him—even suggesting that she was being kept by him.

 

How was he supposed to explain that he was completely innocent?

 

Forget it.

 

There was no point arguing with a bunch of gossipy students.

 

Shaking his head, Fenric pulled out his phone and began browsing the internet. He wanted to search for information related to the next-level dungeon.

 

Online, the forums were once again buzzing about his alter ego—"Shura."

 

However, this time, the screen was flooded not just with awe, but also with gossip and drama.

 

"Last night, the God of Shura once again received an SSS Super-God rating. Boss, you're insane!"

 

"Of course Shura's amazing, but what's the deal with this Belle Morwyn? How'd she get such a high score?"

 

"You even need to ask? They cleared the same dungeon. She clearly just coasted on Shura's efforts!"

 

"Wait, this is the first time Shura's brought someone with him, right? What's Belle Morwyn's background?"

 

"Morwyn... do I even need to spell it out? Her sister's ranked in the top 100!"

 

"Typical nepotism."

 1

"Heh, I heard Belle Morwyn is gorgeous and hailed as a genius. Maybe there were other reasons why the boss brought her along~"

 

"Quit with the sarcasm. If you were beautiful too, maybe you could cling to Shura's thigh! You think he'd even look at you?"

 

"I don't envy Belle Morwyn. I envy Shura!"

 

"Tch. Geniuses can do whatever they want, huh?"

 

"Belle Morwyn? Please, I'm way prettier. Lord Shura, if you're reading this, DM me! I'm cute and talented. Also, my tongue game is strong~ ❤️"

 15

"Hey girl, what's the price for your 'night package'?"

 

"Go to hell, you disgusting pig!!"

 

The flood of comments left Fenric utterly speechless.

 

For the first time, he truly understood how innocent celebrities must've felt in his past life.

 

He and Belle Morwyn had done nothing wrong, yet people were shamelessly speculating and pairing them together. Even if he jumped into the Yellow River, he couldn't wash this off.

 

As the saying went: "The tongues of men can melt gold, and slander ruins reputations."

 6

Still, Fenric didn't care.

 

Let them talk. He wasn't some fame-hungry internet star who lived off views and traffic.

 

He lived off power.

 

Strength was the only thing that mattered.

 

Closing the comments section, Fenric navigated to the Samsara Forum and entered the Strategy Zone.

 

He was looking for information about the Fifth Stage of the Samsara Tower.

 

Tonight, he planned to enter a new dungeon again.

 

Ever since Aurora warned him that in September, a massive compulsory dungeon—PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds—would begin, and many planned to ambush him during it, Fenric had resolved to become stronger as quickly as possible.

 

It was only mid-June now. There were still two and a half months left until September.

 

Fenric was confident that he could grow exponentially stronger before then.

 

Ambush me?

 

Let's see who's hunting who.

 

While searching the strategy section, Fenric was surprised to find that the Fifth Stage of the Samsara Tower only had one available dungeon.

 

It wasn't a massive fantasy world like One Piece.

 

Instead, it was labeled as a Novice Assessment Copy.

 

Its name: "2012".

 2

Fenric's pupils shrank slightly when he saw it.

 

2012?

 

If memory served, that was a disaster film about the end of the world.

 

In that movie's world, based on a Mayan prophecy, December 21st, 2012, marked doomsday—the end of the Mayan calendar, with no dates beyond.

 

When that day came, the Earth was devastated by catastrophic natural disasters: massive earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and tsunamis that submerged continents. Civilization collapsed. The world ended.

 

Recalling all this, Fenric's expression grew grim.

 

If the Fifth Stage dungeon was really based on 2012, how the hell were Samsara players supposed to survive? Anyone who entered would die!

 

Only he knew the movie's plot—and more importantly, the location of humanity's last hope.

 

Fenric frowned.

 

Surely the Samsara System wouldn't throw players into such a hopeless scenario so soon?

 

If it did, how did those top 100 experts even make it?

 

With this question in mind, he clicked on the official dungeon guide.

 

"There is only one dungeon on the Fifth Stage of the Samsara Tower: '2012.'"

 

"Surprised by the name? You should be. Because this dungeon is absolutely terrifying!"

 

"This floor is also known as the 'Novice Assessment Dungeon.' Once you clear it, you'll no longer be considered a novice in the Samsara Space."

 

"I'm the editor writing this, and I've personally experienced it. I can tell you with absolute certainty: this is a disaster-level dungeon."

 

"The main theme of the copy? The apocalypse."

 

"That's right. The end of the world. Global annihilation."

 

"Of course, the Samsara Space doesn't want everyone to die. While the dungeon itself is horrifying, the mission objectives are fairly straightforward—if you're well-prepared, passing it isn't too difficult. The real challenge lies in getting a high rating."

 

"The main objective is simple: survive."

 

"Task scoring works as follows:"

 

Survive 1 day = E rating

 

Survive 2 days = D rating

 

Survive 4 days = C rating

 

Survive 8 days = B rating

 

Survive 16 days = A rating

 

Survive 32 days = S rating

 

"In short, the longer you live, the higher your evaluation."

 

"But beware—this dungeon features constant mega-earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcanic eruptions. In the face of nature's fury, humans are incredibly small and fragile."

 

"Pro tip: form a party before entering."

 

"This is the only dungeon in the Samsara Tower where ally rewards are not shared—meaning, everyone in the alliance gets full rewards independently."

 4

"So don't be a lone wolf. Grab a few reliable teammates, and survive together."

 

"Remember: There's a strength in numbers!"

 1

_______

chapters.name: Chapter 148: Chapter 148: I Refuse to Accept That!
chapters.content:
"Back to the main point!"

 

"After entering the dungeon, the system will automatically assign you a civilian identity, which cannot be changed. Your starting location will be a city."

 

"If you have allies, the system will place them nearby."

 

"From there, you will be granted five hours of preparation time."

 

"Personal advice: during those five hours, gather as many supplies as you can—then run, drive, or fly! Just don't stay where you are, because the first city to sink… is the one right beneath your feet!"

 

"Don't even think about trying to fight against nature. I'm not exaggerating—when it comes to natural disasters, even if your power reaches S-Rank, you won't survive unless you can stay airborne permanently."

 

"There are three main survival strategies available to everyone."

 

"The first is to keep running. The world will be gradually destroyed by a series of escalating disasters that spread across the globe. If you're fast enough, you can stay ahead of them."

 

"Of course, others have tried this before—and at best, they survived for four days. By the fifth day, the entire continent will be swallowed by tsunamis, and the world will be consumed by a scorching sun. Unless you can breathe underwater, there's nowhere left to run!"

 

"The second way is to find a boat and head out to sea."

 

"But this path isn't recommended. Even the smallest tsunami is over fifty meters high. Not even an aircraft carrier can survive that. Do you think your little boat stands a chance? Unless you're unbelievably lucky, you're just buying time before the end."

 6

"The third and riskiest option: get your hands on a military-grade submarine and dive deep into the ocean."

 

"This task borders on impossible… but Adam managed to do it."

 

"It's said that Adam survived 17 days in this dungeon and received an A-rank evaluation!"

 

"The choice is yours."

 1

"Also, don't expect help from any government in the Dungeon World. In a disaster of this scale, even the president is just trying to survive."

 

"Of course, this editor's guide is far from perfect. I recommend checking out other players' guides for additional insights."

 

"And lastly… good luck!"

 

"..."

 

After reading the dungeon guide, Fenric paused, slightly surprised.

 

Then—

 

He laughed!

 

If you asked how to survive the movie 2012, the answer was obvious: get on the Ark.

 2

However, after checking through the forum, Fenric realized that no one seemed to know about the existence of the Ark.

 3

Ha!

 

Then again, it made sense. In the movie, only world leaders were aware of the Ark Project.

 1

According to their calculations, only 400,000 people out of the world's 7 billion would be saved during the cataclysm.

 

Such a colossal, resource-draining project naturally had to be kept secret.

 

So even in the dungeon world, only a tiny handful would know about the Ark.

 

Most Samsara players would be too busy trying to stay alive to uncover that kind of hidden plot point.

 

"Whew…"

 

Fenric exhaled deeply in relief.

 

Tonight, he would return to challenge the dungeon once more.

 

The Samsara Tower using 2012 as the assessment dungeon for novices? That was brutal.

 

The scenario was indeed terrifying—surviving long enough to earn a high evaluation would be extremely difficult.

 

But for Fenric, it was manageable.

 

Why?

 

Because he knew the story.

 

He knew the Ark was the one and only real hope for survival in this dungeon.

 

The Ark—developed by the combined efforts of world powers—was engineered to withstand apocalyptic forces. It could ride out a tsunami and survive the harshest environments.

 

With Fenric's current abilities, boarding the Ark would not be difficult.

 

"Ric, what are you grinning about?"

 1

Jitto's voice rang from behind.

 

Fenric quickly pocketed his phone and replied, "What's up?"

 

"Wanna hit the internet café after school tonight?" Jitto asked eagerly.

 

"Not going." Fenric rejected him without hesitation.

 

How could playing games in an internet café compare to experiencing Samsara dungeons firsthand?

 

"C'mon, don't shut me down right away! There's a new game out—designed to simulate the Samsara space. It's super popular and just hit public beta. Wanna check it out?"

 

Fenric scoffed. "If you could enter a real Samsara space, why would you waste time playing a simulation? Are you brain-dead?"

 3

"Damn… when you put it that way, it actually makes sense."

 

"Anyway, I'm going to read. Don't bother me unless it's important."

 

On the highway...

 

A luxury car sped along the road.

 

In the backseat sat Yuhan, hailed as a goddess by countless fans. She was scowling, eyebrows furrowed, furiously scrolling through her phone.

 

"Girl, what's wrong?" asked a poised and elegant woman sitting beside her. 

 

Yuhan raised her phone with a look of outrage. "Mom, look at this! People are saying I was sponsored by Shura! They're slandering me!"

 2

"Silly girl, that's just how the internet is," the lady replied with a gentle smile, then smoothly shifted the topic. "Your sister called for you this time. I doubt it's something simple. Someone high up has taken notice of Shura—they'll definitely want to ask you a few things."

 

"I know, my sister already warned me. Anyway, I don't even know what they expect from me."

 

"That's fine then. By the way, when is Shura planning to clear the Fifth Stage? Can he still take you with him?"

 

"I wish! But Shura isn't exactly easy to persuade. He only took me last time because my cousin helped me a lot."

 

"Then you'll have to thank your cousin properly later."

 6

"Yeah, I know."

 

While the two chatted, their car entered the capital.

 

That night, 12:00 a.m.

 

Fenric appeared in the Samsara space right on time.

 

His first stop: the personal warehouse—to check yesterday's rewards.

 

Because the dungeon had ended around 5 a.m., and the Samsara Space was about to close, he had logged off before reviewing them.

 

Just like before, he had received four rewards.

 

In addition to points and a golden treasure chest, there were two special items.

 

Fenric picked up one of them—a glove.

 

Its name: Riot Glove.

 

He guessed it was related to the symbiote "Riot."

 

As soon as his hand touched the glove, the system prompt appeared:

 

Special Item: Riot Glove

 

This glove contains part of the symbiote "Riot's" abilities. When worn, it can transform into three weapons: a spear, a broadsword, and an iron ball.

 4

Note: These weapons can repair themselves after being damaged, though recovery takes time.

 

As he read the prompt, Fenric's eyes gleamed.

 

"Not bad at all."

chapters.name: Chapter 150: Chapter 150: Can I Bet the Jade Spirit to You?
chapters.content:
Fenric was momentarily stunned by Aurora's words.

 

The Sixth Stage dungeon was... "Avengers"?

 

If that really was the case, then this so-called "tampered U-disk" was far more valuable than it seemed.

 1

Iron Man's armor—if considered a special item—was definitely a treasure.

 

After all, Fenric couldn't fly yet. But if he had a set of that armor, wouldn't flight become a possibility?

 

Just thinking about it made him laugh.

 

"Alright, I'll accept it," he said with a grin.

 

Belle nodded happily. "Great God Shura, I'll head to the trading center and hand it over to you after I finish my tea!"

 

"Sounds good."

 

Suddenly, Aurora spoke up. "Shura, when you do the Sixth Stage dungeon, if possible... could you collect a few extra suits of armor? I can trade other special items for them."

 

She added quickly, "Of course, this is just a personal request. It has nothing to do with Belle. Her gratitude is sincere."

 1

Fenric chuckled to himself.

 

He knew exactly what Aurora had in mind. If he really brought back an Iron Man suit, she'd probably submit it to the higher-ups for scientific research.

 

"Well, we'll see. You never know what might happen in a dungeon," Fenric said lightly.

 

"Alright, then we'll talk later," Aurora agreed quickly.

 

She wouldn't dare press him too hard now.

 

"Oh, right!" Fenric suddenly remembered something. "Aurora, can you help me gather a few cooldown refresh cards for the dungeons? I can pay with points. I only have one left. If I use it tonight, I won't be able to challenge the dungeon again tomorrow."

 1

A glint appeared in Aurora Morwyn's eyes.

 

"Shura, you really don't rest, do you? Gathering cards won't be a problem. In Area C, I've still got enough clout to gather a few without even spending points."

 

Then she asked, "But… are you planning to challenge again tonight? The fifth-tier assessment dungeon?"

 

Fenric nodded. "Yes."

 

"How confident are you?" Aurora asked curiously.

 

Fenric raised an eyebrow. "Why do you ask?"

 

"I was wondering if you could take Belle along," she said. "Of course, you'll be compensated."

 

Beside her, Belle immediately looked hopeful.

 

The "2012" dungeon was considered a nightmare-level scenario for most Samsara.

 

But for Fenric, reaching an SSS-grade evaluation wasn't all that difficult.

 

As long as one boarded the Ark ahead of time, SSS was practically guaranteed.

 

Bringing along one person wouldn't make much difference.

 

However—

 

Business was business.

 

Fenric wouldn't do anything for free.

 

"I'd say I'm 70–80% sure of getting an SSS-grade rating," he said calmly. "But the real question is… what are you offering in return?"

 

For Fenric, this dungeon was already in the bag. He might as well make the most of it.

 

After all, they could go to the trading center and have Belle Morwyn swear under the Samsara system's fairness rules not to disclose the strategy. That way, the guide would remain his intellectual property.

 2

"What!?" Aurora was visibly stunned.

 

Seventy to eighty percent? And he was aiming for an SSS evaluation?

 

That was insane.

 

If it had been anyone else, she'd have smacked them for bragging.

 

But it was Shura.

 

And Shura's track record spoke for itself. His insight into dungeon mechanics was beyond extraordinary—a true genius.

 

Belle also looked astonished.

 

Even rewards from an SS-grade evaluation were incredible. An SSS-grade reward? That could skyrocket someone's strength.

 

"Great God Shura," Belle said sincerely, "if you're willing to take me through this dungeon, I'll give you all the rewards except for the Samsara points."

 2

Fenric's eyes lit up slightly.

 

An SSS-grade rating came with a golden treasure chest.

 

If Belle handed hers over too… he could get two in one run?

 

That was a massive win.

 

Still, he shook his head. "Not enough."

 

He wasn't easily swayed—even if Aurora was technically an ally now.

 

"The SSS-grade rewards are massive," Aurora admitted with a bitter smile. Then she glanced at her sister and teased, "How about I give Belle to you?"

 3

"Sis!" Belle blushed furiously.

 

Fenric deadpanned, "Miss Aurora, that joke wasn't funny."

 

"Oh? You're not satisfied with Belle?" Aurora chuckled, then turned serious. "Fine then, Shura—just tell me what you want. If I have it, I'll offer it."

 

Fenric thought about it.

 

"Do you have anything that boosts attributes directly? Like the super soldier serum you gave me last time?"

 

Aurora let out a helpless laugh. "That serum was one of a kind. Items that boost attributes are rare. I don't have any right now."

 

Fenric frowned slightly, deep in thought. "Forget it. I can't think of anything I really need at the moment. Can I come back to you when I do?"

 

"Of course!" she smiled. "Just give me a call."

 

The tone of that line felt oddly suggestive.

 

"..."

 

Only after speaking did Aurora realize what she had said, a faint flush coloring her face. Still, she didn't try to take it back—just cast a glare at her giggling sister.

 

"One more thing," Fenric added. "I can take Belle into the dungeon, but she'll need to swear under the system's justice not to reveal the strategy."

 

Under the system's rules, such an oath was binding. Breaking it would result in instant obliteration.

 

Aurora and Belle exchanged a glance. After a brief pause, they both nodded in agreement.

 

Fenric smiled. "In that case, happy cooperation!"

 

"Thank you, Shura!" Belle said gratefully.

 

Aurora nodded too, but she showed her gratitude through actions.

 

"Shura, I'll keep gathering cooldown refresh cards for you. I'll contact everyone I can and handle the trades."

 

"Perfect," Fenric said with a satisfied nod.

 

This was exactly why he agreed to bring Belle along.

 

Aurora Morwyn was very efficient—and having a friend with her kind of resources was always a good thing.

 

"Oh, right. Last time, I sold you the strategy for the first-level dungeon 'World War Z.' It's been a while now. Why haven't I seen any movement?"

 

Aurora smiled and explained, "The government organized a special ops team. They're still in training. But the operation should launch soon."
