chapters.name: Chapter 161: Chapter 161: Double Super God Evaluation!
chapters.content:
"Congratulations! Samsara Player—codename: Shura. In the Samsara Tower dungeon world 2012, you performed exceptionally. During the mission period, you survived for 129 days, completing and surpassing all objectives. Evaluation: SSS!"

 

Super God!

 

The familiar mechanical voice of the Samsara System reverberated through the vast space of Samsara once more.

 

And once again, the name Shura dominated the broadcast.

 

Even though the Samsara players were already numb to his repeated achievements, hearing the name of this particular dungeon shocked them all over again.

 

"2012?"

 

"Wait… isn't that the hardest novice dungeon?"

 3

"What the f*ck? 2012? Did I hear that wrong?"

 

"Survive for 129 days? Are you kidding me? That world gets swallowed up in floods within the first three or four days! Did Shura turn into a fish or something?!"

 

"No way! Did he sprout wings and fly into the sky?"

 

"Should I start hoarding submarines?"

 

"Submarines? Stop dreaming. No submarine can survive underwater for that long! Let me give you some science, kid. Conventional subs can only stay submerged for about a week because of limited fuel and oxygen. AIP-tech subs can go a bit longer—maybe 20 days at best. Nuclear subs? They max out at around 40–50 days before the crew loses it. You're talking 129 days! Impossible!"

 4

"So how did Shura do it? Don't tell me he hijacked a rocket and flew into orbit?"

 

"With 2012's tech? You can't even launch a rocket without a massive crew and months of preparation."

 

"Then what the hell did he do? Don't tell me he really evolved into a fish!"

 

"You're asking me? Who the hell am I supposed to ask?!"

 

The chat was chaotic.

 

"Another super god evaluation? Again? Boss Shura, can you leave some breathing room for the rest of us?"

 

"Right? Life is already hard enough, and now you keep reminding us how useless we are every day. Is this even legal?"

 

"Damn it! Shura isn't the son of the Samsara Space. He's the father!"

 

"What if… what if Shura's aiming to climb to the top of the Samsara Tower with nothing but super god evaluations?"

 

"Ha! If that's true, our C-Zone will crush Adam in no time! Just let Shura grow to his peak, and even those foreign monsters will have to kneel."

 2

"Yeah, no more scraping for Samsara points like beggars during the annual PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds large-scale dungeon. Instead, we'll be the ones earning points."

 2

"Unless those shady factions realize Shura's a threat and try to kill him off early."

 

"Block Shura? Good luck with that! Who's going to stop a monster like him?"

 

The entire Samsara space was buzzing with heated discussion.

 

But just as the broadcast faded, another chime resounded.

 

"Congratulations! Samsara Player Codename: Belle Morwyn. In the Samsara Tower dungeon world 2012, you performed exceptionally. During the mission period, you survived for 129 days, completing and surpassing all objectives. Evaluation: SSS!"

 

Super God!!

 

A double super god evaluation!

 

For a moment, all of Samsara Space went silent.

 

The streets, the lounges, the teahouses—everywhere froze.

 

Someone who was walking suddenly stopped mid-step.

 

Someone drinking in a bar froze, their glass suspended in midair.

 

Even Samsara players mid-battle inside dungeon simulations paused, stunned disbelief plastered across their faces.

 

Then the silence shattered.

 

"What the f*ck—double super god?!"

 

"Belle Morwyn again?! And together with Shura? Who's going to tell me there's no relationship between them? I'll be the first to call them a liar!"

 

"Ugh, so jealous! How did that woman pull this off? Why couldn't Shura choose me instead? I'm gorgeous too!"

 

"Stone hammer! This is proof—Belle Morwyn's totally basking in Shura's glow!"

 

"F*ck me sideways. I thought I was already useless, but this? This is a new level of hopelessness. Shura gets super god ratings alone, and now he's handing them out to others like free candy?!"

 

"Exactly! What we see as impossible dungeons, Shura just strolls through like a walk in the park."

 

"If SSS wasn't the highest rating, I bet Shura would break the scale and score even higher."

 1

"With Shura's skill? He could climb straight to the top with nothing but super god evaluations. No question!"

 

"Hahaha! Actually, having Shura on our side is a good thing. The foreign zones must be losing their minds right now!"

 

"Imagine if Shura started leading raids for us publicly. Our entire zone would rise like crazy!"

 

"Public strategies? Are you dumb? Even his One Piece dungeon strategy never went public. You think he'll hand out his secrets now?!"

 

"True. His methods only work for him. We salted-fish nobodies can only watch and drool."

 

"Still… Boss Shura, take me with you next time! I'll do anything—anything!"

 

"Pfft, you? He's tackling the sixth stage dungeon, The Avengers, next time. Which stage are you on again?"

 

"…Bro, you didn't have to say it like that. My heart hurts."

 

Samsara Space had never been this lively.

 

A double super god evaluation had never happened before—and, of course, Shura was at the center of it.

 

Everyone knew Belle's success was thanks to him.

 

Shura's status instantly soared to new heights.

 

But along with admiration came fear.

 

More than ever, Shura was seen as a threat.

 

Teahouse – Private Box

 

Aurora Morwyn leaned back in her seat, a relieved smile softening her usually cold features.

 

"Belle… this is as far as I can help you. The rest of the path, you'll have to walk on your own," she murmured.

 

Though she hoped Shura would keep protecting her sister, she knew better than to expect it.

 

Shura had already taken Belle under his wing twice. That was purely out of respect for her.

 

Pushing her luck would only damage their relationship.

 

Besides, the next dungeons were not suited for carrying someone else.

 

Just as she was thinking this, her system communicator buzzed.

 

Someone, having heard the broadcast, was contacting her.

chapters.name: Chapter 162: Chapter 162: Avengers
chapters.content:
"Dear Samsara Player Belle Morwyn, you have completed your mission. Your rewards are as follows!"

 

Samsara Points: 50,000 points!

 

Physical Attribute +30 (Added)!

 

Flowing Cloud Skirt x1 (Special Item – stored in your personal warehouse)!

 5

Golden Treasure Box x1 (Stored in your personal warehouse)!

 

Belle's face lit up as the mechanical voice echoed in her ears.

 

Fifty thousand Samsara Points, plus thirty points of attributes—this haul was worth nearly sixty thousand points in total.

 

As for the Golden Treasure Box and the Flowing Cloud Skirt, Belle didn't even bother to check them.

 

They weren't hers to keep.

 

When she first entered the dungeon, she'd made an agreement: aside from the Samsara Points, all other rewards would belong to Fenric—Shura.

 

Therefore, both the special item and the Golden Treasure Box were already his.

 

"You have a new communication request. Aurora Morwyn is inviting you for a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

Belle, who had just returned to Samsara Square, smiled as she accepted the call.

 

"Sister! Long time no see—I missed you so much!"

 

Aurora's face appeared on the screen. She chuckled softly.

 

"Long time? It's only been an hour here. But for you, yes… 129 days is a long time. Save the chatter—come to Teahouse Box No. 2797. I'll be waiting."

 

"Okay!"

 

Belle ended the call.

 

The next moment, she materialized inside Box No. 2797 and immediately spotted Aurora.

 

Seeing her cousin, Belle couldn't hold back and threw herself into Aurora's arms.

 

"Sister! I really missed you so much!"

 

Aurora raised an eyebrow, noticing the subtle changes in Belle's demeanor.

 

"You've changed," she said with a knowing smile. "It seems you went through a lot in this dungeon world."

 

"A lot?" Belle shook her head quickly. "No way! The world of 2012 is difficult, yes… but this was actually the easiest dungeon I've ever done. With Shura by my side, I didn't suffer at all. In fact, I even gained a little weight."

 

Aurora blinked, visibly shocked.

 

In a disaster-ridden world like 2012, surviving 129 days was already a nightmare. To claim she hadn't suffered? Impossible.

 

If it weren't for the fact that Belle had sworn an oath under the laws of Samsara not to leak dungeon strategies, Aurora would have immediately asked: Where did Shura take you to survive 129 days so comfortably?

 

Then, a thought struck her.

 

Aurora narrowed her eyes with suspicion.

 

"Belle, be honest with your sister… Shura didn't… eat you, did he?"

 1

Belle's face instantly turned crimson.

 

"S-sister! What are you saying? Nothing like that happened! Shura is a gentleman—he would never do such a thing!"

 

Aurora smirked.

 

"Really? I recall you used to call him 'God Shura,' but now you're calling him just 'Shura.' That sounds pretty close, don't you think?"

 

Belle: "..."

 

"Oh, come on, don't get all flustered. I'm just teasing you."

 

Belle pouted. "Seriously, nothing happened!"

 1

"Fine, fine. Let's drop it. Tell me, how were the rewards for your super god evaluation?"

 

Belle's eyes lit up again.

 

"Four rewards in total! Just the Samsara Points alone were 50,000! Then there's a Golden Treasure Box, a special item, and 30 attribute points!"

 

"Hiss…" Aurora sucked in a sharp breath. "No wonder Shura is so powerful after climbing just a few floors. The rewards for a super god evaluation are insanely generous!"

 

"Oh! Sister, don't worry—I didn't touch anything else. I came straight here after leaving the dungeon."

 

Aurora sighed in relief.

 

"Good. You promised Shura that everything except the points would belong to him. Don't mess this up."

 

"Do you think I'm stupid, sister?" Belle rolled her eyes.

 

"Not stupid—just… tempted." Aurora gave her a knowing smile. "Even I'm curious about what's inside that Golden Treasure Box."

 

"Sister, what do you want to drink? My treat tonight!" Belle grinned.

 

"Oh, look at you, little rich woman! Then I won't hold back."

 1

While sipping tea, Aurora suddenly asked, "Belle, what's your next plan?"

 

Belle tilted her head. "Plan?"

 

"I mean, your next dungeon."

 

"Ah… I haven't decided yet. I thought I'd take a break for a few days first."

 

"Why? Don't you want to keep tagging along with Shura?"

 

"No… that's not right. I don't want to become a burden to him."

 

Aurora nodded approvingly.

 

"Good. I was worried you might overstep and annoy Shura. It's better this way."

 

Belle sighed. "Sister, am I really that naïve in your eyes?"

 

"Not naïve," Aurora smiled. "Just… inexperienced."

 

After a pause, Aurora's tone became serious.

 

"Belle, I want you to move in with me for now."

 

"Why? What's wrong?"

 

"Some people are getting ideas about you… thinking they can use you to get to Shura."

 

"Dear Samsara Player—Shura. You have completed your mission. Your rewards are as follows!"

 

Samsara Points: 50,000 points!

 

Strength Attribute +30 (Added)!

 1

Night Demon Cloak x1 (Special Item – stored in your personal warehouse)!

 1

Golden Treasure Box x1 (Stored in your personal warehouse)!

 1

Fenric listened to the system prompts with a faint smile.

 

This haul was excellent.

 

And with Belle's Golden Treasure Box also belonging to him, he had essentially gained an extra bonus for free.

 1

He had no doubts Belle would honor their agreement.

 

For now, he didn't rush to open the rewards.

 4

The next dungeon was rumored to be The Avengers. Fenric planned to gather intel on the mission before deciding how to use his new rewards.

chapters.name: Chapter 163: Chapter 163: Don’t Be Impulsive!
chapters.content:
"You have a new communication message: Aurora Morwyn invites you to a video call. Please respond."

 

Not long after Fenric returned to Samsara Square, a communication request from Aurora popped up.

 

He accepted without hesitation.

 

Aurora's beautiful, heroic face appeared on the screen.

 

"Shura, congratulations! Another super god evaluation."

 

Fenric smiled lightly. "Where are you? I'll buy you some tea."

 

"Discuss it with Belle? We've already had two pots of tea tonight—I can't drink anymore!" Aurora chuckled wryly before continuing, "We're at Box 2797 in the teahouse. If you're free, can you come over?"

 

"Alright, I'll be there in a moment."

 

Fenric ended the call and instructed the system to teleport him to the teahouse.

 

Moments later, he walked into Box 2797.

 

Inside, the Morwyn sisters were already waiting.

 

As soon as Fenric entered, both sisters stood up.

 

"Shura, congratulations again," Aurora said warmly.

 

Belle didn't speak. She simply gazed at Fenric, her eyes carrying a deep and unreadable expression.

 

Fenric smiled. "Aurora, we're old friends—no need for formalities. If you want to congratulate me, I should be congratulating Belle as well."

 3

Belle finally broke her silence.

 

"Shura, thank you," she said sincerely. "As per our agreement, the rewards from my dungeon evaluation—everything except the points—belong to you.

 

I received four rewards: Samsara Points, attribute points, a special item, and a Golden Treasure Box. The 30 physique attribute points were directly added to me. As for the other items, if there's something you don't want, you can sell it to me at a high price, right?"

 

Fenric understood the implication: Belle wanted to use her points to compensate him.

 

But he shook his head with a smile. "No need. You've taken good care of me these past months. Don't worry about it."

 

"Taken care of?" Aurora interjected suddenly, arching a brow. "Shura, how exactly did Belle 'take care' of you?"

 

"She cooked every day," Fenric replied, deadpan.

 

Aurora instantly turned to Belle and grabbed her by the ear. "You little rascal! At home, you always act like you can't cook and let me starve, but you were cooking for him? So you lied to me all along?"

 

Belle shot Fenric a glare before pleading, "Sister, I was wrong! I'll cook for you when we go back, I promise!"

 

"You'd better!" Aurora huffed.

 

Fenric couldn't help but chuckle at their sisterly quarrel.

 

Belle quickly changed the topic.

 

"In addition to the points and attribute boost, I also have a special item and a Golden Treasure Box for you, Shura. Let's go to the trading center and hand them over."

 

"Not so fast," Fenric said casually. "What time is it?"

 

Belle blinked. "I… just came out of the dungeon. I didn't check."

 

"It's 3:10," Aurora replied.

 

"Three o'clock, huh? Then I can run another dungeon," Fenric said nonchalantly.

 

The sisters' expressions froze.

 

"Shura, are you serious?!" Aurora's voice rose. "You just came out of a dungeon! Do you really need to push yourself this hard?"

 

"This last dungeon was boring—I stayed in one place for months. I feel like I'm getting rusty," Fenric shrugged. "Besides, the large-scale PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds dungeon will open in September—just two months from now. I want to sharpen my strength and give those plotting against me a little… surprise."

 

Aurora sighed helplessly. "At this rate, in two months, Adam will be crushed under your feet."

 

"All the better," Fenric grinned.

 

"Fine, fine. Since you're set on this, I won't try to stop you."

 

"Aurora, I don't have a dungeon cooldown refresh card right now. I'll need your help with that," Fenric said bluntly.

 

But Aurora wasn't annoyed—in fact, she seemed pleased.

 

His tone meant he treated her as a true friend.

 

"Perfect timing," she said with a smile. "A friend from Area B has three cooldown refresh cards. I'll have them sent over later."

 

"Thanks, Aurore. I owe you one," Fenric replied.

 

"Don't say that. After everything you've done for Belle, this is nothing," Aurora said.

 

"Yes," Belle added, "Shura, if you need anything, just say the word."

 

"Alright, enough of this," Fenric waved them off. "Aurora, tell me about the Sixth Stage Dungeon. I don't know much about it."

 

Aurora stared at him, dumbfounded.

 

"Shura, are you kidding me? You don't even know what it's about, and you're ready to dive in?"

 

"That's why I'm asking you," Fenric replied with a smile.

 

Aurora sighed in defeat. "I really can't win against you. Fine, listen carefully. The Sixth Stage is 'The Avengers.' It's a massive dungeon world, similar to One Piece. Upon entering, you can select an identity, and that identity will carry over to the second stage of the dungeon.

 

The world setting is modern, with advanced technology. The primary mission is to kill an alien species called the Chitauri—at least 20 of them. The mission lasts ten hours, with five hours of preparation time beforehand.

 4

The more aliens you kill, the higher your evaluation score.

 

Once you enter, there's also an organization called S.H.I.E.L.D. Most of them are normal humans, but there are some incredibly strong individuals—Iron Man, Thor, Hulk, to name a few. Be especially careful with Hulk. When he's angry, he can't tell friend from foe, and his power is monstrous."

 2

Aurora hesitated, then added, "Shura, I really suggest you rest tonight and do some research online before diving into this dungeon tomorrow."

 

"I know what I'm doing," Fenric said with a dismissive wave.

 

It wasn't arrogance.

 

Fenric was deeply familiar with The Avengers storyline. In terms of knowledge, who in this world could match him?

 

"Aurora, with your current strength, could you take down Hulk?" Fenric asked curiously.

 

Aurora's lips curled into a confident smile. "Of course. That brute only surpasses me in raw strength—nothing else."

 10

Fenric nodded slightly. He knew then just how far he still had to go to catch up with an A-rank Samsara.

chapters.name: Chapter 164: Chapter 164: What About the Said Nuclear Bomb? (1/8)
chapters.content:
"Aurora, go on. It's better if you tell me everything in detail~"

 

"Alright."

 

Aurora continued, "Once you enter the dungeon, the first thing you must do is edit your identity. After confirming, the system will randomly drop you somewhere in New York City. You'll have five hours of preparation time. After that, the Chitauri will invade.

 

You'll then have ten hours to perform your mission. During those ten hours, the more Chitauri you kill, the higher your evaluation will be when the mission ends.

 

But there's one thing you must remember: when killing the Chitauri, avoid being too high-profile. If you draw too much attention, you'll become a primary target, and that will be a huge problem."

 

"After six hours, a character named Black Widow will close the space-time portal. At that point, you no longer need to hide—just focus on killing as many Chitauri as possible in New York."

 

"Wait a second!"

 

Fenric suddenly interrupted, his face tense. "Did you just say that in six hours, Black Widow will close the space-time channel? And by then, there will still be plenty of Chitauri in New York?"

 

"Yes." Aurora nodded.

 

"What about the nuclear bomb?!" Fenric's expression changed drastically. "Doesn't the government launch a nuke?"

 4

"A nuclear bomb? No!" Aurora looked at him strangely. "There are millions of people in New York. If the government launched a nuclear strike, how many innocent lives would that take? The superheroes and Samsaras players are more than enough to deal with the invading Chitauri."

 

"Then… where did I get the idea about the nuke?" Fenric muttered under his breath, feigning nonchalance. "I guess I read too many unreliable sources online."

 

But his face had already darkened.

 

According to Aurora, the Samsara space had made adjustments to the original Avengers plot. The government no longer resorted to a nuclear strike. That meant Iron Man no longer had to risk his life to hurl a nuclear bomb into space.

 

No… wait.

 

Fenric quickly realized the change was likely due to the influence of the Samsara players. With so many powerful participants joining the battlefield, the government probably saw hope for victory without such desperate measures.

 

That made sense.

 

In the original plot, the government opted for the nuclear option because they saw the Avengers being overwhelmed by the endless Chitauri horde and wanted to prevent the destruction from spreading.

 

After all, there were simply too many Chitauri. The Avengers were powerful, but they were too few—like two fists against a thousand hands.

 

Not to mention the Leviathan-like behemoths rampaging through the city.

 

In the latter half of the original battle, the Avengers were nearly crushed under the endless waves of enemies. Under such circumstances, the government's decision to launch a nuclear strike had been justified.

 

But now, with the Avengers dungeon world filled with Samsara players, the balance of power had shifted.

 

Those who could reach the Sixth Stage were at least C-rank Samsaras, with many at B-rank.

 

These individuals were already superhuman, no weaker than Captain America himself.

 

Fenric, for example.

 

At his current level, Fenric could easily defeat Captain America in a one-on-one fight.

 

Unless Thor was willing to lend his hammer to the Captain, there was no way the man could even put up a fair fight against him.

 1

Thinking of this, Fenric exhaled slowly.

 

Belle noticed Fenric's grim expression and asked gently, "Shura, are you alright?"

 

"I'm fine," Fenric replied with a faint smile.

 

On the surface, he appeared calm, but inwardly, frustration gnawed at him.

 

His original plan had been to use the nuclear bomb to destroy the Chitauri's mothership outright, severing their command link and wiping them out in one decisive blow.

 

But now… the nuke was gone.

 

"Shura, if you're uncertain, you can always wait and challenge it next time," Belle offered, sensing his unease.

 

Aurora glanced sideways at her sister. Belle's concern for Fenric was obvious—far closer than before.

 

129 days of living side by side… something must have happened, Aurora thought.

 

Though, truthfully, if Belle did end up with Shura, Aurora would be pleased.

 

In Samsara space, once someone reached the age of 35 without entering, they were no longer eligible to join.

 

(Note: Those who entered before turning 35 remain unaffected by age restrictions.)

 1

In other words, there were no "old people" among Samsaras—only the young and strong.

 

And Shura… Fenric… he was far from old.

 

Young, strong, and brimming with potential.

 

"Let me think," Fenric said at last.

 

Belle, understanding the weight of his thoughts, immediately held her tongue.

 

Some women are foolish enough to nag or argue when a man is under pressure, just to assert their presence. Belle, fortunately, was not one of them.

 11

Fenric sank into deep thought.

 

Even without a nuclear bomb, it wasn't impossible for him to destroy the Chitauri's mothership.

 

He had his oxygen mask, which allowed him to survive in the vacuum of space.

 2

If he could steal an Iron Man suit, he might be able to fly through the space-time portal and directly attack the Chitauri's command ship.

 

Even if he couldn't completely destroy it, with his current power, he could wreak havoc on their forces—because individually, the Chitauri were weak.

 

But the risks… the risks would multiply tenfold.

 

Charging into the heart of enemy territory alone, even Fenric couldn't guarantee his safety.

 

"Should I try to acquire a nuke myself?"

 

The thought flashed through his mind—but he quickly dismissed it.

 

The preparation window was only five hours.

 

In that time, he had to infiltrate Stark Industries and secure several Iron Man suits. Where would he find the time—or resources—to obtain a nuclear warhead?

 

"Aurora, do you have any heavy weaponry? Missiles? The more powerful, the better," Fenric suddenly asked.

 

Aurora's sharp eyes narrowed. She immediately understood his intentions.

 

"Shura… you're not planning to attack the Chitauri's mothership, are you?"

 

Fenric smiled faintly. "Exactly."

 

It wasn't a plan he could—or needed—to hide. Once he acted, every Samsara players in the dungeon would know.

 

"Shura, you're bold—recklessly bold," Aurora said with admiration. "But with your strength, if anyone can do it, it's you."

chapters.name: Chapter 165: Chapter 165: It’s Quite Sudden! (2/8)
chapters.content:
Aurora thought for a moment before speaking. "I've never heard of any missile-type special item with that kind of destructive power.

 

But, Shura, if your goal is to destroy the Chitauri's mothership, I do have something that might help. It's called Crush and Dissolve. It's a liquid-based special item. According to the system's description, it's extremely powerful—capable of dissolving objects with a volume of over one million tons."

 7

(Note: For reference, an aircraft carrier typically weighs only tens of thousands of tons!)

 

Aurora continued, "However, using it is a bit tricky. You must physically make contact with the target to activate it. The dissolution effect radiates outward, evaporating everything within its range.

 

In other words, if the Chitauri mothership is enormous, you'd need to reach the ship's core to ensure complete destruction."

 

Fenric's eyes lit up. "Yes. That's exactly what I need!"

 

"Alright then. I'll head to the trading center later and give it to you."

 

"Then I won't be polite about accepting it," Fenric replied with a faint smile.

 

Aurora chuckled. "This is how it should be. Honestly, we owe you far too much already."

 

She paused, then added in a serious tone, "But, Shura, I have to warn you. Once you use Crush and Dissolve, the volatilization speed is extremely fast. You'll need to escape immediately, or you'll be caught in the destructive range."

 

"Got it," Fenric nodded.

 

Aurora's expression turned solemn. "One more thing. The Avengers dungeon is far more dangerous than One Piece. In the world of The Avengers, there are actual gods. You must be careful."

 1

Fenric nodded again. Of course, he knew.

 

He was all too familiar with the Marvel universe and its terrifying powerhouses. Even Earth alone was filled with unpredictable dangers.

 

The Sorcerer Supreme alone is terrifying… he thought.

 

"Alright, let's head to the trading center," Fenric suggested.

 

"Good," Aurora agreed.

 

The three of them made their way to the trading center.

 

Fenric first traded with Aurora and obtained Crush and Dissolve.

 

Special Item: Crush and Dissolve

 

A failed creation of a god-tier alchemist. Upon contact, it can dissolve an object with at least a one-kilometer radius and millions of tons in volume. Extremely dangerous—handle with caution.

 

Note: One-time use. Cannot be restored after activation.

 

The liquid inside the glass test tube was a deep crimson, like blood.

 

Fenric accepted it carefully from Aurora, fully aware of its destructive potential.

 

Suddenly, he asked with curiosity, "What would happen if I used this thing here in Samsara space?"

 

Aurora blinked, then let out a laugh. "Don't even think about it. I once wondered the same thing.

 

But I'm guessing Samsara space wouldn't be affected. I heard about someone who once used an indestructible weapon to attack the buildings here. The result? The buildings didn't even get scratched—there wasn't so much as a chipped corner."

 

"Good. That's reassuring."

 

"You two," Belle interrupted with a teasing smile, "aren't you focusing on the wrong thing here?"

 

She pulled out the rewards she had promised Fenric. "Shura, here are the special items I got this time."

 

She handed over a golden treasure chest and a retro-style long dress—the Flowing Cloud Skirt.

 

Fenric immediately waved his hand. "Belle, just give me the golden treasure chest. I don't need the skirt."

 

A skirt? For me? What am I, some noble lady?

 

Sorry—no way Fenric was wearing that!

 

"Shura, don't underestimate it," Belle reminded him. "The skirt provides a 30% damage reduction. It's actually a top-tier defensive item."

 

"Doesn't matter how good it is—it's still a skirt. I'm a man. Do you really want me to charge into battle wearing this thing?"

 5

Belle and Aurora both burst into laughter at his reaction.

 

Fenric sighed. "You should keep it."

 

"Then I'll happily accept this reward," Belle said with a bright smile.

 

She really liked the dress, and Fenric's refusal made it even easier for her to accept.

 

The two then traded the golden treasure chest.

 

Fenric now had two golden treasure chests stored in his personal warehouse.

 

"Shura, wait here. The friend who's bringing the dungeon refresh cards will arrive soon," Aurora said.

 

"Alright."

 

Before long, a tall, muscular young woman entered the trading center.

 

"Sister Aurora, which one of you is the famous genius Shura?" she asked with an energetic grin.

 

Fenric instinctively took a step back.

 1

By the time he left the trading center, it was already 3:30 a.m.

 

He still had time before the next dungeon challenge, so after saying goodbye to Aurora and Belle, he returned to his personal warehouse.

 

Fenric was eager to open the golden treasure chest.

 

"Congratulations! You've opened a Golden Treasure Chest and obtained the special item: Ark Ferry Ticket."

 

Fenric froze, staring at the ticket in disbelief.

 

Seriously?

 

"Damn it, what am I supposed to do with this? The 2012 dungeon is already cleared. This thing is useless to me now!"

 

He almost wanted to curse out loud.

 

A golden treasure chest… and I get this?

 

Fenric picked up the Ark Ferry Ticket.

 

The system chimed again:

 

Special Item: Ark Ferry Ticket

 

Upon use, instantly teleports you to the safest location. If used in the 2012 dungeon, it immediately transfers you to the Ark.

 1

Note: One-time use. Cannot be restored once activated.

 

Reminder: This item can be recycled for approximately 65,000 Samsara Points.

 1

"!!"

 

Fenric was stunned.

 

A ferry ticket is worth 65,000 points?

 

Actually, this item was powerful. Anyone attempting the 2012 dungeon could secure an SSS rating simply by holding this ticket.

 

However, after a brief pause, Fenric made up his mind. "System, recycle it."

 12

It wasn't worth selling or transferring.

 

First, it would be troublesome.

 

Second, he didn't want other Samsaras learning about the Ark in the 2012 dungeon.

 

"Special item recycled. Samsara Player 'Shura,' you've gained 65,000 Samsara Points."

 3

chapters.name: Chapter 166: Chapter 166: You Are Here Again?! (3/8)
chapters.content:
[Tl/n: My bad. I just woke up.]

 

-----

 

The Ark Ferry Ticket also possessed a teleportation function.

 

However, this function was identical to that of Fenric's bracelet—a complete duplication of abilities.

 2

Fenric sighed, then opened the second golden treasure chest.

 

"Congratulations! You've opened a Golden Treasure Chest and obtained the special item: Ark Ferry Ticket!"

 1

"Damn it!"

 

Another one? A second ferry ticket?

 

Fenric was speechless.

 

He guessed that the golden treasure chest he obtained from the 2012 dungeon must have been preloaded with this kind of reward.

 

Well, at least it's stable.

 2

After a moment's thought, Fenric decided to keep this Ark ticket for now.

 

With hundreds of thousands of Samsara points already in his possession, he wasn't in any urgent need to recycle it.

 2

After dealing with the treasure chests, he turned his attention to the remaining special item he hadn't examined yet—a dark, eerie cloak.

 

Fenric picked it up, and the system's prompt rang out:

 

"Special Item: Night Demon Cloak!"

 

A cloak forged in the depths of the underworld, infused with ghostly energy. When worn, your attacks gain devastating effects against demonic creatures.

 

Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

This is excellent. With this cloak, if I encounter a dungeon filled with ghosts or demonic monsters, my power will skyrocket.

 

Satisfied, he carefully placed the cloak back on the shelf.

 

Next, Fenric began managing his Samsara points.

 

From his previous dungeon run, he had received 50,000 points as a reward for the Super God evaluation. Adding the 65,000 points earned from recycling the first ferry ticket, he now had 115,000 Samsara points in total.

 

After considering his options, Fenric spent 30,000 points to upgrade his Conqueror's Haki.

 1

This was essential—after all, the Avengers dungeon would likely throw endless waves of small fry at him.

 

With the remaining 85,000 Samsara points, Fenric converted them all into potential points, gaining 170 points in total.

 

He distributed them carefully, resulting in the following stats:

 

Name: Shura

 

Samsara Number: (Zone C) 90086

 

Physique: 175 → 200

 

Spirit: 350 → 400

 

Strength: 203 → 303

 2

Agility: 175 → 200

 

Potential Points: 0

 

Skills:

 

English (Proficient)

 

Driving (Beginner)

 

Shooting (Proficient)

 

Camouflage (Master)

 

Basic Swordsmanship Technique (Proficient)

 

Special Skills:

 

Conqueror's Haki (Mastery)

 

Armament Haki (Mastery)

 4

Combat Techniques:

 

Savage Charge

 

Abilities:

 

Telekinesis

 

Hundred Poisons Immunity (Passive)

 

Samsara Points: 22

 

Comprehensive Evaluation: B

 

Fenric reviewed his stats with satisfaction.

 

Although his overall rating was still "B," he could easily crush most Samsara players who had just reached that tier.

 

Even within the same rank, the strength gap between Samsara players could be vast.

 

For instance, both One Leaf Knows Autumn and Aurora Morwyn had A-level evaluations, yet the former wouldn't even dare talk tough in front of Aurora.

 

The higher the evaluation level, the larger the strength gap between individuals.

 

In truth, the "Comprehensive Evaluation" was merely a reference metric. It was unreliable to judge someone's true power by that alone.

 

A burst of red light flashed across Fenric's body as the upgrades settled in.

 

He clenched his fists, feeling a surge of raw strength flow through his veins.

 

So powerful!

 

With his current attributes, he was no longer inferior to many A-ranked Samsaras.

 

Fenric could already feel the edge of the A-rank threshold.

 

What he lacked now was a truly formidable ability.

 

Within the Samsara Tower, most A-ranked veterans had unlocked devastating abilities after surviving numerous high-tier dungeons—powers like Logia-type Devil Fruits, superhuman bloodlines, or top-tier martial arts techniques.

 

On the foundation of raw stats alone, Fenric could already obliterate most of his peers.

 2

Many of the strongest abilities in Samsara Space scaled directly with one's four core attributes.

 

If Fenric were to acquire the Gura Gura no Mi (Tremor-Tremor Fruit) now, with his current strength stat, he would instantly ascend to the upper echelon of A-ranked Samsara players!

 

"They say once a single attribute surpasses 1,000, it undergoes a qualitative transformation… That's going to be exciting."

 4

Fenric muttered this to himself as he checked the time.

 

03:44.

 

Only six minutes remained before the teleportation channel closed.

 

Everything was ready.

 

Fenric exited his personal warehouse and teleported to the Samsara Tower.

 

After using a dungeon cooldown refresh card, he stepped onto the Sixth Stage of the tower.

 

A projection of the Tower Spirit appeared before him.

 

"Greetings, Samsara Player Shura. How may I assist you?"

 

"I want to challenge the dungeon," Fenric replied.

 

"The available dungeon world is The Avengers. Are you certain you wish to enter?"

 

"Yes."

 

The moment Fenric confirmed, he was teleported into the white preparation room.

 

The room was bustling with activity.

 

At least a hundred Samsaras were gathered inside, some forming groups and strategizing, while others—lone wolves like Fenric—waited quietly for the dungeon to start.

 

As Fenric appeared, a nearby Samsara caught sight of him and froze, as though trying to recall a familiar face.

 

After a few seconds, realization struck. His eyes widened, and he shouted, "Holy crap—it's God Shura!!"

 

He had seen Shura's portrait before, so recognition came quickly.

 

The outburst immediately drew attention.

 

"It's God Shura!!"

 

"Damn, didn't he just get an SSS-level Super God evaluation? He's already back for another dungeon?"

 

"Unbelievable. We risk our lives for a single dungeon run, but for Shura, it's like drinking water!?"

 

"What, one dungeon per day isn't enough for him? Is he going for two per day now? That's insane!"

 

"Does Shura plan to clear the entire Samsara Tower within two months?!"

 

"Hiss… That's terrifying."

 

"Tch, do you all have to worship him like that? My older brother gave me a powerful Paramecia fruit, and my strength is already B-ranked. I might not be weaker than this so-called God Shura!"

 

"Oh, shut up. You think you're on his level? Stop embarrassing yourself."

 

Fenric's sudden appearance caused a stir among the Samsaras.

 

The fact that he had already completed one dungeon tonight and was diving into another was shocking enough—but to aim for two SSS-level evaluations in a single night?

 

Was God Shura trying to break his own record?

 

As usual, several Samsara players approached him, asking for help or to form a team, but Fenric rejected them all without hesitation.

 

"Attention, Samsara Players," the Tower Spirit's voice rang out. "Teleportation to the mission world will commence in ten minutes."

 1

chapters.name: Chapter 167: Chapter 167: Monster Invasion! (4/8)
chapters.content:
Ten minutes passed in the blink of an eye.

 

The system prompt sounded again:

 

"Teleportation countdown: 10… 9… 8… 3… 2… 1!"

 

When the countdown ended, everyone in the white preparation room was enveloped in a crimson light and vanished.

 

A virtual interface appeared in front of Fenric, displaying a young man with a physique roughly three times more muscular than Fenric's usual body.

 

"Samsara Player—Shura, this is your default appearance in this world. If you are not satisfied, you may customize it now."

 

Fenric glanced at the default avatar generated by the system. It looked impressive enough, so he didn't bother changing it and chose Confirm.

 

The next prompt followed:

 

"Please enter your name.

 

Note: Your identity is set as a civilian by default and cannot be changed."

 

Without hesitation, Fenric typed in the name: "Ronan Anderson."

 

Yeah… I'll stick with this name from now on.

 2

"Identity confirmed. Transmitting to the dungeon world."

 

The red light faded. Fenric found himself standing on a street in New York City.

 

It was early morning—around five or six o'clock. The streets were sparsely populated, lending the city an eerie quietness.

 

"Attention: You have five hours of preparation time. After five hours, the Chitauri invasion will begin."

 

Fenric smiled slightly at the system's prompt.

 

Snap!

 

A hand suddenly clapped onto his shoulder.

 

"Hey, man, I need a word with you."

 

Two tall, dark-skinned men hooked their arms around Fenric's shoulders and casually dragged him toward a nearby alley.

 

A cold glint caught Fenric's eye as one of them pressed a knife against his ribs.

 

"Don't even think about screaming, or I'll carve you up."

 

Fenric only gave a faint smile and walked with them, cooperating as if nothing were wrong.

 

A robbery? Predictable.

 

Fenric had long heard that Asian immigrants in New York were frequently targeted by street robbers or by those racists. To see it happen firsthand was almost amusing.

 11

Two street thugs thought they could rob him just because he looked like an easy target?

 1

They clearly had no idea who they were dealing with.

 

Less than a minute later, Fenric strolled out of the alley unharmed.

 

Behind him, the two robbers lay sprawled on the ground, unconscious.

 

Fenric smirked and muttered under his breath:

 

"Pathetic."

 

His spoils of war amounted to just $27 from their pockets.

 

Better than nothing… enough for a cab ride.

 

Hailing a taxi, Fenric climbed in and said in fluent English:

 

"Take me to Stark Industries."

 

"Sure thing, sir."

 

Twenty minutes later, the taxi pulled up in front of a towering skyscraper.

 

Fenric gazed up at the sleek, gleaming facade and couldn't help but sigh inwardly.

 

Tony Stark… filthy rich as always.

 

His first priority was clear: get the Iron Man armor.

 

The entire plan hinged on acquiring it.

 

Fenric walked into the building.

 

The first floor, which served as a reception hall, was open to the public.

 

But to access the upper levels, one needed to pass through a strict identity verification system.

 

And the Iron Man suits? Naturally, they were stored on the top floor.

 1

Because of their strategic importance, the building's security measures were on par with military installations.

 

Fenric even noticed that some security guards were armed with real firearms, and the screenings were meticulous.

 

Without an internal employee badge, getting past the first floor was impossible.

 

After surveying the situation, Fenric left the building and crossed the street to a café.

 

He ordered a hot drink and sat by the window, eating breakfast while keeping an eye on Stark Tower.

 

The taxi ride had cost him only $6, leaving him enough for a decent meal.

 

Impersonating an employee? Forget it.

 

This wasn't a movie, and the guards weren't idiots.

 

If someone could sneak upstairs with just a fake badge, Tony's armor would've been stolen long ago.

 

Not to mention, Jarvis, Tony's artificial intelligence system, would detect him instantly.

 

There was only one plan left: force his way in.

 

But not yet.

 

At the moment, the Avengers hadn't even started fighting the Chitauri. If he barged in now, he'd risk triggering an early confrontation with the entire Avengers team.

 

Fenric wasn't afraid of one-on-one battles…

 

…but fighting the entire team?

 

Even he wasn't that reckless.

 

There's another way.

 

He could wait for Loki to make his move.

 

In the original timeline, Loki had installed the teleportation device atop Stark Tower to open the space-time portal and summon the Chitauri army.

 

If Fenric's guess was right, Loki would appear directly on the rooftop.

 

Jarvis would have detected any conventional intrusion by now, so Loki must be teleporting in.

 

Time passed.

 

Four hours slipped by, and the morning bustle of New York returned.

 

Fenric stepped out of the café, stretching lazily.

 

Suddenly, his eyes shot upward.

 

A flash of blue light appeared on the rooftop of Stark Tower, followed by the emergence of a glowing portal—Loki and his entourage stepping through.

 

Fenric slapped his forehead.

 

Damn, I almost forgot—Loki has the Space Stone.

 1

Teleporting straight onto the roof? A bold move.

 

Counting on Loki was pointless. Fenric would have to handle this himself.

 

With that decision, Fenric circled to the back entrance of the building.

 

There were far fewer guards there.

 

He crouched, focusing his strength.

 

Boom!

 

The ground beneath him cracked as his legs exploded with power, leaving a spiderweb of fractures on the pavement.

 

A loud whoosh filled the air as Fenric launched himself upward like a human missile, soaring toward the building.

 

He wasn't flying—just jumping.

 1

But with his current strength, clearing a height of ten meters or more was trivial.

 1

Crash!

 

Fenric smashed through a window and landed inside the building—on the eighth floor.

 

"Ahhh!!!"

 

The sudden intrusion startled several young office workers.

 

A few foreign women screamed in terror, thinking a terrorist attack was underway.

 2

chapters.name: Chapter 168: Chapter 168: Iron Man’s Wrath! (5/8)
chapters.content:
"Riing! Riing! Riing!"

 

Suddenly, the blaring of alarm sirens echoed throughout Stark Industries.

 

On the rooftop, where Loki and Dr. Erik Selvig were busy installing the portal device, both froze, their expressions darkening.

 

They thought they had been discovered.

 

Dressed in his usual regal attire, Loki strode to the edge of the rooftop and peered down.

 

After a moment of confusion, his expression relaxed. "Strange… it's not for us."

 

The building's entire security force seemed to be responding to someone else.

 

"It doesn't seem to be about us," Loki muttered, frowning. He turned to Selvig and ordered, "Continue."

 

Meanwhile, Fenric's infiltration had thrown Stark Tower into chaos.

 

Sirens wailed relentlessly as security guards scrambled into action, guns raised, chasing after him.

 

Thud! Thud! Thud!

 

Fenric dashed up the stairwell with explosive speed, rapidly closing in on the rooftop.

 

Sure, taking the elevator would be easier… but only an idiot would pick that option.

 

If someone tampered with the elevator controls, he'd be a sitting duck.

 

At Fenric's current speed, sprinting up the stairs was far faster—and far safer.

 

"Where's the target?"

 

"Just passed the fifteenth floor!"

 

"He's on the seventeenth floor now! Stop him, quickly!!"

 

"Alert Mr. Stark immediately!"

 

The voices of security personnel crackled over their walkie-talkies, their tone filled with panic.

 

"He's here!"

 

"Open fire!"

 

Gunshots rang out.

 

But all that resulted was a massacre of security guards.

 

Fenric's expression remained cold, his steps unyielding as he stormed past the fallen men, leaving corpses behind him.

 7

With his current strength, unless someone like Hulk or Thor appeared, no one could stop him.

 

In mere minutes, Fenric reached the thirtieth floor.

 

The stairwell behind him was littered with bodies.

 

Stark Tower, one of Manhattan's most iconic skyscrapers, had over fifty floors.

 

At Fenric's pace, another five minutes was all he needed to reach the top.

 

Nothing could halt this monster.

 

Far above, high in the sky, the S.H.I.E.L.D. helicarrier drifted, severely damaged.

 

The Avengers, still a newly formed team, had just suffered a brutal defeat, courtesy of Loki's schemes.

 

Hulk had vanished, Thor's whereabouts were unknown, and casualties among the agents were devastating.

 

Agent Phil Coulson had even been "killed" at Loki's hands.

 

"Captain, we found this in Agent Coulson's jacket. He always wanted you to sign it…"

 

Nick Fury, the one-eyed director, dropped a handful of blood-stained trading cards on the table, his voice heavy.

 

"Unfortunately, he never got the chance."

 

Steve Rogers, the Captain, picked up one of the cards. It bore his image—an echo of who he was seventy years ago.

 

The room was quiet, the air heavy with grief.

 

Suddenly, Tony Stark's expression shifted. Without another word, he spun around and bolted out of the room.

 

"Stark?" Nick Fury called out, confused.

 

Tony didn't even glance back. "Someone's breaking into Stark Tower!"

 

The room erupted in shock.

 

Captain America stood abruptly. "Tony, wait for me!"

 

Stark Tower – Fifty-Fifth Floor

 

Fenric finally slowed down.

 

He had reached his destination.

 

"Clack!"

 

The tempered, explosion-proof glass doors slammed shut, locking him out.

 

Fenric smirked. Jarvis was making his move.

 

He clenched his fist, coating it with Armament Haki, and struck.

 

Boom!!

 

The "explosion-proof" glass shattered like fragile candy, scattering shards across the floor.

 

Fenric stepped through without hesitation.

 

"Warning! Sir, this is private property. You have no authorization to enter!"

 1

Jarvis's calm voice echoed from every speaker.

 

Fenric ignored the AI, scanning the room.

 

His eyes lit up.

 

There it was—an entire wall lined with Iron Man suits.

 

He could even name some of them at a glance.

 

Mark IV.

 

Mark V (the portable suitcase model).

 

Mark VI (powered by the new arc reactor).

 

Mark VII (with advanced flight capability).

 

Fenric strode over without hesitation.

 

His targets were clear: the Mark VI and Mark VII suits.

 

The Mark VI, he planned to give to Aurora—she had been extremely helpful to him, and it was worth repaying that favor.

 

As for the Mark VII? That one was for him.

 

The rest? He didn't care.

 

Especially that flashy Mark V suitcase suit. Cool design, sure. But for Fenric, it was nothing more than scrap metal.

 

A suit that couldn't even fly was inferior to his own Armament Haki.

 

As for the iconic Mark 85 nanotech armor or the Hulkbuster? Tony hadn't invented those yet.

 

Crash! Crash!

 

Under Fenric's fists, the protective glass cases shattered one by one.

 

"Warning! Sir, your actions are a severe violation of law. The authorities have been notified."

 

Jarvis's voice remained calm and persistent, but without Tony's authorization, the AI couldn't directly engage him.

 

Fenric ignored it completely.

 

He retrieved both the Mark VI and Mark VII suits, then pulled out a peculiar item: a tampered USB drive.

 

Special Item: Tampered USB Drive.

 

This device contained a super virus capable of rewriting any system, even advanced AIs.

 

Fenric touched the drive to the Mark VII and pressed the activation switch.

 

The beauty of this tool was that it didn't even need a USB port—mere contact was enough.

 

Beep!

 

The Mark VII armor powered up, its lights flickering to life.

 

On the USB's tiny screen, a progress bar appeared:

 

"1%... 2%... 3%... 4%..."

 

The percentage ticked upward rapidly. In less than 100 seconds, the suit's system would be under Fenric's control.

 

Seeing this, Fenric grinned.

 

When the progress bar hit 100%, he immediately stored the Mark VII in his personal warehouse.

 

"Ding! You obtained a special item!"

 

Satisfied, he turned to the Mark VI and repeated the process.

 

Suddenly, a furious voice rang out from behind him.

 

"You bastard! Step away from my suits!"

chapters.name: Chapter 169: Chapter 169: Takes on Two! (6/8)
chapters.content:
Whoosh!

 

The sound of something slicing through the air came from above.

 

Tony Stark, clad in his Iron Man armor, arrived in an instant, thrusters blazing.

 

In his grip, he carried another figure—

 

Captain America.

 

"Asshole! Stop what you're doing immediately!"

 1

Seeing Fenric tampering with his precious suits, Tony completely lost his cool.

 

To Tony, his armors were more than just machines—they were his lifeblood. And now someone was stealing them.

 

When he realized that the Mark VII—the latest armor he had painstakingly developed—was already missing, his fury intensified.

 

His voice was like ice. "Where did you hide my Mark VII?"

 

The Captain stood beside him, shield in hand, staring at Fenric with sharp wariness.

 

Fenric, however, remained calm. He glanced at the tampered USB drive. The progress bar was only at 23%.

 

"Mr. Stark, you have so many suits. How about giving me two?" Fenric said casually, a smirk tugging at his lips. He was clearly stalling for time.

 

"What the hell do you mean by that?" Tony snapped. It was rare for him to get this angry, but this stranger's audacity was beyond tolerance.

 

"Jarvis, locate Mark VII!" Tony ordered through clenched teeth.

 

"I'm sorry, sir. All systems on Mark VII have been modified. I can no longer track or control it," Jarvis replied.

 

Tony's face darkened. His eyes locked onto Fenric like daggers.

 

"Hand over my Mark VII, and I might let you walk out of here alive!"

 5

Fenric chuckled. "Mr. Stark, I'm afraid I have to tell you—Mark VII now belongs to me."

 

"Stark, he's stalling!" Captain America's eyes narrowed. He had already noticed the countdown ticking on the USB drive and called out in warning.

 

"Captain, let's take him down!" Tony roared, fury flaring again.

 2

As soon as the words left his mouth, the thrusters on Iron Man's suit flared. Tony charged forward like a missile.

 

Captain America hurled his shield, the vibranium disc spinning through the air toward Fenric.

 

Clang!

 

The shield slammed into something solid, but instead of deflecting or cutting through, it stopped abruptly—caught in Fenric's hand.

 

The Captain's eyes widened. His attack had been blocked with ease.

 

"Captain, it's not good to throw away your things like that," Fenric said with an amused smile.

 

Without hesitation, he gripped the shield and hurled it back with terrifying force.

 5

Whoosh!

 

The shield cut through the air like a cannonball, its speed boosted by Fenric's overwhelming strength and telekinetic force.

 

Bang!

 

Tony, who was mid-charge, didn't even have time to react. The shield smashed into his armor with enough force to leave a visible dent.

 

"Stark!" the Captain called out.

 

"I'm fine!" Tony grunted, steadying himself. Though his armor was damaged, he wasn't hurt. "Cap, keep him busy!"

 

Captain America retrieved his shield and rushed forward again.

 

But before he could even get close, he felt an invisible force restrain him.

 

Fenric waved his hand.

 

Telekinesis – Activated!

 

The Captain was lifted and flung backward like a rag doll, hitting the wall hard.

 

Tony, seeing this, immediately changed tactics.

 

"Jarvis, divert maximum energy to the arc reactor!"

 

"Energy transfer complete, sir," Jarvis responded.

 

"Let's see you block this!"

 

Tony spread his arms wide. The arc reactor on his chest flared, releasing a blindingly powerful beam aimed straight at Fenric.

 

Fenric, who already knew all of Iron Man's tricks, reacted instantly.

 

He slipped on his Riot Gloves, which expanded into a massive iron sphere.

 

Armament Haki coated its surface in an instant.

 

Boom!!

 

Tony's beam slammed into the iron ball, but it was completely blocked. The heat made the sphere glow red-hot, yet Fenric remained unfazed.

 

"Captain, Stark… you can't stop me. Save your strength."

 

Fenric's eyes shifted to the USB drive—

 

100% completed.

 

He tapped the Mark VI suit, and with a flash, the armor vanished into his personal warehouse.

 

"What… where did you hide it?!" Tony's face darkened further.

 1

But he didn't charge in recklessly again. He had already realized that Fenric wasn't someone he could defeat easily.

 

Captain America stood again, shield in hand, but his heart felt heavy. This man… was far beyond anything he had ever faced.

 2

Superpowers, strange weapons, the ability to make things vanish—

 

Every move Fenric made was abnormal, terrifying.

 

"Captain, Stark, I don't mean you any harm."

 

Fenric smiled, clearly pleased with the outcome.

 

He strolled casually toward them. "We share a common enemy—Loki. In ten minutes, the Chitauri army will invade. I'll fight to protect Earth, just like you."

 3

"..."

 

Hearing that, Tony and the captain looked very ugly.

 

Tony's glare could even melt steel.

 

After all, Fenric had just stolen two of his suits, yet he was saying he wasn't an enemy.

 

If Tony wasn't outclassed right now, he would have already torn Fenric apart.

 

"I think you're more dangerous than Loki," the Captain said grimly. His instincts screamed that this man was trouble.

 

At that moment, Fenric heard the system prompt:

 

"Attention, all Samsara Players participants: The Chitauri invasion begins in 10 minutes."

 

"Only ten minutes left?" Fenric murmured.

 2

Seeing Tony's furious glare behind the helmet, Fenric chuckled. "Relax, Stark. You'll always be the real Iron Man. I have my own mission to handle."

 

Tony's helmet retracted, revealing his face. His voice was calm but deadly serious.

 

"No one steals from me. No matter where you run, I'll find you."

 

Fenric shrugged. "You're welcome to try… but I doubt you'll succeed."

 

With that, Fenric walked to the edge of the balcony. Then—

 

he jumped.

 

Both Tony and the Captain rushed to the balcony, stunned as they watched Fenric plummet from the fifty-fifth floor.

 

As he fell, Fenric unleashed his Mind Power in full force, slowing his descent.

 

Om—

 

The invisible force hummed as it absorbed the impact.

 

Still, a fall from that height was brutal, and even his telekinesis couldn't cancel it completely.

 

Armament Haki coated his body just before he hit the ground.

 

Boom!

 

Fenric smashed into the pavement, carving a massive crater.

 

Pedestrians screamed, scattering in all directions.

 

Then, to everyone's horror, Fenric calmly walked out of the pit—

 

completely unscathed.

 2

chapters.name: Chapter 170: Chapter 170: The Daunting Evil God Loki! (7/8)
chapters.content:
High above the towering buildings, Tony Stark and Captain America stared down at Fenric.

 

They exchanged glances, and both could see the same shock in each other's eyes.

 

Jumping from the fifty-fifth floor without a single injury?

 

Terrifying.

 

Even Captain America, with his enhanced body, knew that if he were to fall from such a height, he would be left in pieces.

 

(In Captain America: The Winter Soldier, he only jumped from a dozen stories high—and that was already pushing the limit.)

 1

"Stark, I don't think you're getting your armor back," the Captain said with a sigh.

 

Tony's jaw tightened, but he refused to respond.

 

He knew the Captain was probably right, but he wasn't about to admit it.

 

Above them, Loki had been watching everything with narrowed eyes.

 

To be honest, Loki was feeling uneasy.

 

Just as Fenric had left earlier, he had looked up—right at him.

 

Loki was certain that this mysterious man had noticed his presence.

 

Then why didn't he interfere?

 

Fenric had clearly said he would fight against Loki's forces, yet when he spotted Loki… he did nothing.

 

The God of Mischief couldn't make sense of this human's intentions, and that made him uncomfortable.

 

"Master! The portal is ready to open!"

 

Dr. Erik Selvig's excited voice broke Loki's thoughts.

 

Loki's eyes gleamed, his unease instantly forgotten. "Do it. Now."

 4

"Yes, Master!"

 

Dr. Selvig immediately activated the Tesseract device.

 

"Ooooom—"

 

A powerful blue beam shot skyward, tearing through the clouds.

 

Moments later, a massive spatial rift opened in the sky above Manhattan.

 

Through the shimmering gateway, the outlines of countless Chitauri soldiers could be seen, lined up and ready to invade.

 

The sheer spectacle drew the attention of everyone in the city.

 

Even Tony and the Captain paled at the sight.

 

Suddenly, a familiar voice echoed in Fenric's mind:

 

"Attention, all Samsara Players. The main mission has been issued!"

 1

"Main Task: Kill at least 20 Chitauri soldiers within 10 hours!"

 

"Time Limit: 10 hours."

 

"Mission Failure: Obliteration!"

 

"Note: The more Chitauri you kill, the higher your mission evaluation will be."

 

Almost simultaneously, every Samsara players participant across New York received the same notification.

 

They had been preparing for this moment. One after another, they sprang into action.

 

But Fenric?

 

He did the opposite.

 

He calmly made his way to an abandoned villa, where he retrieved Mark VII and began his own preparations.

 

The Chitauri invasion didn't concern him—not yet.

 

"Ten hours is plenty of time," Fenric muttered. "Let the others burn themselves out. I'll strike hard when it matters most."

 

Mark VII was unlike any of the previous suits. Sleek, advanced, and versatile, its design resembled a flight capsule.

 

Fans of The Avengers would never forget the scene where Tony, thrown from Stark Tower by Loki, was saved mid-fall when Mark VII flew in, attached itself, and fully assembled around him.

 

Now, the Mark VII was right in front of Fenric.

 

The only problem?

 

He had no idea how to start it.

 

This wasn't his creation, after all.

 

After a moment of hesitation, Fenric simply pressed his hand on the armor.

 

No response.

 

He frowned. "Start?"

 

Click! Whirrr!

 

To his surprise, the armor responded to his voice command.

 

The entire suit lit up, mechanical components shifting and separating with smooth precision.

 

In seconds, the armor began to assemble itself over Fenric's body, piece by piece.

 2

Within a few breaths, there was another Iron Man standing in the room—except this one was Fenric.

 

"Damn, this is awesome!" Fenric couldn't help exclaiming, turning his alloy-covered arms over in admiration.

 

No wonder Tony Stark had become so iconic.

 

A man's dream—mecha.

 3

"Master, this is Zero, at your service," said a calm male voice in his ear.

 

It was the armor's built-in AI.

 

"Zero? Ugh, I don't want some guy's voice talking to me all day. Change to a female voice."

 9

"Understood, Master," the voice shifted instantly into a soft, slightly playful tone. "Would this voice please you more?"

 

Fenric grinned. "Much better. But don't make it too cute—something normal."

 

"Okay, Master," the AI replied, adjusting its tone again.

 

"Perfect. Oh, and from now on, your name's not Zero. I'll call you… Tsunade!"

 11

The name came from one of Fenric's favorite characters from an anime he loved in his past life.

 

"Acknowledged. Tsunade is at your service, Master," the AI responded.

 

Fenric laughed with satisfaction.

 

He began testing the armor's controls, familiarizing himself with its flight and combat systems.

 

"Tsunade, tell me about your weapons."

 1

"Certainly, Master. The shoulder weapon bays can launch 92 micro-missiles simultaneously. Additional missile systems are located in the legs. Each arm is equipped with triple-barrel laser cannons, capable of emitting beams at over 3,000°C. The thrusters in both hands can double as repulsor energy cannons."

 

Fenric's smile widened. "Nice. Very nice."

 

Meanwhile, in Manhattan, New York—

 

The war for humanity's survival had begun.

 

The Chitauri swarmed out of the space-time portal like a relentless tide.

 

"Iron Man" Tony Stark, "Captain America" Steve Rogers, "Hawkeye" Clint Barton, and "Black Widow" Natasha Romanoff were already on the battlefield, fighting tooth and nail.

 

Thor, the God of Thunder, had also escaped his imprisonment to confront his "good" brother, Loki.

 

But the Hulk was still nowhere to be seen.

 

S.H.I.E.L.D. had believed these heroes were humanity's greatest hope against the alien invasion.

 

But they quickly realized something shocking—

 

The Samsaras.

 

A group of mysterious, powerful individuals had suddenly appeared all across Manhattan, slaughtering Chitauri soldiers with terrifying efficiency.

 

According to the original timeline, humanity had been utterly powerless against the Chitauri's technology and strength.

 

Without the Avengers, they would have been annihilated.

 

But now, these Samsara players—each one as strong as a superhuman—were turning the tide of battle.

 

Their desperation to earn high mission scores drove them to fight like madmen.

 

"Someone tell me… where did these people come from?!"

 1

Loki's expression twisted as he watched from above.

 

For the first time, the God of Mischief felt a twinge of unease.

chapters.name: Chapter 171: Chapter 171: The Great God of Shura is Finally Out! (8/8)
chapters.content:
"Brothers, kill!"

 

"Hurry, hurry! Slaughter as many as you can. Once the Shura God makes a move, we won't even get a share!"

 

"Damn it! This is my territory—go find your own spot!"

 

"Stop fighting amongst yourselves! There are plenty of Chitauri for everyone. Stay sharp—safety comes first!"

 

"Yeah! These aliens may not be strong individually, but getting surrounded by them means certain death!"

 

Aboard the Helicarrier

 

Nick Fury, the current Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., observed the chaotic battlefield through the surveillance feeds.

 

Watching the Samsara players' performance, his single eye narrowed in solemn thought.

 

Was this really still the Earth he knew?

 

Since when were there so many powerful humans?

 

"Hill, why don't we have any intel on these people?" Fury demanded.

 

Standing beside him was Agent Maria Hill, his capable second-in-command and a Level 9 S.H.I.E.L.D. agent.

 

"I'm sorry, sir. This is our oversight," Hill admitted.

 

Fury's voice dropped into a cold tone. "After this battle—if Earth still exists—I want a full report on every single one of these people within three days. Understood?"

 

"Understood!" Hill replied firmly.

 

Manhattan

 

From high above, Loki watched as his Chitauri army was held back by the sheer ferocity of the Samsara players. His expression darkened.

 

"The entire army—attack!" Loki ordered, his voice like ice.

 1

From the space-time portal, an overwhelming wave of Chitauri soldiers surged out.

 

Among them were enormous, reptilian leviathans that roared as they smashed through skyscrapers like paper.

 

The Samsara players, strong as they were, found it almost impossible to deal with these massive war beasts.

 

In the Avengers' team, only Thor and the Hulk could bring down creatures of this scale—and even for them, it required tremendous effort.

 1

The tide of battle shifted.

 

The Chitauri began to push forward, gaining the upper hand.

 

Casualties among the Samsara players mounted quickly.

 

Seeing some of their comrades surrounded and torn apart, many Samsara players faltered.

 

The more cowardly ones retreated, planning to hide until the mission timer ran out.

 

The braver Samsara players continued fighting, but even they resorted to ambush tactics instead of direct confrontation.

 

Hours Passed

 

In the blink of an eye, three to four hours had gone by.

 

The Chitauri invasion had expanded, and the battlefield now spanned all of Manhattan.

 

Human forces were being pushed back on every front.

 

For now, the U.S. government refrained from using nuclear weapons. The devastating consequences of such an action made it a last resort no one wanted to authorize.

 

Somewhere Remote

 

"Whoosh!"

 

The sound of something cutting through the air echoed.

 

A red-and-gold figure soared across the sky—Fenric.

 

He was still training with the Mark VII armor, practicing his flight maneuvers.

 

After several hours of trial and error, Fenric finally got the hang of maintaining balance.

 

He wasn't Iron Man-level skilled yet, but at least he wasn't crashing face-first anymore.

 

"Master, energy reserves are running low. Please be cautious," said the gentle female voice of the AI—Tsunade—through Fenric's helmet.

 2

"Tsunade, how much power do we have left?" Fenric asked.

 

"Twenty percent."

 1

"How do I recharge?"

 

"You may replace the reactor for instant replenishment, or recharge via an external power source."

 2

"You can recharge like that?"

 

"Of course, Master."

 

"Good to know."

 

Fenric spotted a residential building below and descended swiftly.

 

Inside, a group of frightened civilians cowered, hiding from the chaos outside.

 

When they saw the red-and-gold armor, their eyes lit up.

 

"Iron Man! Please save us!"

 

"Mr. Stark, we're your fans! Don't die out there!"

 

Fenric raised his visor and grinned. "Look closely—I'm not your idol."

 

The stunned civilians froze in disbelief.

 

"Lend me your home appliances!" Fenric said casually.

 

Before they could respond, he began using their power outlets to recharge the Mark VII.

 3

The charging process was painfully slow.

 

An entire hour passed before the armor's power level rose to 60%—but that was enough.

 13

By now, five hours of the mission time had elapsed.

 

Fenric put the armor away and prepared to finally enter the battlefield.

 

The Battlefield

 

When Fenric arrived, the battle was in full chaos.

 

Iron Man, Tony Stark, was barely evading several Chitauri aircraft, completely outnumbered.

 

Thor stood atop a skyscraper, summoning lightning with Mjolnir to obliterate groups of Chitauri soldiers—but the next moment, a swarm surrounded him.

 

No matter how desperately Iron Man and Thor fought, the Chitauri continued pouring through the portal like an unstoppable flood.

 

Five hours of relentless combat had left both the superheroes and Samsara players utterly exhausted.

 

Yet the invasion only grew worse.

 

The streets of New York were in ruins, filled with fire, rubble, and chaos.

 

The Chitauri aircraft rained energy blasts onto cars and buildings, each shot capable of blowing a vehicle to pieces.

 

Amidst the panic, one man walked calmly against the flow of fleeing citizens—Fenric.

 

His relaxed demeanor was so out of place that it drew the attention of a squad of Chitauri.

 

"Whoosh!"

 

An energy blast shot toward him.

 

BOOM!

 

The explosion engulfed Fenric, but when the smoke cleared…

 

He stood unharmed.

 

The only casualty was his shirt, which was shredded by the blast.

 

"Hmm… the Chitauri's energy weapons pack more power than a rifle, but their penetration is weak. With my body as it is now, I can tank these attacks without even using Armament Haki."

 

Fenric muttered casually, ignoring the Chitauri soldiers rushing toward him.

chapters.name: Chapter 172: Chapter 172: Use Violence to Control Violence!
chapters.content:
Swish! Swish! Swish!

 

Several flying blades shot out under Fenric's control, cutting through the Chitauri soldiers like hot knives through butter.

 

With his current mental power, each flying blade carried more penetrating force than a rifle bullet. Even the armor of the Chitauri could not withstand his attacks.

 

Within moments, the alien soldiers surrounding Fenric fell one after another.

 

The Chitauri tried to counterattack, their energy guns blazing with bright flashes of light.

 

But the blasts barely affected Fenric. The moment he coated himself with Armament Haki, the energy projectiles only felt like light tickles against his skin.

 

The only thing they managed to do was generate heat, slightly singeing his already torn clothes.

 

Fenric walked forward casually, his hands barely moving, blades floating and striking with lethal precision. He strolled across the battlefield as though he were walking through his own garden.

 

Wherever he passed, the Chitauri collapsed.

 

"Boom!"

 

Suddenly, a massive energy cannon shot down from a Chitauri aircraft, striking Fenric directly and making him pause for the first time.

 

"This is from their aircraft, huh?" Fenric muttered with a faint smile. "Not bad… but still not enough to break my defenses. The heat is a little annoying, though."

 

Most of his upper clothing had already been burned to rags, leaving only scraps clinging to his torso. Fortunately, his pants were still intact—otherwise, things would've been awkward.

 3

Two Chitauri aircraft descended, continuously bombarding Fenric with heavy energy blasts.

 

Not wanting his pants to meet the same fate as his shirt, Fenric raised a hand, forming a vortex of psychic energy around himself. The incoming energy blasts deflected off the barrier, ricocheting to the ground nearby.

 2

Blocking energy cannons directly with raw psychic force was inefficient, but redirecting them with a mental twist was far easier and cost him little effort.

 

The moment the aircraft swooped closer, Fenric smirked. He raised his hand slightly… then pressed down.

 

With a sudden pull of psychic force, the aircraft's flight paths twisted violently.

 

"Boom! Boom!"

 

Both aircraft slammed into the ground, exploding into a rain of fire and metal before they could even get close.

 

Fenric didn't even glance at the wreckage. He simply kept moving forward.

 

So far, Fenric hadn't taken a single step back. His overwhelming presence drew the attention of everyone nearby.

 

"Holy crap, who's that guy? He's mowing down the Chitauri like nothing!"

 

"Do you even need to ask? That's the Shura God!"

 

"Damn, the Shura God finally made his move?"

 

"That guy's a monster. His strength is terrifying!"

 

"Heh, don't get too excited. Look at him—he's so arrogant. When the full Chitauri army arrives, let's see if he can still act tough!"

 1

From the shadows, several Samsara players whispered as they watched Fenric's onslaught, their eyes filled with awe and envy.

 

On a rooftop, Hawkeye, Clint Barton, adjusted his aim while watching Fenric's rampage.

 

"Does anyone know who that guy is on Thirteenth Street?" he asked through his comms.

 

A moment later, Tony's angry voice crackled in response. "He's a damn thief!"

 

"A thief?" Black Widow, Natasha Romanoff, raised an eyebrow. "Don't tell me he stole your girlfriend, Tony?"

 

"Worse than that!" Tony said indignantly.

 2

Captain America's voice came over the line, calm yet firm. "Stark, focus on the bigger picture. Loki first, aliens second. Forget your grudges for now."

 

It was clear Steve was trying to stop Tony from doing something reckless.

 

Hawkeye chimed in again. "That guy's drawing a ton of attention. The Chitauri are swarming toward him. Should we back him up?"

 

"No! That guy's not going down anytime soon." Tony snorted.

 

What he didn't say aloud was that Fenric was wearing his stolen armor—something that still burned in Tony's chest.

 1

Fenric didn't care about the growing horde around him. The ordinary Chitauri soldiers weren't even worth his time. With a mere flick of his mental power, they dropped like flies.

 

Aircraft? He dragged them out of the sky with a casual wave.

 

But his display of dominance finally provoked the Chitauri.

 

From the space-time portal, a giant reptilian war beast emerged, its colossal frame shaking the ground with every step.

 

While others might have turned pale at the sight, Fenric's lips curled into a grin.

 

"Finally, a worthy opponent."

 1

He pulled out the Riot Gloves and slid them onto his hands.

 

Not only did Fenric not retreat, he charged forward.

 

"Is this guy insane?" Hawkeye muttered from his rooftop vantage point, unable to believe his eyes.

 

The others also turned their attention toward Fenric.

 

"BZZT—!"

 

The massive creature barreled forward, every collision sent tremors through the ground.

 

In front of it, Fenric's human frame looked ridiculously small—barely the size of the creature's head.

 

But size wasn't everything.

 2

"Zing!"

 

At Fenric's command, the Riot Gloves morphed into a massive iron ball, its surface bristling with sharp spikes. His right hand gripped the weapon tightly, energy swirling around him.

 3

As the two closed in, Fenric's eyes hardened.

 

"Let's see whose strength wins!"

 

With explosive force, Fenric launched himself forward like a cannonball, swinging the iron sphere straight into the monster's face.

 

The impact was brutal—an earth-shattering punch reminiscent of the Hulk's iconic blows.

 

Truthfully, Fenric could have ended the fight more easily with his black blade.

 

But this time, he wanted to use sheer violence to make a statement—a show of power aimed directly at S.H.I.E.L.D. and the world.

 

"BOOOOM!!!"

 

The deafening explosion of impact echoed across the war-torn streets of New York.
