chapters.name: Chapter 186: Chapter 186: Can You Play? How Can You Play?
chapters.content:
At first glance, the man before Fenric looked like an ordinary uncle living out his retirement in peace.

 

Especially with that pair of worn slippers—it was impossible to associate this man with the legendary King of Killers.

 1

Fenric was speechless.

 

Seriously?

 

In the original story, when Sing found him, Fire Cloud had been squatting in a pit.

 

Now, here he was again—still squatting in the same pit.

 

Does this guy spend his whole life… doing this?

 

"Who are you looking for?"

 

The man, disheveled and unkempt like a lazy uncle, raised his head in mild surprise when he noticed Fenric.

 

"I'm looking for you—Fire Cloud," Fenric replied with a faint smirk. "But you should probably put your pants on first."

 

Without another word, Fenric closed the iron door.

 

A short while later, a deep, resonant voice called out, "Alright, boy. Come in!"

 

Fenric reopened the iron door.

 

"What business do you have with me?"

 

The Fire Cloud didn't bother hiding his identity.

 

"Nothing major," Fenric said casually, his smile unwavering. "I heard the legendary King of Killers was here. I came to witness your style—and perhaps have a little sparring match with you."

 

The old killer blinked, sizing Fenric up before shaking his head.

 

"I only fight with worthy opponents," Fire Cloud said flatly. "Boy, you're strong and your blood is raging, but you clearly haven't trained in proper martial arts. I've no interest in fighting you."

 

"Senior, your eyesight is indeed sharp."

 

Fenric chuckled. "You can tell at a glance that I've never formally trained in martial arts. As expected of Fire Cloud!"

 

He then added with a grin, "But I'm very good at fighting. Why not give this junior a little guidance?"

 

Though Fenric had no real animosity toward the man, he admired martial fanatics like him. His tone remained respectful.

 

"A good fighter, you say?"

 

Fire Cloud gave a low laugh. "How good could you be? Come then—throw a punch and show me."

 

His tone wasn't mocking, but it carried a faint disbelief, as though Fenric's words were mere bravado.

 

This wasn't because Fire Cloud lacked judgment—on the contrary, his eyes were sharp.

 

He could sense Fenric's power and vitality, but the absence of a martial foundation made him doubt the young man's true ability.

 

In this world, strength was defined by martial arts, not mysterious abilities.

 

How could someone who never trained properly claim to be "good at fighting"?

 

—-

 

"Alright then," Fenric said, his lips curling into a confident smile. "But don't say I didn't warn you—my fists are heavy. If you can't take it, just tell me."

 

With that, he stepped forward.

 

—-

 

At first, Fire Cloud remained indifferent.

 

But when he saw Fenric's fist suddenly darken, its surface gleaming like polished black steel, his eyes narrowed.

 

The moment Fenric's punch shot forward, the air cracked with a thunderous boom.

 

Whoosh!

 

The sound of the strike tearing through the air was deafening.

 

For the first time, Fire Cloud's expression turned serious. He quickly raised an arm to block.

 

BOOM—!

 

A heavy collision echoed.

 

The old killer staggered back three or four steps, his heels dragging across the ground until he finally stopped just before hitting the wall.

 

Fenric raised an eyebrow in surprise.

 

That punch had carried at least seventy to eighty percent of his strength. With his current stats, he could have shattered a normal human's body with that single blow.

 

Yet this uncle looking man had blocked it with just his arm—without even a scratch.

 

What an impressive level of defense!

 

What Fenric didn't realize was that Fire Cloud was even more astonished.

 

"Natural-born supernatural strength?"

 

His eyes widened as he examined Fenric's blackened fist.

 

"Boy, what's with that hand? Did you train in some kind of iron-body martial art?"

 

But even as he asked, Fire Cloud shook his head.

 

"No… that's impossible. No horizontal training could ever achieve that."

 

And he wasn't wrong.

 

Fenric's Armament Haki could harden his body to the strength of steel. To call it "invulnerable" was no exaggeration. No martial artist could replicate such a feat through traditional training.

 

Fenric merely smiled, saying nothing. Instead, he asked, "Well, senior? Was my punch strong enough for your taste?"

 

A glint of interest flashed in Fire Cloud's eyes.

 

"Boy, since you know my name, you should also know my rule when I fight someone."

 

"I know," Fenric replied calmly. "Either I kill you… or you kill me."

 

"Good," Fire Cloud said, a grin spreading across his face. There was both malice and excitement in that smile.

 

He lived for battles against the strong—and Fenric had just proven himself worthy.

 

"I can't fight seriously in here," Fenric said. "Senior, shall we move somewhere more open?"

 

"Fine by me."

 

They walked out together, easily brushing past the foreign soldiers who were far too terrified to stop them.

 

The chosen battlefield wasn't far—an open wasteland beside the mental hospital.

 

The two stood at opposite ends, facing each other in silence.

 

Fenric's expression turned solemn.

 

He knew better than to underestimate this man. In the original story, Fire Cloud's strength was nothing short of terrifying.

 

He could catch bullets with his bare fingers, crush walls with a single kick, and even survive the divine Buddha Palm Technique that fell from the heavens.

 

By Samsara Space standards, Fire Cloud's strength was likely close to A-rank.

 2

"Young man," Fire Cloud said, "what's your name? I don't kill nameless challengers."

 

"Just call me Shura," Fenric replied.

 

"Shura?"

 

A cold smile tugged at the corner of Fire Cloud's lips.

 

The name was arrogant, almost sacrilegious. In Buddhist terms, Shura referred to beings that rivaled the heavens but were still bound by karma—a symbol of relentless conflict.

 

"Come, then," Fire Cloud said with a low laugh. "Show me what you've got. I'll go easy on you—for now."

 

"Good!"

 

The moment the word left his mouth, Fenric's eyes burned with light. A powerful aura surged around him, majestic and unyielding—like that of an ancient king.

chapters.name: Chapter 187: Chapter 187: Boy, What Kind of Monster Are You?
chapters.content:
"Hmm?"

 

As the oppressive aura of a king swept over him, Fire Cloud's expression shifted, his eyes widening in surprise.

 

"What incredible momentum!"

 

He had never encountered such a forceful presence before. The sheer weight of Fenric's aura was so intense that it slightly shook his own willpower.

 

At that moment, Fire Cloud's curiosity about Fenric deepened.

 

"Boy, momentum alone won't scare me. If you've got guts, come at me!"

 

His sharp eyes locked onto Fenric like a predator sizing up its prey.

 

Seeing Fire Cloud's unwavering stance, Fenric sighed inwardly.

 

So, my Conqueror's Haki isn't strong enough yet.

 1

Even though his presence was overwhelming to most, Fire Cloud's willpower was as solid as iron, reducing the aura's effect on him.

 

"Senior," Fenric said with a faint smile, retracting his aura, "be careful."

 

The moment his words fell—

 

Swish!

 

Fenric's figure vanished.

 

When he reappeared, he was already in midair, descending like a missile toward Fire Cloud, his body coated entirely in Armament Haki.

 

His fist tightened like black steel as he drove a powerful punch directly toward Fire Cloud's face.

 

This time, Fenric was going all out.

 

Seeing the incoming strike, Fire Cloud's face hardened.

 

The sheer pressure of Fenric's punch was palpable—even before it reached him, he could feel the violent wind buffeting his face, his hair whipping wildly.

 

With a roar, he clenched his fist and countered head-on.

 

BOOM—!

 

The clash of fists echoed like thunder.

 

Thud! Thud! Thud!

 

Fire Cloud staggered three steps back before regaining his footing, his right hand trembling slightly and the back of it reddening.

 

Fenric, however, stood unmoving, his arm steady as stone.

 

From this, it was clear—

 

In pure strength, Fenric had the absolute advantage.

 

And with Armament Haki reinforcing his body, even Fire Cloud's explosive internal force couldn't harm him.

 

"Good!" Fire Cloud grinned fiercely. "Now take a punch from me!"

 

With a powerful stomp, he exploded forward, his clawed hand lashing out in a move known as 'Black Tiger Steals the Heart,' aiming directly at Fenric's chest.

 

The old killer's speed was terrifying—nearly at the limit of human capability.

 3

In the original story, he had thrown two punches in a blink, effortlessly defeating the bizarre two 'Harpies Heroes.'

 

But Fenric was not slow either.

 

His agility was now 25 times that of an ordinary human, his reflexes enhanced to superhuman levels.

 

No matter how fast Fire Cloud was, Fenric's eyes could follow every movement.

 3

Whoosh!

 

Fenric's hand shot out, intercepting the attack and gripping Fire Cloud's wrist.

 

The old man's face twitched in surprise—he hadn't expected Fenric's speed to match his own.

 

But Fire Cloud was a seasoned killer. He twisted his wrist, slipping free of Fenric's grip, and countered with a catching technique, attempting to throw Fenric off balance.

 

The move, though simple, carried deadly precision in Fire Cloud's hands.

 

In the next instant, he lunged in close, driving his shoulder forward in a crushing strike—

 

'Shoulder Strike as Steadfast as a Mountain!'

 

Poom!

 

Fenric felt the impact slam into him like a speeding truck, pushing him back slightly.

 

But his Armament Haki had long since covered his body.

 

Truck? Even a tank wouldn't leave a dent, he thought with a smirk.

 

On the other hand, Fire Cloud felt as if he had rammed into solid iron. The recoil numbed his shoulder.

 

"Boy, what kind of iron-body technique are you practicing?" Fire Cloud demanded, his eyes narrowing.

 

Fenric merely smiled and replied, "Senior, you should use your 'Toad Skill.' Otherwise, you won't even scratch me."

 

"Arrogant brat!!"

 

With a snarl, Fire Cloud shot forward again, no longer testing the waters but going all out.

 

BOOM—!

 

His fist hammered into Fenric's abdomen.

 

Fenric didn't dodge. He deliberately took the hit, letting Fire Cloud feel the difference.

 

From their earlier exchange, Fenric had already gauged his opponent's strength—powerful, far beyond ordinary humans.

 

But still, it wasn't enough to surpass Fenric's own raw strength, and certainly not enough to break through his Haki.

 

"Hmm?"

 

Fenric felt a strange force following the punch into his body, probing and vibrating his insides.

 

Internal energy?

 

His eyes glinted with interest. This is unique… but if you think that'll hurt me, you're mistaken.

 

With a slight twist of his torso, Fenric unleashed a shockwave of counterforce, sending Fire Cloud stumbling backward.

 1

Even without Armament Haki, Fenric's body was monstrously resilient.

 

His muscle density had tripled compared to normal humans, his mass compressed into a slim but incredibly heavy frame.

 

By now, even pistol rounds would barely scratch him.

 

For Fire Cloud to hurt him with internal energy alone would be… nearly impossible.

 

"Boy, what kind of monster are you?"

 

Fire Cloud's voice carried genuine shock.

 

In all his life, he had never met anyone with such an overwhelming natural physique.

 

Fenric smirked. "Senior, if you don't use your Toad Skill soon, I'm afraid you might actually get beaten to death."

 

The words struck a nerve.

 

Despite his outward bravado, Fire Cloud feared death.

 

In the original story, when the Landlady unleashed her Lion's Roar and nearly destroyed the Axe Gang casino, Fire Cloud instantly surrendered—only to strike again when the chance arose.

 

It wasn't honor he cared about—it was survival.

 

"Beat me to death? Come!"

 

Fire Cloud's face twisted into a snarl, his fists creaking from the force of his grip.

chapters.name: Chapter 188: Chapter 188: Toad Power vs Thor’s Hammer!
chapters.content:
Seeing that Fire Cloud seemed unconvinced, Fenric shook his head lightly.

 

"Senior, my next punch might be a little heavy. If you can't take it, don't be shy—just say so."

 

With that, Fenric strode forward.

 

When he closed in, he suddenly leaped like a tiger pouncing down a mountain, his fist driving straight toward Fire Cloud's face.

 1

Fire Cloud, wary of Fenric's monstrous strength, tried to dodge—but his expression abruptly changed.

 

What? I can't move?!

 

An invisible force pinned his body in place.

 

It was Fenric's telekinetic power.

 

Though he didn't understand what it was, Fire Cloud knew that this strange ability came from the young man before him.

 

This kid… he's not human. He's a monster with ability after ability!

 

There was no time to dodge!

 

Cursing under his breath, Fire Cloud crossed his arms to block the incoming strike.

 

BOOM—!!

 

The impact sounded like a muffled explosion.

 

For a moment, Fire Cloud felt as if the weight of a mountain had slammed into him.

 

The ground beneath his feet cracked, and his knees bent under the overwhelming force—he was barely able to resist kneeling. His arms went numb, no longer feeling like his own.

 

Fenric, unlike traditional martial artists, relied on raw physical strength and Armament Haki. Though he lacked internal energy, his sheer power was enough to crush through Fire Cloud's defenses.

 

"Kneel!"

 

Fenric's voice was cold as he struck again, telekinesis amplifying the weight of his blow and locking down Fire Cloud's movements.

 

BOOM—!

 

The punch landed.

 

Fire Cloud's mind went blank for a moment, his body giving in as his knees slammed into the ground with a resounding thud, cracking the dirt beneath him.

 1

Fenric stepped back, looking down at him with a faint, almost bored smile.

 

"If the so-called 'Ultimate Killer King' is only capable of this," he said casually, "then this trip was a waste of time."

 

Fenric wasn't trying to humiliate Fire Cloud—he wanted to provoke him. To draw out his strongest technique, the legendary 'Toad Gong.'

 1

In his normal state, Fire Cloud was strong—far stronger than the Landlord and Landlady of Pig Sty Alley. But compared to Fenric's current level, he wasn't enough to spark Fenric's fighting spirit.

 

The only aspect where Fire Cloud stood out was speed.

 

This old man lived by the principle:

 

"In the world of martial arts, there is no move that cannot be broken—only speed that cannot be surpassed!"

 

And he wasn't wrong. In terms of pure speed, Fire Cloud was unmatched.

 

But Fenric had just shattered that belief.

 

For the first time in his life, Fire Cloud had been forced to his knees.

 

His eyes burned with rage.

 

The next moment, instead of standing, he pressed himself flat against the ground.

 1

"Gu-gu-gu—"

 

A guttural croaking sound erupted from his abdomen, deep and resonant like a toad's cry amplified by thunder.

 

Whoosh!

 

A surge of invisible energy blasted outward from him, scattering leaves and dust like a violent gust.

 

"Gu-gu-gu—"

 

The croak grew louder as Fire Cloud's body swelled unnaturally. His muscles bulged, his legs thickened, and his chin puffed out like an inflated balloon—

 

He had taken on the form of a giant toad.

 

With a sharp glare, Fire Cloud's legs coiled.

 

BOOM—!

 

The ground beneath him cratered as he launched himself forward like a cannonball.

 

CRACK!

 

The air itself split as a sonic boom tore through the silence. His speed had surpassed the sound barrier!

 

"Too fast—!" Fenric's eyes narrowed.

 

For the first time in this fight, he chose to defend. Telekinesis had little effect at such velocity, so he crossed his arms in front of him, Armament Haki spreading like black steel over his entire body.

 

BOOM—!!!

 

Fenric's body was blasted off his feet. He flew several hundred meters, crashing through a dirt slope before coming to a stop.

 

In the original plot, Fire Cloud's Toad Gong could launch someone like Sing into the stratosphere.

 

The explosive power behind such a feat was beyond imagination.

 

"Cough! Cough!"

 

Fenric pulled himself from the rubble, feeling the dull throb of blood circulation disrupted.

 

If my Armament Haki wasn't at this level, that blow would've seriously hurt me.

 

BANG!

 

Another sonic boom cracked through the air.

 

Fenric barely had time to react. The moment he heard the sound, Fire Cloud was already on top of him.

 

BOOM—!

 

Another devastating strike hurled Fenric backward, slamming him into a tree that splintered like kindling.

 

His arms ached.

 

For the first time since perfecting his Armament Haki, Fenric had been injured.

 

Yet lying on the ground, Fenric began to laugh.

 

This is the power of Toad Gong?

 

Good. That means Sing's Buddha Palm Technique will be even stronger!

 

The thought ignited a spark of excitement within him. He couldn't wait to test himself against it.

 

But Fire Cloud wasn't done.

 

A shadow loomed overhead, blocking the sunlight.

 

He had leaped high into the air, descending like a meteor aimed to crush Fenric completely.

 

He wants to kill me now.

 

Fenric's expression hardened, a cold light flashing in his eyes.

 

With a thought, Thor's Hammer appeared in his hand.

 

"Zzzt—zzzt!"

 

Electric arcs coiled along the weapon like serpents, crawling up Fenric's arm.

 

(Author's Note: Fire Cloud's power is rated B+, very close to A. Sing with the Buddha Palm Technique is a solid A tier. Navy Admirals rank at A+, near S rank. While someone like Aurora Morwyn sits at high A. Don't underestimate the power gap between tiers!)

chapters.name: Chapter 189: Chapter 189: God of Thunder is Born, Brave and Invincible!
chapters.content:
Dark clouds suddenly gathered in the sky, rolling in like an ominous tide.

 

BOOM—!

 

Lightning streaked across the heavens, and thunder roared like an angry beast.

 

Moments ago, the weather had been bright and sunny. Now, with the sudden arrival of dark storm clouds, even fools could tell that something unnatural was happening.

 

On the ground, Fenric pushed himself up with a swift carp-like movement, standing tall once more.

 

When he raised his gaze, Fire Cloud was already descending like a meteorite, aiming to crush him.

 

Fenric gripped Thor's Hammer tightly and swung it upward in a powerful arc.

 

BOOM—!

 

The hammer smashed into Fire Cloud's abdomen with devastating force, hurling him back into the air.

 

However, the sheer momentum of Fire Cloud's dive also sent Fenric crashing into the earth, carving a large pit beneath him.

 

Pffft!

 

Fenric spat out a mouthful of blood but stood up almost instantly. His formidable physique, reinforced by Armament Haki, allowed him to endure even such violent blows with only minor injuries.

 

From the distance came the guttural sound of a toad's croak.

 

Fire Cloud lay sprawled on the ground, glaring at Fenric with a feral intensity.

 

The hammer blow just now—had it struck his pre-Toad Gong form—would have shattered his organs completely.

 

But with Toad Gong active, his entire body was as tough as a bloated, armored fortress, and his defensive power had increased severalfold.

 

In the original storyline, Sing was able to destroy entire buildings with a single palm strike, yet even that couldn't kill Fire Cloud in his Toad Gong state. This proves just how terrifying this technique really is.

 

Seeing Fire Cloud charging up his strength again, Fenric's eyes grew cold.

 

Thor's Hammer wasn't just for smashing enemies—it was for summoning the wrath of the heavens!

 

Fenric raised the hammer high.

 

BOOOOM!

 

Thunder cracked, and a pillar of lightning as thick as a tree trunk shot down from the heavens, slamming directly into the hammer.

 

Brilliant arcs of lightning erupted, coiling like dragons as they wrapped around Fenric's body. For a moment, he stood like a god of thunder descended upon the mortal world, radiating awe and terror.

 

This upgraded Thor's Hammer made Fenric immune to lightning damage—a special trait he had modified into the weapon.

 

Otherwise, even his mastery of Armament Haki wouldn't have saved him from being fried to a crisp by such violent thunderbolts.

 

In the distance, Fire Cloud froze, his face draining of color.

 

The figure before him was no longer just a warrior.

 

Fenric looked like the God of Thunder himself!

 

After absorbing the thunder, Thor's Hammer vibrated with raw power, glowing as arcs of energy danced along its surface.

 1

Fenric pointed the hammer at Fire Cloud.

 

BOOM—!!!

 

A massive thunder dragon burst forth from the hammer's head, tearing through the air as it struck Fire Cloud's position.

 3

KA-BOOOM—!!

 

The explosion shook the ground, leaving behind a scorched crater. Electricity rippled outward, charring everything within a hundred-meter radius.

 

Cold sweat poured down Fire Cloud's face.

 

Just a little more... If I hadn't moved when I did, I would have been dead.

 

Even with his Toad Gong defense, he knew this thunder strike would have annihilated him.

 

Worse still, thunder's speed rivaled that of light.

 1

There was no dodging it if he wasn't already moving in advance.

 3

Far off, Fenric raised Thor's Hammer again.

 

This time, he didn't bother absorbing the lightning—he called it down directly.

 

Thor's Hammer could either store lightning as a powerful finishing move or summon instantaneous strikes for faster attacks.

 

The former was devastatingly strong. The latter was weaker, but far quicker.

 

CRASH!!!

 

A thunderbolt streaked down like divine judgment, striking before Fire Cloud could even react.

 

There was no chance to dodge!

 

The blast sent him convulsing before he collapsed, losing consciousness instantly.

 

The storm clouds gradually receded, and sunlight returned to the sky.

 

Fenric lowered the hammer and looked at it with satisfaction.

 

This weapon is absurdly powerful. The Thor Hammer truly lives up to its name.

 

This was his first time wielding Thor's Hammer in actual combat, and although he was still unfamiliar with its full potential, he had still easily crushed Fire Cloud.

 

Too strong.

 

With this hammer, Fenric was confident—

 

even Sing with his Buddha Palm Technique wouldn't intimidate him now.

 3

Fenric stored Thor's Hammer back into his personal warehouse and walked toward the fallen Fire Cloud.

 

The old man was charred black, his body smoking like burnt wood.

 

But Fenric could still hear a faint heartbeat.

 

Impressive… even after that, he's alive. That final lightning strike was weaker since I didn't store it first. If I had used the fully charged blow, this old man would already be dead.

 

Fenric glanced at the unconscious Fire Cloud for a moment, then turned and left.

 

He had no intention of killing him.

 

After all, they had no personal enmity, and Fenric had been the one to seek out this fight.

 

Beating someone this badly was already excessive—killing him would be too much.

 3

With that, Fenric continued with his plan.

 

Moments later, the battle site drew a crowd.

 

The commotion earlier had been impossible to ignore, and the storm of dark clouds and thunder over SH City had been visible to half the population.

 

Curious citizens came rushing over.

 

"What the hell happened here? That thunder was insane!"

 

"Look at the ground! It's completely scorched black!"

 

"Not even grass survived… this is terrifying."

 

"Wait, look—there's someone lying there!"

 

"Damn! Is he even human? Did he get struck by lightning?"

 

"This must be divine punishment! He must've done something terrible for the heavens to smite him!"

 

"Stay back! Keep the kids away—those who die from lightning strikes are cursed!"

 

The bystanders gossiped endlessly, completely unaware of the truth.

 

While the civilians were clueless, a few Samsaras who had witnessed the battle were stunned.

 

"Fk! Who was that? Who the hell can summon sky thunder like this?!"

 

"No way… was that guy an A-grade powerhouse? Isn't this supposed to be a normal difficulty dungeon?!"

 

"Laoma, are we still following our plan? What if we run into someone like that?"

 

"Forget it! Let's stay low-key and just finish the mission. This dungeon is way deeper than we thought!"

 

"Damn it… I feel like we've been screwed over by the system!"

 

"Could it be… the Shura Boss? I've heard people say his power might already be above A-rank!"

 

"No way. Can Shura Boss really be that terrifying?"

 

(TL/n: Here's Fire Cloud Powers / Skills;

 

Superhuman agility

 

Superhuman durability

 

Superhuman speed

 

Superhuman strength

 

Superhuman jumping

 

Superhuman flexibility

 

Superhuman reflexes

 

Superhuman precision

 

Superhuman senses

 

Superhuman climbing

 

Pressure manipulation

 

Abnormal movement

 

Cunning and deceit

 

Shockwave generation

 

Earthquake generation

 

Martial Arts Mastery

 

FTE attack/reaction speed

 

Peak Kung Fu fighting skills

 

Zoomorphism

 

Toad Gong Style—His Ultimate Move)

chapters.name: Chapter 190: Chapter 190: Desperate and Terrified!
chapters.content:
As the curious crowd began to disperse, two strange figures walked slowly along the street.

 

One was tall and sturdy, the other short and thin. Both were dressed identically: gray cloth robes, round caps, and dark sunglasses that concealed their eyes and expressions. What made them stand out even more was the long, cloth-wrapped object they carried between them, its shape indistinguishable.

 

The two men walked in perfect sync until they reached the scorched battlefield left by the lightning strike. There, they stopped.

 

"There are clear signs of a fight," the thin man said suddenly.

 

"Yes," the sturdier one nodded. "And not just any fight—a true master was involved."

 

Both men were martial experts themselves. The damage in the area, though subtle to ordinary eyes, was obvious to them. The thin man, though blind, had senses far sharper than most.

 

"Hey, let me check that person over there," the sturdy man said, moving toward the blackened figure of Fire Cloud. As soon as he got a closer look, his face paled.

 

"Ahh!!" he cried out, his voice trembling with shock.

 

"Brother, what is it?" the thin man asked, turning his head sharply.

 

"Go! We need to leave now! The farther we are from here, the better!" the sturdy man shouted, his tone urgent.

 

"What's going on, brother?"

 

"That man… he's the Ultimate Killer, Fire Cloud Evil God—and he's been beaten nearly to death!"

 

Hearing that, the thin man's face turned ashen. Without another word, the two fled, abandoning the scene in fear.

 

Meanwhile, Fenric had arrived at a grand casino.

 

This wasn't just any casino—it was the largest and most opulent den of vice in all of SH City. Beyond gambling, the establishment boasted a dance hall, restaurants, and other luxurious facilities.

 

It also served as the headquarters of the Axe Gang.

 

Fenric walked through the casino's main doors. Inside, the atmosphere was lively and chaotic—well-dressed men and women moved through the bustling space, while the shouts of gamblers alternated between joy and despair.

 

To the left of the casino stood a guarded gate, manned by four Axe Gang enforcers.

 

Fenric headed straight for it without hesitation.

 

"Hey, kid, the gambling tables are over there. This place is off-limits!" one of the guards barked.

 

Fenric merely flicked his finger.

 

Bam! Bam! Bam! Bam!

 

All four guards were instantly sent flying backward, collapsing in a heap.

 

Without slowing his stride, Fenric entered the restricted area.

 

After traversing a long corridor, Fenric stepped into a spacious hall.

 

Inside, several Axe Gang members in black suits were burning incense before a massive statue of Emperor Guan.

 

(Note: Guan Yu, a real general from the late Eastern Han dynasty and Romance of the Three Kingdoms. He was famed for loyalty, righteousness, and martial prowess.)

 1

Fenric's sudden intrusion immediately drew everyone's attention.

 

"Who the hell are you!?"

 

A lackey stepped forward, shouting, "This is Axe Gang territory! If you don't want to die, get out—!"

 

Before he could finish, he let out a scream and was hurled across the hall with a single wave of Fenric's hand.

 

This brazen act inside their own headquarters was like striking a hornet's nest. 

 

Chaos erupted.

 

Suddenly, the sound of countless guns being cocked filled the air. Axe Gang members pulled out pistols, surrounding Fenric in a deadly circle.

 2

"You dare cause trouble for the Axe Gang?! You're courting death! Kill him!" a fat man with a scarred face roared.

 4

This man was the Second Master of the Axe Gang.

 

In the original storyline, he met his end after a disastrous encounter in the Pig Sty Alley, but here he was—ready to fight.

 

At his command, a barrage of gunfire erupted.

 

Bang! Bang! Bang!

 

But instead of falling, Fenric stood unmoved.

 

To everyone's horror, the bullets stopped mid-air, suspended inches from his body as if frozen by some invisible force.

 

The hall went silent.

 

People stumbled backward, terror etched on their faces.

 

"What… what the hell is this?!" someone whispered, trembling.

 

Even the Second Master's face turned pale.

 

Clink! Clink!

 

Fenric casually waved his hand, and all the bullets dropped to the ground with a crisp metallic sound.

 

Then, with another flick of his hand, every single gang member blocking his path was flung aside like ragdolls, crashing into walls and furniture, leaving a clear path for him.

 1

Clap! Clap! Clap!

 

The sound of slow applause echoed through the hall.

 

From the shadows beside the Guan Yu statue, a young man emerged. He had slick, greasy hair, a pale face, and a grin that revealed pitch-black teeth.

 

"Impressive," the man said as he approached Fenric. "Your Excellency truly has skill."

 

This was none other than Brother Sum, the ruthless leader of the Axe Gang.

 

"I don't know how we might have offended you," Brother Sum said with an uncharacteristic bow, "but on behalf of the Axe Gang, I sincerely apologize!"

 1

Sweat beaded on his forehead as he spoke, his instincts screaming that the man before him was no ordinary fighter. Even guns couldn't touch him—he was a monster!

 

"Are you the leader of the Axe Gang?" Fenric asked lightly.

 

"Yes, that's me," Brother Sum replied, bowing even lower.

 

"Good. My name is Shura," Fenric said. "I've come to join the Axe Gang. What do you say?"

 

The hall went silent. Brother Sum stared at Fenric in disbelief. A man this powerful wanted to join them?

 

Fenric smiled faintly. "Relax. I'm not here to take your position. You remain the leader. I'll be the Second Master. Any objections?"

 

"No… no objections!" Brother Sum blurted, his voice filled with relief. "All members of the Axe Gang, welcome Mr. Shura! From now on, he is the Second Master of the Axe Gang!"

 

The fat Second Master didn't dare to say a word. He knew his life depended on silence.

 

As for the Samsaras hidden among the gang members, their faces stiffened when they heard Fenric's alias.

 

Shura.

 

They lowered their heads even lower, pretending not to notice, silently praying not to draw his attention.

chapters.name: Chapter 191: Chapter 191: Shura Is Not Dead, I Can’t Sleep!
chapters.content:
"Your fame +1, current task progress: 1/10,000."

 

"Your fame +1, current task progress: 2/10,000…"

 

"Your fame +1, current task progress: 3/10,000."

 

The system's prompt tone kept ringing in Fenric's mind.

 

Just like that, Fenric had easily become the Second Master of the Axe Gang.

 

In truth, if Fenric wanted to complete his mission more efficiently and achieve a higher evaluation, the best approach would be to establish his own gang.

 

With his current power, building a dominant organization in this world would be child's play.

 

He could flatten all opposition and, in less than a month, control all of SH City.

 

That alone would likely earn him another SSS-level Super God evaluation.

 

But Fenric's motives this time weren't about mission rewards.

 

If rewards were his goal, he would have already gone to the second dungeon to "farm" the ghostly Sadako.

 2

He understood her story, the reason behind her grudge, and how to resolve it. Maximizing Sadako's "favorability" for rewards wouldn't be difficult for him at all.

 

No—this time, his priority wasn't the mission's evaluation.

 

It was something else.

 

Now that Fenric was officially the Second Master of the Axe Gang, his first order of business was straightforward:

 

He had a portrait made—a rough sketch of a man who looked like a beggar. Then, he hired numerous painters to copy it by hand, since photocopiers didn't exist in this era.

 

Once hundreds of copies were ready, he instructed every member of the Axe Gang to search the city for the beggar depicted in the portrait.

 

To ensure success, he issued a generous bounty:

 

10,000 Jade Coins for anyone who found the beggar!

 

(Note: equivalent to $5-6k at that time. Or $100k of today's money.)

 

And where did the money come from?

 

Please—he was Shura, after all. Ten thousand Jade Coins was nothing for him.

 

That night…

 

In a dimly lit room of the Axe Gang headquarters:

 

"Brother Sum, look! This is the man the Second Master is looking for," a subordinate said, holding up one of the portraits.

 

Brother Sum took the sketch, frowned, and muttered, "A beggar?"

 

"Brother Sum really has sharp eyes! I also think he looks like a beggar," the subordinate said with a sycophantic smile.

 

The man in the portrait was filthy, his face smudged with dirt—only a fool wouldn't recognize him as a beggar.

 

"Why is he looking for a beggar?" Brother Sum wondered aloud.

 

"Maybe he's a lost relative?" the subordinate offered, uncertain.

 

Brother Sum thought about it and found that possibility believable.

 

Otherwise, why would Shura use the entire Axe Gang to hunt for someone right after becoming the Second Master?

 

In fact, Sum began to suspect that Shura's real reason for joining the gang was to find this mysterious beggar.

 

The Axe Gang controlled most of SH City. It had eyes and ears everywhere, which made it the perfect network for a search like this.

 

"I asked you to check into the Second Master's background. What did you find?" Brother Sum asked, his tone serious.

 

"We've sent people to investigate," the subordinate replied, "but we found nothing. It's like he came from another world."

 

Brother Sum's brow furrowed.

 

"Then investigate those captains who joined recently as well," he said coldly.

 

Those "captains" were none other than the Samsaras who had infiltrated the gang.

 

"Understood, Brother Sum. I've already sent someone to look into it," the subordinate said quickly.

 

Brother Sum nodded, then asked, "Any news on the assassins I asked you to find?"

 

"Yes!" The subordinate's eyes lit up. "I've heard there's a ranking list of killers in the martial world. Everyone on that list is a true master. The first on the list is the Ultimate Killer, Fire Cloud Evil God. We don't know where he is yet, but we're already sending people to track him down."

 

"Good!" Brother Sum's expression turned sinister. "Hire as many top killers as possible. Tell them this: Whoever can kill the Second Master will be rewarded beyond measure!"

 1

Fenric's overwhelming display of power that day had terrified Brother Sum to his core.

 

As long as Shura lived, Sum knew he wouldn't get a good night's sleep!

 

"Don't worry, Brother Sum," the subordinate said, bowing slightly. "I'll make all the arrangements. We'll definitely find some masters."

 

"And don't let the Second Master find out about this," Brother Sum warned, his eyes narrowing. "He must not suspect it's us pulling the strings."

 

"Understood!"

 

Finally, Sum leaned back on the sofa, exhaling. "What about the Third Master?"

 

The Third Master was none other than the former Second Master—the fat man who had lost his position after Fenric's arrival.

 

Knowing what Sum was really asking—whether the fat man was harboring resentment—the subordinate smiled and replied, "The Third Master is doing well. He's been busy reclaiming turf all day long."

 

Brother Sum nodded, satisfied. "Good. And remember, I want all of SH City under our control. Not one street should remain outside our influence!"

 

"Understood, Brother Sum!"

 

Ten days passed in a flash.

 

During this time, Fenric had almost mobilized the entire Axe Gang to scour SH City, but they still hadn't found the mysterious beggar.

 

Every day, Fenric inspected dozens of beggars, but none of them matched the person in the portrait.

 

Some opportunists even tried to cheat, disguising themselves as the beggar to claim the bounty.

 

Those who attempted such scams didn't live to regret it—Fenric snapped their necks without hesitation, using his mind power to kill them on the spot.

 

After a few such incidents, no one dared to try tricking him again.

 

Still, Fenric was frustrated. The deadline for his mission was just 20 days away.

 

He didn't want to waste more time searching aimlessly, so he prepared to move to Plan B:

 

Find Sing!

 

Just as he was about to issue orders to locate Sing, a gang member rushed in, panting.

 

"Second Master!"

 

"What is it?" Fenric asked.

 

"Someone claims they've seen the beggar you're looking for!"

 

"Oh?" Fenric raised a brow, though his tone remained calm. "Where?"

 

Lately, he had heard similar claims too often to get his hopes up. Most of them were false leads.

 

"They say they saw him in a beggar's den in the north of the city," the man reported.

 

"Who saw him?" Fenric asked.

 

"It was an old woman. We brought her here—she's waiting outside."

 

Fenric nodded. "Bring her in and have her lead the way. I'll go check for myself."

 

No matter how many false alarms there had been, he wouldn't miss a chance to confirm it.

 

What if this time, it really was the beggar he was looking for?

 

—--

chapters.name: Chapter 192: Chapter 192: That’s It? Want to Assassinate Shura’s Boss?
chapters.content:
Outside.

 

Fenric saw the old woman waiting.

 

"Hmm?"

 

The moment his eyes landed on her, he felt something was off.

 

The woman looked honest enough, but sweat beaded her forehead. Most people sweat like that when they're sick—or when they're nervous.

 

Her callused hands and sturdy arms spoke of someone used to farm work. She wasn't that old, her complexion was healthy, and she didn't look ill at all.

 

Which meant her sweating had only one explanation: she was nervous.

 

Fenric's lips curved into a faint smile. There was clearly a trap waiting for him.

 

But instead of getting angry, curiosity sparked in his eyes.

 

What kind of trap? Who's behind it this time?

 

With that thought, Fenric's expression remained calm.

 

"Let's go," he said simply.

 

At the doorway.

 

Three Western cars were already waiting.

 

Fenric approached the middle car, and one of the gang brothers immediately opened the door for him.

 

Seven or eight more brothers boarded the cars in front and behind.

 

As the Second Master of the Axe Gang, he couldn't travel like some commoner. A man of his position needed an entourage—otherwise, where was the dignity?

 

The old woman sat in the car ahead, leading the way.

 

Vroom!

 

The engines roared, and the cars rolled down the road.

 

Cars of this era were primitive—just engines, wheels, and a steering wheel. The ride was rough and bumpy.

 

If I weren't so physically resilient, this would be unbearable, Fenric thought.

 

Half an hour later.

 

The convoy entered the northern part of SH City.

 

Inside a five-story building nearby, by the window, Brother Sum and Shiye sat sipping tea.

 

The weather was bright and clear. Sunlight poured through the windows, warm and pleasant.

 

But neither man could enjoy it. Both were restless, their glances repeatedly flicking toward the street below as if waiting for something.

 

"He's coming!" Shiye suddenly exclaimed, excitement flashing in his eyes.

 

Brother Sum immediately shoved him aside and took the best spot by the window.

 

He wanted to see Shura's death with his own eyes.

 

Brother Sum was known for his vengeful nature.

 

After suffering humiliation in Pig Sty Alley, he hadn't given up—he had even sought the Fire Cloud.

 

Ever since Fenric joined the Axe Gang and stole the spotlight, Sum's resentment had only grown. Over the past ten days, Fenric hadn't shown him an ounce of respect. Sum's hatred for him had become deep and personal.

 

Through the window, he could see three Western cars slowly approaching.

 

Brother Sum's lips twisted into a cruel smile.

 

The good show was about to start.

 

BOOM—!

 

A sudden explosion ripped through the street as the cars crossed a certain spot.

 

The blast was deafening, echoing through the surrounding blocks.

 

The middle car—Fenric's car—was blown high into the air.

 

The two cars in front and behind were caught in the shockwave and flipped violently.

 

"Good!" Brother Sum shouted in excitement.

 

Shiye, grinning ear to ear, added, "He's dead for sure now!"

 

They had laid a trap of buried explosives to deal with Fenric—and they had another backup plan in case he survived.

 

But their celebration didn't last long.

 

As the smoke cleared, Fenric stepped out of the wreckage, dusting himself off. Except for some torn fabric on his suit, he was completely unscathed.

 

The smiles on Brother Sum's and Shiye's faces froze.

 

"This… this…!" Shiye stammered, unable to believe his eyes.

 

How can anyone survive that explosion!?

 

The man standing in the middle of the street didn't look human at all—he looked like a monster!

 

On the street.

 

Fenric rolled his shoulders, glancing around calmly.

 

The ambush had been sudden, but the explosives used were too weak compared to modern military-grade weapons.

 

Even without using Armament Haki, his current physique alone was enough to shrug off the attack.

 

The nearby pedestrians had already fled in terror.

 

Only a few unfortunate souls caught in the blast lay on the ground, groaning in pain.

 

As for the driver who had shared Fenric's car—he hadn't survived.

 

Suddenly, a strange sound floated through the air.

 

It was the sound of a pipa, a traditional stringed instrument.

 

Fenric turned his head and spotted two men sitting calmly on the roadside, playing together.

 

The two men were identical in style—one tall and thin, the other short and stocky. Both wore the same gray robes, round caps, and dark sunglasses that hid their faces.

 

The moment Fenric saw them, he smiled.

 

I know this part of the story…

 

He instantly recognized them as the Harpist—the same deadly duo from the plot of Kung Fu Hustle.

 

Which meant only one thing:

 

Brother Sum had hired them to take him out.

 

Fenric strode confidently toward the duo.

 

Sensing his approach, the two assassins changed their tune—the slow, eerie music suddenly became fast and aggressive.

 

WHUMMM—!

 

The pipa's sound transformed into invisible sound waves, rippling through the air like blades.

 

A strange phenomenon occurred—those waves condensed into transparent sonic blades, slicing toward Fenric.

 

Fenric raised an eyebrow, impressed.

 

Interesting technique… not bad.

 

If the attacks were a little stronger, he might even consider learning it.

 

But instead, he quietly summoned his mind power.

 

Whoosh!

 

It was like a sudden gust of wind, instantly shattering the sonic blades.

 

In truth, Fenric didn't even need to block. Even the Fire Cloud hadn't been able to break through his Armament Haki—how could these two assassins, who had once been beaten by a simple landlady?

 

The only reason Fenric bothered to deflect the attacks was to protect his clothes.

 1

After all, this was a public street—what a shame it would be to walk around with shredded clothes.

 

The wind generated by his Telekinesis power didn't stop after shattering the sonic blades—it surged forward toward the duo.

 

Their expressions changed instantly.

 

They slammed their hands on the pipa strings, producing a powerful counter-wave of sound.

 

WHUM! WHUM!

 

The two sound waves clashed like colliding forces, and for a moment, the assassins managed to hold off Fenric's attack.

 

Then, they struck the strings in perfect unison, producing a sharp, resonant note.

 

WHUMMM—!

 

A harsh, almost metallic sound filled the street.

 

The sound waves coalesced into a terrifying ghostly warrior—an armored phantom wielding a giant blade—charging straight at Fenric.

chapters.name: Chapter 193: Chapter 193: You’re Forcing Me to Usurp the Throne!
chapters.content:
The sonic ghost generals surging from the assassins' instrument were vicious, their spectral blades cutting through the air with a menacing hum.

 

Fenric didn't even flinch.

 

After all, I've read the original story. These two may look impressive, but in reality, their sonic attacks are nothing but flashy tricks.

 

For ordinary people, these sound waves would be deadly. But to Fenric, they were nothing.

 

With a calm expression, he raised his hand, slightly increasing the output of his mental energy.

 

The fierce sonic ghost generals shattered instantly, torn apart as if they were fragile smoke.

 

The sheer force of the psychic shockwave nearly drove the two assassins to their knees.

 

"What… what kind of power is this!?" one of them gasped.

 

"This isn't… sonic power. It's something else entirely!"

 

Fenric's cold snort silenced them.

 

"Even the Fire Cloud almost died in my hands. And you two dare to try and assassinate me?"

 

"!!!"

 

Hearing that name, both assassins—Heavenly Defect and Earthly Cripple—turned pale as death. Their fingers froze on the strings.

 1

"Spare us! Spare us, Master Shura! Spare our lives!" they begged in unison, terror-stricken.

 

Fenric's tone was flat. "Where is the leader of the Axe Gang?"

 

"Just… just behind you! In that building!" Heavenly Defect blurted out without hesitation.

 

For assassins, loyalty was meaningless when their own lives were on the line. They sold out their employer without a second thought.

 

Fenric turned his gaze to the building across the street.

 

His sharp eyes easily spotted two familiar heads peeking out from a fourth-floor window—Brother Sum and Shiye, secretly watching.

 

A faint smile curved Fenric's lips. He raised his hand and waved casually toward the window, as if greeting them.

 

Then, without sparing another glance at the assassins, he strode toward the building.

 

Behind him, the two assassins suddenly convulsed, their necks twisting unnaturally before they collapsed lifelessly on the ground.

 

In the original plot, the landlady and landlord had spared these assassins after defeating them.

 

But Fenric wasn't that merciful.

 

If you dare to try killing me, be prepared to die.

 

Besides, these two had probably murdered countless people. To Fenric, their deaths weren't unjust.

 

Inside the building, on the fourth floor.

 

Brother Sum and Shiye's smug expressions turned to horror the moment Fenric waved at them.

 

"We're done for! He saw us! Brother Sum, let's run!" Shiye panicked and rushed toward the door.

 

CRASH!

 

The sound of glass shattering behind him froze him in his tracks.

 1

"B… Brother Sum?" he stammered, turning back.

 

The rest of his words stuck in his throat.

 

There was already someone new in the room.

 

Fenric sat casually on a chair beside Brother Sum, one hand resting firmly on the gang leader's shoulder.

 3

Shiye knew Sum's temper well. Brother Sum hated anyone touching his shoulders—whoever dared usually ended up with an axe buried in their skull.

 

But right now, Brother Sum didn't even twitch. His entire body was trembling, sweat pouring down his face.

 

A cool breeze blew through the shattered window. Shiye's back went cold, though he couldn't tell if it was from the wind or pure fear.

 

Broken glass littered the floor, evidence that Fenric had simply jumped in through the fourth-floor window.

 

The atmosphere in the room was suffocating.

 

"Shiye, why are you just standing there? Come sit," Fenric said at last, his calm voice cutting through the tension.

 

"Y-Yes! Right away!"

 

Shiye scrambled to the table, forcing a flattering smile as he sat down, barely daring to breathe. His posture was as stiff as a servant waiting for punishment.

 

Fenric poured tea into three cups. "You know, since I became the Second Master of the Axe Gang, the three of us have never sat down for tea together."

 

Brother Sum forced a dry laugh but said nothing. Luckily, Shiye's quick wit saved the moment.

 

"If Second Master wants tea, we'll have tea every day! It would be our honor," he said hastily.

 

Fenric smiled faintly.

 

"I have the time. But I'm afraid Brother Sum won't have any."

 

Sum's face turned ashen. Shiye immediately dropped his gaze, not daring to speak another word.

 

Brother Sum was no fool—he understood exactly what Fenric meant. He was holding a gun at his side, but he didn't even have the courage to draw it.

 

Even explosives couldn't hurt this monster. What good would a gun do?

 

"Brother Sum," Fenric began, his voice calm but razor-sharp, "I told you before—I'm not interested in your position. So why arrange this little assassination game today? Do I have to die for you to sleep peacefully?"

 

Sum's mind screamed: Yes! If you're alive, I'll never sleep well!

 

But the words died in his throat.

 

Fenric's tone turned cold.

 

"Did you really think you could force my hand like this?"

 

Fenric turned to Shiye.

 

"From now on, I'm the leader of the Axe Gang. You're the Second Master. You'll handle the day-to-day matters—but no one disobeys my orders. Understand?"

 

Shiye hesitated only for a moment, glancing at the terrified Sum. Gritting his teeth, he bowed deeply.

 

"Understood, Leader! I will follow you without question from now on!"

 

"Good. The wise know when to bend."

 

Fenric smiled and placed his hand gently on Brother Sum's forehead.

 

"Wait, no—" Sum's plea was cut short.

 

A sharp crack echoed as Sum collapsed to the floor, blood seeping from a neat hole in his forehead.

 

Fenric stood, his voice calm as he addressed Shiye.

 

"Clean this up, Shiye. As long as you remain obedient, I'll let the past go. But if this happens again… you can have tea with Brother Sum again."

 

With that, Fenric turned and left the room, leaving Shiye trembling in fear.

 

The Axe Gang had a new leader.

 

The news spread like wildfire across SH City.

 

Rumors circulated that the new leader, once the Second Master, seized power by killing the infamous Brother Sum with his own hands.

 

Brother Sum's name had long been feared throughout SH City—even children knew of his cruelty.

 

But now, that cruel man was dead. And the man who killed him was known as Shura.

 

System Notification:

 

"Your fame +1, current task progress: 22,3175 / 10,000."

chapters.name: Chapter 194: Chapter 194: Pig Sty Alley, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon?
chapters.content:
After Fenric's decisive rise to power, his reputation soared like wildfire.

 

Now that he was the leader of the Axe Gang, not even the Samsara Players dared to utter a word against him.

 

Soon after, Fenric issued a new order:

 

"Find Sing! Everyone, keep your eyes open and report any leads!"

 

With that command, he returned to his usual hands-off style.

 

Fenric only had one month in this world—why would he waste time fighting for control over territory?

 

He left all administrative matters to the Second Master and the Third Master.

 

The Second Master handled internal affairs and finances, while the Third Master oversaw territory management.

 

On the surface, the Third Master was still "Third," but in reality, his influence had grown immensely.

 

He, too, welcomed the fall of Brother Sum.

 

That morning.

 

Fenric was quietly eating breakfast when a subordinate rushed in.

 

"Leader, there's a powerful old man outside. He says he's an old friend of yours and wants to see you."

 

"Oh?" Fenric raised an eyebrow, a knowing smile tugging at his lips. "Let him in."

 

He already had a good guess who it was.

 

A few moments later, a shabby old man wearing flip-flops was escorted in. His appearance was disheveled, but his presence was unmistakable.

 

Fenric didn't rise from his seat. Instead, he smiled faintly.

 

"So, the Fire Cloud pays me a visit. That's a long journey, senior."

 

The surrounding gang members looked confused.

 

None of them had heard the name "Fire Cloud" before, let alone knew who this bald, frail-looking man was.

 

"Shura," the old man said the moment he saw Fenric, "I came to ask you: Are you a man… or a god?"

 

The last time they had crossed paths, Fenric's final strike had left a deep impression on him—so deep that even after days of recovery, the memory still haunted him.

 

After more than ten days of recuperation, Fire Cloud's wounds had healed. His skin looked fresh, as if he had shed an old layer.

 

But his hair? Completely gone. He was now entirely bald.

 

"Senior, have some breakfast with me," Fenric offered.

 

The old man didn't refuse and sat down, but his sharp gaze never left Fenric.

 

"You still haven't answered me," he pressed.

 

"Of course, I'm human," Fenric replied calmly.

 

The Fire Cloud narrowed his eyes. "Then what was that ability you used? How did you summon lightning from the heavens? No man should be able to control thunder like that."

 

"Oh, that?" Fenric smiled lightly. "Just one of my magic weapons."

 

"Magic weapon?" The old man's eyes glimmered. "A weapon of the immortals?"

 

"Something like that," Fenric said after a short pause.

 

"Think of God of Thunder's hammer—it can summon lightning. It wouldn't be wrong to call it an immortal's weapon."

 

The Fire Cloud's pupils contracted. "Then… are there really immortals in this world?"

 

"I don't know about immortals," Fenric said with a smirk. "But martial arts… martial arts can be limitless. There are techniques in this world that rival the powers of gods and spirits. Senior, if you've got time, why not stay with me for a while? I'll show you something even greater. I'll show you… a miracle."

 

"A miracle?" The old man's curiosity was piqued. After a moment's thought, he nodded.

 

"Very well."

 

He had come today hoping to learn Fenric's secret techniques, and if possible, surpass him. Once he learned, he intended to defeat Fenric and reclaim his invincible status.

 

But Fenric's words intrigued him. If someone this powerful called it a "miracle," it had to be worth witnessing.

 

At that moment, a young gang member pointed toward the sky.

 

"Leader, look! A cloud-piercing arrow!"

 

Fenric looked up. In the distant sky, a brilliant firework burst apart, forming the shape of an axe. It was the Axe Gang's emergency distress signal.

 

A cloud-piercing arrow—when one is fired, the entire gang must respond.

 

No one fired this signal unless they were in extreme danger.

 

Once launched, every member who saw it had to rush to the scene.

 

This was the gang's iron rule, set in stone since the day it was founded.

 

Even as the new leader, Fenric couldn't simply ignore it.

 

Besides, if he gained a reputation for abandoning his men, no one would respect him.

 

"Get ready to move!" Fenric ordered.

 

The subordinates scattered, rushing to prepare.

 

Fenric stood, glanced at the Fire Cloud, and asked,

 

"Senior, would you care to join me?"

 

"Not interested," the old man said with a dismissive wave.

 

As a martial arts fanatic, he cared only for reaching new heights of skill, not for petty disputes or gang matters.

 

"Then please, enjoy your meal."

 

With that, Fenric left.

 

One hour later.

 

The convoy of cars rolled into a remote, poverty-stricken area.

 

From the outside, the place looked like an old apartment complex, but the plaque over the gate read, in bold characters: "Pig Sty."

 

"So, it's here," Fenric muttered with a smile.

 

When the car stopped, a subordinate opened the door for him.

 

Fenric stepped out, followed by a crowd of Axe Gang members.

 

Inside the compound, nearly 570 gang members were already gathered.

 

The moment they saw Fenric, they bowed in unison.

 

"Leader!!"

 

The roar of voices shook the air.

 

The local villagers, terrified, peeked from behind doors and windows but didn't dare step outside.

 

Fenric swept his gaze across the crowd. Among them, he easily spotted several Samsara Players hiding in plain sight.

 

As long as they don't interfere with me, they can stay.

 

"Leader!" The Second Master approached, his face filled with feigned sorrow.

 

"The Third Master… he's dying."

 

"Take me to him," Fenric said coldly.

 

The Second Master led him to a large iron tub.

 

Inside, the once-proud Third Master—now a broken, overweight man—was crumpled like a discarded rag. His spine was clearly snapped, and foam bubbled at his lips. He was down to his final breaths.

 

Fenric sighed inwardly.

 

The inertia of fate is truly strong. Even after all the changes I made to the Axe Gang, the Third Master still ended up here… just like the original story.

 

"Who did this?" Fenric asked quietly.

 

At his words, the Axe Gang members tensed.

 

In an instant, hundreds of them moved, surrounding the entire Pig Sty Alley. Not even a fly would escape.

chapters.name: Chapter 195: Chapter 195: Inexplicably, I Became the Villain!
chapters.content:
"Hurry Up! Say Who Did It?!"

 

The Axe Gang members, their axes glinting coldly in the sunlight, barked harsh questions at the trembling villagers.

 

Fenric stood nearby, watching the scene unfold, and sighed inwardly.

 

Why do I feel like I'm drifting further and further down the path of a villain?

 1

Just then, a timid voice called out from the side, catching his attention.

 

"B-Brother, we're on your side!"

 

Turning his head, Fenric saw a scrawny young man with messy hair and a pleading expression. Beside him stood a round-faced, honest-looking fat man. Both of them sported crude tattoos of axes, pretending to be Axe Gang members.

 

Before his men could beat the two impostors to a pulp, Fenric spoke calmly.

 

"Wait. Bring those two over."

 

At his order, a few gang members dragged the scrawny man and his companion in front of him.

 

"Brother! Are you the leader? My admiration for you is like a surging river—"

 

"Enough." Fenric waved a hand, cutting off Sing's flattery.

 

"What's your name?"

 

"Brother, just call me Sing!" the man said immediately.

 

Fenric's gaze swept over them. "You two have axe tattoos. Do you want to join the Axe Gang?"

 

"Yeah! Boss, that's been our dream!" Sing said with forced bravado, while the fat man nodded furiously.

 

Fenric smirked. "Good. I'll give you a chance."

 

He beckoned, and one of the underlings handed him an axe. Fenric placed it in Sing's hands.

 

"Go prove yourself. Find out who hurt my brothers."

 

Sing stared at the axe, frozen for a moment, before gritting his teeth and walking toward a middle-aged woman.

 

"Who attacked our Axe Gang brother?!" Sing shouted, trying to sound fierce. "I'll count to three! If the culprit doesn't step out, I'll chop her down!!"

 

His voice trembled despite his attempt to appear intimidating.

 

Silence. No one stepped forward.

 

"Three…!" Sing yelled, his face twitching in panic.

 

Still, no one answered.

 

Sing's hand shook as he looked at the terrified woman crouched on the ground, crying softly. His grip on the axe faltered. He simply couldn't bring himself to strike her.

 

"Who is it?!" The Second Master barked from the side. "Don't just stand there and embarrass the Axe Gang!"

 

Fenric watched the scene calmly, curious to see what Sing would do.

 

In the original story, Sing had wanted to join the Axe Gang, dreaming of becoming a feared figure, but deep down he was a kind-hearted man who eventually chose the right path—even striking down the Fire Cloud when it mattered.

 

Urged by the Second Master, Sing squeezed his eyes shut, bracing himself, and raised the axe high—

 

But before he could strike, a voice cut through the tension.

 

"Let her go. I did it!!"

 

Everyone turned to see a towering, broad-shouldered man step forward. His muscles rippled beneath a rough linen shirt, and his stance radiated strength.

 1

A martial artist!

 

Sing exhaled in relief, lowering the axe. Only now did he realize how difficult it was to take a life. Without a truly ruthless heart, one couldn't kill.

 

"Hack him!!" The Second Master shouted.

 

At once, more than a dozen Axe Gang members charged, axes raised high.

 

BOOM—! BOOM—! BOOM—!

 

The brawny man's legs lashed out like whips. He was a master of the [Twelve Kicks of Tam School], and in moments, the attacking gang members were kicked flying, groaning in pain on the ground.

 

Not far away, several Samsara Players huddled together, whispering.

 

"Damn, isn't that guy a master of Twelve Kicks?"

 

"Yeah, he's insane! Look at those kicks!"

 

"He's nothing compared to the Landlord and Landlady. When they step in, it's over."

 

"True… but with Shura here, we've got this in the bag. No need to panic."

 

Within moments, every Axe Gang member who had charged was lying on the ground, moaning in pain.

 

The brawny man stood firm, not a single scratch on him.

 

Just as a few more men prepared to rush in, Fenric's calm voice cut through the chaos.

 

"Stop."

 

Everyone froze, unsure why their leader had intervened.

 

Fenric turned his gaze toward the Samsara Players and spoke coolly.

 

"You lot. What are you waiting for? Isn't this the perfect target for your mission? He's not that strong. I'm leaving him to you."

 

The Samsara Players exchanged looks. Not strong? In Fenric's eyes, maybe, but to them, this man was already a monster.

 

Still, Shura was right. They didn't have much time left for their mission. If they wanted to earn merit and fame, this was their chance.

 

"Leave it to me!"

 

A small but wiry Samsara stepped forward. He moved to stand confidently before the brawny man.

 

"Twelve Kicks Expert, huh? My name is Black Hawk. Remember it. If I kill you, at least you'll know the name of the one who sent you to hell."

 

The brawny man's expression hardened.

 

He knows my technique? This guy is no ordinary thug.

 

Fenric leaned back slightly, as though watching a show.

 

To be honest, even if it was the Landlord or Landlady standing there, Fenric wouldn't bother lifting a hand.

 

This was the perfect chance to let the Samsara Players earn their keep.

 

"Quick fight," Fenric ordered casually.

 

At that signal, Black Hawk lunged.

 

His hands curved into claw-like shapes, his movements fluid and deadly. He sidestepped a powerful kick, closing in with a swipe toward the man's face.

 

Eagle Claw Technique!

 

The brawny man raised an arm to block, but Black Hawk's claws raked across it, leaving three deep gashes.

 

Shocked and angered, the man no longer held back, unleashing his full strength against his opponent.

 

The two clashed fiercely, exchanging blows and counters. Their movements blurred, drawing gasps of awe from the Axe Gang members watching.

 

In the end, Black Hawk's speed gave him the edge.

 

He feinted low, then struck high, clawing at the man's face—blinding one of his eyes.

 

"AAHHH!!" The brawny man roared in pain.

 

Black Hawk raised his claws again, ready to deliver the finishing blow—

 

SWOOSH!

 

A stick flew from a nearby shop, cutting through the air with a sharp crack!

 

Black Hawk's instincts screamed danger. He instantly abandoned his attack and leapt backward.

 

If that stick had struck him, he would've been seriously injured—or worse.

chapters.name: Chapter 196: Chapter 196: Rubber Fruit Ability!
chapters.content:
Whoosh!

 

The Black Hawk dodged the flying stick, but the weapon didn't stop—it continued spinning through the air and struck Sing squarely on the shoulder.

 

Puff!

 

Sing was sent flying, landing right at Fenric's feet, coughing up blood.

 

"Sing! Sing!"

 

The fat companion rushed over in panic, shaking Sing's shoulders. This only made Sing cough up more blood before finally passing out.

 

A pig teammate indeed.

 

Fenric looked at Sing's pitiful state with a blank expression, showing no intention of helping.

 

He knew the plot well and understood just how abnormal Sing's talent truly was.

 

This guy was like an indestructible cockroach—each time he was seriously injured, he'd recover stronger than before. As the landlady once said, Sing was a peerless genius!

 

So, Fenric wasn't worried in the slightest about his survival.

 

The next moment, the breakfast shop owner—also known as the early morning boss—stormed out of the house, wielding his trusty staff, and stepped protectively in front of Coolie.

 

The famed Bagua Stick had arrived!

 

Fenric's eyes swept over the remaining Samsara Players, his voice calm but sharp.

 

"What are you all waiting for? Move."

 

The Samsaras exchanged awkward glances, but they knew better than to defy him. Fenric was the Axe Gang leader now—if they didn't obey, he could crush them without hesitation.

 

This particular "Kung Fu Hustle" copy was already the Seventh Stage of the Samsara Tower.

 

By the time a Samsara reached this level, they usually had enough strength to secure a C-rank evaluation.

 

But for Fenric, C-rank Samsaras were nothing more than rookies.

 

For ordinary people, however, such Samsaras were terrifying monsters.

 

In fact, each one of these Samsara Players might not be any weaker than Coolie himself.

 

"This guy—leave him to me!"

 

A tall, wiry man stepped forward, cracking his knuckles. He walked toward the breakfast shop owner, smirking.

 

"Hey! Listen carefully! The one who will take your life today is named Luppy!"

 

The breakfast shop owner's expression darkened. Without another word, he swung his staff in a powerful horizontal arc toward Luppy.

 

Whack!

 

The staff struck Luppy's leg directly.

 

But then—

 

Something bizarre happened.

 

Luppy's leg didn't break. Instead, it bent unnaturally, twisting like rubber, absorbing the impact completely.

 

It was as if the staff had struck into a muddy swamp rather than a human limb.

 

Luppy grinned, unfazed.

 

The breakfast shop owner's face paled.

 

What the hell…?

 

This was the first time he had encountered something so unnatural.

 

"Let's try this again!"

 

The shop owner swung at Luppy's neck with even greater force.

 

Whack!

 

The staff bent around his rubbery neck, but Luppy's smile remained.

 

Fenric raised an eyebrow, mildly impressed.

 

"So… this guy has the abilities of the Rubber Fruit?"

 1

The resemblance was uncanny.

 

However, Fenric could tell this man's mastery was still in its early stage. His strength was far from impressive—yet the potential was undeniable.

 

After all, the protagonist of One Piece, Monkey D. Luffy, had developed the Rubber Fruit's power to its fourth gear before Fenric crossed over.

 7

If Luppy could grow like Luffy, his future strength could be monstrous.

 

'Damn, even his name. This guy is definitely an Otaku.'

 

Everyone knew the greatest weakness of the Rubber Fruit: sharp weapons like swords.

 

Blunt weapons, such as a wooden staff, could barely harm him.

 

No wonder Luppy dared to challenge the breakfast shop owner—his abilities countered him perfectly.

 

Unless the shop owner's staff had a spearhead, he was practically powerless.

 

After enduring several strikes, Luppy finally seized an opening. His fist shot forward, stretching unnaturally, and slammed directly into the shop owner's abdomen.

 

Wham! Wham! Wham!

 

The force of the blow was immense. The breakfast shop owner staggered backward, his face turning pale from the impact.

 

It wasn't just pain that gripped him—it was fear.

 

The man in front of him didn't feel human. He felt like a monster.

 

The surrounding crowd was equally stunned.

 

Except for Fenric and a few Samsaras, everyone else was frozen in disbelief.

 

Luppy pressed the advantage, chasing after the breakfast shop owner relentlessly.

 

With his rubber body, he completely countered the Bagua Stick techniques. Within moments, the shop owner was on the defensive, being driven back blow after blow.

 

Just as the situation became dire—

 

Clang!

 

A metallic sound rang our.

 

The tailor from the tailor's shop stepped forward, his shirt now removed, revealing arms wrapped in iron rings.

 

Iron Wire Fist!

 

The old tailor's strikes were like steel, and instead of attacking head-on, he grabbed Luppy's extended arms, twisting and entangling them with sheer strength.

 

In mere moments, Luppy was bound and twisted into a tight knot, unable to break free.

 

Now, all three masters—

 

Iron Wire Fist, Bagua Stick, and Twelve Kicks of Tam School—stood united, facing Fenric's forces.

 

"You three, go together!" Fenric ordered coldly, glancing at the Samsara Players.

 

The Samsaras hesitated for a moment, but under Fenric's sharp gaze, they immediately charged.

 

There were eight of them, all at least C-rank in strength. Against three injured masters, the outcome was clear.

 1

Puff! Puff!

 

Within minutes, the three Pig Sty Alley masters were coughing blood, barely able to stand.

 

Fenric's eyes flickered toward the Landlord and Landlady, who were still pretending to be weak among the crowd. A faint smile curved his lips.

 

"Finish them off," he ordered flatly.

 

Fenric wasn't being cruel for cruelty's sake.

 

As the leader of the Axe Gang, he couldn't appear weak.

 

With the Third Master already dead, he needed to show overwhelming authority.

 

The three masters' deaths would serve as an example.

 

At Fenric's command, the Samsaras moved in, weapons raised.

 

The three masters exchanged desperate looks, knowing the end had come.

 

But then—

 

A woman in pajamas, cigarette dangling from her lips, appeared out of nowhere and stepped between them and the Samsaras.

 

She inhaled deeply, then unleashed a deafening roar—

 

"AHHHH!!!"

 

A sonic shockwave exploded outward.

 

Lion's Roar!
