chapters.name: Chapter 197: Chapter 197: Hanging on the Condor Heroes!
chapters.content:
The woman who suddenly appeared was none other than the landlady!

 

The moment she showed up, several Samsaras turned pale and screamed in fright.

 

"Help Shura, help us!!"

 

Before entering this dungeon, they had studied various strategies and information about the Pig Sty Alley masters. Some even memorized the portraits of the landlord and landlady that circulated online.

 

The landlady's appearance was so unique and iconic that there was no mistaking her.

 

"AHHH!!!"

 

A thunderous Lion's Roar!

 

The powerful sonic waves swept across the area like a storm, shaking the ground and blowing the Samsaras back as if a tornado had struck.

 

The landlady's Lion's Roar was far more terrifying than the two assassins zither technique he'd seen before.

 

If she had a megaphone, even Fire Cloud wouldn't be able to endure it!

 

Naturally, the Samsaras stood no chance.

 

Fenric moved instantly.

 

In a single step, he blinked forward, positioning himself in front of the Samsaras. At the same time, he unleashed his Telekinesis to shield them.

 

These Samsaras were fighting under his orders—he wouldn't let them get obliterated here.

 

"Hm?"

 

The next moment, Fenric was mildly surprised.

 

His mental energy, which could shatter heavy objects with ease, wasn't enough to fully block the landlady's sonic roar. He had to push harder, pouring out his strength to barely suppress the incoming shockwave.

 

"Lion's Roar, huh? Not bad… not bad at all," Fenric murmured in admiration.

 

His mental attributes had already exceeded 500 points. For her sonic technique to rival his mental force meant this woman's power was far from ordinary.

 

"Thank you, Boss Shura!"

 

"Thank you for saving us!"

 

The Samsaras, hiding behind him, expressed their gratitude.

 

Fenric waved a hand without turning. "Fall back."

 

A master of the landlady's caliber was far beyond what these Samsaras could handle.

 

The group obediently retreated, relief flooding their faces.

 

"Who are you?"

 

The landlady's sharp gaze fell on Fenric, astonished that someone could block her Lion's Roar head-on.

 

"Me?" Fenric smiled. "I'm the leader of the Axe Gang."

 

"..."

 

The landlady's expression turned serious, losing her usual shrewish tone.

 

"When did a master like you appear in the martial world? I've never heard of you!"

 

"It doesn't matter if you haven't heard of me," Fenric replied with a faint smile. "What matters is that you don't meddle in things you shouldn't."

 

Then, casually, he added, "Landlady, hand over those three behind you. I'll give you some face—and maybe lower the rent here in the future."

 

The landlady lit a cigarette, blowing out a lazy puff of smoke.

 

"And if I refuse?"

 

"Then I'll have to take them myself," Fenric said lightly. "My fists are heavy—try not to get beaten to death. And as for you, landlord, how much longer are you going to pretend to be dead? Do you really think your wife can handle me alone?"

 

His last remark was directed toward the landlord, who was still pretending to be unconscious on the ground.

 

"Ugh…"

 

The landlord sighed and slowly got up, walking over to stand beside his wife.

 

"Why must you always stir trouble?" he muttered. "You've provoked a monster this time. How are we supposed to live after this?"

 

"They're our neighbors—should I just let them die?" the landlady snapped back.

 

"Forget it… after today, let's move," the landlord muttered bitterly.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed slightly.

 

"You two should focus on surviving me first."

 

Before they could react, Fenric struck.

 

His right hand clenched into a fist as he stood his ground, gathering power. At the same time, his mental energy surged forward, pulling the landlord toward him like an invisible hand.

 

"!!"

 

The landlord's expression changed instantly. Realizing Fenric wasn't to be underestimated, he used his ultimate technique on the spot—

 

Tai Chi!

 

Whoosh!

 

Fenric's fist cut through the air like a cannonball.

 

Before it could land, the landlord's left hand gently diverted the force with a subtle pull and twist—

 

Tai Chi—Four Ounces to Move a Thousand Pounds!

 

"Interesting," Fenric said with a faint smile before unleashing a flurry of strikes.

 

Bang! Bang! Bang!

 

Three punches landed in just 0.3 seconds!

 

The landlord's face paled—he couldn't keep up with this speed!

 

Puff!

 

A heavy impact rang out as Fenric's fist connected. The landlord was sent flying, coughing blood as he crashed to the ground.

 

Fenric's punches were no joke.

 

Even the Fire Cloud couldn't match Fenric's raw strength.

 

Although Fenric's rapid strikes were slightly weaker than his full-power blows, they were still devastating.

 

That the landlord only coughed blood instead of being killed outright was remarkable.

 

The landlady rushed over, helping her husband up.

 

"Be careful of his fists—this guy has monstrous strength!" the landlord warned.

 

Fenric nearly rolled his eyes.

 

First the Fire Cloud called me naturally gifted… now this guy too? Is great strength always labeled as divine power?

 

"This man is a real master," the landlord muttered.

 

"Let's go together!"

 

The Condor Heroes couple—landlord and landlady—charged at Fenric in unison.

 

Very soon, they realized just how foolish close combat against Fenric was.

 

His combination of overwhelming strength and Armament Haki made him nearly untouchable.

 

Unless they had a way to pierce his defenses, no amount of hits would work.

 

On the other hand, a single touch from Fenric was enough to make them suffer.

 

Worse, his Telekinesis disrupted their movements, giving him a clear advantage.

 

BOOM—! BOOM—!

 

Within moments, both landlord and landlady were sent flying, coughing blood.

 

They looked at Fenric with shock and disbelief.

 

"Who… who are you really?" the landlady asked, shaken.

 

"Even the Fire Cloud wasn't this strong," the landlord added grimly.

 

"Fire Cloud?"

 

Fenric smirked. "He nearly died at my hands last time. He's living under my roof now, hoping to learn from me."

 

He paused, then added, "If you two have time, feel free to visit. I'm sure he'd love the company."

chapters.name: Chapter 198: Chapter 198: The Boss is Too Handsome, Invincible!
chapters.content:
The landlord and landlady were completely dumbfounded!

 

As top-tier martial masters themselves, they naturally knew the name of the Fire Cloud. Even without having fought him personally, they were well aware that he was considered an invincible figure in the martial world.

 

Yet the young man standing before them claimed to have nearly beaten that legendary evil god to death?

 

Unbelievable!

 

And yet… after witnessing Fenric's overwhelming display of power just now, the claim didn't sound entirely impossible.

 

Fenric had toyed with them as if they were nothing more than practice dummies.

 

Even now, they were gravely injured, and Fenric still hadn't revealed his full strength.

 

A terrifying character like this… they had never seen such a person in their entire lives.

 

"Do you still intend to stop me?"

 

Fenric's voice was calm, but his eyes looked down on them from above, cold and sharp.

 

The landlord and landlady exchanged glances where they lay on the ground. Finally, the landlady gritted her teeth and said, "I still have one last technique. If you can withstand it, we won't interfere any further."

 

"A technique?"

 

Fenric's lips curved into a faint smile. "What, the Lion's Roar amplified with a loudspeaker?"

 

"You—how do you know?!"

 

The landlady's eyes widened in shock. That particular trick was something she had secretly developed in seclusion—no outsider had ever heard of it.

 

Fenric didn't bother to explain. "Even though I'm confident I could take your best shot, I'm not interested in wasting time on you. You're simply not worth it."

 

Then his gaze hardened.

 

"I'm taking those three with me. If you dare to interfere again, I'll kill you where you stand!"

 

Truthfully, Fenric was already merciful.

 1

If not for the respect he held for the legendary Condor Heroes couple, he wouldn't have even bothered with words—he'd have ended this quickly.

 2

He knew the original plot well enough to understand that the landlord and landlady, despite their rough exterior and questionable temperaments, were far from villains. They had been quietly protecting the people of Pig Sty Alley all along.

 1

Such characters—chivalrous and loyal—even in a dungeon world, did not deserve to die.

 

Of course, if they were foolish enough to keep challenging his patience, he would not hesitate to end them.

 

"Second Master!" Fenric called out.

 

The underling quickly rushed over, bowing low. "Boss, what are your orders?"

 

"These three killed the Third Master. According to gang rules, what's the punishment?"

 

"Boss, the rule is to hack them to death with axes—and bury their families alive!" the man replied without hesitation.

 

Hearing this, Coolie, the old tailor, and the breakfast shop owner all turned pale.

 

Even the surrounding villagers were shocked by the brutality of the Axe Gang's rules.

 

Fenric himself couldn't help but find it cruel—yet no wonder no one dared to cross the Axe Gang in SH City.

 

A gang of lunatics like this? Who would provoke them?

 

"I'll give you two some face," Fenric said to the landlord and landlady. "These three will die quickly and cleanly, to avenge the Third Master. Beyond that, I won't pursue anything further."

 

His tone was cold but fair. He had already given them enough face.

 

If they didn't accept this… he would have no choice but to take harsher measures.

 

The couple exchanged looks, hesitation flickering in their eyes.

 

"Thanks for your willingness to spare the others," the old tailor said solemnly.

 

Coolie suddenly stood up, his one good eye fixed on Fenric. "I killed the Axe Gang member. I take full responsibility. Leave the others out of this!"

 

Swish!

 

Before he could say more, his head went flying.

 

Fenric had silently drawn a blade into the air using his mental power, slicing Coolie's neck cleanly.

 

The severed head rolled across the ground and landed at the Second Master's feet, making him jump.

 

"Second Master," Fenric ordered calmly, "bury the Third Master, and place this head before his grave."

 

"Y-yes, Boss!"

 

The Second Master swallowed his fear, picked up the bloody head, and stuffed it into a sack. His hands trembled—this Boss was simply too terrifying!

 

Fenric then turned to the old tailor and the breakfast shop owner.

 

Truthfully, he thought highly of these three masters.

 

But they had insisted on interfering, resulting in the Third Master's death.

 

As the leader of the Axe Gang, Fenric had to set an example. Otherwise, what would his men think of him?

 

"Go in peace," Fenric said softly, raising his hand.

 

Crack! Crack!

 

Two sharp fractures rang out.

 

The old tailor, heir of Iron Wire Fist, and the breakfast shop owner, wielder of the Bagua Staff, both collapsed lifelessly under Fenric's mental power.

 

From beginning to end, the landlord and landlady could only watch in silence.

 

"Ugh…"

 

Seeing the three masters die one after another, the landlord sighed heavily.

 

Even if they had stepped in, they wouldn't have been able to stop Fenric.

 1

This young man was a monster—there was simply nothing they could do.

 

Fenric coughed lightly and turned to address the villagers.

 

"Listen well! From today onward, this area falls under the Axe Gang's protection. Each of you will pay a protection fee of one Jade Coin per month, per head.

 

"Pay it, and you won't have to pay the government's food tax anymore!"

 

The Second Master's lips twitched. He wanted to remind Fenric that one Jade Coin per month was too little, but when he met Fenric's cold gaze, he shut his mouth and didn't dare utter a sound.

 

As for the people, their initial reaction was sorrow—no one liked paying protection fees.

 

But when they heard that the food tax would be abolished, their despair quickly turned to joy.

 

One Jade Coin a month? That was nothing compared to the heavy taxes they'd been suffering under!

 

For years, most of their harvest had been swallowed by the government. Now, with Fenric's rule, they would actually be able to keep their crops.

 

If not for their fear of the Axe Gang's brutal reputation, they might have cheered on the spot.

 

"Landlord, landlady," Fenric added casually, "if you ever have time, come visit me. The Fire Cloud would be interested in sparring with you."

 

Leaving those words behind, Fenric ordered his men to carry away the unconscious Sing and Fatty Bone. Then he turned and walked out of Pig Sty Alley, stepping into his car.

 

It wasn't until Fenric's car had vanished that the Samsaras finally dared to whisper among themselves.

 

"Holy sh*t… Boss Shura is just too strong!"

 

"Yeah! He's completely invincible. We were like children in front of him!"

 

"They say his strength has already surpassed Rank A. I didn't believe it before… but now I do!"

 

"No wonder he sits firmly as the Axe Gang's leader. People like us can't even compare."

 

"By the way, who the hell is this Fire Cloud he mentioned? There's no info on him in any of the strategies!"

 

"Yeah, I'm curious too. The name alone sounds terrifying!"

chapters.name: Chapter 199: Chapter 199: Please Have Mercy!
chapters.content:
When Fenric returned to the Axe Gang headquarters, Sing finally regained consciousness.

 

As expected of a peerless genius!

 

His vitality far exceeded that of an ordinary person.

 

If it had been anyone else struck by that blow, their shoulder bones would've shattered, and they'd be bedridden for months.

 

Yet Sing? He looked almost completely fine.

 

"You're awake?"

 

Hearing Fenric's voice, Sing quickly scrambled to his feet and nervously shouted, "L-Leader!"

 

Fenric waved his hand and interrupted him. "From now on, just call me 'Boss' like the others."

 

Sing's eyes lit up with joy.

 

"Thank you, Boss! Don't worry—I'll give it my all! From today onward, my life is yours!"

 

He looked genuinely thrilled.

 

After all, his dream had always been to join the legendary Axe Gang and become a powerful master.

 

But the gang's recruitment standards were notoriously strict. He never thought he'd be accepted.

 

Now, with Fenric telling him to address him as 'Boss', it was clear he had been acknowledged!

 

Fenric smiled and gave Sing a friendly pat on the shoulder. "Good. Remember what you said."

 

"Go get cleaned up and change into some fresh clothes."

 

Then Fenric casually pointed to one of the gang nearby. "You there—take them both to get a proper meal."

 

Sing was deeply moved.

 

He realized that the infamous Boss wasn't as ruthless or terrifying as the rumors claimed. On the contrary—he was incredibly kind.

 

Once Sing and Fatty Bone had left, Fenric raised his voice and asked the room, "Does anyone know the best doctor in SH City?"

 

The gang members exchanged confused glances. They wondered why the Boss, who seemed perfectly healthy, would suddenly need a doctor.

 

One of the senior members stepped forward and replied with a smile, "I know of a clinic in the eastern district. There's an old doctor named Zhou. He's famous across the city—they call him a miracle worker."

 

Fenric nodded. "Good. Go and invite him here."

 

After giving the order, Fenric made his way to the guest wing and entered the room where the bald-headed Fire Cloud was resting.

 

"Senior Fire Cloud, are you comfortable here?" Fenric asked with a polite smile.

 1

"I'm comfortable anywhere," Fire Cloud replied nonchalantly. "You mentioned a miracle. Where is it?"

 

"No rush. You'll see it tomorrow."

 

The Next Morning

 

Early the next day, Sing was summoned by the Axe Gang's leader.

 

"Boss, you were looking for me?"

 

He hurried over—only to see a bald old man sitting beside Fenric.

 

The moment Sing laid eyes on him, his instincts screamed danger. The man radiated an overwhelming presence, like a sea of blood and death.

 

Sing quickly lowered his head, not daring to stare any longer.

 

Fenric smiled gently. "Sing, do you remember what you told me yesterday?"

 

Sing had a bad feeling, but he responded without hesitation. "Yes, I said I'd dedicate my life to you!"

 

"Excellent."

 

Fenric nodded, then turned to the bald man. "Senior Fire Cloud, I'll leave him to you."

 

Fire Cloud gave Sing a strange look. "This kid is really as special as you claim?"

 

"Of course. You'll see—go ahead and test him."

 

"Why don't you do it yourself?" Fire Cloud asked flatly.

 

"I'm afraid I might kill him by accident," Fenric replied, grinning.

 

Fire Cloud rolled his eyes. If he weren't weaker than Fenric, he wouldn't even bother with this.

 

Still, he stepped forward and stood before Sing.

 

"Kid, don't blame me for going all out," Fire Cloud said coolly.

 

Sing blinked, confused. "Boss? What... what's going on?!"

 

Fenric chuckled. "Relax, Sing. You won't die. Just feel the pain—it's good for you."

 

Before Sing could protest, Fire Cloud struck.

 

Pow!!

 

The punch slammed into Sing's side.

 

His entire body jolted violently. The force of the blow surged through him, bursting out his back and tearing apart the new clothes he'd just put on.

 

Fire Cloud's fists weren't something mere mortals could endure.

 

In this world, only Fenric could take a punch like that and still stand.

 

"Gahh!"

 

Sing spat out a mouthful of blood, dazed and overwhelmed.

 

What just happened?

 

He hadn't done anything wrong—so why had the Boss sicced this terrifying old man on him?

 

As Sing struggled to make sense of it all, the second strike came.

 

BOOM—!

 

This time, it was a palm strike to his abdomen—shattering countless internal veins.

 

Sing flew backward, crashed to the ground, and lay motionless.

 

"One breath left," Fire Cloud muttered as he withdrew his hand. "If he's not as miraculous as you claim, not even the gods could save him now."

 

Fenric, still smiling, turned to the other gang members. "Take Sing to Doctor Zhou. Prepare a full medicinal bath for him!"

 

Once Sing was carried away, Fenric turned back to Fire Cloud.

 

"Senior, just wait and see."

 

A Day Later

 

Sing stood once more before Fenric and Fire Cloud—completely healed, not Single injury in sight.

 

"Senior, what do you think?" Fenric asked.

 

For the first time, Fire Cloud looked genuinely stunned.

 

"There's really such a thing...?"

 

The next moment, he walked around Sing, examining him like a rare artifact.

 

Sing flinched, clearly nervous around the strange old man, and tried to step away.

 

Fenric chuckled. "Sing, how do you feel? Any pain?"

 

Sing hesitated, then answered truthfully. "No... I feel fine."

 

"Excellent."

 

Fenric approached and placed a hand on Sing's shoulder.

 

"What happened yesterday—don't hold it against me."

 

"I wouldn't dare!" Sing said quickly. "Boss, you're too kind. My life belongs to you..."

 

Fenric nodded. "To tell you the truth, you're a martial arts prodigy. You just needed a push. That's why I had Senior Fire Cloud test you—to awaken your potential."

 

Now it made sense.

 

Sing finally understood why he'd been nearly beaten to death… only to wake up submerged in a barrel of rare medicine.

 

He'd heard those herbs were priceless—Fenric had spared no expense to help him recover.

 

Fenric continued, "To turn you into a peerless master as quickly as possible, I've decided... Senior Fire Cloud will beat you once a day!"

 

Sing: "..."

 

Boss!! I'm not sure I want to be a peerless master!!

 1

chapters.name: Chapter 200: Chapter 200: The Shura Gang Leader Who Tricks the Dead
chapters.content:
In the blink of an eye, a week had passed.

 

During that week, Sing was beaten daily by Fire Cloud, left clinging to life each time—only to recover miraculously the next day.

 

Sing: "Should I curse or cry? &#£@$¢!"

 

Despite the torment, the gains were undeniable.

 

After just seven days, his strength had skyrocketed. He could now exchange several blows with Fire Cloud!

 

Such monstrous talent was truly terrifying.

 

Even Fenric couldn't help but sigh. "The Son of Destiny… really is something else."

 

Now it was the eighth day of Sing's beatings.

 

By this point, his entire image had transformed.

 

The once ragged street kid had shed his slum-born look.

 

Now, Sing exuded a sharp, dignified aura. He walked like a dragon, eyes brimming with confidence.

 1

His entire being radiated the presence of a martial master.

 

Fire Cloud eyed him with disbelief and muttered to Fenric, "You were already a monster, but this kid… he might just outshine even you."

 

Fenric nodded in agreement. At this point, all he could do was admire the boy's talent.

 

Judging by the time, the mission was nearing its end.

 

Fenric turned to Fire Cloud. "Senior, Sing's foundation is solid now. Let's give him a real test today."

 

Hearing that, Sing's face changed instantly.

 

Test?

 

Big bro, can we not do this?!

 

Fire Cloud raised an eyebrow. "What do you mean by 'real test'? What if he dies?"

 

"He probably won't," Fenric replied casually.

 

But Sing quickly panicked and cried out, "Boss! I'm human! I can actually die, you know!"

 

Fenric thought for a moment, then said, "Alright, to play it safe, you're coming with me. Once you see her, I guarantee you'll want to live."

 

Without giving Sing a chance to protest, he dragged him off.

 

Currently, Sing's strength was comparable to a mid-tier Axe Gang officer. Still, to both Fenric and Fire Cloud, he was no more threatening than a child.

 

The two got in a car and headed downtown.

 

After a few minutes, they stopped along a street.

 

Fenric leaned out of the car and pointed across the road. "Sing, see that girl pushing the cart?"

 

Sing looked where he pointed.

 

Across the road, a young woman with a pure, innocent face was pushing a small cart down the sidewalk.

 

She looked vaguely familiar…

 

"Yes, Boss. I see her."

 

"Good," Fenric nodded. "Now go rob her—take her change."

 

Sing: "???"

 

He stared at Fenric in disbelief. Was he hearing things?

 

The mighty Axe Gang leader… wanted him to rob a street vendor?

 

"Boss?"

 

"I told you to go—don't argue!"

 

Fenric kicked him out of the car.

 

Sing got up, brushed himself off, and reluctantly walked toward the girl.

 

Fenric watched the scene unfold with great interest from inside the car.

 

The mute girl was pushing her cart toward her usual stall location.

 

Suddenly, a figure dashed toward her, barking loudly: "Robbery! Hand over all your money!"

 

Startled, the girl froze. But when she saw the face of the so-called robber, her eyes widened.

 

She recognized him instantly.

 

He was the same boy who once helped chase away bullies when they were children.

 

She stared at Sing silently, her heart filled with disbelief.

 

This is how we meet again?

 

Sing, still not recognizing her, tried to act fierce. "I said, it's a robbery! Can't you hear me?"

 

Even with all his recent strength, Sing still didn't dare disobey Fenric's orders…

 

The girl, realizing Sing hadn't recognized her, quietly pulled out a small box from beneath her cart.

 

Inside it was an old, long-expired lollipop.

 

She held it out to him.

 

Sing froze.

 

And in that moment, recognition struck him like lightning.

 

It really was her.

 

Like in the original story, they had never truly forgotten each other.

 1

Seeing the lollipop in her hand, Sing was overwhelmed with emotion.

 

Clap! Clap! Clap!

 

Applause echoed from nearby.

 

The "Big Villain" Shura—Fenric—stepped onto the stage.

 

"Sing," he said, "you recognize her now, don't you?"

 

"…Boss…"

 

A familiar chill ran down Sing's spine.

 

Over the past week, he had come to understand Fenric's personality.

 

He wasn't just not a good person—he was something far more dangerous.

 

Since Fenric had taken over the Axe Gang, its public image had improved considerably.

 

But those who truly knew him… knew that when Fenric set his mind to something, nothing could stop him.

 

No matter what it took.

 

He was a master of manipulation… and he loved digging pits for people to fall into.

 

And now… Sing realized he was standing on the edge of another one.

 

He was right.

 

Fenric walked over to the mute girl, gently grabbed her arm, and turned back to Sing.

 

"Sing, don't panic. I won't hurt her—not unless you die today."

 

"…Boss?" Sing's voice was trembling.

 

Fenric smiled like a devil. "But if you do die, I'm sorry to say, I'll have no choice but to sell her to a brothel."

 

He gave a dramatic sigh and said, "So, Sing… you better live."

 

"…Boss… please stop playing around. I don't want to be the top martial artist in the world…"

 

Fenric's face darkened. "After everything I've invested in you, you think you get to quit? You ungrateful brat!"

 

He pointed at Sing, voice turning cold: "This isn't a joke. If you die today, I will absolutely send your childhood sweetheart to a brothel. No hesitation."

 

Sing: "…I'm really gonna die of stress before I become a master…"

 

Fenric ignored him and turned to the mute girl, who stood there with a frightened but pretty face.

 

"Girl," he said gently, "you'll have to stay with me for a few days. Sing lives there too."

 

The mute girl didn't understand the situation at all, but when she heard that Sing was staying with Fenric, she nodded shyly.

 

Fenric grinned, eyes gleaming with mischief.

 

The trap had been set.

chapters.name: Chapter 201: Chapter 201: Nirvana Rebirth!
chapters.content:
Fenric brought the mute girl into the car.

 

As for — Sing

 

He was kicked out of the car and ordered by Fenric to run all the way back to headquarters… as punishment.

 

Staring at the fading exhaust trail, Sing was speechless.

 

Still, he wasn't worried about Fenric doing anything indecent to his childhood sweetheart.

 

When it came to that, Sing trusted the gang leader's character.

 

And so, he started running.

 

Inside the car, Fenric leaned back and closed his eyes, not sparing a single glance at the girl beside him.

 

He really had no interest in "messing around" with the mute girl.

 

Soon, the car returned to the Axe Gang headquarters.

 

Sing, having run at full speed, arrived shortly after the car stopped.

 

Once the mute girl was settled in, Fenric brought Sing into the main hall.

 

"All right, bring it on!" Sing growled, steeling himself as he faced Fire Cloud.

 

The bald martial arts master raised an eyebrow and looked at Fenric with curiosity.

 

"Where did you take this kid? He came back like a completely different person."

 

"Took him to see a girl," Fenric said with a grin.

 

Fire Cloud stared at him blankly.

 

As a true martial arts fanatic—one of the straightest men alive—he had no interest in women or romance. He couldn't relate.

 

He looked back at Sing, then at Fenric. "So, what are you planning this time? How do you want me to beat him?"

 

"I hear for martial artists, unlocking the Ren and Du meridians is a big deal, right?" Fenric replied. "Let's break through both at once!"

 

Fire Cloud gave him a look like he was a complete idiot.

 

"Connecting Ren and Du… that's a martial myth! Even I haven't done it. You want me to do that for him?"

 

Fenric shrugged. "Then just beat him until his muscles and veins are completely shattered!"

 

Sing: "..."

 

I'm starting to regret joining this gang…!

 

"A-Are you serious?" Fire Cloud asked in disbelief.

 

He wanted to point out that no one could survive such a thing.

 

But Sing's recent recovery feats had already shattered his understanding of human limits.

 

"I'm serious," Fenric said, nodding.

 

He remembered how in the original timeline, Sing had his entire body broken by Fire Cloud—only to rise from the ashes, reborn through pain, and become a peerless master.

 

"Good!"

 

Without warning, Fire Cloud struck.

 

BAM!

 

His palm slammed into Sing's chest.

 

PFFF!

 

Sing spat blood and collapsed instantly.

 

The blow had shattered his heart!

 

Without pause, Fire Cloud lifted Sing by the collar and unleashed a flurry of devastating punches.

 

BANG! BANG! BANG!

 

It sounded like war drums.

 

Flesh twisted. Bones cracked. Sing's body rapidly contorted and caved under the brutal onslaught.

 

The gang members watching couldn't take it. They instinctively looked away, their expressions grim.

 

Even for them, this was excessive.

 

After several minutes, Fire Cloud finally stopped.

 

Sing lay on the ground—unrecognizable. His body was mangled beyond recognition, his breath and pulse gone.

 

"Quick! Get Doctor Zhou—wrap him in the miracle ointment!"

 

Fenric gave the order immediately.

 

This time, he had entered the "Kung Fu" world specifically to cultivate a supreme technique.

 

Since he couldn't find the old beggar, Sing was his last hope.

 

If Sing died here, it would mean starting from scratch.

 

Soon, Sing was carried to Doctor Zhou for emergency treatment.

 

But even Doctor Zhou could only do so much.

 

Such heavy injuries—he could only bandage them. Whether Sing lived or not now depended entirely on fate.

 

All anyone could do now… was wait.

 

At first, they thought—even if he survived—it would take at least a full day for him to wake up.

 

But what happened shocked everyone.

 

By noon, Sing had made a full recovery.

 

Not even a scratch remained.

 

It was as if the brutal beating earlier had never happened.

 

A while later, Sing walked back into the main hall.

 

Fenric and Fire Cloud were both waiting—and when they saw him, they froze.

 

Sing's aura had changed again.

 

The last trace of cowardice had vanished, replaced with deep self-confidence and inner calm.

 

Standing before them, his eyes were calm. There was no fear left in them.

 

"Tsk," Fenric let out a sigh.

 

"In this world… Sing is basically a cheat code."

 

"Unbelievable," Fire Cloud muttered. "He really is a miracle!"

 

"Sing," Fenric said with anticipation, "do you remember an old beggar who sold you a manual called Buddha Palm Technique when you were a kid?"

 

Sing blinked, then smiled. "I didn't expect the Boss to know about that. But honestly, that beggar tricked me. It was a fake scroll."

 

Fenric frowned.

 

He could tell Sing wasn't lying.

 

So Sing still hadn't learned the legendary Buddha Palm.

 

In the original story, Sing only awakened it during a fight with Fire Cloud, after being sent flying by a toad technique and seeing the sun in the sky.

 

Thinking of this, Fenric turned to Fire Cloud.

 

"Senior, how about a real match between you and Sing?"

 

Fire Cloud blinked, then showed interest.

 

He could already sense that Sing's power had become unfathomable.

 

And fighting powerful opponents was his greatest passion.

 

"Boss, you know how I fight. I don't stop at 'winner or loser'—I fight to the death. Is this boy ready for that?"

 

Sing turned to Fenric. "Boss, you've been good to me. I'll do whatever you decide."

 

Fenric smiled. "Then go all out. Senior, don't hold back—there's no way Sing will die.

 

As for you, Sing… if you unlock the great technique mid-fight, be merciful when you retaliate!"

 

Fire Cloud: "..."

 

"So you're saying… I'm going to lose?"

 

Fenric nodded. "Be confident. And drop the 'maybe.'"

 

The duel was set to take place in the wasteland outside the city.

 

Fenric even sent someone to Pig Sty Alley to invite the Condor Heroes to watch.

 

Soon, the Landlady and Landlord arrived, and their jaws dropped when they saw Fire Cloud.

 

"He's here too?" they muttered, stunned.

 

Seeing them, Fire Cloud grinned again.

 

"Didn't expect more masters to show up… this is getting fun."

 

Fenric rolled his eyes. "Senior, please beat Sing first. We'll get to your hobbies later."

chapters.name: Chapter 202: Chapter 202: Buddha Palm vs. God of Thunder Shura?
chapters.content:
The battle was nothing short of earth-shattering.

 

Just like in the original plot, after Sing was reborn through Nirvana, his Ren and Du meridians connected, causing his power to surge sky-high!

 

In his normal state, Fire Cloud—once hailed as unstoppable—was utterly overwhelmed by Sing!

 

Fenric observed calmly. Even though Sing hadn't yet grasped the "Buddha Palm Technique," his overall strength was already approaching A-rank. He was catching up—fast.

 

Meanwhile, the Landlord and his wife stood frozen, staring at the battlefield in disbelief, almost questioning their very existence.

 

They had retired from the martial world after reaching the peak of their skills. By their own reckoning, only Fire Cloud stood above them.

 

And yet—

 

Not long ago, Fenric had defeated them with ease.

 

Now, before their eyes stood another young man—stronger even than Fire Cloud.

 

The couple couldn't help but wonder: Is this still the martial world we once knew?

 

BOOM—!

 

Sing sent a devastating kick that knocked Fire Cloud to his knees.

 

The ground cracked beneath him, twin pits forming beneath his knees.

 

It was the second time—

 

Twice now, the infamous Fire Cloud had been forced to kneel.

 

The first time was at Fenric's hands. This time, it was Sing.

 

At first, Fire Cloud looked dazed. Then, his fury erupted.

 

The mighty Fire Cloud, the ultimate killer, brought to his knees by two younger men? Unthinkable!

 

But instead of rising again, Fire Cloud dropped flat onto the ground.

 

Fenric narrowed his eyes. He knew what was coming.

 

"Toad Gong…"

 

"Gu-gua—!"

 

A thunderous toad cry echoed across the arena.

 

Fire Cloud's body began to inflate, ballooning like it had been pumped full of air.

 

"The Toad Magic of Kunlun Sect!?" the Landlord exclaimed in shock.

 

His wife gasped. "That school was supposed to be extinct!"

 

"Gu-gua—!"

 

The cry rang out again.

 

In the blink of an eye, Fire Cloud launched forward like a cannonball, aiming his head straight at Sing.

 

"Pfft!"

 

Fast.

 

Incredibly fast!

 

So fast it created a sonic boom in his wake.

 

Fenric remained composed. He had already deciphered the fundamentals of Fire Cloud's Toad Gong.

 

BOOM—!

 

Sing was struck and sent flying, crashing into the ruins beyond.

 

The Landlord and his wife broke into a cold sweat.

 

As expected of the so-called ultimate killer and once "invincible under the heavens"—Fire Cloud was terrifying.

 

Suddenly, they recalled what the Axe Gang's new leader had once claimed:

 

He had defeated Fire Cloud!

 

Now they truly understood just how terrifying Fenric really was.

 

Quietly, the couple took several steps away from him.

 

The battle raged on.

 

Empowered by Toad Gong, Fire Cloud reversed the tide, pressing Sing hard.

 

In the chaos, Sing was caught off guard and launched skyward.

 

Just like the original plot!

 

Soaring high above, Sing glimpsed the Buddha-shaped clouds and blazing sun overhead. A buried memory surfaced—then everything clicked.

 

Years ago, he had been tricked by a beggar into trading all his money for a martial arts manual.

 

Its name: Buddha Palm.

 

Floating in the air, Sing folded his hands and closed his eyes.

 

Then he dropped—fast.

 

Headfirst, like a comet, flames igniting along his body as he accelerated.

 

The Landlord's wife's eyes widened. "Dear, do you remember the legendary move where someone falls from the sky?"

 

"Yes," the Landlord replied solemnly. "That's the long-lost technique of the Buddha Palm Technique!"

 

Fenric's eyes lit up, a grin spreading across his face.

 

He did it!

 

Sing had finally comprehended the "Buddha Palm."

 

Truly, he was the Son of Destiny.

 

What belonged to him—no one could take away.

 

Whoosh! Whoosh!

 

Sing pierced through the sky, faster and faster.

 

His clothes burned away from the sheer speed, leaving behind trails of flame.

 

A crushing aura erupted from his falling figure.

 

Sensing danger, Fire Cloud let out a panicked toad cry and prepared another Toad Gong strike.

 

But the moment he tried to leap—his body refused to move.

 

Too late.

 

BOOM—!!

 

Sing slammed down with a single palm.

 

The force was apocalyptic. The ground split open into a colossal five-fingered crater.

 

Fire Cloud was pinned at the center, unable to move.

 

With just one palm, Sing shattered the Toad Gong technique and crushed Fire Cloud.

 

Everyone around the battlefield was stunned speechless.

 

Even the Samsaras watching from a distance felt their souls tremble.

 

Some nearly wet themselves.

 

At that moment, a single thought consumed them all:

 

This world is too damn deep! Once the mission timer is up, I'm out of here!

 

Even Fenric was briefly speechless, shaken by the sheer destructive power of the Buddha Palm.

 1

But soon enough, excitement returned to his face.

 

With his relationship to Sing, learning this technique wouldn't be too hard!

 

In the original story, Sing had spared Fire Cloud and even offered to teach him.

 

Clearly, Sing was a generous person.

 

Although Fenric had been rough with Sing in recent days...

 

Overall, he had treated him well.

 

Besides, Fenric reasoned, even if Sing refused, I could always pressure him a little.

 

Now that Sing had broken into the A-rank...

 

Fenric still had Mjölnir.

 

And with the hammer in hand, who would really win or lose? Nothing was certain!

 

"Sing! Go easy on him!"

 

Fenric called out loudly.

 

Fire Cloud hadn't done anything unforgivable lately. In fact, he had helped Fenric on several occasions.

 

Sing, hearing this, immediately pulled back, unwilling to take the old man's life.

 

Fenric strode toward the crater and extended a hand to help Fire Cloud up.

 

"I—I haven't lost yet!" the old warrior growled through clenched teeth.

 

Fenric patted his shoulder.

 

"Senior, no need to deny it. Sing isn't a normal person—you know that. Don't compare yourself to that kind of monster."

 

Fire Cloud's face flushed red, then turned pale.

 

He had lost to Fenric.

 

Now he had lost to Sing.

 

His invincible will had taken a heavy blow.

 

Then, all of a sudden, Fire Cloud turned to Fenric and asked the question everyone wanted to know:

 

"Leader... if you fought this boy, who would win?"

chapters.name: Chapter 203: Chapter 203: Who Is Number One in the World! “Boss, if you fought this boy, who would win?”
chapters.content:
Fire Cloud's sudden question left Fenric momentarily stunned.

 

The crowd nearby perked up, clearly curious about the answer.

 

Fenric thought for a moment, then turned to Sing. "Sing, hit me with your Buddha Palm. Let me see what it's like."

 

The crowd gasped.

 

They had just witnessed how terrifying the Buddha Palm was—strong enough that only the formidable Fire Cloud could survive it. If anyone else took a direct hit, they'd be done for.

 

And Fenric was asking Sing to hit him with it?

 

Had he lost his mind?

 

Only Fire Cloud remained calm. He alone knew just how terrifying Fenric's defensive abilities were.

 

"Boss… I don't know if that's a good idea. What if—"

 

Sing trailed off, but everyone understood the unspoken concern.

 

"What if?" Fenric scoffed. "You think you can kill me with one palm, brat?"

 

Fire Cloud had managed to survive with serious injuries. Fenric's defense was far beyond his.

 

"Step aside, senior."

 

Fenric helped Fire Cloud move to the side, then faced Sing and said calmly, "Come. I want to see the true power of the legendary Buddha Palm."

 

"Boss, are you serious?"

 

"Of course I am!" Fenric snapped. "Don't underestimate me. Now go all out!"

 

As soon as he finished, Fenric activated his Armament Haki, coating his body in a black, steel-like sheen.

 

He wasn't trying to show off.

 

He genuinely wanted to test the power of the Buddha Palm.

 

If it's not to his standard, he wouldn't have bothered wasting his "Temporary Enlightenment Card."

 

Besides, judging by what he'd just seen, the technique was definitely powerful.

 

Seeing Fenric's body harden like tempered steel, Sing finally realized how abnormal his Boss truly was.

 

"Alright, Boss. Brace yourself—I'm coming!"

 

Sing warned, then focused his energy into his Dantian, reared back, and struck forward with a palm from a distance.

 

BOOM—!

 

The air erupted with an explosive shockwave.

 

A raging gust of wind tore through the surroundings. Behind Fenric, a few old, uninhabited mud houses were instantly reduced to ash.

 1

As for Fenric, he was sent flying.

 

He soared several hundred meters before landing hard—though cushioned somewhat by his telekinetic control.

 

Upon landing, his expression shifted slightly. A sharp, metallic taste filled his mouth.

 

He was injured.

 

His exterior was fine—his Grandmaster-level Armament Haki had absorbed the brunt of it—but internally, his organs had taken a hit from the force.

 

The Buddha Palm... truly lives up to its name.

 

It wasn't just destructive—it shook the very soul. Without a doubt, this was the strongest attack Fenric had ever faced.

 

And Sing had clearly held back.

 

"Boss! Are you okay?"

 

Sing rushed forward, worried, and reached out to help.

 

Fenric waved him off and stood up on his own. "I'm fine. I can handle it."

 

The damage to his internal organs wasn't critical. With a few days of rest, he'd be fine. No lasting injuries.

 

Besides, the mission was ending in a few days. Once he returned to the Samsara Space, he could recover completely.

 

Seeing Fenric rise as if nothing had happened, Sing was visibly shocked.

 

"Boss, what is your body made of? How are you this durable?"

 

Even the Landlord couple nearby were horrified.

 

That Buddha Palm had only shredded Fenric's clothes?

 

What kind of monster was this Axe Gang leader?

 

As for the other Samsara participants watching from the sidelines, only one thought echoed in their minds:

 

The Shura Boss is terrifying!

 

"This is my own unique skill," Fenric said casually, then asked, "Sing, tell me honestly—how much power did you use just now?"

 

Sing hesitated for a moment. "Seventy percent."

 

Fenric inhaled sharply.

 

Only seventy percent, and it still did that much damage?

 

What would happen if Sing went all out? Could one palm actually take him down?

 

And yet… Fenric was excited.

 

The stronger the technique, the better!

 

Right now, what he lacked was a truly powerful offensive skill.

 

His Thor Hammer was strong, but it was still an external tool—not something that belonged to him.

 

"Sing, you're one of my people. I want to learn the Buddha Palm from you. You wouldn't refuse your own Boss, would you?"

 

Fenric's eyes gleamed with anticipation.

 

Sing blinked in surprise, then smiled warmly. "Of course not, Boss. If you want to learn, I'll teach you."

 

"Good!" Fenric laughed heartily, clapping Sing on the shoulder.

 

Many of the spectators nearby had their eyes light up at that exchange.

 

Especially the Samsaras—many of them looked like they were already plotting something.

 

Fenric noticed and sneered coldly.

 

Let them try.

 

Sing was trained by him, hand-picked and nurtured. If anyone thought they could swoop in and steal the fruit of his labor—

 

Dream on.

 

Not far away, Fire Cloud limped over and grinned.

 

"I'm still curious. Between the two of you, who's really stronger? Why not settle it? The winner can claim the title of 'Number One in the World!'"

 

At those words, even the Landlord couple's expressions shifted.

 

Martial artists strive for the peak. Who wouldn't want to be the best?

 

But Fenric only chuckled and shook his head.

 

"I'm not interested in being number one."

 

Truthfully, if he used Thor's Hammer, Fenric figured he had a 60–70% chance of winning against Sing.

 

The Buddha Palm was indeed fearsome, but with his hardened physique and Armament Haki, Fenric believed he could withstand several hits.

 

And once he summoned lightning with Thor's Hammer—well, Sing was still human. Few could survive a direct strike from that kind of power.

 

No matter how gifted Sing was, he'd still be knocked out if struck by lightning.

 

Not to mention, Fenric also had the black blade Shusui—if it came to it, he could simply cut off Sing's head.

 

"I don't want to fight the Boss," Sing said with a smile.

 

Fire Cloud looked a bit disappointed.

 

No peak showdown. A shame.

chapters.name: Chapter 204: Chapter 204: Come Back!? (End of Dungeon)
chapters.content:
Back in the city.

 

Fenric immediately dismissed all the Samsaras—no need to let them get in his way.

 

Then, he began studying the Buddha Palm with the help of Sing.

 

Fire Cloud tagged along as well.

 

Initially, Fenric had wondered if he could save the "Temporary Comprehension Card" and use it another time.

 

But he quickly realized—he'd been too optimistic.

 

"Boss, Senior Fire Cloud, I'm not sure how to explain it... You can only watch and learn. I'll show it carefully."

 

Geniuses like Sing may be able to master techniques quickly, but his kung fu foundations are weak, relying entirely on his raw talent.

 

When it came to theoretical martial arts, Sing was utterly clueless.

 

So, even if he wanted to demonstrate the essence of the Buddha Palm, he wouldn't know how to explain it properly.

 

Watching Sing slowly channel the energy for the Buddha Palm, Fenric was completely lost.

 

He didn't know martial arts at all—how could he understand any of this?

 

When Sing finished his demonstration, Fenric turned to Fire Cloud and asked, "Senior, did you understand anything?"

 

"A little," Fire Cloud replied. As a martial arts prodigy, his comprehension was naturally top-tier.

 

"Really? Then can you explain it to me?" Fenric asked eagerly.

 

Fire Cloud said, "The Buddha Palm is essentially a refined way of releasing internal energy. But if the Ren and Du meridians aren't connected, it's impossible to learn it."

 

By the time he finished, Fire Cloud was shaking his head.

 

Fenric's expression darkened.

 

He hadn't known that martial arts required both comprehension and talent. It wasn't just about learning—it was about being born for it.

 

Now that he finally understood this truth... it was already too late.

 

He had spent so much time and effort planning, just to acquire a powerful martial arts technique.

 

And now it seemed like all of that was going to waste.

 

The Temporary Comprehension Card only enhanced understanding—it couldn't give him martial arts talent.

 

But to learn the Buddha Palm, he needed his Ren and Du meridians to be connected.

 

How was he supposed to pull that off?

 

If his meridians were already connected, he would've gone after even stronger martial arts techniques!

 

But to just give up now?

 

Fenric clenched his fists. He couldn't accept it.

 

He'd wasted not only a dungeon opportunity, but also days of preparation.

 

Giving up now would mean all of it was for nothing.

 

At that moment, the Temporary Comprehension Card appeared in Fenric's hand.

 

He was going to take a gamble.

 

Items from the Samsara System often had miraculous effects.

 

If he lost the gamble, he'd just lose the card.

 

But if he won... he'd gain the powerful Buddha Palm!

 

With that thought, Fenric crushed the card.

 

"Notice: You have used the [Temporary Comprehension Card]. For the next 30 minutes, your comprehension is increased by 1000%. Please make good use of this time!"

 

As the system prompt sounded, Fenric quickly turned to Sing. "Sing, can you demonstrate the Buddha Palm again?"

 

"Sure!"

 

Sing immediately complied and began practicing again.

 

Fenric watched closely, but his expression grew increasingly grim.

 

It wasn't a problem of comprehension—he had none of the foundational knowledge needed to understand such an advanced martial technique.

 1

Twenty minutes passed.

 

Sing finished the demonstration.

 

Just as Fenric was about to give up, the system prompt rang out:

 

Ding! Congratulations, you have learned the combat technique [Buddha Palm (Reformed)]!

 

Buddha Palm: Delivers overwhelming palm strikes that create shockwaves. Impact equals approximately 100x the sum of the user's physical and spiritual attributes. Large area of effect.

 1

Caution: This technique consumes a massive amount of stamina and spiritual energy. Use with caution!

 

"!!?"

 

Fenric was stunned.

 

He didn't even try that hard, and yet—thanks to the comprehension boost—he had learned the Buddha Palm?

 

Even if it was the reformed version that didn't require internal energy, it was still a genuine Buddha Palm!

 

Fenric had seen with his own eyes how devastating that palm strike could be.

 

Let's do the math:

 

His current physical attribute = 251

 

Spiritual attribute = 502

 

Combined = 753

 

100x that?

 

That meant his palm strike now had an impact of 75,300!

 1

Insane!

 

With that kind of power, he could level an entire building with a single strike!

 

Fenric glanced at his arm.

 

The strength rating that had previously shown a B had now upgraded to A.

 

He couldn't help but burst into laughter.

 

Sing and Fire Cloud looked on, bewildered by his sudden joy.

 

In the following days, Fenric focused solely on mastering the Buddha Palm.

 

It wasn't because he had become lazy or didn't want more fame.

 

It was simply that he had already become famous throughout SH City.

 

If he wanted to keep building his reputation, he'd need to go to other cities.

 

But with only a few days left, the travel time made that unrealistic.

 

Better to use the remaining time to refine his new technique.

 

After repeated practice, Fenric developed an intuitive grasp of the Buddha Palm's destructive power.

 

Now, with one strike, he could easily demolish an average building.

 

Of course, such power came with a cost.

 

Each use of the technique consumed roughly one-fifth of his stamina and spiritual energy.

 

In other words, he could only use it four times in battle before collapsing from exhaustion.

 

Three uses was safe. His body could recover quickly with rest.

 

Roughly ten hours of sleep, and he'd be fully recharged.

 

A few days passed in a blink.

 

Sing left the Axe Gang and opened a candy store with the mute girl. The two lived happily together.

 

On Fenric's last day in this world, he visited the candy shop to say goodbye.

 

As for Fire Cloud, he had seemingly disappeared—perhaps bitter that Fenric learned the Buddha Palm while he hadn't. He might've returned to his school to pass on the Toad Style instead.

 

The moment Fenric stepped inside, Sing spotted him.

 

"Boss? What brings you here?"

 

Even though he had left the Axe Gang, Sing still regarded Fenric as his Boss.

 

After all, he wouldn't have opened this candy store without Fenric's help.

 

"I'm leaving soon. Just came to say goodbye."

 

"Leaving? Where to?"

 

Fenric smiled. "Back to my world."

 

Mission Countdown Initiated: 10, 9, 8... 3, 2, 1!

 

It was time.

 

All Samsaras were withdrawn from the world of "Kung Fu Hustling."

 

Congratulations! Samsara "Shura" has performed excellently in the dungeon world "Kung Fu Hustle." Within one month, he gained 300,000 fame, completed the mission beyond expectations, and received the highest evaluation: SS!

 3

Inside the vast space of Samsara, the system's announcement echoed once again.

 

Many Samsaras were stunned.

 

They were used to seeing Shura dominate the rankings—but this time was different.

 

Not because he performed well again.

 

But because for the first time ever, Shura only received an SS rating instead of his usual SSS.

 

And this was supposed to be a normal difficulty dungeon?

 

What happened?

 

Was the Shura God... finally running out of steam?

 1

The Samsara Space erupted with speculation.

 2

chapters.name: Chapter 205: Chapter 205: Has the Genius Shura "Fallen"?
chapters.content:
[Translator Note: There was a Super Typhoon in my country. My place was in signal #3. Anyway, I'm back.]

 7

....

 

"SS grade? Not SSS? What happened to the Great God Shura?"

 

"Incredible! There's actually a day when the Shura God doesn't get a Super God rating?"

 

"Damn, I thought I misheard it. It really is missing an S!"

 

"More importantly, wasn't the dungeon just the standard difficulty version of Kung Fu? How did Shura end up with just an SS?"

 

"Is the great Shura finally running out of steam?"

 

"Heh, so Shura isn't invincible after all!"

 

"Haha, no way! Just an SS rating? What a joke!"

 1

"Come on, you people are ridiculous. Everyone makes mistakes now and then. What's wrong with Shura having a slip-up? You just love to drag others down!"

 

"Seriously—what's so bad about an SS evaluation? How many of you have even gotten that before?"

 

"Clearly, Shura's consistent top-tier performance made some jealous dogs foam at the mouth!"

 

"Who are you calling a jealous dog?!"

 

"Hey, I wasn't talking about you—unless the shoe fits?"

 

"You bastard, do you have a death wish? I'll punch you into next week!"

 

"Try me! Let's see if the Samsara System doesn't teach you a lesson in humility!"

 

In the Samsara Space, a storm of heated discussion erupted.

 

To the average Samsara player, it was jarring to see Shura—known for constantly achieving SSS-level Super God evaluations—suddenly end up with a mere SS.

 

For many, Shura was synonymous with Super God rankings. Anything less felt off.

 

Some even began to argue over whether Shura was "washed up."

 

That was the problem with being too dazzling in the public eye—one mistake and everyone jumps on it. While Shura had amassed legions of fans, he had just as many lurking critics waiting for a chance to gloat over a fall from grace.

 

And now that moment seemed to have arrived—at least in their eyes. The news spread fast, and ridicule followed like a flood.

 

Entertainment City.

 

In a cold drink shop, Arke and a few friends were lounging around with fruit juices when the system broadcast chimed in. They paused mid-conversation.

 

"Huh? Isn't Shura the genius who always gets Super God evaluations? Why only SS this time?"

 

"Yeah! It feels... strange seeing that."

 

"Maybe it was just a slip-up. SS is still an incredible rating. He's still a genius."

 

"Or maybe he really is starting to fade..."

 

Arke frowned at their comments. She quietly opened her friend list. Shura hadn't come out yet—he was likely still receiving his mission rewards.

 

"I don't believe you'd make a mistake, Shura," she whispered to herself.

 

Personal Consignment Center.

 

Belle Morwyn was browsing through the listings, checking for any useful items in preparation for her next dungeon run—The Avengers.

 

Suddenly, she heard the system notification.

 

Shura... only got an SS evaluation?

 

Not a Super God rating?

 

For no reason she could explain, Belle felt a sudden pang of worry. She logged out of the system and returned to the real world.

 

In the Capital. Real World. Early Morning.

 

Yuhan(Belle) stepped up to her cousin's room and knocked.

 

Knock knock knock!

 

"Sis, are you asleep?"

 

An irritated voice came from inside. "You woke me up just to ask that? Get in here already!"

 

Vivienne had turned in early, but now she was up again. As Yuhan entered, she saw her cousin lying lazily on the bed in thin pajamas.

 

Vivienne's curvy figure was hard to ignore—especially her deep cleavage, which Yuhan glanced at enviously.

 

"What's the emergency, waking me up like this?"

 

Yuhan shook herself back to focus. "Sis, Shura just got an SS evaluation."

 

Vivienne blinked. "Wait, Shura? As in the Shura? He didn't get SSS?"

 

"Nope. Just SS. Double S, not triple."

 

A hint of surprise flickered across Vivienne's delicate face, followed by a small smile. "SS is still an excellent rating."

 

"But... it's Shura," Yuhan emphasized.

 

"So what? He's still human, isn't he? Humans make mistakes sometimes."

 

She then eyed her cousin with suspicion. "Wait a second—don't tell me you've got a thing for Shura?"

 

"N-No!" Yuhan said quickly, flustered. "Don't say weird things!"

 

"Whatever. I'm too sleepy to tease you. If you're that worried, just ask him yourself when he logs back in."

 

—---

 

Samsara Space

 

[SYSTEM] Notification:

 

"Dear Samsara—Shura, you have completed your mission. Your rewards are as follows:

 

• Samsara Points: 27,500

 

• Strength +20

 

• Dungeon Cooldown Refresh Card ×1 (stored in Personal Warehouse)

 

• Silver Treasure Chest ×1 (stored in Personal Warehouse)"

 

Fenric listened to the rewards announcement with a calm expression.

 

By his standards, this was probably the worst reward haul he'd ever gotten.

 

Still, he didn't care much.

 

After all, he hadn't gone into the Kung Fu Hustle dungeon for the mission rewards. He went there for something else—and he'd gotten what he wanted.

 

The fact that he still earned an SS evaluation was enough. Fenric was satisfied with the result.

 

Without delay, he headed to his personal warehouse.

 

Of the four rewards, the first three didn't interest him much.

 

But the Silver Treasure Chest—that caught his attention.

 

He had opened many Gold and Silver treasure chests before, but this one seemed... different.

 

Just from the name, he could already guess the contents wouldn't be as good as a Gold Chest. But curiosity got the better of him.

 

What could be inside?

 

Without hesitation, Fenric opened it.

 

"Congratulations! You have opened the Silver Treasure Chest and received the combat skill scroll: Lion's Roar Technique."

 

Fenric raised an eyebrow at the system prompt.

 

Lion's Roar Technique?

 

Wasn't that the yelling technique used by the landlady?

chapters.name: Chapter 206: Chapter 206: So, This Was the Goal of the Great God Shura!
chapters.content:
Lion's Roar Technique—a sonic attack.

 1

To be honest, at Fenric's current level, he couldn't help but look down on it.

 

Compared to his telekinetic abilities, this skill was underwhelming.

 

What was the point of learning a technique that required you to shout at your enemy during battle?

 4

Just imagining it was embarrassing.

 

So, without hesitation, Fenric tossed the Lion's Roar Technique scroll into his storage. He had zero interest in learning it.

 3

Next, he turned his attention to his hard-earned Samsara Points from the last mission.

 

From the Kung Fu Hustle dungeon, he earned a total of 27,500 Samsara Points.

 

After a moment of thought, Fenric used 25,000 points to redeem 50 potential points.

 

He left 2,500 points in reserve—just in case.

 

He allocated the 50 potential points carefully among his attributes. His updated status looked like this:

 

Name: Shura

 

Samsara Number: (Zone C) 90086

 

Physique: 251 → 264

 1

Spirit: 502 → 526

 1

Strength: 349 → 369

 1

Agility: 251 → 264

 1

Unallocated Potential: 0

 1

Skills: English (Proficient), Driving (Beginner), Shooting (Proficient), Camouflage (Master), Basic Sword Technique (Proficient)

 

Special Skills: Conqueror's Haki (Mastery), Armament Haki (Master)

 

Combat Skills: Savage Collision, Buddha Palm

 

Abilities: Telekinesis, Hundred Poison Resistance (Passive)

 

Samsara Accumulation: 2522

 

Comprehensive Evaluation: A

 

This was Fenric's current state.

 

Comprehensive Evaluation: A.

 

But...

 

When he exited his personal warehouse and visited the Samsara Tower, he checked the Top 100 Global Masters list—and his name wasn't there.

 

Clearly, despite his progress, he was still far from the world's top-tier masters.

 

"You have a new communication message. 'Belle Morwyn' is requesting a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

Just after exiting the warehouse, the system notification popped up.

 

Fenric accepted the request. A holographic video lit up, revealing a familiar elf girl. Seeing her, Fenric smiled.

 

"Belle. Good evening."

 

"Shura," Belle Morwyn asked with concern, "I just heard the Samsara system broadcast. Why did you only get an SS evaluation this time? Did something happen?"

 

Fenric chuckled. "It's normal to get an SS."

 

"It's normal for others. But for you, it's strange. You usually get Super God ratings."

 1

He fell silent for a moment.

 

But he knew Belle meant well. So he replied, "Don't worry, there's no accident. This time, a lot of people entered the same copy with me. You'll probably see the reason by tomorrow."

 

"All right, I didn't mean to pry. I was just worried. You must be tired after clearing that dungeon. I'll let you rest."

 

"Okay. You get some rest too."

 

The call ended.

 

Fenric didn't linger in the Samsara space. He logged out.

 

Back in the real world.

 

In his small apartment, Fenric glanced at the glowing "A" rank symbol on his arm and smiled in satisfaction.

 

He headed into the bathroom, checking the house along the way.

 

The place he shared with his father wasn't big—two bedrooms and a living room, maybe 70 square meters at most.

 

It was livable… but cramped.

 

Now that his strength had reached A-rank, even within the entire Samsara system, few could match him.

 

And with an artifact like Thor's Hammer in hand, he had no problem ensuring his own safety.

 

He'd kept a low profile long enough.

 3

It was time to stop shortchanging himself. Time to upgrade to a more comfortable life.

 

He planned to buy a better house. If his father wanted to live with him, great. If not, he'd live alone.

 

The Next Morning.

 

Fenric went to school as usual.

 

He didn't act like some edgy loner and suddenly drop out just because he had power. That'd be childish.

 

Better to kill time at school like a "salted fish," rather than explain everything to his father at home.

 

Besides, he'd only be here for two or three more days.

 

When he arrived, Fenric thought the other students would be buzzing about his performance last night.

 

They weren't.

 

Instead, today's topic was darker—a student from Class 3 had died in a Samsara dungeon two days ago.

 

Apparently, they entered the Young and Dangerous copy in the safe zone.

 2

That dungeon, despite being in a "safe zone," was notoriously difficult and dangerous. Most low-level Samsaras wouldn't dare touch it.

 

A student died.

 

It was a big deal in the school, so naturally, everyone was talking about it.

 

Fenric listened for a while but quickly lost interest.

 

Death in the Samsara space was nothing new. Especially in the Samsara Tower, people died nearly every night—never to return.

 

Fenric himself had taken many lives.

 

Why should he care about a random student's death?

 

He pulled out his phone and started browsing.

 

Online, people were gossiping about his alternate identity: Shura.

 

"Wow, even Shura gets SS evaluations?"

 

"Thought he was unbeatable! If even he only gets SS now, maybe next time it'll just be S!"

 

"Yeah! I thought he was some god-tier player. Kinda disappointing."

 

"You jealous idiots the ones we call 'red-eyed dogs'? You think you can bring down Shura's name with one SS-level run?"

 

"Bro, don't pay attention to these losers."

 

"Shura's achievements were too overwhelming. Of course people are gonna hate."

 

"The funniest part? Some even say Shura's 'past his prime'. Ridiculous. If someone can score SS while being 'washed up', then what does that make the rest of you who can't even get a B?"

 

"+1. These clowns are like dropouts mocking a straight-A student for getting a B once. Pathetic!"

 

"Jealousy really is the original sin."

 

"Yo! Stop arguing and check the Samsara forums! Shura didn't underperform last night at all! He just didn't chase the main objective!"

 

"Yeah, I saw that too. Someone who was in the same dungeon posted the whole breakdown. Turns out Shura faced off against a ton of big names!"

chapters.name: Chapter 208: Chapter 208: Horror! A Total Mess!
chapters.content:
BOOM—!

 

Smoke and dust billowed from a building outside the school. Explosions rang out one after another, resembling the detonation of some kind of chemical compound.

 

But this was a school district—chemical plants weren't allowed anywhere nearby.

 

"Attention all students! Please evacuate immediately to Teacher Building No. 7!"

 

The sudden announcement blared from the school's Public Address system. It was the principal's voice, serious and urgent.

 

Teacher Building No. 7 was located at the back gate of the school.

 

Students froze for a moment—then chaos erupted as they bolted from their classrooms.

 

"Do not panic! Remain calm and proceed in an orderly manner! Homeroom teachers, maintain order!"

 

But the principal's words only fueled the panic.

 

The more he urged calm, the more frenzied the students became. Teachers struggled to regain control, but no one was listening. Everyone could sense this was no ordinary incident.

 

Fenric moved with the crowd, feeling a sense of unease.

 

Based on his understanding, this world was more chaotic than the Earth of his previous life, thanks to the existence of Samsaras. Some individuals, once empowered, acted recklessly—committing crimes with little restraint.

 

Still, society remained relatively stable.

 

Especially in major nations. Armed with nuclear weapons, they kept even the most unruly Samsaras in check. No one dared stir real trouble.

 

But this… this was different.

 

Before long, Fenric and the rest of the students made it safely out through the school's back gate.

 

Police quickly sealed off the surrounding area. Dozens of officers patrolled the streets, using loudspeakers to urge citizens to stay indoors.

 

A heavy tension settled over the city.

 

Fenric returned home.

 

"Ric? I was just about to call you! That explosion—was it near your school?" his father, Eric, asked with concern.

 

"Yeah. I'm not sure what's going on yet. The school staff evacuated everyone. There are police everywhere," Fenric replied.

 

"Must be the work of a supernatural again… something similar happened a few years ago."

 

Father Eric's face was clouded with worry.

 

"Ric, don't go out today. Stay home."

 

"Alright. You too—try to get some rest."

 

Fenric retreated to his room and turned on his computer to search for information.

 

Surprisingly, there was almost nothing online.

 

Most netizens were still busy praising Shura for easily clearing an SS-level dungeon.

 

Some users briefly mentioned hearing an explosion—but their posts were swiftly deleted.

 

Such a massive incident, yet not a single solid report on the Internet? That was definitely abnormal.

 

Even local forums were eerily quiet.

 

Occasionally, a post would pop up—but it would be taken down almost immediately.

 

It was clear: the government was suppressing the news.

 

Fenric frowned. This wasn't normal. If it were just another supernatural criminal, there'd be no need to hide the details like this.

 

Still, he didn't dwell on it too much. As long as it didn't affect him, he could stay out of it.

 3

He'd ask Aurora later. As a high-ranking official, Aurora Morwyn would surely know more.

 

For now…

 

Fenric opened the Samsara Forum to check for strategies related to the eighth floor of the Samsara Tower.

 

Just like the seventh floor, the eighth had two dungeons.

 

BOOM—!

 

Before he could read further, the roar of helicopters thundered outside his window.

 

Fenric rushed over and looked up.

 

Several military helicopters, painted in camouflage, sped across the sky toward the heart of the city.

 

Troops also began to appear in the streets below.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed.

 

In this world, much like the Earth he once knew, military forces didn't enter urban areas without a serious reason.

 

To deploy the army meant something huge had happened.

 

His brows furrowed. He needed more information—and fast.

 

He pulled out his phone and dialed Isla Wynn.

 

Among all his friends, only Isla came from the upper class. If anyone knew something, it would be her.

 

The call connected quickly.

 

"Hello? Fenric?"

 

"Yeah, it's me. Isla—have you heard anything? There's a huge commotion in the city."

 

Isla's voice was tense.

 

"Fenric, are you still at home? You need to get out—now. The entire city's about to be locked down."

 

"What happened?"

 

"I don't know all the details. But my dad said a terrorist organization got their hands on some kind of virus from the Samsara Space… it's already spread through the city. Lots of people have died."

 2

"The military is taking over completely. We're evacuating soon. Fenric, do you want to come with us? I can tell my dad—we can bring your family along."

 

Before Fenric could reply, the line went silent.

 

"Hello? Isla?"

 

He checked his phone—no signal.

 

When he returned to his computer, the Internet was down too. No access to any websites.

 

Fenric's expression darkened.

 

A virus? Powerful enough to trigger a full-scale military response?

 

A sense of unease crept into his chest.

 

He wasn't worried about himself—his immunity made him invulnerable to toxins or infections.

 

But his father was just an ordinary man.

 

Without hesitation, Fenric headed to Eric's room.

 

"Ric? Look outside. The army's everywhere…"

 

His father was wide awake, unable to sleep amid the chaos. His face was filled with concern.

 

This was already beyond anything they'd seen before—not even the last supernatural crisis came close.

 

"Dad, pack your things. We're going to the countryside."

 

Their family had a mud-brick house back in the village, abandoned since Fenric's grandparents passed. But it could still serve as a temporary refuge.

 

"Is it really that serious?" Eric asked.

 

"It is," Fenric said firmly. "I just spoke to a classmate. Her family's well-connected, and she said a virus has leaked. It sounds credible. Better safe than sorry."

 1

Father Eric's face turned solemn.

 

"Alright. Let's get our things and go. We'll stay in the countryside for a few days."

chapters.name: Chapter 209: Chapter 209: Virus from "Prototype"!
chapters.content:
Isla was right.

 

Sure enough, the city had been placed under military lockdown.

 

No one was allowed in or out, and a strict curfew was enforced. Without special clearance, it was forbidden to walk the streets at random.

 

Now, the only people permitted to move freely were the police and soldiers.

 

When Fenric and Chen's father attempted to leave their community, they were stopped by police stationed at the gate and advised to return.

 1

Of course, if Fenric truly wanted to leave, nothing could stop him.

 

With his current strength and arsenal of special items, even an A-rank powerhouse couldn't hold him back.

 

But Fenric wasn't the type to make things difficult for the officers just doing their job.

 

Given the situation, he decided it would be best to cooperate with the authorities—for now—and gather information.

 

As of now, the entire city was under closed management.

 

During mealtimes, staff delivered supplies door-to-door: rice, vegetables, meat—enough to feed a family of three for two or three days.

 

The internet remained offline. It seemed that all major network providers had been evacuated. Nearby signal towers were either shut down or jammed, rendering mobile phones completely useless.

 1

No internet. No calls. No online access at all.

 1

Clearly, the move was intended to prevent information leaks and public panic.

 

That night, Fenric could hear distant sounds from the city center—inhuman roars and sporadic bursts of gunfire.

 

His expression darkened. He planned to enter the Samsara Space later that night to investigate.

 

Finally, it was midnight.

 

When the full moon tattoo on his arm began to glow a faint red, Fenric pressed his hand against it and instantly vanished from his room.

 

Upon entering Samsara Space, he immediately opened his friend list. Three contacts were offline.

 

After a moment's thought, he headed for the Entertainment City and entered the bar.

 

The bar in Samsara Space was always bustling with people—a perfect place to gather intel and overhear valuable information.

 

"Brother, is your area under military lockdown too?"

 

"Lockdown? What lockdown?"

 

"Damn, you seriously don't know?"

 

"Haven't heard anything like that."

 

"My city's locked down too. Which city are you from?"

 

"HA City. You?"

 

"CZ City."

 

"What the hell are you guys talking about? Why isn't there any news about this online?"

 

"Bro, the internet's down where we are. Total blackout!"

 

"Has to be something major. The government doesn't move like this unless it's serious."

 

Just a few minutes in the bar, and Fenric had already picked up valuable intel.

 

Apparently, multiple cities were under lockdown.

 

Then, a prompt popped up from the system:

 

"You have a new message. 'Belle Morwyn' is requesting a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

Fenric left the bar immediately and accepted the call.

 

Moments later, Belle's spirit avatar appeared before him.

 

"Belle, you came at the perfect time. I've got questions," Fenric said. "My city's been locked down by the military. Do you know why?"

 4

"I do."

 

She had logged in specifically to inform him.

 

"Great. Do you have time now? Let's meet at the teahouse and talk there."

 

"Sure."

 

After ending the call, Fenric reserved a private box at the teahouse and waited.

 

A short while later, Belle Morwyn arrived.

 

"Belle, what exactly is going on?" Fenric asked.

 

"Shura, do you remember the 116 Incident back in 2009?" she asked.

 2

Fenric paused, then nodded. "Of course."

 

The 116 Incident referred to a rebellion launched by a group of Samsara on November 6, 2009.

 

Fenric had even referenced the incident before when he sold his "World War Z" strategy to counter moral grandstanders at the bar. He knew the story well.

 

In fact, most people in the country did.

 

"Even though the 116 Incident was ultimately suppressed by the authorities," Belle said, "many of its members survived."

 

"They've been operating in the shadows ever since, gradually accumulating resources. In secret, they formed a dangerous organization called the Red Light Society."

 1

"They aim to create a world where Samsara reign supreme, hidden in the dark, biding their time."

 1

"This latest event was orchestrated by them. They managed to obtain a sample of the Blacklight Virus from the Samsara Tower instance 'Prototype'—and today, they released it to plunge the world into chaos."

 

Fenric's eyes widened.

 

"Blacklight Virus?!"

 3

This virus was far more terrifying than the T-virus from Resident Evil. The Blacklight Virus wasn't just lethal—it accelerated evolution itself.

 

Once infected, even ordinary people would mutate into zombie-like creatures—except these ones could evolve into powerful monsters.

 

And if the host happened to be an "[Evolved]"?

 

They could awaken all kinds of terrifying abilities.

 

Shifting arms into blades, transforming their bodies into living armor—those were just the basics. The real powers were catastrophic!

 

The virus was even more potent than the symbiotes from Venom.

 

The Blacklight Virus came from Prototype 577.

 

Back on the old Earth, Prototype had been a popular open-world sci-fi action game. The plot featured a city infected by the virus, teeming with mutated monsters.

 1

Fenric had played it and loved it.

 

But he never imagined Prototype would appear in the Samsara Tower… or that the virus sample could be brought into the real world.

 

That was insane.

 

"The virus is extremely dangerous," Belle continued. "It turns people into evolvable mutants. Thankfully, it's not easily contagious—it can't spread through air or water. With proper containment, it can be controlled."

 

"Our country's systems are robust. We've already taken the right steps. But in smaller, unstable nations… things could get ugly."

 

Fenric's expression turned grim.

 

"Wait, Belle… are you saying the Red Light Society released this virus worldwide today?"

 

"Yes," she replied. "According to intel my sister acquired, several small countries have already seen their capital cities fall. It's only a matter of time before they become full-on monster zones."

 2

"..."

 

Fenric was speechless.

 

This Red Light Society… their methods were absolutely insane.
