chapters.name: Chapter 210: Chapter 210: The Global Situation is Grim!
chapters.content:
[Translator Note: My bad. I just copy pasted the note lmao. Here's the goal needed to reach before the next arc start: +1500 stones = the next arc chapters.]

 

----

 

"Shura, my sister has already gone to CK City to suppress the Samsara chaos there, so she hasn't arrived yet," Belle explained.

 

"But she should be here soon. At this point, if those caught in the chaotic samsara can't escape, they'll have no choice but to take refuge in Samsara Space."

 

"My sister knows a lot more than I do. If you have questions, you can ask her once she arrives."

 

Fenric nodded. "What would you like to drink? It's my treat."

 

"Tranquility Tea, thank you!" Belle smiled softly, then added, "Shura, if you ever need help, just say the word."

 

"Alright."

 

When the tea arrived, the two chatted casually while sipping it.

 

About half an hour later, Aurora Morwyn entered Samsara Space and was soon brought to the private box by Belle.

 

"Shura, Belle—you two seem quite relaxed." Aurora greeted with a smile.

 

It was clear from her slightly tired expression that she had been working hard.

 

"Here, have some Tranquility Tea. Sit and rest for a bit," Fenric offered.

 

"Then I won't be polite!"

 

Aurora took a sip and sighed with satisfaction. "The tea here in Samsara Space is still the best. No matter how high-end the real world's tea is, it just can't match this taste and effect!"

 

"Sister, how's the situation?" Belle asked, turning serious.

 

Aurora replied, "Domestically, things are temporarily under control. But the international scene is a mess—it's likely to get worse and stay that way for quite a while."

 

As she spoke, Aurora's brows furrowed.

 

"According to expert analysis, more powerful zombies will definitely appear overseas. There's even a strong possibility of this escalating into a long, drawn-out war between humans and zombies."

 

After all, not many countries in the world had the same environmental advantages as Jadeveil Nation.

 

"Even the Cindralock Dominion, despite being called the world's strongest, is several levels behind when it comes to internal management and crisis response," she added.

 3

Fenric asked, "I heard that several cities in Jadeveil experienced black light virus leaks this time?"

 

"Yes," Aurora nodded. "Seventeen cities, all under military martial law."

 

She paused, then asked, "Shura… don't tell me the city you're in is one of them?"

 

Fenric shrugged. "Bingo."

 

"Do you need help?"

 

"If I ask for help now, won't that give away who I am?" Fenric chuckled.

 

Aurora quickly waved her hands. "No, no—don't misunderstand! I didn't mean it that way."

 

Fenric laughed and waved dismissively. "It's fine, I was just joking. Even if you did know my identity, it's no big deal. I trust you."

 

Of course, that was just polite talk. But the truth was, Fenric no longer cared as much about keeping his identity a secret.

 

After all, he was now an A-level Boss. He couldn't stay hidden in the shadows forever.

 

"How long will the military lockdown last?" he asked.

 

If it was a short duration, he could wait it out. But if it dragged on, he'd consider leaving the city altogether. With his abilities, escaping unnoticed would be easy—even without Aurora's help.

 

"About three days, depending on the local situation," Aurora answered. "Once the virus source is neutralized, the lockdown should be lifted."

 

"Three days…?" Fenric muttered.

 

Didn't that mean he'd miss the college entrance exam?

 

Then again, it didn't really matter anymore. That exam was trivial to him now.

 

"When will the internet be back?" he asked.

 

"Tomorrow," Aurora said. "There's no way to keep this under wraps much longer. At tonight's meeting, the plan was approved for the government to announce it publicly tomorrow, so they can maintain narrative control."

 

Fenric breathed a sigh of relief.

 

Finally, the internet!

 

Life without it had been incredibly dull.

 

Aurora suddenly said, "Shura, I heard about your SS rating from last night… and that boy, Sing—I have some impression of him. When I ran the dungeon previously, he was just a member of a minor gang. Is it true that he's now a peerless master?"

 

Fenric was slightly surprised but answered honestly, "He's got talent, that's for sure. But to become a true peerless master, someone would need to help him break through the Ren and Du meridians."

 

He paused, then added, "Probably only Fire Cloud could do that. Not even the famous married couple from Pig Sty Alley could guarantee it."

 

Aurora nodded, wisely refraining from probing further about Fire Cloud. That kind of question would lead into deeper, more dangerous strategies.

 

"I heard many people online say that Sing's Buddha Palm is unbelievably strong. Shura, did you learn it too?"

 

"Yeah."

 

Fenric answered without hesitation. There was no reason to hide it.

 1

"So the rumors were true…" Aurora said with admiration. "Shura, you're incredible!"

 

"You flatter me too much," Fenric laughed.

 

"No, I mean it," Aurora insisted. "Many online are speculating that your strength has already reached A-level. Is that true?"

 

When Fenric nodded, the Morwyn sisters both gasped, astonishment written all over their faces.

 1

"Shura, you're amazing!" Aurora said. "No one before has ever reached the eighth floor of the Samsara Tower and gotten an A-level rating this early. Even Adam only got his A-level after clearing the fourteenth floor. You're twice as fast as him!"

 

Belle added, "Shura, I thought reaching B-level was already impressive… but compared to you, I'm nowhere near."

 

"You two keep praising me like this, and I might float away," Fenric joked.

 

"Alright, enough flattery," Aurora said suddenly, her expression turning serious. "Shura, my informant told me that Adam cleared the 31st floor last night… and received an A-level mission rating."

 

She looked directly at him.

 

"He's already left the rest of us behind. Right now, our only hope of catching up to him… is you. If you need anything—resources, intel, support—just say the word. I'll help however I can, even if it means putting everything on the line. None of us want Adam to reach the 33rd-floor authority first."

 

Fenric's eyes gleamed at her words.

 

Of course, he didn't want anyone else to get that 33-level access either.

 

But… he had only just cleared the eighth floor. The gap between him and Adam was still huge.

 

"I'll do my best," Fenric replied, then asked, "By the way, do either of you have a real strategy guide for the eighth floor? The official one online is basically just a scam."

chapters.name: Chapter 211: Chapter 211: Don’t Even Lillian Know?
chapters.content:
"I don't even have internet access over there anymore. I can't look up the walkthrough," Fenric said helplessly.

 

Aurora chimed in, "Shura, if I remember correctly, there are two dungeons on the eighth floor. The standard one is Blade Runner, and the difficult one is [A Bride Ghost Story], right?"

 7

She glanced at him and added with a knowing smile, "Judging by your personality, I bet you're planning to challenge the hard-mode dungeon?"

 

Hearing the names of those two worlds, Fenric paused to think. After a moment, he nodded. "Yeah, I'm probably going with [A Bride Ghost Story]."

 

"Thought so." Aurora's tone grew more serious. "I have a few special beads on me. They don't have any offensive capabilities, but they can protect your soul."

 

"In the dungeon world of [A Bride Ghost Story], there's a particularly powerful tree demon that can harm people's souls. Want me to give you a string for protection?"

 

Fenric's eyes lit up. "Then I won't be shy!"

 

He remembered clearly—[A Bride Ghost Story] wasn't just about the tree demon. The old Black Mountain Demon in the underworld was even more terrifying, capable of sucking away souls directly.

 

If he was really going to dive into that dungeon, then those Buddhist prayer beads Aurora mentioned were exactly what he needed.

 

"Alright then, I'll head to the trading center and give them to you later," she said. "But keep in mind, the prayer beads are disposable. They only work once."

 

"That's fine. Thanks, Aurora!"

 

"What are you thanking me for?" she laughed. "Didn't you say before there's no need to be polite between us?"

 

"Fair enough. I'll take you up on that," Fenric chuckled.

 

"Good." Aurora smiled. "Let's go to the trading center. I'll give you the beads there. I have a meeting to attend afterwards. I've forgotten most of the dungeon's strategy guide—have Belle go back and copy it for you."

 

"Got it!"

 

With that, the group split up.

 

Aurora and Fenric headed to the trading center, while Belle logged off to hand-copy the official [A Bride Ghost Story] walkthrough.

 

Trading Center

 

A string of prayer beads dropped into Fenric's hand.

 

[Special Item: Bodhi Prayer Beads (One-time use)]

 

"These prayer beads have been enchanted by a Bodhisattva. When worn, they protect the wearer's soul from external evils."

 

Note: This is a one-time-use item. The effect expires within 24 hours after activation.

 

Once the transaction was complete, Aurora said, "Shura, I have to return to reality for that meeting."

 

"Alright, go handle your business."

 

Aurora logged out and disappeared from the Samsara Space.

 

Shortly afterward, Belle reappeared at the trading center entrance and handed Fenric a neatly handwritten page.

 

"Shura, I copied the official walkthrough for [A Bride Ghost Story] word for word. Here, take a look."

 

In the Samsara Space, real-world objects weren't allowed to be brought in. Any unprocessed item from reality would be confiscated after three hours. Luckily, three hours was more than enough for Fenric to finish reading the guide.

 

Looking at the page filled with elegant, flowing handwriting, Fenric couldn't help but smile. "Thanks."

 

"It's no trouble. Go ahead and study the guide. I won't bother you anymore," Belle said, then quietly stepped away.

 

Left alone, Fenric focused on the strategy guide.

 

Belle's handwriting was not only beautiful and precise, it also made the dense information easier to absorb.

 

He'd heard rumors that Belle was considered a "goddess" at one of the elite middle schools—not just because of her looks, but because she was also a top student.

 

The guide she copied was an unabridged, official walkthrough:

 

Walkthrough: [A Bride Ghost Story]

 

Before attempting this dungeon, we recommend learning basic Taoist techniques or equipping yourself with special items that can counter supernatural beings. This is a world ruled by monsters and ghosts—brute force alone won't help you.

 

The main mission is to collect Yin Qi(*ghostly aura) by hunting monsters.

 

Base requirement: 1500 Yin Qi

 

Lowest-level mummy: ~100 Yin Qi

 

Average ghost girl: ~300 Yin Qi

 

Millennial Tree Demon (Boss): ~15,000 Yin Qi

 

If you defeat smaller monsters along the way, a total S-rank score is possible.

 

After entering the dungeon, you'll appear in a forest. Head south to find the ruined Orchid Temple, where a strange Taoist priest named Yan Chixia resides.

 

Don't underestimate him. He may look disheveled, but he's a powerful demon-slaying expert who wields high-level Daoist techniques.

 

If you're not confident in soloing the boss, it's wise to gain Chixia's trust. With his help, taking down the Millennial Tree Demon becomes significantly easier.

 

However—be careful. If he lands the killing blow, he gets all the Yin Qi. Even if you do most of the damage, the system only rewards whoever gets the final strike.

 

His giant sword is a rare anti-demon item. Unless you're strong enough, don't even think about trying to take it from him.

 

On the second day, a timid scholar named Naichen will arrive at the temple while traveling to take the imperial exam.

 

Avoid him. He's not helpful and easily becomes a liability.

 

Warning: Don't bring too many people into this dungeon. The Orchid Temple is under the domain of the Millennial Tree Demon, so other monsters stay away. Too many players means too few monsters to go around—fail to meet the Yin Qi quota, and you'll be erased.

 

The dungeon duration is seven days. Make every hour count.

 

Final note: This dungeon is extremely difficult. Be prepared to attempt it more than once.

 6

After reading the strategy, Fenric almost laughed aloud.

 

There was one glaring omission—Nie Lillian, the most important plot character, wasn't even mentioned.

 

Lillian held the key to entering the underworld.

 

In the underworld, the opportunities for monster hunting were practically endless.

 

But of course, no one else knew the full story like he did. And with only seven days granted by the system, it was unlikely other Samsaras could trigger the crucial events involving Lillian and the Black Mountain Demon in time.

 

So their ignorance was understandable.

 

But Fenric was different.

 

He knew the plot.

 

And now, a rough plan was already taking shape in his mind.

chapters.name: Chapter 212: Chapter 212: All Scared Away!
chapters.content:
01:22 AM.

 

That was the time.

 

Fenric paused to think, then returned briefly to the real world. After confirming that everything was normal, he came back to the Samsara Space.

 

Without delay, he headed straight for the Samsara Tower.

 

Standing before its gates, Fenric used a dungeon cooldown-refresh card.

 

He had previously acquired one from "Kung Fu Hustle" and still had one refresh left. For now, his stock of cooldown cards was more than enough.

 

He stepped forward.

 

Fenric arrived on the eighth floor.

 

An elf spirit materialized out of thin air and greeted him.

 

"Hello, dear Samsara participant—Shura. How may I assist you today?"

 

"I'm here to run a dungeon," Fenric said.

 

"Very well. Please select the dungeon world you wish to enter."

 

With a wave of her hand, a holographic projection appeared before Fenric.

 

Two options lit up on the screen:

 

Blade Runner (Normal)

 

A Bride Ghost Story (Difficult)

 

Fenric didn't hesitate. He immediately selected A Bride Ghost Story.

 

Selection confirmed.

 

The next moment, he was teleported into a sterile white room.

 

There were only six or seven other people present.

 4

As Fenric appeared, several participants frowned.

 

This dungeon had relatively few monsters and ghosts—one person could clear it alone. Two was manageable. Three made things tight. Four practically guaranteed one person would be eliminated.

 

The more players there were, the fiercer the competition—more wolves, less meat.

 

No one wanted someone else encroaching on their chances.

 

"Tch. Another person joined? Let me scare him off."

 

One Samsara participant scowled and began to approach Fenric.

 

"Don't!"

 

Another participant grabbed his arm urgently.

 

"That guy's no ordinary player—he's Shura! We can't afford to mess with him."

 

"What? Why should we give way?" the first man protested. "Red Devil, since when did you get so timid?"

 

"Are you stupid? You seriously don't recognize the Shura God himself? If you've got the guts, go challenge him. But I'm out of here!"

 

"...F*k, I didn't notice at first. Red Devil, wait up, bro!"

 

When the others overheard it was Shura, they were visibly stunned. After a brief hesitation, they left one by one.

 

In the end, only two participants remained.

 

Fenric: "..."

 

He hadn't expected this.

 

Was he already that intimidating?

 

Just his presence alone could make people flee?

 

Still, it was fine. Less interference, less trouble.

 

He glanced at the two who stayed behind but said nothing. Since they chose to remain even after learning who he was, it meant they weren't easily scared.

 

No words were needed. The challenge had already been accepted.

 

Fenric knew the plot—was he supposed to be afraid of a little competition?

 

Time passed quickly.

 

Soon, only ten minutes remained.

 

Once the countdown entered the final ten minutes, players could no longer quit, and no new participants could join.

 

The two remaining players exchanged conflicted looks, hesitated... and finally logged out.

 

They knew well—it was foolish to compete with a Shura-level boss.

 

A system message echoed:

 

"Attention all Samsara participants: the mission world teleportation will begin in ten minutes."

 

Now, only Fenric remained in the preparation room.

 

Though it was originally a public dungeon, it had effectively become Fenric's solo run.

 

The ten-minute timer ran out.

 

Another system prompt followed:

 

"Teleportation countdown commencing—10, 9, 8... 3, 2, 1!"

 

As the countdown hit zero, a red glow enveloped Fenric.

 

He vanished.

 

When Fenric regained his vision, he found himself standing in a forest.

 

Flowers bloomed across the ground, willows swayed gently, and the scenery was serene and beautiful.

 

However—

 

Despite the apparent sunshine and calm, the wind carried a strange chill.

 

Even with Fenric's strong physique, he could feel the oppressive presence of Yin Qi in the air.

 

The system prompt rang out again:

 

"Main Mission Issued

 

Objective: Collect Yin Qi.

 

Current Progress: 0/1500

 

Task Details: Defeat evil entities to absorb Yin Qi.

 

Time Limit: Seven Days

 

Failure Condition: Obliteration

 

Note: The more Yin Qi you collect, the higher your mission rating will be!"

 

Hearing the prompt, Fenric looked up at the sky. The sun was already dipping toward the horizon.

 

He began heading south.

 

According to the official guide, the south led to Orchid Temple, where Yan Chixia was currently staying.

 

Fenric's plan was simple: meet Chixia and ask if he could escort him directly into the underworld. If that worked, he wouldn't have to go through Lillian's storyline.

 

An hour later—

 

Fenric stood outside a dilapidated temple, deep in the jungle.

 

The temple looked ancient and abandoned. Ivy crept over its crumbling walls.

 

A moss-covered stone stele stood at the entrance. On it were carved characters: Orchid Temple.

 

By now, the sun had completely set. Night wrapped its cold arms around the forest.

 

Fenric didn't hesitate. He stepped through the archway into the temple courtyard.

 

The yard was overgrown with weeds, untended for years.

 

Just as Fenric was about to go deeper inside, a figure leapt down from an attic above and landed firmly in front of him.

 

"Kid, this isn't a place you should be poking around in," the man warned.

 

He was a middle-aged man with thick eyebrows, sharp eyes, a bushy beard, and a rugged aura. He wasn't tall, but his presence was formidable.

 

Fenric immediately recognized him—Yan Chixia.

 

"Senior, are you the famed hero Chixia?" Fenric asked respectfully, bowing slightly.

 

His appearance had been adjusted by the system—he now wore ancient-style robes fitting the dungeon's era.

 

Chixia looked surprised. "You know me?"

 

Fenric smiled. "There are many portraits of Hero Chixia outside. You're quite famous."

 

Chixia nodded in understanding.

 

Over the past few years, he had meddled in many affairs, offended numerous officials, and was long wanted by the government.

 

"You know I'm a wanted man, and you're still here?"

 

Chixia narrowed his eyes, feigning hostility.

 

Fenric, having read the original story, knew Chixia was righteous beneath his gruff exterior. Otherwise, he wouldn't have saved the protagonist Naichen.

 

"I've heard about Hero Chixia's integrity. I don't believe a word the government says."

 

Fenric clasped his hands again.

 

"Master Chixia, I have a request."

comments.content: thanks for the chapter and thanks for your hard work and can't wait for more chapters soon

chapters.name: Chapter 213: Chapter 213: Special Item, Empyrean Sword
chapters.content:
"Don't listen, don't listen!"

 

Chixia didn't give Fenric a chance to speak. "Kid, this isn't a place for you. Get out of here—now!"

 

Fenric was a little speechless.

 

He knew Chixia meant well, but that tone was hard to swallow.

 

"Beardy, you don't need to worry. Isn't it just a Thousand-Year Tree Demon?"

 

"...Huh?"

 

Chixia was stunned. "You know there are monsters here and still dare to come?"

 

"Of course. I'm here to slay demons."

 

Fenric wasn't afraid of the Thousand-Year Tree Demon.

 

Based on its depiction in the film, that genderless, grotesque spirit only had disgusting attacks. In terms of real strength, it wasn't much.

 

The real trouble was the Old Black Mountain Demon from the underworld—that one was tricky. Fenric wasn't fully confident about him.

 

That's why he came to find Chixia. He wanted to team up to face the real boss.

 

"Arrogant brat!"

 

Chixia gave him a few more glances and snorted. "What's your current cultivation? And you dare to talk about killing demons? Do you know that tree demon has cultivated for over a thousand years? You're courting death!"

 7

Fenric couldn't be bothered to explain.

 

He asked directly, "Beardy, my real target is the Old Black Mountain Demon hiding in the underworld. Can you take me to him?"

 

"You even want to go after that thing!?"

 

Chixia stared at him like he was looking at a madman.

 

The Black Mountain Demon had profound Taoist power. Even he wouldn't dare provoke such a terrifying existence.

 

Fenric still looked young—no matter how early he'd started cultivating, even from the womb, he couldn't possibly be a match for the Black Mountain Demon.

 

"You really don't know how high the heavens are!"

 

Chixia scoffed. "Who's your master? I'd like to ask them why they trained a fool like you just to send him to his death!"

 

Fenric sighed.

 

This guy's too stubborn!

 

"Beardy, it looks like you won't take me seriously unless I show you something. No offense, then."

 

As his words fell, Fenric activated his Telekinesis power.

 

Chixia, standing opposite, suddenly felt his body freeze—unable to move. He was pulled forward, completely out of his own control.

 

Startled, Chixia struggled repeatedly but found he couldn't resist at all.

 

Though a martial arts master, Chixia was still within mortal limits. With Fenric's current strength, his Telekinesis power could lift objects weighing over a thousand catties. Controlling someone like Chixia was no problem at all.

 

Fenric then clenched his hand into a claw and reached for Chixia's neck.

 

Alarmed, Chixia shouted,

 

"Heaven and Earth in Harmony—Empyrean Sword Technique!"

 

Buzz!

 

From the room behind, a heavy sword flew out with a low hum.

 

"Form of the Sword—Manifest!"

 

Another shout, and the epee shot straight toward Fenric like a deadly arrow!

 

Fenric recognized it as Chixia's Taoist technique—and he admired it.

 

But…

 

Hurting him? Almost impossible!

 

Armament Haki instantly coated Fenric's palm.

 

At the same time, he activated his Telekinesis again, locking onto the flying sword in mid-air.

 

Then—he reached out with an open hand and grabbed the sword's edge head-on.

 

Chixia was stunned and tried to warn him.

 

"Be careful!"

 

But in the next moment—

 

His voice stopped.

 

A look of shock appeared on his face.

 

Fenric's palm firmly grasped the sword, and aside from a minor cut that bled slightly, there was no real injury.

 

That sword… it could slice through copper and iron. Yet it barely scratched this young man's hand?

 1

What kind of monster was he?

 

What Chixia didn't know was that Fenric himself was just as surprised.

 

This was the first time a sharp weapon had actually broken his skin since he began using Armament Haki.

 

Then came the system alert.

 

Ding! Special item detected.

 

Item: Empyrean Divine Sword.

 

Forged in ancient times, this divine blade is peerless and holds strong power over demons and spirits.

 

Note: Only Taoist cultivators can unleash its full potential.

 

Fenric was stunned once again.

 

He had read the guide before coming here. He knew Chixia's sword was a special item.

 

But this?

 

A legendary divine weapon?

 

No wonder, in the original story, the Old Black Mountain Demon was slain with a single strike from this blade!

 

In that moment—

 

Fenric's desire was stirred.

 

Even if he couldn't wield Taoist techniques, this sword had innate power to restrain demons. The next time he encountered a ghost-infested dungeon, having this weapon would make things much easier.

 1

"Hey! Who are you really?" Chixia demanded. "And what technique did you just use?"

 

Fenric casually withdrew his Telekinesis grip and let go of Chixia.

 

"Beardy, now do you understand how capable I am?"

 

"Hmph!" Chixia snorted. "I'll admit you've got some skill. But if you think that's enough to take on the Old Black Mountain Demon, you're dreaming!"

 

Chixia was a demon-slaying specialist, a master of martial techniques.

 

But Fenric wasn't a demon—and with his current abilities, Chixia had no chance of matching him.

 

At this point, Fenric's strength had already reached the level of an A-rank boss. He was no longer some green rookie.

 

"Are you dumb or something?" Fenric frowned, his tone growing blunt. "Since I dared to come after the Old Black Mountain Demon, I obviously have my own plan. Quit the nonsense—just tell me how to get to the underworld!"

 

"You—!"

 

Chixia's face flushed with anger.

 

But still, he answered, "The Black Mountain Demon is entrenched in the City of the Dead, between the border of yin and yang. The living can't enter. You'd need someone on the inside to open the way into the yang realm—otherwise, there's no way in."

 

Fenric immediately recalled the original plot.

 

In it, Lillian had been captured for a ghost marriage, and Chixia had guided the protagonist into the underworld.

 

Looks like if he wanted to enter the underworld and take on the Black Mountain Demon, he'd need to work with Lillian after all.

 

"Hey! Kid! Give me back my sword!"

 

Chixia saw Fenric still holding his weapon and quickly demanded it back.

 

"Here."

 

Fenric tossed the sword back to him without hesitation.

 

It wasn't that he didn't want it—

 

But he still needed Chixia's help to enter the underworld.

 

Of course…

 

If something happened and Chixia lost the sword while inside the Black Mountain Demon's territory…

 

Well, Fenric wouldn't feel too bad about "picking it up."

 

"Beardy, I'll deal with the Thousand-Year Tree Demon first. After that, I'll find a way to get the Black Mountain Demon to open the path from the inside."

 

"Once that's done, you take me in."

chapters.name: Chapter 214: Chapter 214: Girl Lillian, Are You Tired from Acting?
chapters.content:
"Are you seriously planning to go after the old Black Mountain Demon?"

 

Chixia couldn't help but speak up. "That thing is a black mountain turned demon through cultivation! You provoke it, you die. How do you expect to kill it?"

 

Fenric didn't doubt Chixia's words.

 

In the original plot, Chixia's Empyrean Sword only managed to destroy a clone of the old demon. In the third part of [A Bride Ghost Story], the Lord of Black Mountain reappears as a massive mountain-shaped entity—terrifying beyond imagination.

 

Fenric's plan was simpler: enter the underworld, slaughter the countless ghosts and demons under the Black Mountain Demon's command, and harvest a massive amount of Yin value.

 

As for killing the Black Mountain Demon himself?

 

That wasn't a requirement—just a bonus.

 

"I want to give it a try."

 

With that, Fenric activated his disguise skill, feigning righteousness. "I heard the Black Mountain Demon is a great scourge—its sins innumerable. I'm going to eliminate it and bring peace to the people!"

 

Chixia: "…"

 

He seriously suspected the young man in front of him was either insane or unbelievably naive.

 

"You're sincere, and I don't want to crush that. But that demon is terrifying beyond belief. You can't possibly handle it."

 

Fenric suddenly grinned. "Hey, Bearded One, how about a bet?"

 

He eyed Chixia's sword. "Your sword looks nice. If I manage to kill the Black Mountain Demon, how about you give it to me?"

 

Chixia was taken aback, then barked out a curse. "You brat—you've got good eyes! This sword is a treasure. But fine. If you really can kill that monster, I'll personally hand it over to you!"

 

"Deal!" Fenric laughed. "But first, I'll kill that old tree demon. After that, I'll find a way into the Dead City, and then you—yeah, you—will help me go after that monster in Black Mountain!"

 

Chixia frowned. "That old witch is no joke. Its true form is a thousand-year-old tree demon, and it's drained countless men of their pure yang energy. Its magic is boundless. Even I wouldn't face it head-on."

 

"Then wait for my news."

 

Fenric didn't bother arguing. He left those words behind and turned away, striding into the night.

 

A long night—the perfect time for demons to dance.

 

Leaving Orchid Temple, Fenric didn't go far. He stopped in a stretch of wilderness, caught a hare using his Telekinesis powers, gathered some dry branches, and lit a fire to roast it.

 

As for the fire source?

 

Whether it was Thor's Hammer or the Mark VII suit, both had built-in ignition functions.

 1

And this fire wasn't just for cooking.

 

Fenric deliberately made it large and obvious—an invitation to any nearby female ghosts.

 1

Soon, the rabbit meat was nearly done. Just as Fenric was about to take his first bite, the distant sound of a zither began to drift through the night air.

 

In the dead of night, deep in deserted wildlands, someone was playing a zither?

 

Any fool could sense something was wrong.

 

Well—except for fools like the protagonist Naichen.

 

Fenric, fully aware this was a female ghost's baiting technique, picked up his rabbit meat and casually followed the music.

 

A short while later, Fenric reached a riverbank.

 

An elegant attic stood by the water, and from within, a beautiful woman dressed in flowing white played the qin gracefully.

 

She looked to be around eighteen or nineteen. Her hair fell like a waterfall, and her features were delicate—brows like distant mountains, eyes like moonlit stars, and skin glowing with a soft, cloud-like radiance.

 

She was breathtaking.

 

As beautiful as a figure painted by a master.

 

Even Fenric couldn't help but sigh—this girl was stunning enough to make hearts race.

 

No wonder Naichen had refused to believe she was a ghost.

 

This was Lillian.

 

Yes, the very same.

 

And coincidentally, Fenric was looking for her.

 

When Lillian finished her piece, Fenric clapped.

 

"Beautiful," he said with a grin. "I don't know much about music, but it sure sounded good to me."

 

Lillian feigned surprise and panic, her expression pitiful. "Who are you? W-Why are you here?"

 

It was an act, of course.

 

She'd served the old tree demon for years, luring countless men to their doom. She was more skilled at seduction than any club girl.

 

Normally, one little show of panic was enough for men to throw themselves at her.

 

But tonight felt… off.

 

She waited a long moment, yet Fenric didn't so much as budge.

 

Still seated, still smiling, he simply watched her.

 

Suspicious now, she peeked up at him—this strange, handsome man who showed no lust in his eyes.

 

Was he... immune?

 

She gritted her teeth. Time to ramp it up.

 

Suddenly, she stumbled and fell—right into a nearby branch.

 

Riiiip.

 

Her clothes tore, revealing a large expanse of fair skin.

 

"Ah!"

 

She cried out, hugging herself and sneakily glancing at Fenric again.

 

Still no reaction.

 

He just kept smiling.

 

Fenric was watching a show—her performance.

 

Truthfully, Lillian's acting was excellent. If Fenric didn't already know the story and her identity as a ghost, even he might have been fooled.

 

At last, seeing her efforts, he decided to speak.

 

"Miss Lillian," he said cheerfully, "you've been acting for quite a while now. Aren't you tired? Want a break?"

 

When Fenric called her by name, her face immediately paled.

 

"Who… who are you?" she stammered.

 

"Me?" Fenric smiled. "I'm here to save you, Miss Lillian."

 

"Save me?" Lillian narrowed her eyes. "And how exactly do you plan to do that, my 'savior'?"

 

"Simple," Fenric said. "I know your bones are buried and suppressed under the thousand-year-old tree demon. You're being forced to do this. Just tell me where that old thing's real body is, and I'll help you destroy it. Free you from this cursed fate. Let you reincarnate."

 

"!!"

 

Now she was truly shaken.

 

"Who… who are you?" she asked again, trembling.

 

Fenric shrugged. "Still don't believe me?"

 

He glanced at her ankle.

 

There, a delicate bell was fastened—the same bell used to summon the thousand-year tree demon.

 

In the story, every time she lured in a man, Lillian would ring the bell to summon her "grandma" to feed.

 

With a flick of his finger, the bell snapped free and flew into Fenric's palm, guided by his Telekinesis.

 

"Stop! Don't touch that!"

 

Lillian's face turned pale as she lunged to stop him—but it was already too late.

chapters.name: Chapter 215: Chapter 215: Thousand-Year Tree Demon
chapters.content:
"This bell must belong to Miss Lillian… used to summon that old witch, right?"

 

Fenric smiled as he held the small bell between his fingers.

 

"My lord, don't shake it! If you do, Grandma will come!" Lillian cried out anxiously.

 

In truth, after Fenric exposed all her secrets, Lillian had begun to believe him—at least a little. She had long dreamed of escaping her torment, but never had the chance. Her bones had been suppressed by the Thousand-Year Tree Demon, trapping her in servitude, unable to reincarnate. All she could do was carry out the demon's bidding.

 

"Don't worry, Miss Lillian. Since I said I'd save you, I will save you." Fenric twirled the bell thoughtfully and asked, "Let me ask you something—I've heard that old tree demon has ties to the Black Mountain Demon. Did she promise to give you to him as a concubine?"

 

"My lord… how do you know that?" Lillian's eyes widened in shock.

 

Fenric chuckled lightly. "Oh, just a wild guess. So it's true, then? She really betrothed you to that Black Mountain freak?"

 

Lillian nodded sadly, her voice soft and pitiful. "You're right. Grandma has already promised me to the Black Mountain Demon. In seven days… I'll be wed."

 

Seven days?

 

That's exactly when the mission ends.

 

The Samsara System really knows how to time things.

 

No wonder the Samsara Tower had existed for so long, and the other Samsaras still didn't realize how important Lillian was—or how big a boss the Black Mountain Demon actually was.

 

It seemed if Fenric wanted to infiltrate the Black Mountain Demon's territory, he had to find a way to push the wedding forward.

 

His eyes turned to Lillian again. Seeing her sorrowful face stirred a strange feeling in his heart.

 

She wasn't just beautiful—her natural charm made every glance and movement tug at a person's soul.

 

"Miss Lillian, like I said, if I say I'll save you, I will. But I have a plan—and I'll need your help."

 

Fenric struck a heroic pose and activated his disguise skill, appearing like a righteous hero with the world on his shoulders.

 

"I came here to vanquish evil and save the innocent. The Black Mountain Demon has committed countless atrocities. I've long wanted to rid the world of his blight.

 

So, lovely lady… will you help me destroy some demons~?"

 

Lillian was taken aback. "My lord, the Black Mountain Demon has cultivated for ten thousand years. How could I possibly help you?"

 

"You can start by taking me to his domain," Fenric asked directly.

 

Lillian shook her head, apologetic. "I'm sorry, my lord. The Black Mountain Demon resides in the City of the Dead. If he doesn't open the passage, no one can enter."

 

Fenric nodded, then grinned. "No problem. Let's deal with that old tree demon first. She's been bullying you for too long."

 

With that, he raised the bell and gave it a firm shake.

 

Ding ding dang dong—!

 

The bell's chime wasn't loud, but it pierced the air like a blade, traveling far and wide.

 

Lillian's face turned pale with horror. It was too late to stop him.

 

"My lord, she's coming! Hurry, leave while you still can!" she pleaded. "Grandma's power runs deep—you're no match for her. Please, trust me and go!"

 

In the original storyline, Lillian was kindhearted. Though she served her "grandma," she despised the suffering it caused. Every time she witnessed the tree demon devour humans, she would silently weep.

 

Now, with Fenric here to save her, she didn't want him to die in vain.

 

Fenric sighed.

 

First, Chixia didn't believe in him. Now even Lillian thought he couldn't defeat the Thousand-Year Tree Demon?

 

Did he really look that weak?

 

Whatever.

 

Too lazy to argue.

 

With a flick of his wrist, Fenric summoned a cloak.

 

Night Demon Cloak.

 

Wearing it would imbue his attacks with spiritual energy, letting him strike ghosts, demons, and monsters with full effectiveness.

 

He slung the cloak over his shoulders, then drew his black sword—Shusui.

 

And in his storage… he still had a divine weapon:

 

Thor's Hammer.

 

Thunder—the ultimate bane of demons.

 

With the Night Demon Cloak and Thor's Hammer, even if more tree demons show up, he could flatten them without mercy.

 

These two items were the reason Fenric dared to tackle the [A Bride Ghost Story] dungeon.

 

Otherwise, how would he even consider challenging the Black Mountain Demon?

 

Fenric wasn't one to gamble on uncertainty.

 

Suddenly—

 

Whoosh—whoosh!

 

A fierce wind howled around them, stirring sand and shaking trees violently.

 

Nearby locust trees bent and moaned, their leaves shrieking.

 

Lillian's face went pale. "She's here!" she cried.

 

"Miss Lillian, step back."

 

As Fenric spoke, the earth began to quake.

 

Thick, serpent-like tree roots slithered from the ground, coiling around him from every direction.

 

BOOM—!

 

Something massive was charging from the distance.

 

Looking closely—

 

It was a grotesque tongue, thicker than a human body!

 

Fenric didn't hesitate. With a sharp swing—

 

Shing—!

 

Splurt!

 

Shusui sliced the tongue clean in two.

 

"AARGH—!!"

 

A thunderous, otherworldly scream rang out—deeper and more chilling than a wild beast's cry.

 

The Thousand-Year Tree Demon had just taken a serious hit.

 

Next moment, a figure materialized before Fenric.

 

It was difficult to tell if this middle-aged person was male or female, but from the clothes, she appeared more feminine.

 

This was none other than the Thousand-Year Tree Demon—the "Grandma" Lillian spoke of.

 

She wore a dark crimson robe. Her hair was styled high like an old matron's, and her features bore a demonic elegance. A millennium of cultivation had allowed her to assume a human form.

 

"Who are you!?" she asked coldly.

 

Her voice shifted as she spoke—sometimes deep and rough like a man, sometimes shrill and sharp like a woman. The dissonance made Fenric's skin crawl.

 

Ignoring her tone, Fenric pointed directly at Lillian and said bluntly:

 

"Old witch, that female ghost is yours? Well, she's mine now!"

 

He intentionally provoked her.

 

As expected, the Thousand-Year Tree Demon, hearing herself called an old witch and realizing Fenric intended to take the one ghost she relied on most, erupted with fury.

 

"Presumptuous!"

 

Without warning, countless tree branches—thick as legs—lashed toward Fenric like an army of pythons, coming from every direction.

 

A dense, overwhelming assault.

 

Fenric quickly sheathed Shusui and summoned Thor's Hammer.

 

Then, he raised it high.

 

BOOM—!!

 

As if in answer, the heavens growled with thunder.

 

The sky darkened instantly, clouds surging overhead...

chapters.name: Chapter 216: Chapter 216: This Person is Terrifying!
chapters.content:
BOOM—!

 

A flash of lightning split the sky.

 

Thunder crashed down, striking Fenric's Thor's Hammer directly.

 

Countless bolts of lightning were drawn into the hammer. Arcs of thunder danced wildly around Fenric, enveloping him in an electric storm.

 

He stood like a deity in the heart of lightning.

 

Even the thick surrounding branches dared not approach him anymore.

 

Faced with such violent power, the ancient tree demon and Lillian instinctively trembled with fear.

 

Lillian, especially, was so frightened that she kept backing away, like a startled cat.

 

She could feel it clearly—if that lightning struck her, she would be obliterated!

 

In the next moment, Fenric pointed the Thor's Hammer toward the ancient tree demon. A thick thunder dragon burst out, roaring from the hammer and racing across the sky, striking the distant monster with blinding force.

 

Zzzzt!

 

A massive explosion erupted where the lightning landed, forming a thunderous blast radius filled with crackling electric arcs.

 

Within a hundred meters, the land was scorched—barren and blackened.

 

"AHHHHH!!!"

 

The tree demon had no time to dodge—it was the speed of light! The strike landed squarely, and a wretched scream echoed as its body charred on the spot.

 1

In the blink of an eye, the tree demon clone turned into a smoldering chunk of burnt wood.

 

All the surrounding branches instantly recoiled, vanishing without a trace.

 1

Far off in the distance, the real body of the tree demon reappeared. Pale-faced, it stared at Fenric in sheer terror.

 

Just now, one of his clones had been annihilated by that thunder in a single strike!

 

He never expected that this human could command such terrifying lightning.

 

Thunder—descended from the heavens—was the natural nemesis of all demons!

 

Luckily, the ancient demon was always cautious. Whenever he went out to devour humans, he never used his main body.

 

If that had been his true form just now, he would've been dead!

 

There would've been no chance to resist.

 

He scrutinized Fenric from afar and realized—he was merely a mortal. At most, his vitality and blood were stronger than average.

 

But how could a mortal command thunder?

 

Was he... the reincarnation of the Thunder God?

 

From a distance, Fenric's voice rang out loudly:

 

"Old demon! I know you're still alive! From now on, this beautiful ghost is mine. If you've got a problem with that, come to Orchid Temple and face me! Even if that old bastard Black Mountain shows up—I'm not scared!"

 

Fenric intentionally raised his voice when mentioning Black Mountain, making sure the old demon heard every word.

 

Sure enough, the tree demon took the bait. She turned to leave—intent on informing the Black Mountain Old Demon.

 

It wasn't a bad move. After all, she'd already promised Lillian to the Black Mountain demon. Technically, she belonged to that demon now.

 

If someone else stole her, it wasn't her problem.

 

Let Black Mountain handle it.

 

She'd just sit back and enjoy the show.

 

With that, the old tree demon's figure vanished.

 

She had no intention of provoking that terrifying human again.

 

Even more terrifying than the bearded man in Orchid Temple!

 

"My lord, the tree demon has fled," Lillian whispered cautiously.

 

Fenric lowered Thor's Hammer in his hand.

 

Instantly, the storm clouds dispersed, and sunlight returned.

 

Fenric was very pleased with the power of the hammer.

 

Fighting monsters with lightning was way too convenient.

 

"Miss Lillian, do you believe now that I can save you?" he said with a slight smile.

 

Lillian looked at him in awe, then suddenly knelt down.

 

"I didn't realize the great god had descended in person. Please forgive my ignorance!"

 

Fenric blinked in surprise.

 

Did she just call him a god?

 

"Stand up," he said helplessly. "I'm not a god. I'm just a human."

 

"A... human?" Lillian looked disbelieving. "How can a human command thunder from the heavens?"

 

Fenric scratched his head. "Just assume I have... boundless magic."

 

"Anyway, I said I can save you, and I will. But I'll need your help in return—to lure out the Black Mountain demon."

 

Seeing his strength, Lillian nodded without hesitation. "Thank you for your grace. I'll cooperate however you need!"

 

Fenric nodded with a smile.

 

At that moment—

 

A loud voice rang out from the distance: "Where's the monster?!"

 

A figure soared through the air and landed before them.

 

It was Chixia!

 

When he saw Lillian, he glared and shouted, "You vile spirit! How dare you show yourself again? Die!"

 

Shing!

 

With a flash, his sword left its sheath, slashing toward her.

 

Lillian turned pale in terror. She had no time to dodge.

 

Fenric sighed and used his Telekinesis to shove Chixia aside, saving her.

 

"Seriously, Big Beard? Can't you assess the situation first before swinging your sword?"

 

Chixia looked at him, frowning. "Boy, she's a ghost! Why are you protecting her?"

 

"I know she's a ghost—but not all ghosts are evil," Fenric replied, shielding Lillian. "Lillian is kind-hearted. She's not like the others. Put away your sword."

 

"You fool! She was hanging around that old demon—no good ghost would do that!"

 

Lillian bit her lip, clearly upset by the accusation.

 

Fenric groaned. "I'm not arguing with you. You're too stubborn to convince. Let's head back to Orchid Temple and talk things out there."

 

"Wait!" Chixia paused, narrowing his eyes. "I heard thunder earlier. What happened?"

 

"Oh, that? I summoned lightning and destroyed a clone of the tree demon," Fenric said nonchalantly.

 

"What?!"

 

Chixia was stunned. "You can summon lightning? That's impossible!"

 

Fenric pointed to the blackened area in the distance. "See for yourself. That's where her clone burned. Go look."

 

Chixia followed the direction Fenric pointed to and found the thunder-charred zone.

 

At the center was the trunk of the clone—now just a husk of dead wood.

 

He'd been fighting that demon for years and could tell at a glance—it was the dryad's clone.

 

"You..."

 

Fenric waved dismissively. "If you've got more questions, save them. We'll talk later."

 

Chixia grunted. "Fine. What about the ghost?"

 

"She's Lillian. I'm saving her from her cursed fate. So she's coming with us."

chapters.name: Chapter 217: Chapter 217: Frightened the Old Dryad!
chapters.content:
"I was born into a family of officials.

 

My father was framed by a corrupt official and exiled three thousand miles away.

 

While traveling with him, I was murdered.

 

He buried my remains beneath an old locust tree.

 

I never expected that the locust tree had long since gained sentience and cultivated into a spirit.

 

It seized control of my bones, forcing me to seduce men and absorb their Yang energy on its behalf.

 

Now it wants to marry me off to the Black Mountain Demon..."

 

Inside Orchid Temple, Lillian recounted her tragic story, her voice choked with sobs and grief.

 

After hearing her out, Chixia's expression softened. The hostility in his eyes faded; he no longer held resentment toward Lillian.

 

Fenric stepped forward and comforted her, "Lillian, don't worry. You'll stay here tonight. At first light, we'll retrieve your bones. If that old tree demon dares interfere, I'll roast her into charcoal."

 

Upon hearing this, Lillian bowed deeply to Fenric. "Thank you, young master… If I recover my bones, I can finally reincarnate and stop harming others."

 

Fenric nodded and turned to Chixia. "Beardy, Miss Lillian is bound to the Black Mountain Demon through a forced marriage contract. If we just let her go, that monster won't take it lightly—he'll come for her. When he does, I want you to lead me into the Dead City. Deal?"

 

Chixia was stunned, then muttered, "So that's your plan? A clever scheme. It might work… but it's risky. That place is the demon's domain. They say countless monsters and ghosts roam its streets. Are you truly… sure?"

 

Fenric laughed confidently. "Don't worry, Beardy. I won't drag you into a trap. That old demon's committed too many sins—he should've been dead long ago!"

 

Fenric's bold declaration seemed to stir Chixia's blood. He shouted, "Alright then! I'll accompany you through this trial!"

 

Lillian, standing beside them, stole a glance at Fenric.

 

In the original tale, Lillian was easily moved. Just because Naichen didn't insult her and shielded her from a small snake, she grew fond of him—eventually falling for him in silence.

 

But Fenric had saved her directly. And compared to Naichen's timid demeanor, Fenric's image and aura were far more captivating. It was only natural that Lillian would be drawn to him.

 

The next morning.

 

At dawn, Lillian was nowhere to be seen.

 

Fenric understood—she was a female ghost, after all. She couldn't appear in daylight.

 

"Beardy, let's move."

 

Just as they were about to depart, Fenric asked, "By the way, you know where her bones are buried, right?"

 

"Yes, in the back mountain."

 

Soon, Chixia led Fenric behind Orchid Temple, to a desolate hill dotted with graves. It resembled a mass grave site.

 

Among the scattered tombs stood one belonging to Lillian.

 

Nearby, a massive old locust tree towered above them, its lush branches casting shadows over half the hillside and blotting out the sky.

 

Fenric asked, "Beardy, is this the old dryad's true body?"

 

"Yes… and no," Chixia replied, shaking his head.

 

"Don't talk in riddles. Just spit it out."

 

"It is her original body," Chixia explained. "But after cultivating into a spirit, she detached herself from it. Now, any of the locust trees on this mountain can serve as her vessel. You want to destroy her? Just felling this big tree won't work. You'd have to uproot every locust tree in the entire mountain."

 

Fenric nodded in realization.

 

No wonder Chixia stayed at Orchid Temple for so long in the original tale without killing the demon—it wasn't cowardice; the tree monster was simply too elusive and cunning to destroy.

 

In the story, even after a millennium, the tree demon wasn't truly slain—only severely wounded by Chixia.

 

"What if I destroy just this tree?" Fenric asked.

 

"That would wound her, yes. But not fatally. Worse—it would enrage her."

 

"Oh? Enrage her?" Fenric smirked. "Even better."

 

As soon as he finished speaking, Thor's Hammer appeared in his hand.

 

Chixia's eyes widened. "When did you bring a hammer?"

 

Fenric couldn't be bothered to explain. He raised the hammer high.

 

Suddenly—

 

Dark clouds rolled across the sky.

 

BOOM—!

 

Thunder cracked. What had been a clear morning was now cloaked in ominous black clouds. Even a fool could tell something unnatural was happening.

 

Chixia stared at Fenric in shock.

 

"Beardy, stay back!" Fenric warned.

 

Electric arcs began to flicker around his body as he summoned the storm.

 

BOOM—!

 

A lightning bolt surged down from the heavens, striking Thor's Hammer. The weapon absorbed it fully, crackling with divine energy.

 

Fenric stood bathed in lightning, like the God of Thunder himself.

 

Chixia instinctively backed away, face filled with awe and disbelief.

 

He had never imagined Fenric possessed such terrifying power.

 

Next moment—

 

With a swing of the hammer, Fenric unleashed a thunder dragon—a roaring bolt of electricity tearing through the air toward the ancient locust tree.

 

BOOM—!!!

 

A deafening explosion erupted.

 

Thunder and lightning danced in a wide radius. The trunk of the massive tree—thicker than an elephant's body—snapped with a thunderous crack.

 

Blood-red sap gushed from the wound.

 

Moments later, flames burst forth, devouring the ancient tree.

 

"ROOOAR!!!"

 

A pained howl echoed through the mountain, like a wounded beast.

 

"Ahhhhhh!!"

 

The nearby locust trees screamed in response, their shrieks sharp and piercing like magical cries.

 

With a clang, Chixia unsheathed his sword, watching the surroundings warily.

 

But Fenric remained calm.

 

"Keep howling," he muttered coldly, "and I'll blow up your whole mountain!"

 

With another swing of Thor's Hammer—

 

BOOM—! BOOM—! BOOM—!

 

Lightning rained from the blackened skies, smashing into tree after tree.

 

In mere breaths, the hillside was devastated—splintered trunks, scorched earth, smoldering roots.

 

It was as if the mountain had been bombarded by missiles.

 

Then—silence.

 

All the ghostly wails vanished. The remaining locust trees visibly trembled in terror.

 

Gulp.

 

Chixia swallowed hard, staring blankly at Fenric.

 

Brutal!

chapters.name: Chapter 218: Chapter 218: Evil Thief, Let Go of Lillian!
chapters.content:
"Huff... Huff..."

 

The raging fire continued to burn fiercely.

 

Fenric's madness had caused widespread devastation to the surrounding area.

 

The old tree demon was trembling in fear!

 

Even Chixia looked visibly shaken!

 

The power Fenric had just unleashed was terrifying beyond words.

 

Controlling Sky Thunder?

 

How could any normal human possibly do that?

 

The next moment, Fenric calmly stowed away Thor's Hammer.

 

Blowing up the mountain wasn't his true goal—it was a warning, a show of overwhelming power meant to frighten the Thousand-Year Tree Demon.

 

Releasing thunder through Thor's Hammer consumed immense mental energy. With Fenric's current spiritual reserves, he couldn't sustain it for long.

 

Even in the Marvel movies, Thor himself couldn't continuously summon thunder with his hammer. It took a toll.

 3

As Fenric stored the hammer, the dark clouds above quickly dispersed, and the sky returned to clear, sunny weather.

 

"Beardy, stop staring. Dig out Lillian's bones already."

 

Snapped out of his shock, Chixia shot Fenric a complicated look, then started digging.

 

As for the nearby locust trees? Not one dared to make a sound—not even a fart.

 

Fenric's destructive power had left a lasting impression on the old tree demon. At this point, it desperately hoped Fenric would leave soon.

 

This human... is a nightmare incarnate!

 

Soon after, Lillian's grave was unearthed.

 

Just like in the original tale, five black-gold pagodas(*or stele) were found buried within.

 

Chixia blinked in surprise. "Why are there so many?"

 

"Take them all," Fenric replied.

 

He collected all five pagodas without hesitation.

 

That night...

 

Fenric was about to summon Lillian when a loud voice rang out outside Orchid Temple.

 

"Chixia! I know you're hiding in there! Come out and fight me!"

 

Inside, Chixia's expression stiffened. A helpless look crossed his face as he sighed, "Brother Yihao... he's here to spar again."

 

Fenric nodded, already recognizing this part of the story. This was where the original plot began to unfold.

 

In that version, the old man Yihao ended up dying miserably—drained dry by the Thousand-Year Tree Demon.

 

"If it's your business, then deal with it yourself," Fenric said coolly.

 

Chixia nodded, drew his sword, and dashed out the door.

 

Soon after, the clanging of blades and martial arts echoed from outside.

 

Fenric turned his gaze to the five golden pagodas and called out, "Lillian, you can come out now."

 

"Young Master, I'm here~"

 

Fenric turned, exhaling silently. Why do these female ghosts always sound sexy?

 

"Lillian, is your soul vessel among these pagodas?"

 

"Yes," she replied, pointing to one of them. "That one is mine."

 

Fenric helped her up, picked up the corresponding golden pagoda, and then turned to the others.

 

"Alright, the rest of you—go reincarnate already!"

 1

From the void, four voices echoed in unison:

 

"Thank you, Young Master!"

 

And with that, the remaining four pagodas vanished.

 

Fenric could have absorbed them for a good sum of Yin points. But doing so would undermine the "hero" persona he had carefully cultivated. Besides, he had his eyes on far more powerful monsters in the City of the Dead.

 

These four were hardly worth the effort.

 

"Lillian, I still need your help dealing with the Old Black Mountain Demon. So, reincarnation will have to wait a little."

 

Lillian bowed deeply. "Say no more, Young Master. Your great kindness—Lillian will never forget it. If I can do anything to help you, I will gladly offer myself."

 

"Good," Fenric smiled. "Lillian, I need you to help me with a little performance."

 

"Please, give your orders."

 

"First, change your appearance—look miserable. Then go back to the Thousand-Year Tree Demon and cry to the old hag. Say I'm not human, that I abused you horribly, and demand to marry as soon as possible."

 

Then he added with a reassuring smile, "Of course, don't worry. With me here, I won't let the Black Mountain Demon lay a finger on you. The moment he shows up... is the day he dies."

 

Lillian, clever as ever, quickly caught on.

 

Her eyes lit up with admiration. What a bold and cunning man!

 1

"Yes, Young Master. I will make sure the act is convincing."

 

Immediately, she set about transforming herself.

 

First, she tore her clothes, then used spirit energy to create bruises and scratch marks on her skin. In no time, she looked pitifully abused.

 

"My Lord... how's this?"

 

Fenric glanced at her and felt something was still missing.

 

Then it clicked.

 

The hairstyle.

 

"Your hair's still too neat. Come here, I'll help."

 

He stepped forward and tousled her hair until it looked appropriately messy.

 

As he leaned in, Lillian caught a whiff of his masculine scent. Her mind turned blank.

 

Her cheeks flushed red, and she shyly averted her gaze.

 

A ghost... in love with a human... such a cruel fate.

 

There could be no future between them.

 

"All done!" Fenric said, stepping back. He nodded in satisfaction at her appearance.

 

Now, Lillian looked completely miserable—tattered clothes, disheveled hair, bruised skin. She was the very image of a woman abused by a heartless man.

 

"Evil thief! Let go of that girl!"

 

Suddenly, a voice barked from behind.

 

The tone was righteous, but it carried a hint of hesitation.

 

Fenric's keen senses had already detected the stranger long ago. He just didn't find it worth acknowledging—until now.

 

Turning around, he saw a young scholar carrying a bundle on his back.

 

He was delicate in appearance—thin, refined, with a gentle elegance.

 

The protagonist of this world—Naichen.

 

At the sight of him, Fenric felt instant annoyance.

 

This trash protagonist again.

 

He hated Naichen when he first watched the movie. The guy was just a pretty face, surviving only because the heroine constantly protected him.

 

Without Lillian, he would've been long dead—his soul sucked dry.

 

"Evil thief! Let go of that girl!" Naichen repeated.

 

The moment he saw Lillian, he was awestruck by her beauty. Her pitiful appearance stirred his righteous heart. Seeing Fenric "laying hands" on her, he instinctively intervened.

 

But something didn't feel right.

 

Both the "fairy" and the "villain" were calmly watching him.

 

Even worse, the "fairy" was hiding behind the villain... and she looked scared of him?

 

What... what is going on here?!

chapters.name: Chapter 219: Chapter 219: Queen — Lillian!
chapters.content:
"Lillian, you go first."

 

"Yes, young master!"

 

Neither of them paid Naichen any mind.

 

Lillian was just about to leave when Naichen suddenly stepped forward with a hopeful look.

 

"Miss, don't be afraid of that thief—I," he said, forcing a smile.

 

Pfft!

 

In the next instant, before Naichen could finish his sentence, he was sent flying through the air, coughing up blood mid-flight before crashing into a wall and falling unconscious.

 

He had been struck by a wave of Telekinesis from Fenric.

 

Ordinarily, a regular person would've died instantly from such a blow.

 

But Naichen, protected by the mysterious luck of the Son of Destiny, only ended up severely injured—but alive.

 

Startled, Lillian froze in place.

 

Fenric spoke calmly, "Lillian, follow the plan. If the old tree demon doesn't cooperate, tell her I'll uproot every locust tree in this forest within two days."

 

"Yes, young master."

 

Lillian didn't spare Naichen a single glance. She floated off without hesitation.

 

A short while later, Chixia returned.

 

"Hm?"

 

Noticing Naichen unconscious on the ground, he frowned. "What happened to this kid?"

 

Fenric replied indifferently, "He didn't know his place. Tried to provoke me, so I taught him a lesson."

 1

Chixia frowned. "Wasn't that a bit much?"

 

He had a vague feeling there might be some hidden connection between himself and Naichen.

 

"Well, he's the one who couldn't mind his own business. How was I supposed to know he was so fragile?" Fenric shrugged.

 

Chixia said nothing more.

 

In his eyes, Fenric was now the top priority.

 

With Fenric's power, he could finally see a chance to destroy the Black Mountain Old Demon.

 

As a man of righteousness, Chixia couldn't pass up the opportunity.

 

Still, he couldn't simply leave Naichen to die.

 

He quickly gathered some wooden sticks and fashioned a crude splint, securing Naichen's broken limbs. The poor boy had multiple fractures all over his body.

 

Once done, Chixia took out a healing pill and placed it into Naichen's mouth.

 

Fenric didn't bother to help. He simply found a comfortable spot, lay down, and closed his eyes for a nap.

 

—---

 

The Thousand-Year Tree Demon resided in a courtyard nestled in the center of a lake.

 

As night fell, more female ghosts emerged into the yard, their numbers growing.

 

Yet tonight, none of them dared to raise their voices.

 

Everyone could sense it—Grandma was in a terrible mood.

 

Terrible enough that even the wind felt colder.

 

The cause was obvious.

 

The commotion during the day had startled every spirit and demon within 50 kilometers.

 

A human had drawn down heavenly thunder, causing Grandma herself to suffer injuries.

 

Worse still, the human was absurdly powerful, and Grandma had no courage to retaliate.

 

Inside a dark room, the ancient tree demon, known to all as Grandma, sat sulking in a large chair.

 

Beside her, a female ghost in a flowing teal dress tried to console her.

 

"Grandma, please don't be angry. Even though my sister was taken away, you still have me. I'll serve you faithfully and help you catch many more handsome young men."

 

Grandma sighed. "Evy, you've always been the more sensible one. From now on, I'll be depending on you."

 

Though her words were kind, Grandma's thoughts were still with Lillian.

 

Lillian was not only stunningly beautiful, but also cunning and seductive—no man she targeted had ever escaped her grasp. She was her most valuable subordinate.

 

More than that, Lillian was a key piece in her alliance with the Black Mountain Demon.

 

With Lillian gone, how could she face that fearsome creature?

 

Just then, a female ghost's voice called from outside:

 

"Grandma, Sister Lillian has returned!"

 

"Oh?"

 

Grandma's expression changed instantly. "Quick, send her in!"

 

Moments later, Lillian burst into the room.

 

"Grandma!!"

 

She threw herself into the old demon's arms, weeping bitterly.

 

Seeing her disheveled and injured appearance, Grandma's face changed.

 

"Lillian? What happened? Why are you hurt like this?"

 

Lillian was a masterful actress. She immediately put on a pitiful expression and began sobbing.

 

"Grandma, he's horrible... he abuses people for fun! He beats me, scolds me, and even said he's going to eat me!"

 

Evy, standing to the side, couldn't help but smile gleefully at this.

 

Grandma glared at her but gently patted Lillian.

 

"Don't be scared, child. With a beauty like yours, what man would truly harm you?"

 

Lillian shook her head and cried even harder.

 

"No, Grandma! He's a monster in human skin! I don't want to stay with him anymore. Please, save me!"

 

"This..." Grandma hesitated and sighed. "Child, even I cannot deal with someone like him."

 

"Please, Grandma," Lillian begged. "He said that once he's bored of playing with me, he'll come for both of us!"

 

"What?!"

 

Grandma's eyes widened in shock, quickly replaced by rage.

 

That human had not only stolen her subordinate, but now dared to threaten her life?

 

This was going too far!

 1

But no matter how furious she felt, Grandma was helpless against that terrifying man.

 

If she weren't rooted to this place by her nature as a tree demon, she would've fled Orchid Temple long ago.

 

Now, she was caught between a rock and a hard place.

 

She couldn't fight him… and she couldn't run.

 

"Lillian! Lillian! Think of something, quickly!" Grandma snapped.

 

Lillian was just about to suggest her plan when Evy stepped in first.

 

"Grandma, have you forgotten?" Evy said with a sly smile. "Sister has a marriage agreement with the Black Mountain Demon. That man is far too powerful to face directly—we'll have to outsmart him."

 

She leaned closer.

 

"You could notify the Black Mountain Lord and let him deal with it. Considering how much he values Sister, he won't stand idly by."

 

"The Black Mountain Lord has cultivated for ten thousand years—his power is immense. If he and that human fight, surely one of them will be injured, if not both. Grandma, you might even benefit from their clash!"

 

Lillian's eyes narrowed. Evy had stolen the very words she was about to say.

 

Of course, she understood Evy's true motive—this wasn't help, it was a setup.

 

Evy wanted to push her from one fire pit into another.

 

But that was fine. If she'd said it herself, Grandma might've suspected something.

 

After all, what sane woman would willingly throw herself into the clutches of the Black Mountain Demon?

 

Coming from Evy, though, the plan sounded… reasonable.

 

"Evy, you have a point," Grandma said thoughtfully.

 

She had considered asking the Black Mountain Demon for help before.

 

But that old monster was notoriously hard to deal with—and his help came with a steep price.

 

Still, Evy's words made sense.

 

If those two powerhouses fought, and the Black Mountain Demon was wounded, she might just find a way to gain some of his power for herself!

chapters.name: Chapter 220: Chapter 220: Smash into the Underworld and Start Spawning Monsters!
chapters.content:
"Lillian, did you hear what Evy just said?"

 1

The old tree demon spoke with feigned righteousness. "Grandma doesn't seek to profit like a fisherman—so long as we can kill that man and avenge you, that is enough!"

 

Lillian quickly responded in full cooperation, "Everything is up to Grandma."

 

"Good." The old tree demon nodded in satisfaction, helping Lillian up. "In that case, I'll inform Master Black Mountain. He'll deal with him."

 

"Thank you, Grandma."

 

As if remembering something, Lillian suddenly added, "Grandma, I snuck out without permission. He might already be suspicious. I must hurry back before he notices."

 

The old tree demon smiled warmly. "You're always so thoughtful, Lillian."

 

"You'll have to endure a little longer. At most three days, and Master Black Mountain will take action. Once he's dead, you'll finally be safe."

 

"Lillian understands. Grandma, I'm heading back now."

 

"Go, then."

 

After leaving the old tree demon's lair, Lillian rushed straight toward Orchid Temple.

 

"My lord! Mission accomplished!"

 

The moment she saw Fenric, Lillian reported excitedly, "Grandma agreed. She's going to invite the Black Mountain Demon! She said within three days, Master Black Mountain will act!"

 

Her joy was unmistakable.

 

To serve the Young Master—it was her honor.

 

Fenric smiled, pleased. "Very good! Lillian, you've done well."

 

"It wasn't difficult at all. I'm happy just to be of help to you," she said, lowering her head shyly.

 

She didn't know why, but in front of Fenric, she always felt bashful.

 

Suddenly, a groan of pain came from the side.

 

It was Naichen. He had just regained consciousness and was writhing in pain.

 

"Don't move!" Chixia warned. "You've got several broken bones. I just realigned them. If you move now, you'll cripple yourself."

 

Naichen froze, terrified.

 

Then he saw Lillian and his eyes lit up—only to dim again the moment he noticed Fenric nearby. Fear overtook him.

 

He hadn't seen Fenric strike, but he could guess who had injured him.

 

This was Naichen—timid and spineless. Though he'd been hurt, he harbored no thoughts of revenge.

 

Fenric ignored him entirely. He turned to Lillian. "Lillian, stay close to me for the next few days."

 

"Yes, my lord!" she said sweetly.

 

Watching this, Naichen realized he had completely misunderstood Fenric.

 

This man wasn't some evil thief at all!

 

"I… I apologize, my lord. I misjudged you," Naichen said nervously.

 

Fenric said nothing, but Chixia couldn't help muttering, "Scholar, he beat you like that and you're apologizing?"

 

"I was wrong. It's only right to admit it," Naichen said honestly.

 

Chixia shook his head and dropped the subject.

 

Fenric spoke. "Beardy, take this kid away at dawn. We'll be going up against the Black Mountain demon soon—it's too dangerous for him to stay."

 

"Agreed," Chixia nodded.

 

"The Black Mountain demon? Who's that?" Naichen asked.

 

No one answered.

 

—--

 

Two days passed in a flash.

 

That night—

 

Fenric was sound asleep when Chixia suddenly rushed in and shook him awake.

 

"Boy, get up! Something's happening!"

 

Outside Orchid Temple, the faint sound of gongs and drums echoed.

 

Fenric sprang up. "Lillian?"

 

"I'm here, my lord."

 

Lillian appeared beside him in an instant.

 

Her expression was calm—completely unbothered.

 

These past two days had been the most peaceful in her afterlife. No need to harm others, no orders barked from Grandma, and both Fenric and Chixia treated her with respect.

 

Her mindset had changed. She was now willing to risk everything to help Fenric defeat the old Black Mountain Demon.

 

"Stay by my side," Fenric told her gently.

 

The moment he spoke, a violent wind howled outside.

 

WHOOOSH!

 

Leaves and dust blew into Orchid Temple, making the entire structure creak as if about to collapse.

 

Chixia's face darkened. "Heavy demonic presence!"

 

"Aah!" Lillian cried suddenly. "My lord!"

 

In the next instant—

 

She was sucked away by a powerful force and vanished before Fenric's eyes.

 

"Beardy!!" Fenric roared.

 

"I saw it!" Chixia shouted. Drawing the Empyrean Sword, he chanted a spell: "Princess Paramita!" and swung his blade toward where Lillian had vanished.

 

Woosh—!

 

The air split open, revealing a dark, swirling portal.

 

"Boy, if we don't return by dawn, we'll be trapped in the underworld forever!" Chixia warned.

 

"Got it!" Fenric replied, leaping into the darkness without hesitation.

 

Chixia followed close behind.

 

—---

 

The wind roared. The sky turned pitch black.

 

All around them, there was nothing but gloom and desolation. Not a soul in sight.

 

This… was the underworld.

 

As soon as Fenric landed, he felt a strange discomfort. A living human had no business here.

 

"Close your eyes. I'll open your Heavenly Vision," Chixia said from behind.

 

Fenric obeyed. He felt something cool touch his eyelids.

 

When he opened his eyes again—ghosts. Endless, swarming ghosts filled the underworld.

 

But Fenric wasn't afraid. In fact, a grin crept onto his face.

 

His first time in the underworld to farm monsters—it was kind of exciting.

 

He pulled out his Night Demon Cloak, wrapped it around his shoulders, and fastened it securely.

 

"Huh?" Chixia stared in surprise. "Kid, you've got some rare gear on you."

 

Even with his sharp eye, he couldn't discern the depth of power within the cloak.

 

"Don't admire it now, Beardy. Let's find Lillian!" Fenric said urgently.

 

"Right!" Chixia pulled out a compass. A pointer in its center began to spin wildly as he chanted a silent incantation. Finally, the needle fixed itself pointing toward the front-left direction.

 

"There!" he declared, stowing the compass and taking off.

 

But Fenric was even faster—rushing ahead at over 100 yards per second. Even with light-foot techniques, Chixia struggled to keep up.

 

This kid really is a monster, he thought.

 

But the stronger Fenric was, the more stable this monster-farming trip would be.

 

Soon, they heard noise from ahead.

 

A strange procession was moving forward—ghouls and beasts of all shapes escorting a lavish sedan chair.

 

Inside the sedan was Lillian, now dressed in red.

 5

The moment Fenric saw her, his eyes turned cold.

 

Without a word, he charged straight in.
