chapters.name: Chapter 221: Chapter 221: Admit it! You Are the God of Thunder!
chapters.content:
"Young Master!"

 

Lillian's face lit up with joy when she saw Fenric rushing toward her.

 

"Lillian, don't be afraid. I'm here."

 

As soon as he spoke, the Black Blade Shusui appeared in Fenric's hand. Instantly, Armament Haki cloaked his body like a black flame.

 

With the power of a raging beast, Fenric charged, cutting down the monstrous creatures that surrounded them.

 

At the same time, several flying blades shot from Fenric's side like bullets, slicing through the ghostly horde.

 

"Puff! Puff! Puff!"

 

Screams echoed through the night as countless demons and monsters fell, unable to withstand Fenric's full assault.

 

Under the cover of the Night Demon Cloak, none of them could hide from his relentless attacks.

 

"Slash!"

 

With one swing, the Black Blade Shusui cleaved a towering monster clean in half.

 

Elsewhere, a ghostly figure lunged forward, spear aimed straight at Fenric's chest—only for the tip to snap on impact, as if striking indestructible metal.

 

These low-level demons were utterly powerless before him.

 

"Vajra defence? Not bad."

 

Chixia's voice came from behind, his tone filled with awe.

 

Fenric's display left him speechless. Whether it was his Telekinesis power, his mastery of Armament Haki, or his sheer physical strength—Fenric was like a one-man army.

 

If Fenric claimed to be a god descended from the heavens, Chixia would believe him without hesitation.

 

Fenric didn't reply. He was fully immersed in the thrill of harvesting souls.

 

"You killed an evil creature and gained 160 Yin Qi. Current task progress: 160/1500."

 

"You killed an evil creature and gained 300 Yin Qi. Current task progress: 460/1500."

 

"You killed an evil creature and gained 220 Yin Qi. Current task progress: 680/1500."

 

In less than three minutes, Fenric had slaughtered the entire "welcoming committee."

 

Chixia had watched the whole thing, but never found an opening to step in.

 

Fenric's task progress had already skyrocketed past 5,000.

 

"Lillian, are you hurt?" Fenric asked.

 

"I'm fine, young master!" she replied joyfully.

 

"Good."

 

Suddenly, the ground began to tremble violently.

 

"Who dares cause havoc here?!"

 

A deafening roar tore through the air like a hurricane.

 

Lillian's joy instantly turned to fear. Her face went pale, while Chixia's expression darkened. Even Fenric grew solemn.

 

He could feel it—the suffocating pressure in the air.

 

The Black Mountain Demon had spoken.

 

A being who had lived for thousands of years—just his voice alone carried overwhelming might.

 

There was no doubt: this demon was far beyond the A-rank threshold.

 

But Fenric… wasn't afraid.

 

He had Thor's Hammer.

 

And thunder was the bane of monsters.

 

Not only that—he still had several special artifacts hidden on his body.

 

Even if the Black Mountain Demon was vastly stronger, Fenric was ready for battle.

 

"Beardy, take Lillian and fall back! I might accidentally hurt you during the fight."

 

As he spoke, Fenric pulled out the Bodhi Rosary and hung it around his neck—warding against soul attacks from the Old Demon.

 

Then he swapped out the Black Blade Shusui for Thor's Hammer.

 

Seeing the Mjölnir-like hammer, Chixia's eyes widened. "Can you really handle this alone?"

 

"No problem!"

 

As Fenric raised the hammer high—

 

"BOOM—!"

 

Dark clouds rolled in.

 

In seconds, the already gloomy underworld became even darker.

 

Seeing this, Chixia and Lillian immediately ran far to the side.

 

The last time Fenric wielded Thor's Hammer, its power had left them shaken.

 

"BOOM—! BOOM—! BOOM—!"

 

Suddenly, the sound of countless footsteps and horses' hooves echoed across the ground.

 

Moments later—

 

An army of ghosts and monsters appeared before Fenric.

 

Tens of thousands of them, clad in ancient armor, stretched across the landscape like a black tide.

 

Chixia gasped.

 

No wonder the Black Mountain Demon was so arrogant. This army alone was terrifying!

 

But Fenric's reaction was the opposite.

 

Points—a mountain of points!

 

To him, this wasn't a threat. It was a treasure trove!

 

If he wiped out the army, the Yin Qi he'd gain would surely earn him a Super God evaluation!

 

"Attack!!"

 

One ghost general raised his sword and bellowed the command.

 

With a roar, the monstrous horde charged.

 

Fenric simply scoffed.

 

In the next instant—

 

Conqueror's Haki — unleashed!

 

A crushing aura burst from him like a tidal wave.

 

It was as if an ancient king had descended.

 

Even Chixia and Lillian behind him felt the urge to kneel.

 

"Fwoosh!"

 

The sheer pressure from his Conqueror Haki formed a visible storm that swept over the enemy ranks.

 

"Thud! Thud!"

 

Thousands of monsters collapsed, unconscious before they even reached him.

 

Of course, they weren't dead.

 

Fenric still needed to "deliver the final blow" to claim his points.

 

Only a handful of powerful enemies remained standing—ghost generals and elite monsters.

 

All of them stared at Fenric in terror.

 

Chixia was dumbfounded. 

 

He must be a god!

 

What else could explain such divine pressure? Just his aura alone had felled thousands.

 

"Who… who are you?"

 

A voice echoed from the shadows—cold and bewildered.

 

The Black Mountain Demon had finally spoken, stunned by what he had just witnessed.

 

"The one who's here to take your life!"

 

Fenric replied coldly, raising Thor's Hammer.

 

"BOOM—!"

 

A lightning bolt tore through the sky and slammed into the ghost general.

 

"AAAHH!!"

 

The general barely managed a scream before being obliterated—his body turned to ash in an instant.

 

Thunder—the ultimate nemesis of monsters and ghosts!

 

"Impossible!"

 

The Black Mountain Demon's voice rang out in disbelief. "This is the underworld! How can you summon thunder here?!"

 

Fenric didn't answer.

 

He simply raised his hammer again and began bombarding the fallen army with lightning.

 

Each strike brought him closer to his mission's completion.

 

"BOOM—! BOOM—! BOOM—!"

 

Thunder and lightning rained down like divine punishment.

 

In mere moments, the battlefield had become a hellish Purgatory of Thunder.

 

—---

chapters.name: Chapter 222: Chapter 222: Unexpected Ending!
chapters.content:
BOOM—! BOOM—! BOOM—!

 

Thunder roared across the sky, lightning streaking down like divine punishment.

 

Dark clouds stretched endlessly above—this was Thunder Purgatory!

 

Each strike of lightning carved out a massive thunder ring on the ground, thick bolts dancing wildly as they tore through demons like reapers of judgment.

 

Blood soil flew in all directions. Craters formed one after another—

 

The battlefield looked like it had been carpet-bombed by missiles!

 

Any monster or ghost struck by lightning was instantly obliterated, not even ashes remained.

 

"You have killed the evil creature. Gained 610 Yin Qi.

 

Current mission progress: 6,870/1,500…"

 

"You have killed the evil creature. Gained 490 Yin Qi.

 

Current mission progress: 7,360/1,500…"

 

"You have killed the evil creature. Gained 550 Yin Qi.

 

Current mission progress: 7,910/1,500…"

 

"You have killed the evil creature. Gained 770 Yin Qi.

 

Current mission progress: 4.68 million/1,500…"

 

After just a few minutes, the massive army of monsters—tens of thousands strong—was completely wiped out by Fenric.

 

His mission progress had skyrocketed past four million!

 

Terrifying.

 

At this rate, even if he didn't kill the Black Mountain Demon, Fenric was certain he'd return with a guaranteed Super God Evaluation.

 

That thought made him grin.

 

"Black Mountain Demon!"

 

Fenric shouted into the darkness, "Get out here and die!!"

 

"..."

 

Only silence responded.

 

"???" Fenric frowned. "Where the hell did he go?"

 

"Hey, Black Mountain Demon? Don't play turtle now! Come out!"

 

"Stop yelling!" Chixia's voice came from behind. "You scared him off!"

 

He sounded exasperated as he looked at Fenric.

 

The person capable of frightening the infamous Black Mountain Demon into running away without a fight—

 

Across the ages, this was probably the only one.

 

"…The hell?" Fenric muttered.

 

He didn't expect it either.

 

The Old Demon ran without so much as a face-off?

 

"Young Master… you're… amazing," Lillian whispered in awe, gazing at Fenric with admiration.

 

To be honest, in all her years as a ghost, she had never seen anyone so absurdly powerful.

 

Fenric, however, looked annoyed.

 

The Black Mountain Demon ran off without even saying hello?

 

That was basically slapping him in the face!

 

Unacceptable.

 

"Beardy, that guy's territory is near the City of the Dead, right? Let's go! I'll find him there and beat the crap out of him!"

 

Fenric's expression turned vicious.

 

After all, killing that demon would give him a huge chunk of Yin Qi.

 

His true goal was securing the Super God rating—he needed to make the outcome certain.

 

"The Black Mountain Demon is probably hiding in the City of the Dead…"

 

Chixia shook his head. "But forget it. Since he chose to run, he won't let you find him that easily."

 

"You only have yourself to blame—you were too aggressive and scared him off!"

 

Fenric had no words.

 

Honestly, if it came down to a real fight, it wasn't certain who would win.

 

But the demon chose to run.

 

And Fenric… couldn't chase him.

 

He didn't know tracking spells or techniques.

 

He couldn't even pinpoint the enemy.

 

"Forget it. Let's go back," Fenric muttered.

 

"Alright," Chixia replied. He took out the Empyrean Sword, muttered "Prajna Paramita," slashed the air, and opened a rift back to the land of the living.

 

"Lillian, let's go."

 

"Yes, my lord."

 

The two disappeared from the underworld.

 

A short while later, they returned to Orchid Temple.

 

In the room, someone was already there—

 

No. Not someone. Something.

 

It was the Thousand-Year Tree Demon!

 

Seeing Fenric suddenly reappear, the old tree demon froze in shock.

 

She had just come to take a look—she never expected the disaster star to return so soon!

 

"Old hag!" Fenric snapped. "You dare show your face? Since Black Mountain Demon ran off, I'll use you as target practice!"

 

Before she could respond, Fenric lunged.

 

BOOM—!

 

With a single blow, the old tree demon exploded into pieces—

 

She'd abandoned a clone just to escape!

 

Everyone: "…"

 

Fenric sighed.

 

Now even demons fled on sight.

 

Where was the fun in that?

 

Chixia shook his head. "Kid… I've cultivated for decades, and I've never seen anyone like you. You show up—and demons run for their lives!"

 

Fenric didn't know what to say.

 

He hadn't meant for it to be like this…

 

Now he was actually worried.

 

The mission timer was only halfway, and there were no more monsters to kill!

 

Sure, those demons weren't strong enough to beat him,

 

but if they ran, there was nothing he could do.

 

He couldn't use spells.

 

He couldn't track them.

 

His mind power wasn't omnipotent.

 

Just like now—the tree demon saw him and abandoned her clone without hesitation!

 

Forget it!

 

If he couldn't grind more kills, then so be it.

 

With his current Yin Qi value, getting a Super God Evaluation should still be no problem.

 

Suddenly, Fenric remembered something.

 

"Beardy, you said you'd give me your sword if I killed the Black Mountain Demon, right? Now he runs when he sees me—I can't help that. But does it still count? Can I have your sword?"

 

Chixia paused. "…Your hammer is practically a divine weapon. Why do you want my sword?"

 

Smart man. He'd clearly realized Fenric's thunder technique came from the hammer.

 

Fenric lied with a straight face: "The hammer drains too much energy. I need a low-cost weapon to slay demons."

 

Chixia thought it over, then nodded. "True. The sword might be better in your hands."

 

He pulled out the Empyrean Divine Sword and handed it over.

 

"This sword has been with me for twenty years. Take good care of it—and let it drink demon blood."

 

Fenric received it solemnly. "Of course."

 

Internally, he was ecstatic.

 

With this indestructible Empyrean Divine Sword and his Black Blade Shusui, he was basically ready to retire!

 

"You don't know Taoist arts, do you?" Chixia said. "You should learn them—only then can you bring out the true power of this sword."

 

Fenric's eyes lit up. "Beardy, how about teaching me a few techniques?"

 

But Chixia shook his head. "This is where we part ways. I'm leaving."

 

Without hesitation, he turned and departed, traveling through the night without a second thought.

 

"Damn. Why are you running like I will rob you?"

 

Now, only Fenric and Lillian remained in the room.

 

"Lillian," Fenric asked gently, "are you planning to reincarnate?"

 

Lillian lowered her head and didn't reply.

 

"…Can you wait a few more days? I have to stay a little longer. Can you delay your reincarnation until then?"

 

"…Okay!"

 

She agreed instantly.

 

Then realizing how fast she answered, Lillian blushed and looked down again.

 

Fenric smiled, watching her shy expression.

chapters.name: Chapter 223: Chapter 223: The Super God Evaluation Reappeared, That Man Is Back!
chapters.content:
"Congratulations! Samsara player 'Shura'—in the Samsara Tower dungeon world [A Bride Ghost Story]—has performed exceptionally. Within seven days, he obtained 4.68 million Yin points, far exceeding the dungeon's objective. He has received a perfect evaluation: SSS!"

 

Super God!!

 

Samsara Plaza.

 

The Dungeon Hall.

 

And all across the dungeon worlds where Samsaras were still performing missions...

 

Every single Samsara player in the Samsara space heard the broadcast loud and clear.

 

SSS—Super God Evaluation!

 

It appeared once again.

 

Yet most people remained calm, some even took it for granted.

 

That man... is on the screen again!

 

"Another Super God evaluation? Is this Shura's first?"

 

"Who can even remember anymore? Other than that one time in Kung Fu Hustle, every dungeon Shura's cleared has been Super God."

 

"Exactly. Back when he got an SS-rank in Kung Fu Hustle, jealous idiots claimed Shura was washed up. And then—boom—face slap!"

 

"Yeah, he's just too much. Even when he slacks off, he still pulls an SS like it's nothing."

 

"It's simple: the guy's got raw talent, rock-solid foundations, and insane strength. Missions that are nightmares for us? Shura probably clears them half-asleep."

 

"Now the question is—when is the great Shura surpassing Adam?"

 

This was the prevailing sentiment among the crowd.

 

However, those who had personally experienced [A Bride Ghost Story] were still reeling from the system's announcement.

 

"W-what?! 4.68 million Yin points? Are you kidding me?!"

 

"Did Shura slaughter the entire family line of the Thousand-Year Tree Demon or something?!"

 

"No way. That's gotta be a cheat!"

 

"I remember the Tree Demon was a nightmare to kill. You had to burn down every locust tree around Orchid Temple... What the hell did Shura do to get that kind of Yin harvest?"

 

"Not even nuking the entire temple would give you that much Yin!"

 

"Terrifying... Shura must've unlocked some unknown, god-tier strategy!"

 

Those who knew the dungeon well understood just how absurd that Yin total was. Killing the Thousand-Year Tree Demon alone only granted around 15,000 Yin points.

 

Even if you wiped out every ghost and demon around Orchid Temple, you'd barely break the tens of thousands.

 

Four million-plus Yin? Where were that many ghosts even hiding?!

 

"Dear Samsara player 'Shura', you have completed your mission. Your rewards are as follows:"

 

Samsara Points: 50,000

 

Strength +30 (Applied)

 

Impersonation Mask ×1 (Stored in personal warehouse)

 1

Golden Treasure Chest ×1

 

Hearing the system prompt, Fenric's expression remained calm, though memories from [A Bride Ghost Story] still lingered in his mind.

 

After Chixia's departure, he had spent his days napping and his nights wandering with the ghost beauty, Lillian.

 

Naturally, a lonely man and a beautiful spirit together each night led to... inevitable things.

 4

Unfortunately, Lillian was still a ghost—and destined for reincarnation. Fenric could not remain in the dungeon world indefinitely.

 

In the end, he had to personally escort her to reincarnate.

 

Ironically, the Thousand-Year Tree Demon wasn't even killed by Fenric—but by the Black Mountain Demon, who was furious after being deceived and manipulated by the Tree Demon into facing powerful enemies. In his rage, he wiped out her demon army—and the Tree Demon along with it.

 

Fenric shook his head and stopped reminiscing.

 

He made his way to his personal warehouse—time to open his loot.

 

In the Personal Warehouse:

 

Fenric first picked up the Impersonation Mask.

 

Immediately, the system chimed in:

 

"Special Item: Impersonation Mask

 

With this item, you can alter your appearance and impersonate anyone—provided you have access to their DNA (a single strand of hair is sufficient).

 

Note: Each use lasts for 3 hours. After time expires, you will revert to your original form."

 

Fenric blinked, momentarily stunned.

 

"This thing doesn't boost combat power... but with clever use, it could be ridiculously effective."

 

Setting the mask back on the shelf, Fenric picked up the Golden Treasure Chest and opened it.

 

"Congratulations! You have opened the Golden Treasure Chest and received a special item: Diamond Sutra!"

 

Inside the chest was a set of ancient scriptures.

 

"Diamond Sutra?"

 

He recalled how Chixia often chanted the mantra "Princess Paramita" during their time together. That spell, he now realized, originated from this scripture.

 

Fenric picked up the Diamond Sutra, and once again, the system spoke:

 

"Special Item: Diamond Sutra

 

According to legend, this was preached by Buddha Shakyamuni to the Venerable Subhuti beneath the Solitary Garden's Only Tree.

 

One of the core texts of Mahayana Buddhism. Upon understanding, it has the power to dispel demons and evil, and even opens the path to Buddhahood.

 

Note: Requires extremely high Buddha-nature to comprehend.

 

Reminder: Special items can be recycled. Estimated recycle value: 60,000 Samsara points."

 

Fenric frowned.

 

Then, without hesitation, he recycled the Diamond Sutra for 60,000 Samsara points.

 2

"Buddha-nature? Yeah... that's not me."

 2

Currently:

 

Fenric's Samsara point balance now exceeded 110,000.

 

This round of rewards wasn't massive—but it wasn't bad either.

 

But truthfully, what pleased him the most... was the sword gifted to him by Chixia.

 

The Empyrean Divine Sword!

 

This blade had multiple mythological versions across various stories, but one thing remained consistent—it was a legendary weapon.

 

It wasn't just powerful—it suppressed evil, possessed incredible sharpness, and was forged with materials of the highest quality.

 

Compared to it, even his weapon, Black Blade Shusui, paled in comparison.

 1

Fenric drew the Empyrean Sword, gripping it firmly.

 

It was long, heavy, gleaming with a chilling light—and it felt perfectly suited to his now-overwhelming strength attribute.

 

Black Blade Shusui had officially retired.

 

That blade had served him well—but it no longer matched the Fenric of today.

 

Most people would've sold it or given it away.

 

But Fenric?

 

He simply stored it—perhaps it would be useful as a gift or favor in the future.

 2

chapters.name: Chapter 224: Chapter 224: The Emperor? It’s Not Wrong to Kill!
chapters.content:
With 110,000 Samsara points, Fenric paused for a moment, then used them all to exchange for potential points.

 

A full 220 potential points.

 

Fenric distributed them optimally across his four attributes. A short while later, his updated stats were:

 

Name: Shura

 

Samsara Number: (C Area) 90086

 

Physique: 264 → 310

 

Spirit: 526 → 620

 

Strength: 369 → 403

 

Agility: 264 → 310

 

Allocable Potential: 0

 

Skills: 1423

 3

English (Proficient)

 

Driving (Beginner)

 

Shooting (Proficient)

 

Camouflage (Master)

 

Basic Sword Technique (Proficient)

 

Special Skills:

 

Conqueror's Haki (Mastery)

 

Armament Haki (Mastery)

 3

Combat Techniques:

 

Savage Collision

 

Buddha Palm

 

Abilities:

 

Telekinesis

 

Poison Immunity (Passive)

 

Samsara Points Remaining: 2,522

 

Comprehensive Rating: A

 

His Spirit attribute had surpassed 600, now sitting at 620!

 

Even Strength broke through the 400 mark.

 

At this level, Fenric could absolutely dominate and eliminate anyone on the same tier.

 

By the time he returned from his personal warehouse, it was already 3:00 a.m.

 

After a moment's thought, he entered his personal dungeon: "The Great Wall."

 

The original plan? To visit his 27th fiancée.

 3

But what awaited him there infuriated him.

 

The Little Emperor of Bianport—who clearly had something wrong with his head—had issued an imperial edict summoning General Lin Mei to the capital, assigning her as the Commander of the Imperial Forest Army.

 

On the surface, it looked like a promotion.

 

But only fools would miss the deeper meaning.

 

Everyone in the Song Dynasty knew by now: General Lin Mei's fiancé belonged to the Immortal Realm.

 

So for the Emperor to suddenly summon her?

 

He was clearly using Lin Mei as leverage to threaten Fenric!

 2

The moment Fenric received the news, his expression turned ice-cold.

 

He said nothing.

 

He simply donned the seventh-generation Mark armor, stormed into Bianport under the cover of night, and—

 

took the foolish Emperor's head.

 

Before dying, the young Emperor revealed the true masterminds behind the plot:

 

Several high-ranking ministers, nearing death, had sought the secret of immortality from the Immortal Realm.

 

So they forced the Emperor to issue the edict, targeting Fenric to achieve their ambitions!

 

Big mistake.

 

They had angered him.

 

And once Shura was provoked, it didn't matter if you were a veteran of three dynasties or even a living saint—

 

He would send you all to meet the King of Hell early!

 

With Fenric's overwhelming power, there wasn't a soul in the entire Song Dynasty who could stand in his way.

 

That very night, Bianport City ran red with blood. Fenric's wrath reduced the capital to a slaughterhouse.

 

Then came his warning:

 

"If anyone dares target General Lin Mei again…"

 

In a city of a million souls, not one person doubted his words.

 

Because Fenric could fly—courtesy of his battle armor.

 

In ancient times, anyone who could soar through the skies was considered a god.

 

That act alone cemented Fenric's name as a divine figure.

 

Leaving only those chilling words behind, Fenric turned and flew off in his armor.

 

As for what would happen to Bianport now—

 

Who would inherit the throne?

 

He didn't care.

 

If Lin Mei wanted it, he'd place her on the throne with one hand, making her the second Empress in history after Wu Zetian.

 3

After resolving Lin Mei's issue, Fenric returned to the real world.

 

Real World

 

It was past 4:00 a.m.—the quietest time of night.

 

But tonight, the city was far from quiet.

 

In the distant city center, a faint glow of fire lit up the sky.

 

Fenric stepped out of his room and saw Father Eric sitting on the couch, deep in thought.

 

"Dad, why haven't you gone to sleep?"

 

"Ric, you're back?" Eric replied quickly. "There were explosions downtown not long ago. I don't know what's going on."

 

Fenric frowned.

 

Explosions?

 

Could it be that a powerful biochemical creature had appeared?

 

He was all too aware of the Blacklight Virus's power. Given enough time, it could spawn monsters on par with the Tyrants from Resident Evil.

 

If that kind of monster was loose, the human army would struggle to contain it—

 

Unless powerful Samsaras stepped in.

 

But that wasn't the real threat.

 

The true danger lay in the "[Evolveds]"—those rare humans who didn't become zombies when infected, but instead mutated into something worse.

 

In martial arts terms, these were "chosen ones", one in a million.

 

Once infected, if they didn't collapse…

 

They transformed.

 

Gained immense strength. Their bodies became living weapons.

 

Hands turned into blades, hammers, shields—it was child's play.

 

In terms of combat ability, they rivaled Symbiotes like Riot.

 

Even worse, they retained their human intelligence and appearance, making them terrifying opponents.

 

Fenric had played the game Prototype. The protagonist? Also an [Evolved].

 1

In game terms, these beings had at least B-rank strength.

 

"Dad, pack up your things. I'm taking you back to the countryside. We leave now!"

 

"But the city's on lockdown—how will we go?" Eric asked, puzzled.

 

Fenric didn't answer.

 

He simply summoned Mark 7 and activated it.

 

Clang—whirr—click!

 

With mechanical whirring, the Seventh Generation Armor rapidly disassembled and reassembled around him.

 

Before Father Eric's stunned eyes, Fenric transformed into a sleek, armored figure.

 

"This… this…"

 

Eric was speechless, stunned to silence.

 

As a humble factory worker, he had never seen anything like this.

 

"Don't worry, Dad," Fenric said through the suit's mechanical voice. "It's something I got from the Samsara space."

 

There was no longer any need for Fenric to hide who he was.

 

Especially not from someone as trustworthy as his father.

 

After a long pause, Eric finally found his voice.

 

"This thing… can it fly?"

 

"Of course it can~"

 

"Alright, Ric. Give me a moment to pack. Then we'll go."

 

"And bring a thick jacket," Fenric reminded him. "It's cold up there."

 

Soon, Father Eric returned with a large bag—mostly clothes and some heavier items.

 

Fenric took him to the rooftop, picked him up, and took off slowly.

 

To protect his father from the wind, he flew at a steady, reduced speed.

 

As for satellites and radars?

 

The armor's onboard AI—Tsunade—jammed them all with ease.

 

Tony Stark's tech was over 50 years ahead of its time. Of course, it had anti-detection systems.

 

After safely settling his father in the countryside, Fenric returned to the city.

 

He was going to investigate what exactly had happened in the city center.

chapters.name: Chapter 225: Chapter 225: Give You Face? Even Shura Provokes Him?
chapters.content:
When Fenric returned to the city, it was already five o'clock in the morning.

 

A faint light crept across the sky.

 

Wearing battle armor, Fenric avoided flying directly over the city and instead landed in a remote area. Though the armor could block radar scans, flying too close would expose him to the naked eye.

 

He navigated the city by foot.

 

With his mental strength now exceeding six hundred, he could glide briefly in the air—practically flight in short bursts.

 

Combined with his agility, even a city lockdown couldn't stop his movements.

 

Soon, he reached the city center.

 

The scene was utter chaos.

 

Cratered roads, shattered buildings, and flames erupting skyward. Corpses littered the ground—both human and monstrous zombies. From a bird's-eye view, it looked like the apocalypse had descended.

 

It appeared that the Blacklight Virus had leaked into the urban area, causing massive destruction.

 

Fenric frowned. He decided to act once dawn fully broke.

 

Just then, an armed squad was moving cautiously through the high-rise ruins. Equipped with night vision goggles, they appeared to be searching for something dangerous.

 

Suddenly, a dark figure leapt out from another building like a wolf pouncing on prey.

 

Across a 20-meter-wide street, the figure cleared the distance in a single bound—explosive power evident. Mid-air, its arms began to mutate grotesquely.

 

A monster.

 

Fenric narrowed his eyes.

 

He immediately recognized it—an [Evolved], someone infected and mutated by the Blacklight Virus.

 

Just like the heroine "Alice" from Resident Evil, this [Evolved] possessed immense strength.

 2

"Enemy attack! Enemy attack!"

 

Rat-tat-tat!

 

"Watch the flanks!"

 

"Call for backup!"

 

But the squad stood no chance.

 

If the [Evolved] was a tiger, the armed team was a flock of sheep.

 

Slaughter ensued.

 

In seconds, the seven- or eight-man squad was butchered. The [Evolved] tore through them like a whirlwind of blades and gore. Blood painted the ground red—limbs torn, bodies broken. A massacre.

 

They didn't even manage to send a distress signal.

 

This one [Evolved] alone showed terrifying strength and ruthless brutality.

 

From a distance, Fenric observed silently.

 

He noticed something odd.

 

Despite the [Evolved] overwhelming strength, it didn't flee the city. It wasn't trying to escape—it was hunting people deliberately.

 

Then, as if sensing Fenric's presence, the [Evolved] abruptly turned its head.

 

The next moment—

 

It lunged.

 

Exploding off the ground, it soared through the air with predatory intent, crossing the gap between buildings like a bird of prey.

 

Fenric blinked in mild surprise.

 

Then, he laughed.

 

A cold, mocking laugh.

 

"I wasn't even planning to look for you, and you come straight to me?"

 1

There's a road to heaven, yet you don't take it; you barge into hell instead.

 

It wasn't arrogance.

 

An [Evolved] dares to hunt him?

 

Delusional.

 

As the [Evolved] approached, it opened its mouth and growled in a guttural accent:

 

"Samsara...?"

 

Fenric's expression shifted.

 

"A foreigner?"

 

His irritation flared.

 

Some bastard had the audacity to barge into Jadeveil Nation, slaughter people, and even force him and his father to relocate overnight?

 

Unforgivable.

 2

Without another word, Fenric raised his hand and flexed his fingers.

 

Telekinesis energy activated.

 

He would beat this bastard until even his mother wouldn't recognize him.

 

The [Evolved] body seized up mid-air—frozen by Fenric's mental grip.

 

Armament Haki surged around Fenric's body.

 

With a flash, his iron fist smashed directly into the [Evolveds] skull.

 

The brain—always a weakness for infected creatures—was targeted.

 

Even Blacklight [Evolveds] weren't immune.

 

Despite being immobilized, the [Evolveds] mutated arms shifted into blade-like weapons, stabbing toward Fenric's torso.

 

It was a desperate move.

 

If Fenric didn't change his attack trajectory, he would be impaled.

 

But he didn't flinch.

 

BOOM—!

 

The two collided violently.

 

The [Evolved] was sent flying like a ragdoll.

 

Fenric stood unscathed.

 

"You think you can hurt me with that?" he muttered.

 

With Grandmaster-level Armament Haki protecting him, an [Evolved] didn't even qualify as a threat.

 1

Just as the [Evolved] was about to crash into a wall, Fenric yanked him back mid-air with Telekinesis force.

 

Then—

 

BOOM—! BOOM—! BOOM—!

 

Fenric turned the [Evolved] into a living sandbag.

 

Blow after blow rained down.

 

Even if this [Evolved] had evolved to the level of "Brother A" from the game, he still wouldn't stand a chance.

 

Fenric was an A-rank boss now.

 

[Evolveds] were, at best, B-rank. They couldn't even penetrate his defenses—let alone fight back.

 

With each strike, the [Evolveds] regeneration faltered. Though their healing was strong, it came at a high physical cost. After Fenric's onslaught, the creature was visibly drained.

 

Fenric finally stopped.

 

Grabbing the creature's throat with one hand, he lifted its battered body with the other.

 

Then—

 

He squeezed.

 

"Aaaaaaghhh!!"

 

The [Evolved] screamed in agony.

 

Crack!

 

Blood splattered.

 

Fenric ripped out its spine with one brutal motion.

 1

Savage. Ruthless. Absolute.

 2

Fenric stared at the dying creature, expressionless.

 

Even though the corpse was in pieces, the [Evolved] clung to life—infected bodies had a frightening vitality.

 

From a distance came the sound of rushing footsteps and the rumble of military vehicles.

 

The commotion had drawn the military's attention.

 

Fenric casually dropped the [Evolveds] severed head, plucked a clump of hair from a nearby corpse, and took out a fake mask.

 

Next moment, his body began to change—becoming shorter, rounder.

 

Within seconds, he had transformed into a plump middle-aged man.

 

An exact replica of the corpse lying nearby.

 

----------

 

[Translator's Note:]

 

It's been a while since I last did a mass release, so here's the deal — since Monday is when the power stones reset.

 

This deal is valid before the next arc begins. Once the arc officially starts, the deal will be canceled.

 

Also, a quick note about updates — my schedule has shifted a bit since I sometimes wake up around 10 AM to 1 PM, so I usually check the rankings and post updates between 10–11 PM instead before I update.

 

Next Arc Deal – Over 20+ Chapters!

chapters.name: Chapter 226: Chapter 226: The Number One Master Is Here!
chapters.content:
[Translator's Note:]

 

We've reached Rank #3, which means 5 new chapters!

 

Also, just a friendly reminder — if you're unsure about who's who in the upcoming arc, you can check out my Patreon for a more immersive reading experience.

 

------

 

"Don't move!"

 

"Hands in the air!"

 

A group of soldiers quickly surrounded Fenric.

 

Naturally, Fenric had no intention of surrendering—no one in this world could make him raise his hands in submission. 

 

With a casual motion, he threw the severed head and bodies of the [Evolved] to the ground in front of the soldiers and said coldly, "These are the ones you're looking for. I took care of them for you."

 

"Be careful—they're infected with a virus. Keep them for research."

 

The [Evolved] were now decapitated, his bodies and heads separated. He's now beyond saving, barely clinging to life. One of the heads still had a pulsating spine attached, twitching grotesquely—an eerie and terrifying sight.

 

The soldiers were visibly shaken. Even hardened men like them had never seen anything this bizarre.

 

Fortunately, their company commander recognized the [Evolved] and immediately realized Fenric wasn't lying.

 

These were the ones responsible for today's black light virus outbreak in the city.

 

After confirming the identities of the corpses, the commander's shock quickly turned to respect. He approached Fenric politely and asked, "Comrade, may I ask for your name? You captured this [Evolved]. The military will issue a reward."

 1

His respectful tone wasn't surprising. Everyone here knew how dangerous those [Evolved] were.

 

Several B-rank Samsaras in the city had already been slaughtered by them, and even their own military suffered heavy casualties trying to engage them. The top brass had even requested A-rank Samsaras support.

 

No one expected a single man—an unassuming, pot-bellied, middle-aged stranger—to wipe out such a threat so effortlessly.

 

Still in disguise, Fenric gave a faint smile and replied, "No need for a reward. I just couldn't stand some arrogant bastard acting like he owned our land."

 1

"I'm leaving now. Make way."

 

No one dared to stop him.

 

Anyone capable of killing an [Evolved] like that had to be an A-rank Samsara at least.

 

The company commander memorized Fenric's face, then waved his hand. "Let him through. Disperse."

 

Fenric strolled away without looking back.

 

Not a single soldier moved to block him.

 

Once Fenric had vanished into the distance, the company commander turned to his men. "Was anyone recording just now?"

 

"We got it, sir!"

 

"Good. Notify HQ immediately!"

 

Meanwhile...

 

After leaving the city and confirming no one was tailing him—and that there were no surveillance drones around—Fenric removed his disguise.

 

The mask he wore was incredibly advanced, capable of altering both his face and body shape.

 

If I wore this and impersonated the president of the Cindralock Dominion... he mused. I could probably pull it off.

 

What if I ordered a nuclear strike on Adam in the president's name?

 2

He chuckled aloud at the thought.

 

Tempting—but impossible. The real power in the Cindralock Dominion lies with the conglomerates. The president is just a puppet. Even if he tried to launch nukes, the lawmakers would veto it before the order was carried out.

 3

With that amusing thought set aside, Fenric made his way back to his old countryside home. By the time he arrived, the sun had already risen.

 

He headed to the county seat, caught a ride to another city, and spent four million in cash to buy a new house in a quiet neighborhood.

 

Since it was a full-cash purchase, there was no need for a mortgage. The process was simple. After signing the contract, the agent told him he'd receive the property certificate in about 20 business days.

 

He got the keys that same day.

 

The house was 130 square meters, fully furnished, and ready for move-in.

 

Fenric was very satisfied.

 

Later that day, he returned to the countryside to pick up his father.

 

Father Eric stood in the new home, visibly emotional as he looked around.

 

He turned to Fenric, his eyes sharp with concern. "Ric… be honest with me. Did you go to the Samsara Tower?"

 

Truthfully, when Fenric first revealed the Mark VII armor, Father Eric already had his suspicions. Though not a Samsara player himself, he understood enough to know that such equipment couldn't be found in the Safe Zone.

 

"Yes," Fenric said without hesitation. "I did."

 

Father Eric sighed. "You're a grown man now. I can't stop you from making your own choices… Just promise me one thing—take care of yourself out there."

 

"I will," Fenric replied with a nod, then quickly changed the subject. "You can have the master bedroom."

 

Father Eric shook his head. "I'll stay for a few days, but once I settle my affairs back home, I'm returning. I'm not used to city living."

 2

Fenric frowned slightly, thought for a moment, but said nothing. He nodded in silent agreement.

 

It didn't matter. His father's independence meant he'd have more freedom himself.

 

At the same time...

 

In a temporary command office, a major in military uniform stood reporting to a stern-looking general.

 

"Commander, we've finished our initial investigation. The suspect used some unknown method to perfectly impersonate a deceased person and fooled everyone. So far, we haven't been able to uncover his real identity."

 

"Based on the battle traces, the fight didn't last long, and there was minimal damage. The [Evolved] must've been eliminated almost instantly. Judging by the injuries… the enemy's combat level is likely A-rank or higher."

 

The general furrowed his brow. "Have any A-rank Samsaras arrived in the area recently?"

 

"None, sir. We've confirmed it with reliable sources."

 

Just then, the phone on the general's desk rang.

 

He picked it up, listened, and his expression changed.

 

"Yes, understood. I'll be there immediately."

 

After hanging up, the general stood up and barked an order. "Get the lieutenants. We're going to meet Commander Song."

 

The major's eyes widened. "Commander Song? You mean…"

 

"Who else?" The general shot him a look. "Jadeveil Nation's number one master!"

 4

Hiss—! 

 

The major involuntarily drew a sharp breath. His face lit up with awe and excitement.

 

As a Samsara himself, he had long idolized the legendary Commander Song.

 

"Bring all the intel we've gathered," the general added. "Commander Song is probably here about that mysterios expert."

 

"Understood!"

chapters.name: Chapter 227: Chapter 227: Fight Against the Dungeon, and the Great Powers Contend for Hegemony!
chapters.content:
Night fell. 

 

Fenric now lived in a new house. With no internet installed yet, he could only rely on his mobile phone for the time being.

 

He turned it on and connected to the network.

 

The online world was abuzz with a single topic: the Blacklight Virus.

 

Earlier that morning, the authorities had issued a public announcement, revealing that foreign terrorists had released the Blacklight Virus within the country. Chaos had erupted in 17 cities, and the death toll had already reached the tens of thousands.

 

Fortunately, the situation was now under control.

 

The news sent shockwaves across the internet.

 

Countless netizens condemned the terrorist organization and analyzed the broader implications of the outbreak, especially its impact on humanity's living environment.

 

While the domestic situation had been contained, many smaller, unstable nations hadn't been so lucky. Some had completely collapsed, descending into zombie-infested wastelands.

 

Thankfully, the "Blacklight Virus" wasn't highly contagious—it couldn't spread through air or water. If it had, a full-scale global biochemical disaster might have unfolded.

 

Fenric glanced at the discussions, skimmed a few posts, then lost interest.

 

He was far more concerned about the ninth floor dungeon of the Samsara Tower than the Blacklight Virus.

 

Let the higher-ups worry about that mess.

 

For Fenric, the top priority was still—getting stronger!

 

After opening the Samsara Forum, he skipped all unrelated threads and went straight to the strategy section.

 

But to his surprise...

 

He couldn't find an official walkthrough for the ninth floor of the Samsara Tower.

 

There was plenty of information about the tenth floor—apparently the "[Final Destination]" copy—but the ninth floor? Nothing. 

 2

It struck Fenric as odd.

 

Curious, he typed "About the Ninth Floor of the Samsara Tower" into the search bar, eventually finding a few strategy posts shared by other users.

 

But they were all speculation—no solid information.

 

After sifting through the posts, Fenric finally understood the reason:

 

The ninth floor of the Samsara Tower was a confrontation-type dungeon. Samsaras from various countries and regions would be placed into a single dungeon to compete for dominance.

 

Everyone knew the name of the dungeon: "Three Kingdoms." But no one knew its contents.

 

Why?

 

Because anyone who completed the dungeon would automatically forget the experience after leaving.

 

No strategies could be shared.

 

This was likely a protection mechanism built into the Samsara System.

 

After all, if everyone knew the tricks, what would be left of the struggle for hegemony?

 

Fenric put down his phone, frowning.

 

He hadn't expected a confrontation-style dungeon.

 

With no one remembering the layout or events, it meant everything would have to be figured out on the spot.

 

But Fenric wasn't too worried.

 

With his current power, clearing the dungeon wouldn't be a problem.

 

Still, the lack of narrative intel meant he couldn't prepare specific countermeasures in advance.

 

—--

 

At exactly midnight...

 

Fenric entered the Samsara Space.

 

"You have a new communication request. 'Aurora Morwyn' is requesting a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

As soon as he logged in, the system prompted him.

 

He chose [Accept].

 

A 3D holographic image of Aurora appeared—elegant and commanding.

 

"Shura, come have some tea!"

 

Fenric knew she had something to discuss, so he replied simply, "Sure."

 

The two met in a private room at a teahouse.

 

"Shura!"

 

Aurora greeted him with a bright smile.

 

"I haven't had a chance to congratulate you yet. You scored another Super-God evaluation in the '[A Bride Ghost Story]' dungeon! You're incredible—you even managed to rack up so much Yin Energy!"

 

Fenric chuckled. "I broke into the underworld. Too many ghosts down there—I couldn't not kill them."

 

"I see~"

 

Aurora's eyes lit up, but she was smart enough not to probe further.

 

That was Shura's strategy. If he wanted to share it, fine—if not, she wouldn't press.

 

Then, as if casually, she brought up another topic.

 

"By the way, Shura… yesterday morning, a mysterious powerhouse appeared in AH City and eliminated a Blacklight Virus [Evolved]. Do you know anything about that?"

 

Fenric admitted without hesitation. "That was me."

 

There was nothing to hide.

 

With his current strength, he no longer needed to conceal his identity like before.

 

"So it really was you."

 

Aurora nodded, as if her suspicions had been confirmed.

 

"We checked all domestic A-Rank powerhouses. Once we ruled them out, it was clear who it had to be. On behalf of the military, I want to thank you. That [Evolved] caused major problems."

 

Fenric waved her off. "It was no big deal. I'm from Jadeveil Nation too—if some ghost dares cause trouble on our soil, I'll be the first to put them down."

 

Aurora laughed brightly. "In that case, I'll issue the order to end the investigation when I return."

 

Her words were more than thanks—they were a gesture of goodwill.

 

She was letting Fenric know that if he wanted to keep his identity private, she'd respect that.

 

Fenric smiled. "What are you drinking? My treat."

 

"Oh? A local tycoon like you? I'll take you up on that!"

 

The two ordered Tranquility Tea and began drinking slowly.

 

The tea had excellent effects—regular consumption could soothe the mind and reduce extreme psychological tendencies among Samsaras.

 

After all, they constantly faced life-and-death trials. Over time, it was easy to develop issues—bloodlust, mental instability, and so on.

 

Tranquility Tea was likely created to heal the soul damage sustained by Samsaras.

 

As they drank, Aurora suddenly asked:

 

"Shura, are you about to challenge the ninth floor of the Samsara Tower?"

 

Fenric nodded. "I'll enter it tonight."

 

"You really don't stop, huh?" she sighed, then leaned in, her tone turning serious.

 

"Shura, I've received intel. Several foreign powers are planning to ambush you inside the ninth-floor dungeon."

 

"Oh?"

 

A sharp glint flashed in Fenric's eyes. His aura shifted—cold and domineering.

 

"Then let them come."

 

"There's no strategy information about the ninth floor on the internet because of the memory wipe. But I've managed to collect some intel—partial details from within the dungeon."

 

Aurora offered, "Let me share what I have. I hope it helps, even a little."

chapters.name: Chapter 228: Chapter 228: So I Was Waiting for Shura!
chapters.content:
Aurora Morwyn began to explain the details of the ninth-level dungeon.

 

"Actually, I don't know too much about it. The ninth layer is set in an ancient wartime era, featuring three major factions—Wei, Shu, and Wu."

 

Upon hearing this, Fenric's expression remained calm, but a flicker of surprise flashed through his mind.

 

Wei, Shu, Wu...?

 

Isn't that the Three Kingdoms period?

 

So the ninth-level dungeon was really based on the Three Kingdoms era.

 3

Perfect.

 

Fenric was quite familiar with that period of history—at least, from Earth's perspective. But then he remembered that the historical timeline in this world diverged completely from Earth's.

 

In other words, no one here would know about the Three Kingdoms the way he did.

 

Aurora continued, her voice steady.

 

"After entering the dungeon, every three zones will form a group. Each team is assigned to one of the three factions and will engage in battle with the others. Normally, the Samsara System ensures balance by not matching vastly different power levels together."

 

"In our case, Area C is likely to be grouped against the Cindralock Dominion from Area E and the Winterveil from Area B."

 

"As for faction assignment, it's completely random. We Samsaras don't get to choose."

 

She paused briefly, then added, "This dungeon has strict limitations. Special items, advanced skills, combat arts, and even 27-series abilities are all disabled. You can only rely on your four basic attributes and simple foundational skills."

 

"The reason those foreign forces chose to strike now is because the restrictions in this dungeon severely limit your power. They think you'll be weakened here. Shura, you must be cautious."

 

"That's all I know. I don't even have information about the mission objectives."

 

Aurora finished speaking in a single breath, then took a sip from her teacup.

 

"I understand," Fenric replied with a slight smile. "Aurora, thank you. What you've shared is incredibly helpful."

 

Despite the heavy restrictions in this dungeon, Fenric wasn't worried in the slightest.

 

His base attributes were absurdly high. Even without his abilities, he could overpower enemies of the same tier with raw stats alone.

 

Aurora frowned slightly and teased, "We're still saying thanks? I thought we were past formalities."

 1

Then her tone turned serious again. "Don't forget, the rewards for this dungeon are generous. The winning side receives double the rewards, while the losers will face punishment. Don't get careless."

 

Fenric nodded. "Got it."

 

"Well then, I won't bother you any longer."

 

Aurora rose and made her way out.

 

Watching her leave, Fenric mentally noted the favor.

 

Originally, he had considered giving the Black Sword Shusui to either Aurora or Belle as a token of gratitude.

 

Aurora probably wouldn't use it—but Belle might.

 

Yet something felt off.

 

Aurora hailed from a prominent family in the capital, and the Armand family (of One Leaf Knows Autumn) was another notable household there.

 

And Shusui had been seized from the Armand family.

 

If he gave it to Belle and the Armand family found out, things could get awkward fast.

 

They wouldn't act openly, of course—but they might quietly hold a grudge.

 1

Fenric wasn't about to make enemies on someone else's behalf.

 

After Aurora left, Fenric remained seated in the private box.

 

There was no rush.

 

The teahouse boxes were cheap—only 10 Samsara Points per hour—so staying longer wasn't an issue.

 

Besides, the ninth-level dungeon only opened once per day, at 3:00 AM.

 

It was still early.

 

After lounging in the room for another two hours, Fenric finally got up and instructed the system to send him to the Samsara Tower.

 

At the Gates of the Samsara Tower…

 

A crowd of Samsaras had already gathered.

 

When they saw Fenric appear—still in his masked assassin form—their eyes lit up.

 

Some had even been preparing to leave but chose to linger instead.

 

"Hahaha! I knew Shura would show up for the ninth-level dungeon tonight!"

 

"I've been waiting for this guy for ages!"

 

"Hey, why are we all waiting for him? Planning to gang up?"

 

"You fool! Tonight's dungeon is a team-based battle. Even if we're in the same match, our tasks probably won't conflict. And with Shura on our side, we'll definitely cruise to victory!"

 

"Fk! That makes so much sense, bro!"

 

"So that's why you guys were hanging around here!"

 

Fenric: "..."

 

Listening to their whispered chatter, Fenric felt a bit speechless.

 

These Samsara players were really... crafty.

 

But as long as they didn't interfere with him, he didn't mind. The Samsara Tower didn't belong to him, after all. He couldn't exactly kick them out.

 

As for whether they'd actually get to ride his coattails to victory—that would be up to fate.

 

More irritating to Fenric were the Samsaras loitering just to spy on him—to report back to their foreign backers.

 

He didn't care.

 

If they wanted to target him, they'd better be ready to get counter-killed.

 

Fenric's instincts were right.

 

At the Samsara Tower entrances in both Area E and Area B, large crowds of Samsaras had also gathered.

 

News had already spread: Shura has entered the ninth-level dungeon.

 

Many elite Samsaras from foreign zones had come, ready to launch a preemptive strike.

 

Some were even famous prodigies.

 

"Hey, look! 007's here too!"

 

"God, even Tom showed up!"

 

"Didn't Tom already break through to B-rank?"

 

"Yeah. He's got Adam backing him. He's the top talent in Area E right now."

 

"This time, Shura from Area C is so dead!"

 

Interest in tonight's ninth-level dungeon was growing rapidly.

 

Even high-ranking officials from various nations were beginning to take notice.

 

With so many genius Samsaras participating, any losses would be a serious blow.

 

Fenric paid no attention to the growing buzz.

 

After the dungeon cooldown expired, he refreshed his entry card and walked straight through the gates of the Samsara Tower, entering the ninth level.

 

A glowing elf spirit materialized before him.

 

"Hello, honored Samsara Shura. What assistance do you require?"

 

"I'm here to enter the dungeon," Fenric replied.

 

"This is the confrontation-type dungeon: Three Kingdoms. Are you sure you wish to proceed?"

 

"I'm sure."

 

As soon as he confirmed, Fenric was instantly teleported into a white chamber.

 

It was crowded—full of people.

 

Very crowded.

chapters.name: Chapter 229: Chapter 229: The Battle for Hegemony Begins!
chapters.content:
"Here he comes! The boss—Shura is here!"

 

"Finally, hope has arrived! This wave, we're all following Shura!"

 

"As long as we hug his thigh, if Master Shura eats meat, we can at least drink the soup!"

 

"Don't celebrate too soon—I heard there are foreign forces trying to snipe Shura in this dungeon!"

 

"For real?!"

 

"Damn it, why say that now? Don't let the city gate fire burn us pond fish!"

 

"I'm out! When gods clash, mortals should get out of the way!"

 

"I'm not leaving. I believe in Shura. If he dared to show up knowing people are gunning for him, that means he's fully confident."

 

"Yeah! Shura's the real deal—never failed a dungeon, always goes super god mode, and always walks away with an SSS rank! If anyone's reliable, it's him!"

 

"Snipe the Shura boss? Ha! I hope they don't get counter-killed instead!"

 

At that moment, at least a hundred Samsara players had gathered in the preparation room, with more still arriving.

 

As soon as Fenric appeared, the place erupted in chatter.

 

Suddenly, a Samsara stepped forward and declared, "Great God Shura, I'm Monkey! I just reached a comprehensive Level B. If our tasks don't conflict, I'm willing to follow your lead. Let's teach those foreigners a lesson!"

 

His words had just landed when his companion chimed in, "Me too, Lord Shura! I'm Liuer. As long as our objectives align, I'll follow your command without question!"

 

Their enthusiasm sparked a wave of similar declarations.

 

"And me!"

 

"Count me in! Let's give those outsiders a hard slap!"

 1

"I'm in!"

 

"Great God Shura, as long as it means fighting off the foreigners, I'll follow your every word!"

 

In the end, the majority of Samsaras present openly expressed their willingness to follow Shura's orders.

 

The unified display of loyalty fired up the entire crowd.

 

Energy surged. Morale soared.

 

And Fenric?

 

He laughed.

 

A full, pleased laugh.

 

He raised his voice and said confidently, "Alright then! Let's deal with the foreigners—together!"

 3

If their missions didn't clash, teaming up to crush outsiders only made sense.

 

After Shura gave his blessing, the energy in the preparation room reached a fever pitch.

 

Then came the system announcement:

 

"Attention all Samsaras: Teleportation to the mission world will begin in 10 minutes."

 

More and more Samsaras continued to gather.

 

By now, at least 200 had assembled.

 

The chatter never stopped—except around Fenric, who had closed his eyes to rest. Out of respect, no one dared disturb him.

 

Ten minutes passed in a flash.

 

"Teleportation countdown starting: 10, 9, 8... 3, 2, 1!"

 

When the countdown ended, red light enveloped everyone in the room, and they vanished from sight.

 

"Matching opponents..."

 

"Match successful. Your competitors this round: Zone E and Zone H."

 

"Assigning factions..."

 

"Faction assigned: Cao Wei."

 1

"Warning: This is a counter-dungeon world. Special items, skills, fighting techniques, and abilities are prohibited."

 

Inside the red light, each Samsara received this notification.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed.

 

Zone H?

 

Wasn't that the Thousand Lanterns Island Nation?

 1

How very coincidental.

 

A new interface floated before him—a virtual figure of an ordinary soldier appeared.

 

"Samsara player 'Shura', this is your default appearance in this world. Please customize it if desired."

 

Fenric made a few adjustments—not to make himself look overly awe-inspiring, but just enough to have clean features and an honest face, something that would inspire trust.

 

"Age defaulted to 20. Please enter your alias for this world."

 

He thought for a moment.

 

Then, reversing his nickname "Shura," he typed: Arush.

 4

"Alias confirmed. All Samsaras will be fluent in this world's language automatically."

 

The red glow vanished.

 

When Fenric's vision returned, he found himself inside a military tent.

 

Through the tent's entrance, he saw an open training ground. A massive banner fluttered proudly in the wind, bearing a single bold character: "Cao."

 

"So this is Cao Ying?"

 

Fenric smiled with satisfaction. Being assigned to Cao Cao's army was a stroke of luck.

 

Everyone knew—during the Three Kingdoms era, Cao Cao was the strongest warlord.

 

Sure, Liu Bei had his famed Five Tiger Generals, adored by future generations.

 

But what use was fan service in the middle of a mission?

 

Fenric wasn't here to chase legends—he was here to clear objectives.

 

Looking around, he took in the crude interior. Straw mats served as beds. A few soldiers lay about, resting.

 

Beside each man lay a redwood spear—including one next to Fenric.

 

Pikemen, huh?

 

Fenric narrowed his eyes and tried activating his telekinesis.

 

Nothing.

 

The spear didn't budge.

 

"Just as I thought—Telekinesis powers are sealed."

 

He tried activating Armament Haki.

 

Still nothing.

 

But...

 

Fenric clenched his fists.

 

He could still feel the Power coursing through him.

 

He smiled confidently.

 

As long as he had power—and plot awareness—he'd still dominate.

 

"System Alert: Main Mission Initiated (Code: Arush)"

 1

Main Mission 1: Earn Reputation Points

 

Objective: Earn at least 1000 reputation points in 15 days

 

Current Progress: 0/1000

 

Failure: Obliteration

 

Note: Higher rep = better final score

 

Main Mission 2: Win the Team Battle

 

Objective: Lead your faction to victory within 15 days

 

Failure: Lose half the rewards from Mission 1

chapters.name: Chapter 230: Chapter 230: This Military Commander Is So Fierce!
chapters.content:
"Hint: Task 2 rewards will be based on individual performance!"

 

Fenric blinked in surprise when he heard the system prompt.

 

Before he could process it, a deep, rhythmic drumbeat echoed outside—

 

BOOM—! BOOM—! BOOM—!

 

The sound resonated through the ancient barracks, signaling the call to assemble.

 

Around him, several resting soldiers leaped up like startled rabbits. Grabbing their weapons, they rushed out of the tent without hesitation.

 

"Drums are sounding! Formation orders in place! Those who delay will be punished!"

 

"Arush! Why are you still standing there? Hurry to the training grounds!" an older soldier shouted.

 

Fenric quickly followed the crowd outside.

 

Soon, wave after wave of soldiers converged on the training field.

 

Fenric, tall as he was, saw nothing but a sea of heads stretching out endlessly. There were so many Cao army soldiers that he couldn't even begin to count them.

 

When the drumming ceased, the entire field was packed.

 

Then, a general in heavy armor strode onto the central platform.

 

He was a burly man with a powerful frame, emanating the presence of a true warrior.

 

The moment Fenric laid eyes on him, he immediately recognized the man.

 

There was only one one-eyed general under Cao Cao's command—Xiahou Dun.

 

"You lot have been gathered today to perform martial arts," Dun barked. "The Lord himself is watching and has granted you this chance. If you've got skills, now's the time to show them. Promotions await the worthy!"

 

Clearly, Dun tried to rally the troops, but he wasn't the most eloquent speaker.

 

Still, Fenric understood the gist—today's event was a martial arts showcase.

 

In other words, a competition.

 

He figured Cao Cao was planning something and wanted to use this tournament to scout out talent quickly.

 

Fenric's eyes gleamed. He immediately realized that this was a golden opportunity arranged by the Samsara system—a public stage for the Samsaras to demonstrate their strength and earn prestige.

 

"Begin the martial arts performance!" Dun declared before stepping down from the platform.

 

Immediately after, a young man in soft armor leapt onto the stage.

 

"I am Zhong Jin, a subordinate of General Dun. If anyone dares, come up and challenge me!"

 

It was clear that Zhong Jin was the first official test—an initial hurdle to gauge the strength of contenders.

 

Fenric wasn't eager to step in just yet.

 

Instead, he scanned the crowd—then his gaze landed on a group of officials standing atop the observation platform to the left.

 

Some were in armor, others in long gowns. Clearly, these were Cao Cao's senior officers and advisors.

 

At the center stood a man who instantly drew Fenric's attention.

 

He wore a robe embroidered with a hundred flowers, appeared to be in his fifties, and stood just under seven feet (roughly 1.7 meters). Though not tall, his calm demeanor and piercing gaze radiated authority.

 1

The generals and strategists surrounding him deferred to him like stars orbiting the moon. Even Dun stood respectfully behind him.

 

It didn't take long for Fenric to piece it together.

 

Cao Cao.

 1

 

 

Only the infamous "Wife Stealer Cao" could command such presence.

 

Soon, a new challenger stepped onto the stage.

 

"I am Liu Chu! I respectfully request a duel!"

 

Dressed like a regular soldier, Liu Chu surprised everyone with his skill. His power and speed outmatched Zhong Jin from the get-go. If not for Zhong Jin's extensive battle experience, he would've lost in seconds.

 

Fenric, watching his technique, could tell immediately—

 

Another Samsara.

 

A few minutes later, Zhong Jin lost.

 

The crowd erupted into murmurs and surprised gasps.

 

On the observation platform, Cao Cao smiled. "That man is quite skilled. Dun, your subordinate underestimated his opponent."

 

Dun's expression tightened with embarrassment. He scowled and inwardly cursed Zhong Jin—how could he lose to a mere recruit?

 

The competition continued.

 

Liu Chu proved to be strong and swift, clearly boasting over 100 points in both strength and speed attributes. His strikes were fast and brutal, defeating several opponents before finally being bested by another Samsara.

 

That Samsara won mostly because Liu Chu had exhausted himself.

 

Soon, the arena became the Samsaras' playground.

 

With overwhelming power and combat prowess, they made short work of the regular soldiers.

 

Time passed quickly.

 

After about an hour, a Samsara named Iron Bull dominated the stage.

 

This brute possessed immense strength—Fenric estimated at least 150 points—and had clearly mastered basic boxing techniques to a high degree. His fists struck like sledgehammers, and he had already defeated sixteen opponents in a row.

 

On the observation platform, the generals looked increasingly grim.

 

None of them had expected so many powerful fighters to emerge during what was supposed to be a simple exhibition.

 

Worse, their own troops had been thoroughly humiliated.

 

As their subordinates fell one after another, their pride as commanding officers took a serious hit.

 

Seeing that Iron Bull was still undefeated, one burly military officer in black and blue armor finally stepped forward and addressed Cao Cao:

 

"My Lord, watching this warrior has stirred something in me. Allow me to test his strength!"

 

Cao Cao raised an eyebrow, then chuckled. "Miaocai, are your hands getting itchy?"

 

Miaocai was Pang De's courtesy name.

 

Pang De grinned. "Exactly, my Lord. It's been a while since I've seen such impressive hand-to-hand skills. I'm eager to stretch my limbs!"

 

"Very well," Cao Cao said with a nod. "Go, but be merciful."

 

Truthfully, Cao Cao was in a good mood.

 

So many hidden talents among his ranks—his army was full of potential. There was no shortage of future champions.

 

Pang De saluted, then performed a standing flip from the elevated platform.

 

BOOM—!

 

He landed with such force that the ground cracked slightly.

 

Without missing a beat, Pang De walked calmly toward the ring.

 

Back at the observation area, Fenric had been paying close attention to the building platform.

 

When he saw the general leap down from such a height unscathed, his brows furrowed.

 

Something's off.

 

Even in the fictional world of Romance of the Three Kingdoms, generals didn't usually transcend human limits.

 

To land from that height without injury? Physically impossible for a normal human being.

 

The resilience Pang De just displayed clearly surpassed the bounds of natural human endurance.

 

There was only one explanation:

 

The Samsara system had tampered with the generals as well.

 

It didn't just regulate Samsara players—it enhanced the native characters too.
