chapters.name: Chapter 256: Chapter 256: The Samsaras in Zone E Can’t Sit Still!
chapters.content:
The Samsara Space was in an uproar.

 

Everywhere, discussions rang out. Fenric—known to all as Shura—had done the unthinkable. He had survived a nuclear explosion.

 

To ordinary Samsaras, it was simply shocking news, something to chatter about in disbelief. But to those preparing to challenge the tenth floor of the Samsara Tower, it was terrifying.

 

"F*ck, did I hear that right? A nuke went off in [Final Destination]? That's not a dungeon, that's suicide!"

 

"I'm out. From now on, I'm staying right here. I'm no Shura—I can't survive a damn nuclear blast."

 

"Heh, idiots. Do you think Death starts with nukes? First, it hunts you with smaller disasters, then raises the difficulty bit by bit. Only someone like Shura, who can't be killed by normal means, would force Death into using a nuke. Name one other person who's seen a nuclear strike inside the copy!"

 

"True. Getting a Super God evaluation isn't supposed to be easy."

 

The casual Samsara players were stunned, but those at higher levels realized something more important: Shura's rise was no longer a possibility—it was a fact.

 

Anyone who could walk out of a nuclear blast alive could no longer be treated as a "newcomer." Fenric was now a force, a giant among Samsara players.

 

In Jadeveil Nation, people celebrated. Even though Shura hadn't joined the government, his strength as a compatriot was a source of pride, not threat. But abroad, the atmosphere was far more sour.

 1

Every powerful Samsara was the equivalent of a living nuclear weapon. And now, a newcomer on the tenth floor could already survive the real thing. What would he become by the twentieth? An S-rank monster?

 

For many, one Adam was already too much to stomach. Now there was another.

 

The most unsettled of all was the Cindralock Dominion.

 

In Zone E, Samsara players reacted with fury and disbelief.

 

"Damn! Did the system glitch? How can some tenth-floor rookie survive a nuke!?"

 

"What a joke! Did the toy explode instead of the real thing?"

 

"Look at Shura, then look at our 'Tom'… depressing."

 

"No way. Shura had to have cheated! No one survives that!"

 

"Cheating? Don't be stupid. The Samsara System never makes mistakes. Like it or not, Shura just proved his survivability is unmatched—number one."

 

The E-Zone buzzed with bitterness and denial.

 

In an entertainment city, inside a private bar box, one man sat drinking alone. His Samsara avatar was unremarkable—plain clothes, balding, shabby. But everyone who knew him understood his name carried weight.

 1

Adam.

 

The world's number one.

 

The system broadcast had echoed in his ears, but his expression didn't change. Only when the glass in his hand suddenly shattered with a sharp crack did his feelings show.

 

Cold light flickered in his eyes.

 

Adam stood, tossed a handful of Samsara points to cover the damage, and logged off without a word.

 

Back in the real world, he picked up his phone and dialed.

 

The line clicked.

 

"Have you found Shura's identity?" Adam asked, his voice low.

 

"There are some leads," came the calm reply. "Two days ago, in AH City of Jadeveil Nation, a Blacklight Virus adapter was killed. Witnesses say a mysterious master was responsible. Initial suspicion: Shura himself. Our people are still investigating his true identity."

 

"Good. Find him. As soon as possible!"

 

"Understood, Your Majesty the Pope."

 1

Meanwhile, Fenric had returned to Samsara Space.

 

His body was fully healed, but his heart carried exhaustion. The final minutes inside the nuclear firestorm were an ordeal he would never forget.

 2

System Notification:

 

"Dear Samsara player, Shura. You have completed your mission. Your rewards are as follows:

 

Samsara Points: 55,000

 

Samsara Wanted x1

 1

Credit Black Card x1 (special item, stored in your personal warehouse)

 

Golden Treasure Box x1 (stored in your personal warehouse)"

 

Even with new treasures in his hands, Fenric wasn't eager to check them. Instead, he slumped onto a sofa, letting his mind settle.

 

The calming effect of Tranquility Tea worked quickly, quieting his restless spirit.

 

Then another prompt appeared:

 

You have a new communication message. 'Belle Morwyn' requests a video call. Please respond.

 

Fenric blinked in surprise, then accepted.

 

Belle's elegant figure appeared on the screen.

 

"Shura," she said with a gentle smile. "Congratulations. Another Super God evaluation."

 

Fenric sighed softly. "Thank you."

 

She studied his face. "What's wrong? You seem… troubled."

 

He shook his head, unwilling to explain. "Belle, are you free? Come have some tea. I'm in Box 3465."

 

"Alright," she replied. "Wait for me."

 

The call ended.

 

Not long after, Belle arrived at the teahouse.

 

"Shura." She greeted him warmly.

 

Fenric smiled faintly. "Sit. I already ordered Tranquility Tea for you."

 

"You don't look well. Did something happen?" she asked, her voice soft with concern.

 

Fenric exhaled. "It's nothing. Just tired. I'll rest soon."

 

Her brows furrowed slightly. She knew him well—his strength, his will, his unyielding nature. For a man like Shura to show fatigue, the ordeal must have been beyond brutal.

 

She thought back to the announcement, her heart tightening.

 

"Shura… was the nuclear explosion that terrifying?"

 

Fenric froze for a moment, then gave a wry smile. "Terrifying, yes. But I endured. I just need rest."

 

"Don't push yourself so hard," Belle murmured. "Even you need time to breathe."

 

Fenric's gaze softened. "I'll be fine."

chapters.name: Chapter 257: Chapter 257: The Name of Shura Appears on the Global Master List!
chapters.content:
Half an hour later.

 

"Belle, thank you for coming to talk with me. I feel much better now."

 

Belle Morwyn smiled softly, her voice gentle. "Shura, we're good friends. There's no need to be so polite."

 2

She then rose gracefully to her feet. "You should rest early."

 

"Alright."

 

Fenric watched her departing figure with quiet admiration.

 

There was a saying: a woman is like water, capable of nourishing a man's heart. At this moment, Fenric felt the truth of it deeply.

 6

Belle was indeed gentle and considerate. After sharing a simple conversation with her, much of the exhaustion weighing on him had faded.

 

He felt renewed—confident and strong once more.

 

But he also knew: only women of true gentleness could give such comfort. In this age, such women were rare. Most were self-centered, difficult, and exhausting to be with. The kind who drained rather than nurtured. A man who married such a woman would not find rest, but only endless fatigue.

 

Fenric did not log off immediately. Instead, he headed to his personal warehouse.

 

From his recent mission, he had obtained two particularly novel rewards.

 

One was a black credit card.

 

The other, a Samsara Wanted Order.

 

Fenric picked up the credit card first.

 

The system's prompt rang out:

 

Special Item: Black Credit Card

 

A credit card usable only in mission copies set in modern societies. It carries a spending limit of 100 million USD.

 

Note: Cannot be used in the real world.

 

Fenric blinked in surprise.

 

It seemed both useless and invaluable at the same time. Perhaps not a combat tool, but certainly a practical one. Next time he entered a modern-world copy, he would never need to worry about money again.

 

Placing it back on the shelf, he picked up the rolled parchment of the Samsara Wanted Order.

 

Consumable Item: Samsara Wanted Order

 

Contains the identity of a wanted criminal.

 

Defeating the target yields bonus Samsara Points and a random ability from the criminal.

 

How to use: Break the seal to reveal the target's information.

 

Fenric frowned slightly.

 

Interesting… so it's like a bounty mission? Who could the target be?

 

For now, he decided to wait before unsealing it.

 

Finally, he withdrew the Golden Treasure Box and opened it.

 

Congratulations! You have obtained the ability: Death Sense!

 

Death Sense (Passive): Alerts you to danger in advance.

 2

Strength of sensation varies. When the warning is overwhelming, avoid at all costs—your life is at stake.

 

Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

As expected of a golden treasure chest. Always something good inside.

 

Though not directly increasing his combat power, this passive ability massively strengthened his survivability. With Death Sense, his chances of avoiding fatal danger had increased by at least seventy percent.

 

"Similar to Spider-Man's spider-sense… but stronger. Not bad."

 1

Fenric smiled, satisfied.

 

Now only his Samsara Points remained. He had earned 55,000.

 

After some thought, he exchanged 50,000 points for 100 Potential Points, leaving 5,000 as reserve.

 

He then distributed the potential evenly among his four attributes.

 

Name: Shura

 

Samsara Number: (C Zone) 90086

 

Physique: 345

 

Spirit: 690

 

Strength: 413

 

Agility: 345

 

Allocable Potential: 0

 

Skills: English (Proficient), Driving (Beginner), Shooting (Proficient), Camouflage (Master), Basic Sword Technique (Proficient)

 

Special Skills: Conqueror's Haki (Mastery), Armament Haki (Superior)

 

Combat Techniques: Savage Charge, Buddha Palm

 

Abilities: Telekinesis, Hundred-Poison Immunity (Passive), Death Sense (Passive)

 

Samsara Points: 5,281

 

Comprehensive Evaluation: A

 

Fenric studied the property panel with satisfaction.

 

Very strong.

 

Closing the warehouse, he turned his attention to the Global Master List.

 

His name had yet to appear.

 

Then, summoning Thor's Hammer into his hand, Fenric watched as the list suddenly shifted.

 

The 99th rank was pushed down to 100, and the original 100th place vanished entirely.

 

And there it was—his vest name.

 

Shura – 99th Place!

 

Fenric's gaze sharpened.

 

This meant that with just Thor's Hammer, his power was enough to stand among the top 100 masters in the world.

 

Each one on that list was a giant, someone courted by nations, someone who commanded respect and fear.

 

Fenric exhaled, calm but resolute, then withdrew the hammer back into his warehouse.

 

Immediately, his name disappeared from the rankings, and the displaced masters returned to their positions.

 

Satisfied, Fenric logged off from Samsara Space.

 

One Minute Earlier, Zone E.

 

Three Samsaras were walking toward Samsara Tower Fourth Floor, chatting idly as they passed the Global Master List.

 

Suddenly, one of them froze and screamed:

 

"OH MY GOD! LOOK AT RANK 99—!"

 

"Wha—Shura?! Damn it!"

 

"That guy just cleared a tenth-floor copy, and now he's in the top 100?"

 

"God… is this man a demon?"

 

"Huh? Wait—why did his name just vanish?"

 

"Were we seeing things?"

 

"Impossible! All three of us hallucinating at once? No way."

 

"Then what happened? A system error?"

 

The three Samsaras stared at the list, unwilling to look away, as if the truth might appear again at any moment.

chapters.name: Chapter 258: Chapter 258: Class B Wanted Criminal!
chapters.content:
The next morning.

 

Fenric opened his eyes. Sunlight slipped through the curtains—it was already past nine.

 

Stepping out of his room, he saw Father Eric packing his belongings.

 

Fenric paused. "Dad, are you going on a long trip?"

 

Father Eric smiled. "AH City has been unblocked. I plan to return today."

 

Fenric frowned. Unblocked already? Just two or three days?

 

Could the Blacklight Virus really be contained so easily?

 

Then again, in this world filled with powerful Samsaras, even virus hosts stood little chance of causing chaos. It was nothing like the Prototype world, where a protagonist with overwhelming abilities and a corrupt government behind him had plunged Manhattan into an uncontrollable disaster.

 

"Maybe… wait a couple more days to see how the situation develops?" Fenric suggested.

 

Father Eric shook his head. "I'm not used to staying here. There are things at home I need to handle. Don't worry, I'll be fine."

 4

Fenric didn't press further.

 

After sending his father off at the station, he did not return home. Instead, he pulled out the Samsara Wanted Order.

 

He was deeply curious about this thing.

 

A quick search online revealed nothing. Clearly, it was a rare item even within Samsara Space.

 

Without hesitation, Fenric broke the seal and unrolled it.

 

No visions. No dramatic light.

 

Just an unremarkable sheet of paper, A4-sized, with a sketch of a fierce-looking man and details listed beneath.

 

Name: Choi Hojae

 

Origin: Soule, Willowland

 

Strength Evaluation: Class B

 

Wanted Reason: Violation of Samsara Contract – Murder of Contract Partner

 

Note: The Eye of Pursuit has been temporarily activated. If within one kilometer of the target, their position will automatically be locked.

 

Reminder: After activation, you have three days to assassinate the target. After three days, the warrant will expire.

 

Failure: No punishment.

 

Fenric's brows furrowed.

 

A bastard who not only violated the Samsara contract but even murdered his partner? Ruthless.

 

But stranger still—if Samsara Space wanted him gone, why not erase him directly? Why delegate?

 

Does this mean that Samsara Space can't touch someone once they hide in the real world? That its influence is limited outside?

 

Then what about mandatory large-scale events like the annual "Battle Royale"? If enforcement was possible there, why not here?

 

Fenric exhaled slowly. No point overthinking. I'll ask him myself once I reach him.

 

The man was only B-class. Fenric wasn't concerned.

 

Later that day, he visited Computer City to buy a new high-end machine and arrange broadband services. With money, everything moved smoothly. By afternoon, everything was set up—he could finally enjoy proper internet at home.

 

When evening came, Fenric headed to a deserted construction site. Unfinished concrete frames loomed in silence, no pedestrians, no surveillance cameras.

 

Perfect.

 

From his storage, he summoned the Mark VII Armor.

 

"Clank! Click!"

 

The mechanical voice echoed as the armor pieces locked into place, wrapping around his body.

 

In mere breaths, Fenric had transformed into a steel titan—an iron giant in the night.

 

"Tsunade, destination: Soule, Willowland."

 1

"Received, Master."

 

"And activate the shielding system. I don't want radar picking us up."

 

"Understood."

 

7:30 PM.

 

Soule was at its liveliest. The capital glowed—traffic jams, neon lights, crowded streets. Stylish young women filled the avenues, some arm-in-arm with friends, others out fishing for "catches."

 

Choi Hojae, 32, was in his prime.

 

Years of grinding through Samsara Space had given him power. Using it, he climbed into the ranks of Soule's underworld, eventually becoming head of a powerful syndicate. Only the consortium behind the organization stood above him.

 

Though barred from entering Samsara Space due to past actions, he didn't mind. Why risk his life in dungeons when he could live like a king here?

 

He slept until noon, feasted daily, and enjoyed endless wealth. As for women—any he desired, he took. And when they resisted… he forced them. More than a dozen had already died under his abuse.

 

To him, it was a life worthy of an emperor.

 

That night, he stepped out of a luxury hotel, grinning as he slid into his car. In the top suite of another hotel nearby, a young starlet waited for him fresh from the shower.

 

"What a wonderful evening," Choi laughed. Another night of indulgence awaited him.

 

But what he didn't know was that far above, eyes were watching.

 

Fenric had just arrived in Soule. Luck was on his side—he had locked onto the target almost immediately.

 

The Eye of Pursuit worked flawlessly. Within a kilometer of the target, Fenric could sense him instantly, his figure glowing red in his vision.

 

For now, Fenric made no move.

 

He knew Soule was home to several A-class Samsaras. Making a scene in public could draw them out.

 

He wasn't afraid… but unnecessary attention was wasteful.

 

Patience.

 

The hunt had only just begun.

chapters.name: Chapter 259: Chapter 259: The Bloodline Awakens!
chapters.content:
Not long after, Fenric appeared inside a luxurious hotel building.

 

His appearance had changed—he now wore a disguise mask, altering his features into the likeness of one of Choi Hojae's subordinates.

 

Though he wasn't sure which floor Choi Hojae had entered, the temporary Eye of Pursuit gave him an undeniable advantage. In Fenric's sight, the man glowed like a firefly, impossible to miss.

 

Guided by the mark, Fenric stopped at the 28th floor, outside Room 2812. The presence inside confirmed his suspicion: the target was there.

 

Two young men in suits stood guard by the door. When they saw Fenric approach, the one on the left barked something in Willowlean.

 

Fenric didn't understand, nor did he care to.

 

With a flick of his hand, there was a sharp crack. Both men's necks twisted at unnatural angles as they collapsed lifelessly to the floor.

 

He didn't bother with a keycard. Instead, Fenric lifted his foot and struck.

 

Boom!

 

The reinforced door shattered instantly under his kick.

 

The noise startled the occupants inside.

 

A man and a woman turned sharply, clearly interrupted in the middle of their "work." The man was none other than Choi Hojae.

 

At first startled, Hojae's expression quickly shifted to anger when he recognized Fenric's assumed face.

 

"You bastard! What the hell are you doing?!" he cursed in Willowlean language, mistaking Fenric for his subordinate.

 

Fenric only caught the swearing.

 

The next moment, his mind power surged.

 

Buzz!

 

Choi Hojae froze in place, bound by an invisible force. His eyes widened in disbelief.

 

Fenric's cold voice broke the silence, switching to English. "Do you speak English?"

 

Hojae's face twisted with unease. "...Who are you?" he stammered in accented English.

 

"Samsara," Fenric replied flatly. "I took the order from Samsara Space. I'm here to execute you."

 

Hojae paled, his earlier suspicion confirmed.

 

Then, desperation flared in his gaze. His throat expanded, and he let out a violent scream.

 

A piercing, high-frequency shriek tore through the room.

 

Shatter!

 

The glass windows burst apart.

 

The woman at his side clutched her head and screamed as her eardrums ruptured, blood streaming down her ears.

 

But Fenric stood unaffected.

 

It wasn't because his ears were naturally resistant—Death Sense had warned him just before the attack, and he had quickly cloaked himself in Armament Haki. The protective energy shielded every inch of his body, including his ears.

 

Even so, Fenric raised an eyebrow. "So, he had this kind of ability hidden away? Interesting."

 

With a flick of his wrist, a longsword materialized in his hand. The blade gleamed as he pressed the tip against Hojae's throat.

 

The shrieking stopped instantly.

 

The woman, however, had already collapsed—her fragile body couldn't withstand even a few seconds of the sonic assault.

 

"Answer my question, and I'll give you a clean death," Fenric said coldly.

 

Hojae's bravado crumbled. He trembled, eyes darting. "Please... sir. I can give you all my money. Just let me go!"

 

Fenric's expression remained unmoved. "Do you think I need your money?"

 

Hojae faltered, realizing the absurdity of his offer. What use was wealth to someone like this?

 

Fenric pressed the blade closer. "How did you escape the compulsory summons of Samsara Space?" His voice was icy. "Answer me, or I'll take my time before killing you."

 

Hojae clenched his jaw, then finally blurted, "It's simple! Just cut out the full moon tattoo on your arm. That's it!"

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed in surprise. That's all it takes?

 

"Please," Hojae continued desperately, "I also have rare items. You'll definitely want them—"

 

Fenric snorted. "Special items? Since when can those be traded privately?"

 

Everyone knew the Samsara Space's rules: such items could only be exchanged through the official Trade Center. Private deals were punished severely.

 

But Hojae shook his head frantically. "I'm telling the truth! I'm no longer bound by Samsara Space. That's why my items can be traded freely, here in the real world!"

 

"Oh?" Fenric gave a faint smile.

 

Then he thrust his sword.

 

Puff!

 

The blade pierced straight through Hojae's throat.

 

His eyes bulged in shock, blood bubbling at his lips as he stared at Fenric with disbelief.

 

"My greatest strength," Fenric said evenly, "is that I'm not greedy."

 1

Hojae's body twitched, then went limp. His head slumped forward as life fled from his eyes.

 

Ding—!

 

A chime echoed in Fenric's mind.

 

"Congratulations. You have eliminated the wanted criminal, Choi Hojae. Reward: 30,000 Samsara Points."

 

Fenric frowned. Only thirty thousand? For a B-rank target?

 1

It had been easy for him, but most Samsaras at that level would have struggled or failed. Still, the reward felt paltry. Stingy system...

 

Just then, something shimmered above Hojae's corpse.

 

A glass vial appeared, hovering in the air.

 

Fenric caught it instinctively and stared at its contents—several milliliters of vivid red liquid, like blood.

 

Ding—!

 

The system chimed again:

 

"Consumable Item Acquired: Saiyan Bloodline (Modified).

 17

Upon use: permanently fuses Saiyan genes.

 

Grants +50 to Physical Attributes, +50 to Power Attributes.

 

Additional Effect: By expending Samsara Points, user can evolve into a Super Saiyan, drastically amplifying combat strength."

 

"Holy!"

 

Fenric's breath caught. His eyes widened.

 

Saiyan bloodline?! From a mere B-rank Samsara?!

 

Super Saiyans were warriors capable of destroying planets.

 1

If Hojae had truly unlocked that power… Fenric admitted to himself, today's mission might have ended with his corpse instead.

 1

chapters.name: Chapter 260: Chapter 260: The Battle Begins!
chapters.content:
Saiyan!

 

From the anime Dragon Ball.

 

A race of legendary warriors once hailed as the strongest in anime history.

 

For Fenric to obtain Saiyan blood in this mission was beyond a pleasant surprise—it was a monumental gain.

 

If the Samsara Space had been accessible right now, he would have entered immediately to study it in detail.

 

But for now, he carefully stored the vial of Saiyan blood into his personal warehouse, preparing to leave.

 

At that moment—

 

Boom!

 

A sonic boom thundered across the sky.

 

A figure in shorts and a crimson cloak shot across the distance, stopping mid-air outside the hotel window. Hovering effortlessly, the man's piercing gaze locked onto Fenric.

 

Down on the street below, pedestrians who had heard the sonic boom looked up in shock.

 

"Look, it's the superhero—Golden Sage King!"

 

"It's really him! Oppa, you're so handsome!"

 

"Oppa, I love you!"

 

"Why is Senior Golden Sage King here? Did a criminal appear in that hotel?"

 

"Hah, this is going to be good. That guy's unlucky now! Senior Golden Sage King is ranked on the 24th floor of Samsara Tower, ranked 96th on the world's top 100 list! He's also the number one powerhouse of Willowland Republic. Whoever's inside is done for!"

 

"Yeah, thanks to Senior Golden Sage King, Soule's been much safer!"

 

"Safe, huh? Don't forget—the Co-Zhu Society under his control is the biggest gang in the city."

 

The crowd erupted with excitement as though they were watching a celebrity. The already bustling street became deafening.

 

Fenric couldn't understand their language, but their reactions told him enough: this man was famous.

 

And judging by the sonic boom earlier, his speed alone placed him at least at A-rank.

 

If not for his Eastern face and gaudy costume, Fenric might have mistaken him for a certain muscular hero from the DC universe.

 

"Looking for me?" Fenric frowned, replying in English.

 

He guessed the man possessed some alien bloodline, likely granting him super-hearing similar to Superman's. That would explain why he had arrived so quickly. The only question was—how close was he to the real Superman?

 

"Who are you? Why are you committing crimes in Soule?" Golden Sage King demanded righteously.

 

Fenric nearly gagged at the sight.

 

Really? In this day and age, someone still insists on playing superhero? And he's not even young—what's with the second-hand delusions?

 

He was too lazy to argue. His tone was flat. "I'm leaving. If you plan to stop me, try. Otherwise—get lost."

 3

Golden Sage King's face darkened.

 

In the next instant, he vanished.

 

Whoosh!

 

The air cracked as he closed the distance in a blur, throwing a devastating punch straight at Fenric.

 

To ordinary eyes, his movement was invisible.

 

But Fenric was far from ordinary.

 

He clearly saw the attack and chose not to counter. Instead, he crossed his arms, coating them in Armament Haki to brace for impact.

 

He wanted to test the man's strength.

 

Boom!!

 

The blow landed like a cannonball.

 

Fenric's body was blasted backward, crashing through the hotel wall. Debris rained as he shot across the building, bursting out the far side before plummeting toward the ground.

 

Screams echoed from the street as pedestrians scattered.

 

Just before hitting the pavement, Fenric's body jolted. He halted in mid-air, hovering above the ground.

 

He was flying.

 

His psychic power now allowed him to sustain short bursts of flight.

 

But compared to Golden Sage King's effortless speed, it was crude at best.

 

Still, Fenric was mildly impressed. His strength attribute's higher than mine… but nowhere near the true Superman.

 

"This guy must've obtained a weakened version of the Kryptonian bloodline. Weaker than the original—but still formidable," Fenric analyzed inwardly.

 2

Golden Sage King descended after him, drawing even louder cheers from the crowd.

 

"Oppa!" "Oppa!"

 

The man ignored the shouting fans. His cold eyes fixed only on Fenric.

 

"You're impressive. To withstand my strike without dying… Reveal your true identity and surrender. Do that, and I'll spare your life." He spoke in English.

 

Fenric chuckled. This man really loved theatrics.

 

"Enough nonsense. If you want to fight, then fight."

 

With that, Fenric dropped to the ground.

 

His flight couldn't match the other man's; it would be foolish to battle him in the sky. And while he had Mark VII armor, against an A-rank powerhouse it would be nothing more than a fragile toy—scrap metal waiting to be torn apart.

 

Golden Sage King's expression darkened further.

 

Turning to the crowd, he called out, "This place will soon become a battlefield. Evacuate immediately!"

 

The onlookers obeyed, retreating in panic. Still, most only moved a safe distance away, hiding behind barriers while excitedly pulling out their phones.

 

They were already planning titles for the footage:

 

"Mysterious Master vs. Superhero Golden Sage King!"

 

Whoosh!

 

The air split again.

 

The two A-rank masters finally clashed head-on.

 

Golden Sage King's fist blurred toward Fenric's face.

 

This time, Fenric didn't defend.

 

He clenched his own fist and swung forward to meet it.

 

BOOM!

 

The collision was like thunder erupting from the earth.

 

A shockwave burst outward, tearing through the street in all directions. Wind roared, scattering debris and knocking people off their feet.

 

Gasps filled the air.

 

Two fists colliding—yet the force was enough to cause a hurricane.

 

The citizens stared in awe.

 

Everyone knew Golden Sage King was the number one powerhouse in Willowland Republic.

 

But who was this mysterious stranger who could match him blow for blow?

chapters.name: Chapter 261: Chapter 261: The Man Causing Trouble in the Capital—Shura?
chapters.content:
"Not bad! You actually managed to block seventy percent of my strength!"

 

Golden Sage King's voice was confident, yet his eyes carried a hint of solemnity.

 

"Try taking another punch!" he roared, lunging forward with another strike.

 

"Boom!"

 

The force behind his fist split the air apart, followed by a deafening sonic boom. This time, Golden Sage King was no longer holding back—he was going all out.

 

Fenric, however, remained calm.

 

He raised his fist.

 

And punched.

 

Fenric knew he couldn't match the Golden Sage King in raw strength, so this time, he activated Savage Charge.

 

The skill not only granted him five seconds of invincibility but also instantly tripled his strength.

 

"Boom!!"

 

Their fists collided once more.

 

"!!"

 

Golden Sage King's expression changed drastically. It felt as though he hadn't struck a man at all, but an immovable mountain.

 

In the next moment, an overwhelming force surged from Fenric's fist.

 

Golden Sage King's entire body was hurled away like a cannonball.

 

"Crash!!"

 

He smashed through a streetlamp, snapping it in half, before tumbling into the roadside greenery, rolling to a stop.

 

Though he possessed a body of steel—a weakened version, but still formidable—Fenric's blow left him reeling, blood surging within his chest.

 

Fenric narrowed his eyes, watching as the so-called superhero rose to his feet again.

 

This guy's strength… it's no joke. Probably one of the strongest I've faced so far.

 

(What Fenric didn't yet know was that his opponent was among the top 100 on the global ranking list.)

 

"You've angered me!" Golden Sage King roared. His eyes glowed crimson, and suddenly, Fenric felt a chilling wave of imminent death wash over him.

 

His face darkened.

 

Damn it, don't tell me…!

 

The next instant, twin beams of searing red energy shot from Golden Sage King's eyes—his heat vision.

 

A speed-of-light attack.

 

Fenric had no time to dodge.

 

"Zzzz!!"

 

The rays slammed into him, burning through his Armament Haki and scorching his skin.

 

"Hiss—!"

 

The pain was excruciating. Fenric gritted his teeth. The temperature had to be at least 2,000 degrees Celsius—hotter than the nuclear shockwave he had once endured in another trial.

 

At such temperatures, steel itself would melt into liquid. And yet, Fenric's body, reinforced with Armament Haki, was being burned alive.

 

His left arm blocked the beams, while his right hand opened into a palm. With a surge of power, he thrust it forward.

 

"Boom!!"

 

Golden Sage King was blasted away, his vision going dark as a massive golden palmprint engulfed him.

 

Buddha's Palm!

 

For the first time, Fenric unleashed the technique in actual combat.

 

His current physical attribute sat at 345 points, while his mental attribute reached 690 points—over 1,000 in total. And the Buddha's Palm amplified that combined strength a hundredfold.

 

That strike carried over 100 tons of force.

 

"Boom!!"

 

A nearby office building shuddered as its load-bearing walls gave way.

 

"Run!!"

 

Citizens screamed in panic. Dust and smoke billowed as the structure collapsed, debris crashing like an apocalyptic landslide.

 

With a single palm, Fenric had reduced a building to rubble.

 

Onlookers stared at him in shock and fear.

 

A monster…!

 

Just like the Golden Sage King, this mysterious man was at least an A-class Samsara.

 

Fenric ignored their terrified gazes. His mask concealed his identity, and it would last for hours yet.

 

Still, he frowned. Burns marked his arms and body from the earlier heat vision.

 

Super strength, super speed, steel body, and heat vision…

 

This man was undeniably a weakened version of Superman.

 

From the ruins came a crash.

 

"Crack—"

 

Golden Sage King staggered out, covered in dust, his clothes torn, his expression grim.

 

Despite the blow, his steel body had absorbed most of the damage. Internally, he was shaken, but far from defeated.

 

"That palm… was it the Tathagata's Palm?" Golden Sage King's eyes sharpened. "Are you Shura?"

 

Fenric blinked, caught off guard by his sharp deduction. Then he smirked beneath his mask and answered without hesitation.

 

"Yes. I am."

 

The words detonated like thunder among the crowd.

 

"What?! He's Shura?!"

 

"Impossible! Didn't Shura just clear the 10th floor of the Samsara Tower?"

 

"And now he's fighting the Golden Sage King to a standstill?! He's a monster!"

 

"Shura Oppa! Oppa, you're so handsome! I want to date Shura Oppa!!"

 

"Who's Shura?"

 

"You don't follow Samsara news, old man! He's a legend already!"

 

"Old man? How dare you! I'm only 51! I'm still in my prime!"

 

The chaos in the crowd only grew, voices overlapping in hysteria.

 

Reporters were already dialing their editors with trembling hands:

 

"Chief! Breaking news! Hurry—get the news van to XX Road, near the Heqiu Hotel!"

chapters.name: Chapter 262: Chapter 262: The Destructive Power Is Amazing!
chapters.content:
Fenric's open admission of his identity as Shura was not made recklessly.

 

Unlike before, he no longer needed to hide in the shadows. He was not afraid of being besieged. And if things truly turned against him, he still had a way to escape—his teleportation bracelet, coupled with the supersonic flight of the Mark VII Armor. If he wanted to leave, no one could stop him.

 

"So you really are Shura!"

 

Golden Sage King's eyes widened slightly. "You're strong. As expected of the man hailed as the most talented figure in Samsara Space."

 

He puffed out his chest and introduced himself proudly, "My name is Jo MinKi, though most call me Golden Sage King. I'm the strongest player in Willowland Country—and ranked 96th on the world's top 100 list."

 

His cold gaze locked onto Fenric. "You should feel proud. Not many can push me this far."

 

Fenric's brows rose faintly. He had already recognized Golden Sage King as a high-level A-rank powerhouse, but he hadn't expected him to be in the global top 100.

 

The next moment, Golden Sage King burst into loud, arrogant laughter.

 

"Shura! I don't care why you came to Soule or who you killed. No matter your reasons, I'll keep you here today. Adam has long wanted to meet you!" His smile twisted. "Snuffing out a genius like you—it should feel glorious, don't you think?"

 

His body lifted into the air, and in his hand materialized a glowing blue blade—a lightsaber straight out of Star Wars.

 

This time, he was done playing.

 

"If you want to keep me," Fenric replied flatly, his eyes narrowing with a dangerous gleam, "that depends on whether you have the ability."

 

With a thought, Mjolnir—the Hammer of Thor—appeared in Fenric's hand. Now that he knew his opponent was ranked among the top 100, there was no room for carelessness. He was eager to see just how strong such a master truly was.

 

"Boom!"

 

Another sonic boom tore through the air. Golden Sage King vanished, reappearing before Fenric in the blink of an eye. The lightsaber slashed straight for Fenric's neck, its scorching blade capable of cutting through anything.

 

Fenric didn't dare test whether Armament Haki alone could block it. Instead, his mental power surged.

 

While his telekinesis couldn't bind someone of Golden Sage King's level, it could at least disrupt his speed—enough to make a difference.

 

In that instant of slowed movement, Fenric twisted aside, dodging the lightsaber's arc. Mjolnir whirled in his grip and slammed toward Golden Sage King's chest.

 

But Golden Sage King reacted with inhuman reflexes. Taking the hit head-on, he flipped midair and delivered a brutal kick to Fenric's ribs.

 

"Boom!"

 

Both men were knocked back.

 

Golden Sage King's kicks could shatter iron plating, yet Fenric only felt his blood stir slightly before steadying again. Armament Haki reinforced his body like unbreakable armor—lacking against extreme heat, perhaps, but formidable against physical blows.

 

Even if Fenric stood still, Golden Sage King's barehanded strikes would barely scratch him.

 

Landing firmly, Fenric raised Mjolnir high above his head.

 

"Hah!"

 

The clear night sky darkened as black storm clouds gathered in mere seconds.

 

"Boom!"

 

Thunder rolled, shaking the heavens.

 

Golden Sage King's eyes narrowed. "That hammer… Is it Thor's Hammer?"

 

Fenric didn't bother answering.

 

If he wants to serve Adam and deliver me like a dog, then words are meaningless. I'll just crush him here.

 

"Boom!!"

 

A colossal bolt of lightning struck Mjolnir, crackling across Fenric's body. Bathed in lightning, he resembled a god of thunder descending upon the earth.

 

The citizens watching below froze in terror, finally understanding what it truly meant to face an A-class Samsara. No wonder nations prized such beings—their power was monstrous.

 

But Golden Sage King wasn't about to let him unleash that thunder unchallenged. His eyes flared red again.

 

Twin beams of heat vision lanced toward Fenric—just as Fenric brought down Mjolnir, releasing all the thunder he had gathered.

 

"Zzzzzz!!"

 

Both were struck at once—Fenric seared by the burning rays, Golden Sage King blasted by divine lightning.

 

Onlookers felt their scalps prickle. Two A-class powerhouses, tearing into each other without restraint—it was terrifying.

 

In the end, Fenric endured better. His Armament Haki was ironclad, his skin thick and battle-hardened. With Mjolnir in hand, his combat power was nearly on par with Golden Sage King's.

 

The Golden Sage King, however, proved vulnerable to lightning. Like Superman, his magical resistance was poor. Though his steel body could shrug off physical strikes, thunder tore through him, leaving his figure charred and staggering.

 

Even so, his vitality was monstrous. Though injured, his fighting spirit burned hotter.

 

"Shura!" he roared, golden light blazing around him. "I'll kill you!!"

 

The aura surrounding him surged violently, his speed spiking.

 

Fenric's instincts screamed in warning—an unmistakable sense of mortal danger.

 

He instantly summoned another storm bolt, hurling it at his charging foe.

 

But when the lightning struck, it dispersed harmlessly against Golden Sage King's golden aura.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed. A buff ability… something like Savage Charge!

 

There was no time to dodge.

 

At the last instant, Fenric activated his own Savage Charge, gripping Mjolnir tight as he charged headlong to meet him.

 

"BOOM—!!!"

 

Their collision erupted like a falling sky.

 

The asphalt street caved in, forming a massive crater. Cracks raced outward like a spiderweb, splitting the ground for hundreds of meters.

 

Fenric's body was flung back violently, smashing through the walls of a supermarket. He crashed through shelves and displays, tearing through the building before finally stopping.

 

If not for the invincibility buff, he would have been gravely injured.

 

Panting, he steadied himself. This guy really is worthy of the top 100. He's on a whole different level.

chapters.name: Chapter 263: Chapter 263: Strange Woman, Another A-Rank?!
chapters.content:
The battle between Fenric and Golden Sage King had already drawn the attention of the local government.

 

Boom!

 

A deafening roar echoed as a helicopter appeared overhead, blades slicing the night sky. Sirens wailed on the streets below, police rushing in from all directions.

 

But the most alarming arrival was from above—an enormous robot flying in from the distance.

 

"Senior Golden Sage, where is the enemy?"

 

The robot's metallic voice rumbled as it hovered, its very presence confirming one thing: the pilot was a Samsara.

 1

Fenric had just pushed himself up from the rubble when his death sense screamed danger.

 

"Shura, I advise you not to resist."

 

The crisp, cold voice came from the side. Fenric turned to see a woman aiming a bizarre-looking gun at him, its muzzle locked onto his chest.

 

With Fenric's current strength, ordinary firearms meant nothing. Yet the moment that strange weapon fixed on him, his instincts flared. His death sense whispered warnings—this gun was dangerous.

 

Clearly, it wasn't ordinary. Its power could threaten him, though it lacked the force to kill.

 

"Beauty, I don't like people pointing guns at me."

 

Fenric's voice was low as arcs of lightning crackled across Thor's Hammer, electricity dancing up his arm.

 

Zi-zi-zi!

 

The woman's brows knitted, but she said nothing—she simply pulled the trigger.

 

Whoosh!

 

Instead of bullets, a glowing orb of green light shot forth.

 

A magic gun!

 

Fenric instantly felt the danger. If struck, this attack would cause real trouble. He twisted his body, narrowly avoiding the blast.

 

But to his surprise, the green orb curved mid-flight, homing back toward him.

 

Whoosh! Whoosh!

 

Two more orbs streaked out as the woman fired again, her expression icy.

 

Three glowing projectiles flanked Fenric from all sides.

 

"Enough!"

 

Fenric swung Thor's Hammer, summoning a bolt of thunder that tore through the sky and struck at the woman.

 

But her body shimmered, turning translucent, and the lightning passed harmlessly through her.

 

Fenric narrowed his eyes. What kind of ability is that?

 

At the same time, he could tell—this woman was no ordinary opponent. She was another A-Rank.

 

"Zi-zi-zi!"

 

Fenric hurled thunder at the green orbs, shattering them on contact. The light dissolved instantly, unable to withstand the storm's fury.

 

Boom!

 

The air cracked as Fenric vanished, reappearing in front of the woman in a blur of motion. He whipped his leg toward her head in a vicious kick.

 

The woman's eyes widened. She tried to retreat—

 

—but his strike was intercepted.

 

Clang!

 

Golden Sage King appeared, blocking Fenric's kick.

 

"Miss Song, this man is my prey. Don't interfere."

 

Though his words were directed at her, Golden Sage King's glare never left Fenric. His body, however, trembled slightly, sweat dripping down his forehead.

 

That last exchange had drained him—just as Fenric's Buddha Palm and Savage Charges had consumed much of his energy.

 

Fenric exhaled slowly. He, too, was nearing his limits.

 

Boom!

 

The giant robot finally descended behind Fenric, landing with earth-shaking force. Its metallic voice boomed:

 

"Senior Golden Sage, we don't wish to interfere with your hunt. But your battle with Shura is tearing apart the city. The President fears Soule itself will not survive if this continues. We were ordered to assist."

 

"Senior Golden Sage, end this quickly."

 

Golden Sage King's brows furrowed. He said nothing, but gave a curt nod. Even in his arrogance, he could not ignore the President's will.

 

The three of them turned, encircling Fenric.

 2

"Shura," the robot rumbled, "you are undeniably strong. To stand against Senior Golden Sage proves your worth. But against the three of us together, you have no chance. Surrender."

 

Fenric eyed the trio. The robot's design looked familiar, yet he couldn't place whether it came from a movie or an anime.

 

Still, their combined might was undeniable. Golden Sage King alone already pressed him to his limits. Against three A-Ranks, Fenric knew the outcome—he would be crushed.

 

He wasn't a fool. He didn't need to fight to the death here.

 

"Today's been fun," Fenric said calmly. "But this fight ends here. Another day, I'll return… and we'll play again."

 

"You think you can run?" the robot sneered. "You won't escape."

 

The woman's eyes suddenly widened as realization struck. "No—he has teleportation!"

 

The instant her words fell, Fenric's form blurred—and vanished.

 

Teleportation. His trump card. Not even a secret anymore, thanks to the One Piece dungeon.

 

The three stood frozen, faces dark with frustration.

 

"Bastard! No wonder he dared to cause chaos in Soule," the robot roared. "With teleportation, he can come and go as he pleases!"

 

The woman's voice was low, solemn. "We've provoked a monster. And worse—a monster with limitless potential. When he returns, he'll only be stronger."

 

Her words silenced the others. Even Golden Sage King's expression hardened.

 

The man they called Shura had just broken through the tenth floor of the Samsara Tower. And already, he was this strong.

 

Suddenly, Golden Sage King's ears twitched. He closed his eyes, floating into the air as if listening to something distant.

 

Moments later, his eyes snapped open, sharp and focused.

 

To the north, a blazing ball of fire rose into the sky.

 

Boom!

 

In a flash, Golden Sage King vanished, racing toward the flames.

chapters.name: Chapter 264: Chapter 264: Radiant and Domineering!
chapters.content:
Half an hour later.

 

Fenric had already crossed the border and was flying above a small county town.

 

"Shura!!"

 

A furious roar came from behind, followed by the sharp whistle of something slicing through the air.

 

His death sense flared—danger! Fenric shifted sideways in an instant.

 

Om—!

 

Twin beams of blazing heat barely missed him. Fenric's expression darkened. He descended immediately, landing hard on the ground.

 

It wasn't that he feared the heat rays. What he feared was losing his toy—the Mark VII armor.

 

He recalled the armor into the Samsara space just in time. 

 

Boom! 

 

A figure crashed down in front of him, sending up a spray of dirt and stone.

 

It was none other than Golden Sage King, a Golden cloak flapping behind him.

 

"Shura! Don't even think about escaping me today!"

 

Fenric gripped Thor's Hammer, his gaze calm and voice cutting.

 

"Alone? You really dare chase me by yourself? Do you actually think you're Superman?"

 

"I alone am enough to deal with you!"

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed. He wasted no words, raising Thor's Hammer as dark clouds began to boil above.

 

Boom!

 

The once-clear night sky thundered, lightning flickering within the rolling darkness.

 

Golden Sage King, of course, didn't wait to be struck. He shot forward, speed blurring, closing in fast.

 

But Fenric's reaction was sharper—and his mind power already wrapped around his foe, hindering his movement.

 

Clang!

 

Thor's Hammer connected squarely with Golden Sage King's face. The blow carried crushing weight, as if a mountain itself had slammed into him.

 

The Golden Saint King was hurled backward, his own fist only glancing off Fenric's shoulder.

 

Boom!

 

He crashed into a roadside slope, half-buried in dirt. His ears rang, stars exploded across his vision.

 

Fenric's hammer strikes weren't just heavy—they were devastating.

 

Boom—!

 

Thunder rolled again. Hearing it, Golden Sage King's expression shifted. He scrambled up from the pit despite the dizziness.

 

Crack!

 

Lightning tore from the heavens, slamming down on him.

 

"Arghhh!!!"

 

He screamed as his body lit up, engulfed in searing current.

 

Like Superman, his physical resistance was extraordinary—but his magical resistance was pitiful. Lightning was his natural bane.

 

Though his body endured, his nerves burned. Smoke curled from charred flesh.

 

Before he could recover, a shadow fell. Fenric descended like a war god, hammer raised, eyes filled with murderous intent.

 

Boom—!

 

The earth exploded under the strike, gouging out a massive crater.

 

Golden Sage King lay sprawled within, scorched and blackened, looking more like a corpse than a warrior. Yet somehow, he still clung to life. His vitality was monstrous, his special gear protecting him further—his cloak singed, but the shorts still intact.

 

Fenric clicked his tongue. A cloak is fine. But shorts? Over armor? Unacceptable.

 

"Shura! I'll kill you!!!"

 

With a roar, Golden Sage King erupted from the crater, dirt raining down. His eyes burned red—the heat rays charging again.

 

But before he could fire, a cold, commanding voice rang out.

 

"Golden Sage King, how dare you cause trouble in Jadeveil's territory?"

 

The words cut like a blade. Golden Sage King froze, heat rays vanishing, face twisting in shock. He turned stiffly, as if he'd seen a ghost.

 

Floating calmly in the air behind him was a woman in a crisp military uniform. Her bearing was heroic, her aura undeniable.

 

Sweat broke instantly across Golden Sage King's brow.

 

"M-Marshal Vivienne…" His voice trembled. "Commander Song, this is a misunderstanding! Shura—he invaded Soule, killed people there! I only pursued him!"

 

Before her, the Golden Saint King—arrogant moments ago—looked like a schoolboy caught by the headmistress.

 

Fenric, however, remained calm. His gaze locked on the woman, but inside he was rattled.

 

When did she arrive? I didn't sense her at all.

 

With his current heightened senses, for anyone to escape his notice… was terrifying.

 

This was the first time Fenric had seen Vivienne in the real world.

 

In the Samsara space, her image was imposing, almost masculine. But here—though equally commanding—she carried a softer beauty. Long legs, pale skin, sharp brows, starry eyes. The uniform only enhanced her heroic aura.

 

Fenric studied her carefully. She was far stronger than he had expected.

 

At the same time, Vivienne's eyes met his.

 

Neither looked away. Two strong wills collided silently in the air.

 

For that moment, Golden Sage King stood between them like an oversized third wheel.

chapters.name: Chapter 265: Chapter 265: You Are Suspected of Entering the Country Illegally!
chapters.content:
Vivienne and Fenric simply looked at each other in silence, neither speaking at first.

 

Then, Vivienne's lips curved into a faint smile.

 

Fenric returned the gesture with one of his own.

 

"Golden Saint King!"

 

Her smile vanished the moment she turned her gaze on Golden Sage King, her tone sharpening into steel.

 

"I don't know whether Shura is at fault, but you dared to trespass into my territory without authorization. That is a provocation against jadeveil itself. As a soldier of the Jadeveil Nation, I absolutely cannot ignore this!"

 

Golden Sage King's expression stiffened, his confidence faltering.

 

"Commander Song, what do you mean by this?" he demanded.

 

Both spoke in English.

 

Because of the Samsara space, English had become common languages; countless dungeons used them. Other small languages appeared only rarely. For most Samsaras, proficiency in these two tongues was essential.

 

"The meaning is simple." Vivienne's voice turned cold. "You're coming with me. Golden Sage King, I am officially detaining you for illegal entry. You may choose to resist—if you dare."

 

Golden Sage King's face darkened.

 

"Commander Song, don't forget my position in Willowland Republic. If you dare detain me, are you not afraid my country will declare war on Jadeveil Natii?"

 

Vivienne gave a disdainful laugh, lips curling.

 

"War? With you as the excuse? Hardly worthy."

 

"!!!"

 

Golden Sage King's face flushed blue with rage. His chest heaved as if he might explode—but in the end, he bit back his fury. He had no confidence to continue pressing.

 1

Such was the sorrow of small nations.

 

"I hope you won't regret this decision," he spat, his words harsh—but his actions obedient. He raised his hands in surrender.

 

For all his bluster, Golden Sage King was not a fool. He knew full well the woman before him was terrifying beyond measure, far beyond what he could handle.

 

Vivienne glanced back at Fenric.

 

"Shura, I'll be taking him. You don't mind, do you?"

 

"Not at all." Fenric smiled faintly.

 

Vivienne gave a small nod, seized Golden Sage King, and flew off with him.

 

The so-called Golden Saint King, who had roared moments ago that he would kill Shura, now appeared utterly cooperative as Vivienne led him away. Deep down, regret gnawed at him—regret for ever chasing Shura into Jadeveil land. He had no idea what price he would have to pay to return home.

 

Soon, the figures of Vivienne and Golden Sage King vanished from sight.

 

Fenric let out a quiet sigh.

 

Aurora Morwyn was indeed a wise woman.

 

From start to finish, she had never once embarrassed him, never even asked about his true identity.

 

Afterward, Fenric summoned the Mark VII armor, suited up, and took to the skies once more.

 3

By the time he returned home, it was already past nine in the evening.

 

He powered on his computer, intending to research strategies for the 11th floor of the Samsara Tower—only to discover he had become the hottest search topic online.

 

The internet was flooded with videos of his battle against Golden Sage King.

 

Comment sections overflowed with reactions:

 

"Holy sh*t! Did he just level a building with one palm? Is this the true power of the Great God Shura?"

 

"This combat strength is insane."

 

"Wait, isn't that guy in the shorts and red cape the Golden Saint King from Willowland Republic?"

 

"It is him! Who else would dress like such a clown?"

 

"Say what you will, the Golden Saint King is still strong. He's ranked 96th on the top 100 list, right? And Shura not only tied with him but even seemed to have the upper hand. That's terrifying!"

 

"Ugh, I'm a little disappointed in Shura's looks though. He just seems like some random passerby. I always imagined a peerless, handsome figure."

 1

"Idiot. Do you really think that's his real face? The Willowland Republic police already announced that the guy shown is some no-name local. Obviously, Shura used special props to disguise himself."

 

"Yeah, I saw that notice too. They even claimed Shura ran to Soule to kill people and that's why Golden Sage King fought him."

 

"Hahaha, Willowland netizens are hilarious. A while ago they insisted Shura was one of them, now they're saying it was all a misunderstanding sparring match."

 

"Soon enough, everything in the world will apparently belong to the Willowland Republic."

 

"Back to the real point—Shura fought the Golden Sage King and gained the upper hand. That's the real headline!"

 

"What about the follow-up? Who actually won!?"

 

"Tongue for follow-up!!"

 

Before long, the official channels released breaking news:

 

[The 'Golden Saint King' of Willowland Republic has been arrested by Jadeveil's military on suspicion of illegal entry.]

 

The internet erupted instantly.

 

"What the hell? Didn't he just fight Shura in Soule? How was he suddenly arrested here?"

 

"Don't tell me… Shura dragged him back himself? If that's true, Shura is even scarier than we thought."

 

"Come on, be serious. Even if Shura could fly, he's not as fast as Golden Sage King. If Golden Sage King wanted to escape, he could've."

 

"Unless Shura used a special item to capture him!?"

 

"Think, people. If Shura had caught him, would the officials phrase the announcement like that?"

 

"Exactly. Jadeveil has plenty of top experts. It's more likely the Golden Sage King chased Shura across the border, and that's when our military detained him."

 

"Makes sense. After all, Jadeveil has dozens of masters ranked in the top 100."

 

"Still, this arrest could have international consequences."

 

"Unless the Cindralock Dominion gets involved, what's there to shake?"

 

The entire network buzzed with speculation.

 

Rumors already claimed that Shura's overall strength had surpassed A-rank, making him the only one at that level on the 10th floor of the Samsara Tower. With the release of tonight's video, public curiosity about his power soared.

 

Fenric had once again become the center of worldwide attention.

chapters.name: Chapter 266: Chapter 266: Life from the Planet Cybertron
chapters.content:
Inside a vast conference room, the President of the Cindralock Dominion and members of the House of Representatives were watching a video.

 

The footage showed Shura clashing with the Golden Sage King.

 

When Shura leveled an office building with a single strike and then summoned thunder to rain down from the skies, the President and his lawmakers could not hide their astonishment.

 

By the time the video ended, every face in the room had turned grave.

 

"Shura has truly risen," the President murmured, his tone heavy. "And he has done so in less than a month."

 

The words made the atmosphere sink even further.

 

They all remembered—Adam had taken over a year to climb from rookie to A-rank. Yet Shura, in just over half a month, had already reached the level where he could contend with a master ranked in the world's top hundred.

 

The difference in talent was terrifying.

 

"We cannot allow him to grow any further," an elderly congressman pressed. "Is there no way to eliminate him?"

 

"In the Samsara space, none," someone replied. "At equal rank, no one can match Shura. If we act, it must be in the real world."

 

"Have we discovered his identity yet?"

 

The Director of the Intelligence Bureau cleared his throat.

 

"There has been some progress. Shura once intervened and killed a Blacklight Virus adapter in AH City. Our experts speculate that he may be from AH."

 

"Find him quickly," the President ordered. "If we delay, his strength will only increase."

 

The Director hesitated before speaking again.

 

"I'm afraid that won't be easy. Jadeveil is secretly shielding Shura's personal data, blocking all citizen records from AH city. Without that information, acquiring anything useful has become… nearly impossible."

 

"..."

 

The grim expressions in the room deepened.

 

Shura's rise had been too fast. Given more time, even Adam might no longer be able to stop him.

 

Finally, the Intelligence Director offered a path forward.

 

"Our best hope lies with Mr. Adam. If he can clear the 33rd floor dungeon and seize greater authority, then perhaps we can contain Shura."

 

At that moment, the heavy doors of the chamber opened.

 

The President's aide strode in quickly and leaned down to whisper in his ear:

 

"Sir, the President of Willowland Republic just called. He hopes you will pressure the Jadeveil Nation into releasing Mr. Golden Sage King."

 

The President rubbed his brow irritably. Jadeveil was no minor power to be pushed around. Their relations with the Cindralock Dominion were already strained; even if he applied pressure, Jadeveil would hardly bend to his will.

 

When he relayed the matter to the room, silence fell.

 

One congressman finally suggested, "Mr. President, you could hold a press conference. Publicly condemn Jadeveil."

 

Condemnation, at least, would serve as both a gesture and an explanation to their allies. It would show they had not ignored the matter.

 

The President considered, then nodded.

 

"Good. Contact the White House. Summon the media. We will hold a press conference."

 6

"Yes, sir."

 

As the aide departed, another lawmaker raised a harsher point:

 

"Mr. President, the domestic Blacklight Virus outbreak is still not fully under control. The negative impact has been enormous. Your approval rating has already fallen below forty percent. You must be careful."

 

The President sat back with a bitter expression.

 

"Is there no good news left to tell me?"

 

No one answered. In recent days, there has been nothing but bad news.

 

—--

 

Similar meetings were being held across the world.

 

Shura's name had now reached the highest levels of power.

 

World leaders were forced to reconsider their stance toward Jadeveil Nation, because none of them were fools. They knew it was only a matter of time before Shura's achievements in the Samsara space eclipsed Adam's. And that time might not be far off.

 

After browsing the endless online discussions for a while, Fenric closed the page with disinterest.

 

Praise from netizens was nothing new to him; he had grown numb to it.

 

Instead, he opened the Samsara Forum and navigated straight to the strategy section, searching for official guides.

 

Soon, he found the details for the 11th floor of the Samsara Tower.

 

Two dungeons were listed:

 

"Total Recall" — Difficulty: Normal

 3

"Transformers" — Difficulty: Hard

 2

Fenric's eyes immediately lit up.

 

Both were based on science fiction movies he remembered from his previous life.

 

After only a moment's thought, he made his decision.

 

Tonight, he would challenge "Transformers."

 1

It wasn't only because of the higher difficulty and rewards.

 

What drew him most was the AllSpark, the mysterious artifact that gave birth to the mechanical lifeforms. If it existed in the dungeon as a special item, and if he could bring it back… it would be a devastating trump card.

 

With it, he could form an army of mechanical soldiers to unleash against any enemy who dared provoke him.

 

Not only would such power dominate inside the Samsara space, it could shake the real world as well.

 

The Cindralock Dominion's repeated attempts against him would not be forgotten.

 

With renewed determination, Fenric skipped past the "Total Recall" notes and opened the "Transformers" strategy.

 

"The hard-level dungeon 'Transformers' introduces the mechanical lifeforms of the planet Cybertron. These robots are colossal, equipped with advanced weaponry, and capable of transforming into various machines.

 

The primary mission is simple: eliminate the Cybertronian lifeforms.

 

Warning: unless you are exceptionally strong, do not attempt this dungeon. The difficulty is extreme, and the enemies are overwhelming."

chapters.name: Chapter 267: Chapter 267: News from Aurora Morwyn!
chapters.content:
(PS: Don't worry if you haven't watched Transformers. The author won't follow the original plot.)

 4

"To be honest, I don't recommend challenging the Transformers dungeon," the strategy began.

 

"There aren't many mechanical lifeforms inside, and they're extremely skilled at camouflage. Most of the time, they disguise themselves as common Earth vehicles. Unless they transform, it's nearly impossible to distinguish them."

 

"The system only gives five days for this mission, and earning a high evaluation is extremely difficult."

 

"Here's some intelligence collected by the top players about the mechanical lifeforms you might encounter:"

 

Ironhide — Height: 7.9 meters. Alternate form: Topkick pickup truck.Bumblebee — Height: 5.2 meters. Alternate form: Chevrolet Camaro.Optimus Prime — Height: 8.5 meters. Alternate form: red-and-blue semi-truck.

 

Blackout — Alternate form: MH-53 helicopter. Houses the scorpion-like Transformer, Scorponok.Starscream — Height: 9 meters. Alternate form: F-22 Raptor fighter jet.

 

Barricade — Alternate form: police cruiser.

 

Brawl — Alternate form: main battle tank.

 

Frenzy — A small robot specializing in infiltration and sabotage. Difficult to detect.

 

After reading through the official guide, Fenric chuckled.

 

No mention of the AllSpark at all…

 

But that was to be expected. The mission time was only five days—likely too short to reach the climactic battle between Autobots and Decepticons. The absence of Megatron in the strategy confirmed it.

 

The AllSpark—also known as Fire Source—was the most important artifact in Transformers lore. It was the origin of all mechanical life on Cybertron, capable of turning any electronic device into a sentient Transformer.

 

If Fenric could obtain it, he could potentially create his own army of mechanical soldiers.

 

A bold, almost reckless plan formed instantly in his mind.

 

If everything goes smoothly, I'll secure another Super God evaluation… and if luck is on my side, I might just bring back the AllSpark.

 

Midnight soon arrived.

 

Fenric entered Samsara Space on time.

 

The first thing he did was heal himself. His battle with Golden Sage King had left burns across his body from several direct hits of heat rays. They weren't life-threatening, but they'd certainly hinder his performance in the dungeon.

 

"System, heal me."

 

Healing was one of Samsara Space's greatest benefits. It could cure any injury or disease, giving even terminally ill Samsaras a second chance at life. Of course, the service came at a price.

 

"Samsara Shura, treatment will cost 260 Samsara Points. Confirm?"

 

"Confirm treatment."

 

A beam of crimson light descended, washing over him. In seconds, his wounds were gone.

 

Almost immediately, a new system prompt appeared:

 

"You have received a new communication request. Aurora Morwyn invites you to a video call. Please respond promptly."

 

Fenric's lips curled into a small smile. He accepted.

 

Aurora Morwyn's striking, heroic face appeared on the screen.

 

"Good evening, Aurora," Fenric greeted.

 

"Good evening, Shura," Aurora replied with a faint smile before sighing. "I watched your battle with Golden Sage earlier. Your power is… incredible. To achieve that level of strength right after clearing the tenth floor—it's unprecedented in Samsara's history."

 

"Normally, such drastic leaps in power only happen after clearing specific dungeons. Yet you haven't even touched those, and you're already this strong. I can't imagine how terrifying you'll be by the time you reach the twentieth floor."

 

Fenric smiled modestly. "Compared to you, I'm still far behind. Are you sure you're not just flattering me?"

 

Aurora shook her head, her expression turning serious. "We caught a spy tonight. He was trying to steal information on all AH City residents. Combined with the incident with that Blacklight Virus host, foreign powers are now almost certain you're from AH City."

 

Fenric raised a brow but didn't look surprised. "Even if they confirm my identity, it won't matter much."

 

Aurora nodded. "True. With your current strength, you can protect yourself. Still, Shura, I advise you not to leave the country. As long as you remain here, I can provide some level of support."

 

"Understood," Fenric replied with a small laugh, his gaze softening as he studied her face. Aurora had helped him immensely since they became allies, and he felt genuinely grateful.

 

"You're entering a dungeon tonight, aren't you?" she asked.

 

"Yes. Transformers."

 

"I figured as much." Aurora smiled. "Then I wish you another Super God evaluation. I won't keep you."

 

The call ended.

 

Fenric moved to his personal warehouse and retrieved a glass vial containing a crimson serum—Saiyan Bloodline (Modified).

 

Consumable Item: Saiyan Bloodline (Modified)

 

Effect: Permanently fuses Saiyan genes into the user. Grants +50 Strength, +50 Constitution.

 

Note: Saiyan Bloodline has the potential to evolve into Super Saiyan, drastically increasing combat power.

 

Fenric turned the vial in his hand thoughtfully. "System, if I use this, what changes will I undergo? I won't suddenly grow a tail and turn into a giant ape under a full moon, will I?"

 

"Please rest assured. This serum only integrates partial Saiyan traits into your genome, enhancing your physical capabilities. It will not alter your core genetic structure. However, because of this limitation, the power boost will be weaker than that of a true Saiyan."

 

"Oh?" Fenric narrowed his eyes. "And if I manage to trigger Super Saiyan?"

 

"In Super Saiyan form, Strength will increase tenfold, while all other attributes will increase fivefold. Duration: 30 minutes."

 3

Fenric frowned. In Dragon Ball, a Super Saiyan's power was boosted fiftyfold, not ten. Clearly, this was a heavily nerfed version.

 

Still, even with the adjustments, it was a tremendous power-up.

 

Then another system prompt appeared:

 

"Warning: Each Samsara may only integrate one bloodline in their lifetime. Please use this item cautiously."

 

Fenric froze.

 

So once I use this, I'll never be able to fuse with another bloodline? Not even if I encounter something like Kryptonian DNA… or Saitama's physique?

 1

For the first time since obtaining it, Fenric hesitated.

 1

chapters.name: Chapter 268: Chapter 268: Knowing the Plot, You Can Do Whatever You Want!
chapters.content:
"Then system, how many Samsara Points are required to evolve into a Super Saiyan?"

 

"500,000 points."

 

Fenric's brows furrowed.

 

Five hundred thousand Samsara Points…!

 

No wonder the wanted man Choi Hojae had never evolved into a Super Saiyan. For most Samsaras, that number was astronomical.

 

Even for Fenric, gathering that many points would be extremely difficult. He'd need several consecutive Super God evaluations just to come close.

 1

After a moment's thought, Fenric placed the vial of Saiyan blood back on the shelf. He would hold off on using it for now.

 

If he never found a stronger bloodline in the future, he could always return to it.

 2

Besides, a tenfold increase in power was already monstrous.

 7

By his current attributes, that would push his strength past four thousand. One punch would be enough to shatter the world around him.

 

Still, Fenric couldn't shake the thought that better bloodlines might exist—ones that could push his potential even further.

 1

When he left the warehouse, it was already half past midnight.

 

Without hesitation, Fenric headed straight for the Samsara Tower's eleventh floor.

 

He still had a dungeon refresh card. Once this was used, it would be gone for good.

 

Activating the card, he stepped into the tower's gates and was instantly transported to the eleventh floor.

 

From the balcony there, he could see almost the entirety of Area C below.

 

An elf spirit materialized beside him, bowing politely.

 

"Welcome, dear Samsara Player Shura. What assistance do you require?"

 

"I want to enter a dungeon," Fenric said.

 

"Understood. Please select your target world."

 

With a graceful wave of her hand, a holographic screen appeared before him.

 

Two choices glowed on the panel:

 

Total Recall (Normal)

 

Transformers (Hard)

 

Fenric didn't hesitate. "Transformers."

 

The selection locked.

 

As always, he was teleported into a white preparation room.

 

He had assumed few would choose the Transformers dungeon.

 

To his surprise, seven others were already there.

 

Fenric frowned slightly. According to online guides, this dungeon contained only a limited number of mechanical lifeforms. With so many Samsaras, how could the kills possibly be divided? Weren't they afraid of failing the mission and being obliterated?

 

Even if each of them managed to kill one, their evaluations would surely suffer.

 

But that was their problem, not his.

 

When the others noticed Fenric appear, their expressions shifted.

 

"Shit, that's Shura!" one whispered nervously.

 

"Will he mess with our plan?"

 

"Maybe we should wait for the next run…"

 

"Relax. Our plan's about the coordinates hidden in the glasses. It has nothing to do with Shura."

 

"But what if he's here for the glasses too?"

 

"Impossible. My cousin was the one who discovered the secret in those glasses. No one else in the world knows about it."

 

"And what if there's nothing at those coordinates?"

 

"Then so be it. If you want a high evaluation, you can't shy away from risks. Do you think the Samsara Tower is some amusement park? Look at Shura—he's achieved Super God evaluations. Did he face any less danger? Whether it was the alien nest in Avengers or holding off nuclear strikes in Final Destination, every one of those was life or death."

 

They spoke in hushed tones, but Fenric's sharp ears caught every word.

 

A faint smile tugged at his lips.

 

He knew exactly what glasses they were talking about.

 

In the original Transformers plot, the protagonist's great-grandfather left behind a pair of antique spectacles, their cracked lenses secretly etched with Cybertronian coordinates.

 

Clearly, these Samsaras hadn't uncovered the full truth, yet they dared to enter this dungeon banking everything on those glasses.

 

Fenric had to admit, their courage was impressive.

 

But as for himself—he was here for AllSpark. He would not yield it to anyone.

 

The glasses held no interest for him. He already knew the plot. He already knew exactly where the AllSpark was hidden.

 

Which meant these Samsaras were destined to be a step behind him.

 

"Attention, Samsara players. Mission teleport will begin in ten minutes."

 

The system prompt echoed through the preparation room.

 

None of the eight participants left.

 

Everyone remained silent, focused on the countdown.

 

Ten minutes passed in a flash.

 

"Teleportation countdown: 10… 9… 8… 3… 2… 1!"

 

Scarlet light enveloped their bodies, and they vanished.

 

—--

 

Beyond Earth, life thrived elsewhere in the universe.

 

In the far reaches of space, there existed a metallic world called Cybertron, home to the mechanical lifeforms known as Transformers.

 

They had once lived in peace—until Megatron, leader of the Decepticons, rose to power.

 

Thus began a war that raged across their planet and beyond.

 

"Main mission released!"

 

Objective: Kill at least one mechanical lifeform.

 

Duration: 5 days.

 

Failure: Obliteration.

 

Warning: The existence of Samsara Space must not be revealed to the inhabitants of this world.

 

Hint: Killing more, or more powerful, mechanical lifeforms will improve your evaluation.

 

When the system prompt ended, Fenric found himself standing on the streets of a bustling city.

 

It was a bright afternoon. Sunlight spilled across the wide streets, giving the metropolis a languid, almost idyllic air.

 

Catching sight of a storefront window, Fenric studied his reflection.

 

A tall young man, about twenty years old, gazed back at him. Handsome, sharp, nearly identical to his real self.

 

The system had prepared this appearance by default.

 

Fenric nodded in approval.

 

Then he turned from the glass, his eyes sharpening.

 

It was time to put his plan into motion.
