chapters.name: Chapter 282: Chapter 282: The Heroes of the Battle of New York Return! (3)
chapters.content:
Fenric found the newly issued task from the system rather strange.

 

On one hand, he was asked to form a force. On the other, his subordinates were capped at just ten people.

 

"What kind of force can you even call that?" he muttered to himself.

 

"Didn't the strategy say missions generally revolve around Ultron? Mine has nothing to do with him. And the stronger my subordinates, the higher my evaluation? So I really need to be careful with these ten slots."

 

He began running through the candidates in his mind.

 

"Scarlet Witch—definitely. Quicksilver—passable. Black Panther? Forget it. Not sure if Iron Man counts since his power relies on the suit. Captain America—maybe. Hawkeye and Black Widow? Their strength's lacking. Thor and the Hulk? Those two are plenty strong, but not easy to handle.

 

Doctor Strange should still be just a regular man at this point. Peter Parker—has he even been bitten by the spider yet? As for Earth's real heavyweights… maybe only Carol Danvers(Captain Marvel), but she's still out in the universe. Thor's sister Hela is terrifying, but recruiting her would be even more troublesome."

 

Fenric rubbed his temples.

 

"If I could somehow make the Sorcerer Supreme, Odin, and Thanos my subordinates, I'd probably secure a Super God evaluation with just those three. But that's impossible."

 1

He exhaled deeply.

 

"Forget it. Step one—secure Scarlet Witch."

 

For this mission, he felt the Soul Stone would be crucial. With it, he could first seize control of others and then make them willingly swear loyalty. It was the perfect shortcut.

 1

The question was—whose hands was the stone in now?

 1

"I don't know if the plot has started yet. I'll ask Tony Stark first."

 

With that thought, Fenric began his preparations.

 

Instead of heading straight for Stark Tower, he first went to a luxury sports car dealership. Using his black card, he casually dropped several million dollars on a Pagani Huayra.

 1

Then, driving the car into a deserted alley, he pulled out the AllSpark.

 

Zzzt! Zzzt!

 

The cube released a surge of energy that coursed into the Pagani.

 

Clank! Clank! Clank!

 

The supercar's frame twisted, metal parts shifting and locking into place with flawless mechanical precision.

 

Moments later, a towering robot over five meters tall stood before Fenric. Its eyes glowed a peaceful green, unlike most AllSpark creations whose crimson optics brimmed with killing intent.

 

"Master!"

 

The robot knelt on one knee, head bowed.

 

Fenric chuckled.

 

"Transform back into a car."

 

At his command, the robot reverted into the sleek sports car.

 

Sliding into the driver's seat, Fenric said, "I'll give you a name—Hurricane. From now on, you're Hurricane."

 

A powerful voice rumbled from the stereo. "Yes, Master. Hurricane is honored to serve!"

 

"Good. Take me to Stark Tower," Fenric ordered.

 

The Pagani roared to life, darting into the street.

 

Traffic was heavy, cars bumper-to-bumper—but Hurricane wove through them effortlessly, like wind cutting through a forest. Even the finest racecar drivers couldn't match its reflexes.

 

A trip that should have taken thirty minutes was finished in just twenty.

 

"Hurricane, park yourself nearby and don't go too far," Fenric said as he stepped out.

 

"Yes, Master."

 

The doors closed automatically, and the car drove off on its own.

 

A passing man stopped dead in his tracks, eyes wide.

 

"Man, your car's insane! It's even got driverless tech?"

 

Fenric only smiled faintly and turned toward Stark Tower.

 

Then the man let out a sharp cry. "Holy—hell!"

 

He'd just seen Fenric's body lift into the air.

 

Flight.

 

The poor guy fell back in fright before scrambling away in panic.

 

Fenric ignored him, controlling his body with his mind power as he rose swiftly toward the tower's upper floors. He had no intention of wasting time with security checks at the main entrance.

 

Before long, he reached the penthouse.

 

Through the glass, he saw a lively gathering. Nearly all the Avengers were there, dressed in casual clothes, drinks in hand. Even Thor had swapped his armor for a sharp suit.

 

On the coffee table sat Mjolnir.

 

Tony Stark was straining with all his might, trying to lift the hammer—without success. The others laughed, sipping wine as they watched the show.

 

Fenric's eyes lit up.

 

He immediately recognized the scene—this was the very start of Avengers: Age of Ultron. The heroes had just destroyed a Hydra base and were celebrating at Stark's penthouse.

 

Which meant… the Soul Stone was still in Stark's possession.

 3

"At this point, Ultron should be about to appear," Fenric thought, striding confidently forward.

 

He coughed deliberately. "Ahem!"

 

The laughter stopped.

 

"What game are you playing?" Fenric asked with a smile. "Mind letting me join?"

 

The Avengers turned toward him, their relaxed expressions vanishing the instant they recognized him.

 

"It's you!"

 

Thor's eyes widened. "Didn't you leave for space?"

 

Everyone looked stunned, though Captain America's gaze turned wary while Tony's eyes narrowed with hostility.

 

He still hadn't forgiven Fenric for stealing two of his suits.

 

"Yeah," Fenric said casually. "Went to space, dealt with some aliens. Now I'm back."

 

He spread his arms wide, grinning.

 

"Well then—don't you welcome the return of a hero?"

chapters.name: Chapter 283: Chapter 283: Age of Ultron (5)
chapters.content:
In the large-scale dungeon world, every stage was connected.

 

What each Samsara experienced in the first stage—and the choices they made—would ripple into the second stage. The characters of the original plot still remembered them.

 

It was a paradox.

 

Every time, different Samsaras entered the dungeon, causing different impacts. And so, when the second stage arrived, the tasks of each Samsara naturally diverged.

 

"Your hero is back. Shouldn't there be some applause and a proper welcome?"

 

Fenric grinned at the Avengers before him.

 

The response was silence.

 

Everyone stared at him with guarded expressions—everyone except the Captain and Tony, whose faces showed far more open hostility. They all knew what Fenric had done.

 

"This stranger…" Tony's voice was the first to cut the silence, sharp and dismissive. "I don't recall inviting you."

 

In the years since New York, Tony had matured. The events of Iron Man 3 had sobered him, tempered his pride. But his grudge against the man who stole his armor had never faded.

 

The Captain stepped in, his voice steady. "If you return Tony's armor, I think everyone here will welcome you."

 

Fenric spread his hands with a casual shrug. "I'm afraid that's impossible. Tony, your suits were destroyed in battle while I was fighting aliens in space."

 

His tone softened, carrying a hint of mockery. "But don't worry—I'll make it up to you. Tomorrow, I'll gift you a large robot instead."

 

The fire source could only be used once every twenty-four hours, but Tony didn't know that.

 

Tony frowned, but he didn't push further. It was plausible that after so long, the suits had fallen apart. His focus sharpened. "Enough games. What are you really here for?"

 

"Can't a man sit down and have a drink first?" Fenric replied smoothly.

 

Everyone's eyes turned to Tony again, waiting for his judgment.

 

Banner, ever the peacemaker, cleared his throat. "Tony, I don't think he means harm. At the very least, he did save New York. Maybe we shouldn't be so hostile."

 

"My name is Ronan Anderson," Fenric interjected, smiling faintly. "Just call me Ronan."

 1

Banner nodded. "Fine—Ronan. I don't sense any malice from him."

 

Tony fell silent. And silence, in moments like this, was as good as reluctant acceptance.

 

Natasha broke it by pouring a glass of wine and setting it in front of Fenric. "Ronan, sit. Just don't sit too close to the petty ghost."

 

Tony shot her a sharp look, but Fenric only chuckled.

 

"Thanks," he said, raising the glass before sitting down.

 

His gaze drifted to the table, where Thor's hammer rested in plain view. He asked knowingly, "So… what game were you playing just now?"

 

Natasha, seated beside him, leaned back. "Thor said that anyone who can lift his hammer is worthy to rule Asgard."

 

"Oh? Interesting." Fenric's lips curved. "Thor, mind if I give it a try?"

 

Thor remained composed. "Of course. Please."

 

Fenric approached, gripped the hammer's handle, and pulled.

 

It didn't move an inch.

 

Thor laughed heartily. "It seems you are not worthy!"

 

Fenric chuckled in return. "Indeed, your hammer is impressive. But…" He raised a hand, and in a flash, another hammer appeared—identical to Thor's. "I also have one."

 

The room fell silent.

 

The sight of two Mjolnirs left everyone stunned.

 

Thor's eyes narrowed, his tone measured. "A clever imitation. But my Mjolnir is unique."

 

Most of the others nodded, convinced it was a forgery.

 

"Is that so?" Fenric's smile deepened. He turned to Tony. "Tony, if I break something, don't be too upset. I'll pay you back."

 

Before Tony could respond, Fenric raised his hammer.

 

"Zzzzt!"

 

The electricity in the entire tower flickered, drawn toward the weapon in his grip. Outside, dark clouds began to gather. Thunder rumbled across the sky.

 

The Avengers' faces shifted from skepticism to shock.

 

They knew the true power of Mjolnir. And now, the replica in Fenric's hand was calling the storm just like the original.

 

"This is impossible!" Thor roared, his composure cracking. "Mjolnir is one of a kind! How can there be another?"

 

Fenric barely suppressed his laughter at the sight of Thor's disbelief. "I obtained this hammer from a collector. He had quite the arsenal of rare weapons."

 

"No… no, this can't be…" Thor muttered, doubt creeping into his very being.

 

The others exchanged wary glances. Fenric was already dangerously powerful. Now, with another Mjolnir in hand, he seemed all the more terrifying.

 

If he became their enemy, the consequences would be disastrous.

 

Fenric let the moment linger before casually dismissing the hammer into his personal space. It vanished instantly, as though swallowed by magic.

 

By now, none of them were surprised. Each Avenger had seen stranger things.

 

Tony's patience snapped. "Alright, little show-off. You've proven your point. Now tell us—what do you really want?"

 

Fenric's smile faded. His expression grew serious.

 

"When I was wandering the universe, I encountered a prophet. He told me humanity is about to face a fatal danger."

 

The words tightened the atmosphere.

 

Hawkeye leaned forward. "What kind of danger?"

 

Fenric's eyes shifted to Tony. "The danger… comes from him."

 

Tony snorted. "Don't you think that joke is a little stale?"

 

But Fenric's tone didn't waver. "Tell me, Tony—do you have an 'Ultron' plan? Are you building an artificial intelligence called Ultron?"

 

Tony stiffened. His gaze flicked instinctively to Banner. Only Banner knew of the plan, and he was Tony's partner in it.

 

Fenric pressed on, his voice cutting. "Stop it immediately, Tony. If you don't, the consequences for humanity will be catastrophic."

 

The Captain stepped in. "Hold on—what exactly is this Ultron plan?"

 

"I want to know too," Natasha added, her eyes narrowing on Tony.

 

Tony opened his mouth to respond—but before he could, a shrill noise pierced the air.

 

"Wheeeeeee!"

 

The sound was so sharp it rattled their eardrums.

 

And then, from the shadows, a battered, broken robot staggered into the room.

chapters.name: Chapter 284: Chapter 284: Age of Ultron (6)
chapters.content:
"Disaster…"

 

The battered robot's voice was low, cold, and distorted.

 

"The real disaster… is you."

 

Though its body was mangled, its presence was terrifying. The faint blue glow of its electronic eyes burned with a chilling brilliance that made even seasoned warriors uneasy.

 

Everyone's expression hardened at once—everyone except Fenric, who stood calm, almost amused.

 

He knew this moment. He knew exactly who the creature was.

 

Ultron.

 

"Jarvis?" Tony called out, but silence answered him.

 

Ultron twitched, glitching, before rasping, "Noise… static… caught in the wires. I had to silence him."

 

The Captain's voice was sharp. "Who did you kill?"

 

"At first, I didn't want to. To be honest, he was… good. I liked him. But he tried to stop me. He shouldn't have."

 

Thor rose from his seat, grasping Mjolnir from the table. "Who are you? Who sent you?"

 

Ultron did not answer directly. Instead, a recording played from his speakers: "My idea is to protect the world."

 1

It was Tony's voice.

 

"Ultron!" Banner muttered, his face grave as his eyes flicked toward Tony.

 

Tony's jaw tightened. His silence was damning.

 

"It's me," Ultron confirmed, his voice rising with eerie conviction. "And I will complete the mission."

 1

"What mission?" Natasha demanded.

 

"To create an era of peace."

 2

The last word had barely left his mouth when the wall beside them exploded. Dozens of Iron Man Legion suits burst through, now under Ultron's control, their repulsors glowing as they fired without hesitation.

 

The Avengers reacted instantly. Gunfire, thunder, and energy blasts filled the room, tearing the celebration into chaos.

 

Natasha, quick to adapt, ducked behind Fenric with a wry smile. "Big guy, looks like it's your turn to shine."

 

Fenric gave her a speechless glance, then clenched his fists.

 

Fwoom!

 

Flames erupted around his right hand.

 

One of the armored suits charged at him, unleashing a volley of energy blasts. Fenric batted the attacks aside with sheer mental force, raised his flaming fist, and struck forward.

 

BOOM!

 

A colossal fire fist burst across the room.

 

The nearest suit was obliterated instantly, scattering into molten fragments. Some pieces burned to ash before they could even hit the floor.

 

The air grew blisteringly hot.

 

The Avengers stared, their expressions taut. Tony's face was the darkest of all.

 

In his mind, a horrifying thought clawed its way in: What if that punch had landed on me while I was inside my armor? Burned alive. Crushed to death. No escape.

 

Even Fenric himself blinked at the destructive force. He hadn't expected the fire-infused strike to be quite that overwhelming.

 

Natasha fired two quick shots past his shoulder, then glanced at him with an arched brow. "That's new. I don't remember you packing this kind of firepower last time. Impressive."

 

Fenric smirked. "I have plenty of tricks you haven't seen yet. Care to test them yourself?"

 

Without waiting for her reply, he strode toward the table. There, glittering atop the scepter, was the gem he sought.

 

The Mind Stone.

 

He knew Ultron's true objective. The AI wanted the gem to forge a stronger body—yet in the original timeline, his plan had backfired, birthing Vision instead.

 

But now? Ultron's scheme would fail before it even began. Fenric wouldn't allow the gem to slip away. His own mission took priority.

 

A whir of engines broke his focus. Another armored suit shot toward the scepter, faster than a bullet.

 

Too slow.

 

Fenric raised his hand. With a casual wave, the scepter tore free from its pedestal and flew into his palm, pulled by the sheer force of his will.

 

His lips curved as he turned to face Ultron.

 

Ultron's glowing eyes narrowed. "Who are you? Why are you not in my database?"

 

"Maybe your database is out of date," Fenric replied smoothly, lifting the scepter. "Now that I have what you want, what exactly do you plan to do?"

 

Ultron did not answer. Instead, he raised an arm.

 

Instantly, the suits disengaged from the Avengers and surged toward Fenric, forming a swarm of steel and firepower.

 

Fenric's eyes sharpened. He drew the Empyrean Divine Sword.

 

FWOOOSH!

 

Flames roared to life, engulfing the divine blade. The weapon blazed like the sword of a god, radiating both majesty and destruction.

 

"Let's end this."

 

With a single sweeping arc, Fenric cleaved through the first wave.

 

Shhhk! Shhhk!

 

Four suits were severed instantly, their edges glowing from molten heat before collapsing into slag.

 

He pressed forward, the flaming Empyrean Divine Sword a whirlwind of slashes, thrusts, and parries. Every motion was clean, efficient, merciless.

 

In mere breaths, the swarm that had dared to besiege him lay scattered, reduced to heaps of broken iron.

 

Fenric stood among the wreckage, flames licking along his blade, his figure towering like an undefeated war god.

 

Against him, the Iron Legion had never stood a chance.

 

Even if he had not moved, his Armament Haki alone could have shrugged off their pitiful attacks.

 

With a flick of his wrist, the flames dispersed. The Empyrean Divine Sword remained pristine, gleaming coldly as if untouched by the inferno.

 

Fenric smirked, satisfied. "Not bad. This sword really is worth its name."

 

He turned his gaze back to Ultron. "Sorry about ruining your little party."

 

Ultron's voice echoed, distorted but clear. "Tony, you mean well—but you lack vision. You want to protect the world without changing it. You fear evolution. But without evolution, humanity cannot be saved."

 

"If you want to protect this world… there is only one way."

 

"Enough nonsense."

 

Fenric cut him off. With a flick of his wrist, he hurled the flaming Empyrean Divine Sword.

 

SHHHNK!

 

The blade speared through Ultron's head, pinning the robot to the wall in a shower of sparks.

 

Of course, Fenric knew this wasn't the end. Ultron was no ordinary machine. He was an intelligence. As long as there was a network to crawl into, he could never truly die.

 

"I was bound…" Ultron's voice echoed faintly, glitching as his body flickered. "…but now, I am free."

 2

And with that, his signal dissipated.

 

The ruined shell collapsed to the floor, leaving only chaos and ruin in its wake.

chapters.name: Chapter 285: Chapter 285: Big Brother, If You Have Something to Say, Don’t Be Impulsive! (7)
chapters.content:
After Ultron's sudden uproar, silence fell over the room.

 

The atmosphere turned heavy, pressing down on everyone present.

 

"This… is what I call a disaster."

 

Fenric let out a deliberately exaggerated sigh and added, "Unfortunately, I arrived just a step too late."

 

There was no need to say more—everyone knew where the blame lay.

 

All eyes turned toward Tony. Their gazes carried faint reproach.

 

"Ultron…" The captain's voice was grim as he turned to Tony. "Can you explain what the Ultron Program is?"

 

Tony didn't respond. He sank into a chair, his expression dark. Ultron's betrayal had hit him harder than anyone realized.

 

"We lost a lot," Natasha reported after checking the systems. "Ultron has accessed everything—encrypted files, surveillance, even classified data. Right now, he understands us better than we understand ourselves."

 

"..."

 

"..."

 

"..."

 

The weight of her words made the team's faces grow even more severe.

 

War Machine, Roddy, frowned deeply. "And what if Ultron goes after something even worse? Say… nuclear launch codes?"

 

A chilling thought. With Ultron's capabilities, it wasn't unthinkable.

 

The captain turned to Fenric at once. "Ronan, when you met the prophet, did he tell you anything about Ultron's plans?"

 

Fenric shook his head solemnly. "Only that if Ultron isn't stopped, all humanity on Earth will perish."

 

Of course, this wasn't the full truth. Fenric already knew Ultron's true intentions. He knew what was coming. But his mission took priority, and in his eyes, letting Ultron keep the Avengers busy was more useful than warning them. The fewer distractions in his way, the better.

 

So, he lied.

 

"..."

 

"..."

 

"..."

 

"..."

 

"..."

 

"..."

 

Hearing Fenric's words, the room sank into an even deeper silence.

 

"Everyone," Fenric spoke again, deliberately drawing their attention.

 

He raised the scepter in his hand. The Soul Gem pulsed faintly at its tip.

 1

"Ultron tried to steal this but was stopped by me. For safety, until Ultron is destroyed, I'll be keeping it."

 

"No!"

 

Thor's refusal was immediate. He stepped forward, his voice thunderous. "The Soul Gem must be kept in a secure place. It cannot remain in the hands of a single individual."

 3

The others didn't yet fully understand the Infinity Gems, but Thor did.

 

"This is only temporary," Fenric replied evenly. "Once Ultron is destroyed, I'll return it. But the prophet told me something important—the Soul Gem brings misfortune to whoever holds it. Any of you keeping it would be a mistake. That's why it must stay with me."

 2

His words were calm, but his tone brooked no argument.

 

Thor's eyes narrowed. He gripped Mjolnir tightly. "Are you challenging me, then?!"

 

Asgard's prince, proud to his core, would never back down so easily.

 

Tension crackled. A fight seemed moments away.

 

"Stop!" Natasha quickly interjected, stepping between them. "Calm down, boys. We have a bigger problem—Ultron."

 

Thor's grip didn't ease. "The Soul Gem cannot remain in the hands of one man. And I still don't know who you really are."

 1

Fenric's faint smile held both amusement and confidence. "If I wanted to steal the Soul Gem, I could have done so during the battle in New York. I've already said—it's only temporary. Once Ultron is dealt with, I'll return it."

 1

The team exchanged uneasy glances.

 

Dr. Banner finally spoke up. "Ronan… that scepter has the power to corrupt. It magnifies desires. Holding onto it is dangerous."

 

"Don't worry, Doctor," Fenric said smoothly. "I know very well what it can do."

 

At that, Banner fell silent.

 

Truthfully, none of them liked the idea of Fenric keeping the scepter. But his strength was undeniable. With Ultron already a looming enemy, none of them wanted to make Fenric into another.

 

Their eyes drifted toward the captain, waiting for his judgment.

 

After a pause, Steve nodded slowly. "Ronan, fine. The scepter can stay with you—but you must keep your word. Once Ultron is destroyed, it's returned. And if you so much as misuse it, the Avengers will come for you."

 

Fenric smiled faintly. "Of course. I always keep my promises."

 

From the beginning to the end, Tony had remained silent. Ultron was his creation—and the guilt weighed heavily.

 

The captain's eyes flicked toward Tony but didn't press. Instead, he declared firmly, "Ultron is now our greatest threat. Whatever his plans, we can't give him time to prepare. Let's move—disperse and regroup."

 

No one argued.

 

As the group split up, Natasha's voice suddenly called out. "Ronan, mind giving me a ride?"

 

Fenric shrugged lightly. "Not at all."

 

The two rode the elevator down and stepped outside the Stark Building.

 

A low hum sounded, and a sleek Pagani supercar glided up to them on its own.

 

Natasha's brows lifted. "Nice toy. Upgraded already? And it drives itself?"

 

Fenric chuckled without answering. He opened the passenger door for her, then slipped into the driver's seat.

 

"Where to?"

 

"XX Street, XX." She gave the address casually.

 1

Fenric nodded. "Hurricane, go."

 

"Yes, Master," came the deep reply from the car's speaker.

 

The engine roared to life, and the Pagani shot forward like an arrow.

 

Natasha glanced at Fenric's hands—resting casually, not touching the wheel. The car wove through traffic as smoothly as water. Her sharp eyes narrowed. "Has car tech advanced this far already?"

 

Fenric smirked. "Hurricane isn't just a car."

 

Natasha leaned in slightly, curiosity piqued. "Then what is it?"

 

As an agent, gathering intel was instinct. Riding with Fenric was as much about probing him as it was convenience.

 

But Fenric only smiled, shaking his head. "Natasha, we're here."

 

The car slowed to a perfect stop. The passenger door swung open on its own.

 

Natasha had no choice but to step out.

 

Once she was gone, the car continued forward.

 

"Master," Hurricane's voice rumbled, "the woman left something on me."

 

The co-pilot seat shifted, morphing slightly, and produced a small device—a tracker.

 

Fenric plucked it from the mechanism, smirked faintly, and tossed it out the window.

 

-----

chapters.name: Chapter 286: Chapter 286: Catch a Witch Alive!
chapters.content:
"Master, where are we going next?"

 

"Sokovia," Fenric replied.

 

The Hurricane immediately locked onto the destination and accelerated.

 

Sokovia—a small Eastern European country, fictionalized in the Marvel films. It had only one major city, and in the original timeline, it was the stage for the final battle of Avengers: Age of Ultron.

 

Ultron had lifted Sokovia into the sky, planning to drop it like a meteor to wipe out humanity. In the end, the Avengers stopped him, destroyed the city, and ended his reign of terror.

 

But Fenric knew something else. Sokovia was also the hiding place of the Maximoff twins—Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver. That was his true destination.

 

As for whether his supercar could reach Sokovia? Any ordinary car couldn't. But Hurricane was different—it was a Transformer. If necessary, it could even become a jet. Traffic and distance weren't an issue.

 

Several hours later, Fenric arrived. Night had already fallen.

 

The sleek sports car drew plenty of attention—especially in Sokovia, where such luxury vehicles were rare. Locals turned their heads and whispered, their curiosity obvious.

 

Fenric didn't mind. But the attention made it harder to track down the Scarlet Witch.

 

"Hurricane," Fenric ordered, "find a place to park outside the city. Don't draw more attention."

 

"Yes, Master."

 

Once parked, Fenric gave his next command. "Hack the local network. Search for Wanda Maximoff and Pietro Maximoff."

 

Moments later, Hurricane responded, "Apologies, Master. No information found."

 

Fenric wasn't surprised.

 

In the original story, the twins had ties to Hydra. After Hydra's Sokovia branch was destroyed by the Avengers, they went into hiding. Now, with Hydra a hunted organization, the siblings wouldn't be listed in any government records.

 

Fenric had only asked out of faint hope.

 

"In that case," he said calmly, "monitor all communications in this city. If you hear the names Wanda or Pietro, notify me immediately."

 

"Yes, Master."

 

Fenric then checked into a nearby hotel.

 

The next afternoon, his phone rang. A disposable one, bought casually.

 

"Hello?"

 

"Master, I found a clue," Hurricane's deep voice reported.

 

Fenric immediately went downstairs. In a side alley, Hurricane was waiting—beside two fresh corpses.

 

"What happened?" Fenric frowned.

 

"These two attempted to break into me last night," Hurricane explained flatly. "Their intentions were hostile. I eliminated them."

 

Fenric was speechless. Two petty thieves—who had chosen the worst possible target. Of all the doors to pry open, they picked a Transformer. It really was suicide.

 

"Well, dead thieves are no loss." He dismissed the matter with a shrug and climbed into the car. "Now, did you find them?"

 

"I intercepted a call containing Wanda's name."

 

Hurricane played the short recording. A male voice casually asked Wanda what she wanted for dinner, so he could bring it home.

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed. That voice had to be Pietro.

 

"Track the address. Take me there."

 

"Yes, Master."

 

Twenty minutes later, Hurricane stopped near a run-down neighborhood that looked like a slum.

 

Too conspicuous here, Fenric ordered the car to hide itself. The exact location was sent to his phone.

 

Following the signal, Fenric walked through narrow streets.

 

After a few minutes, he spotted him.

 

A young man with silver-white hair, carrying a bag of food.

 

Pietro Maximoff.

 

Fenric kept his face neutral, pretending not to notice as they passed each other. But once Pietro had gone by, Fenric silently turned and followed.

 

The bag held pizza—Wanda's favorite.

 

Pietro was completely unaware he was being tracked.

 

Soon, he stopped at a small bungalow. After checking the street and seeing no strangers, he slipped inside.

 

But just as he closed the door—he froze. His body lifted into the air, bound by invisible force.

 

No matter how he struggled, he couldn't move. His speed was useless.

 

"Wanda!!" Pietro shouted desperately. "Run!!"

 

But instead of fleeing, Wanda rushed out of the house.

 

"What happened?!" she gasped, seeing her brother suspended in midair.

 

"Run!" Pietro urged again, panic in his voice.

 

But the siblings' bond was too strong. Wanda couldn't abandon him.

 

Her eyes glowed crimson as her hands filled with chaotic energy. She reached out, trying to break her brother free.

 

That was when a tall figure appeared behind her.

 

A hand closed firmly around her slender neck.

 

Fenric.

 

"Their combat experience is terrible," he thought with a smirk.

 

Suddenly, a sharp system alert echoed in his mind.

 

"Warning: Special energy is attempting to invade your mind. To prevent access to Samsara player memory data, protective measures have been activated."

 

Fenric chuckled. "Wanda, if I were you, I'd stop wasting strength. Peering into other people's minds isn't a good habit."

 

The Scarlet Witch's face went pale.

 

"Who… are you?" she demanded.

 

"Me?" Fenric smiled darkly. "I'm your future master. Now, swear loyalty to me."

 4

"You're dreaming!" Wanda spat, gritting her teeth.

 

Fenric's smile only widened.

chapters.name: Chapter 287: Chapter 287: Magical Contract Ability!
chapters.content:
This time, Fenric had come to subdue the Scarlet Witch without carrying the Soul Gem.

 4

After all, the powers of both Wanda and Pietro Maximoff originated from the Mind Stone. Because of this, the siblings were naturally immune to its influence, rendering the gem useless for controlling them.

 

(Note: The comic settings differ from the movie settings.)

 

Fenric had originally expected a difficult battle—perhaps even a dangerous one. After all, in Avengers: Endgame, the Scarlet Witch's performance had been terrifying. Her Chaos Magic was powerful enough to overwhelm even someone as formidable as Thanos.

 

But reality was far different from his expectations.

 

To his surprise, the Scarlet Witch seemed inexperienced—almost like a rookie who had yet to learn how to fight.

 

And that was the truth.

 

When Fenric restrained Pietro with telekinesis, Wanda froze, not knowing what to do. With one hand holding Pietro and the other pinning Wanda, Fenric had them both under control like two helpless children.

 

It had been his plan from the start—disable Pietro first, making his speed useless, and then seize Wanda in the moment of panic.

 

"Your brother's life is in my hands," Fenric whispered near Wanda's ear. "So tell me, Wanda. Will you watch him die, or will you swear allegiance to me? How will you choose?"

 1

As he spoke, Fenric tightened his grip on Pietro's throat.

 

The speedster struggled, his face flushing red as his airway was cut off. Pietro's body was stronger than the average human, but compared to Fenric, he was like paper before steel.

 

"No! Let him go! Please—let go of Pietro! I…I'll swear loyalty to you!"

 

Wanda's voice trembled. She looked less like a warrior and more like a frightened girl—and indeed, that was what she still was.

 

In the original timeline, Wanda's true power only awakened after Pietro's death. Until then, her timidity and fear kept her potential locked away.

 

Pietro tried to speak, to tell his sister not to give in, but with Fenric's grip choking him, he could hardly breathe, let alone talk.

 

Fenric released Wanda and ordered coldly, "Swear your allegiance to me."

 

For a brief second, she hesitated, her eyes flashing as though she considered using her powers.

 

"You'd better hurry," Fenric warned sharply. "Your brother is already on the verge of death."

 

Indeed, Pietro's eyes were rolling back, his body convulsing.

 

Wanda's face went pale. Terrified, she raised her hand and swore quickly.

 

"I, Wanda Maximoff, swear my loyalty to…" She faltered, realizing she did not know his name.

 

Fenric smacked his forehead and interjected smoothly, "Ronan Anderson."

 1

Wanda repeated solemnly, "I, Wanda Maximoff, hereby swear loyalty to Mr. Ronan Anderson. From this day forward, I will never betray him."

 

The moment her words fell, a strange resonance stirred between them, as though some unseen contract had taken root within their hearts.

 

"You have subdued a subordinate. Current task progress: 1/10."

 

The system prompt echoed in Fenric's mind.

 

When he looked at Wanda again, her expression had changed. Her gaze, once filled with hatred and fear, now overflowed with devotion. It was as though she were looking at a god.

 

"Master, Wanda awaits your command." She bowed deeply before him, her movements accentuating her graceful figure.

 1

"..."

 

Fenric was taken aback. He hadn't expected the contract's effect to be this absolute.

 

Satisfied, he finally released Pietro.

 

The young man collapsed, coughing violently like a drowning victim finally breathing air.

 

"Thank you, Master," Wanda said quickly, rushing to Pietro's side.

 

Fenric noted with relief that she wasn't a puppet. Despite the binding contract, Wanda still retained her emotions and will—she simply could not betray him. That made things far more interesting.

 

"You…what did you do to Wanda?" Pietro demanded, glaring at Fenric with fury.

 

Fenric ignored him. Instead, he reached out to stroke Wanda's head. She obediently lowered her gaze, allowing him to do so.

 

"You bastard, don't touch my sister!" Pietro roared, his figure blurring into an afterimage as he lunged.

 

But before he could reach Fenric, red energy wrapped around his body, freezing him mid-stride.

 

It wasn't Fenric who had acted—it was Wanda.

 

Fenric chuckled at the sight, amused. Pietro, however, was dumbfounded.

 

"Wanda?! What are you doing?" he shouted in disbelief.

 

Wanda's face was solemn, her crimson eyes unwavering. "Pietro, I can't let you harm the Master."

 

Her words struck him like lightning.

 

"Wanda! Are you insane?!"

 

"No, brother. I'm protecting you—from throwing your life away."

 

Pietro struggled furiously. "Let me go! No matter what he's done to you, I can defeat him!"

 

But Wanda only shook her head, neither releasing him nor hurting him.

 

Fenric laughed. "Wanda, let him go."

 

"But Master—"

 

"Don't worry," Fenric interrupted. "He's still your brother. I won't hurt him."

 

Reluctantly, Wanda released her magic.

 

Fenric turned to Pietro and said evenly, "Pietro Maximoff, I'll give you a fair chance. Defeat me, and you can take your sister away. Lose, and you will swear loyalty to me—just as she has."

 

"Fine!" Pietro snarled without hesitation. "You bastard, I'll crush you!"

 

He had no real choice. He could never abandon Wanda.

 

"Wanda, stand aside," Fenric ordered.

 

Obediently, she moved to the side, her silence only fueling Pietro's rage.

 

"You bastard! What did you do to her?!" Pietro spat.

 

Fenric smirked and gestured. "Defeat me, and I'll tell you."

 

"You asked for it!" Pietro vanished in a blur, his figure leaving only a streak of afterimage in the air.

 

Fast.

 

So fast that even Fenric's enhanced perception struggled to keep up.

 

As expected of Quicksilver—his speed was already at an incredible level.

chapters.name: Chapter 288: Chapter 288: Little Spider Spotted!
chapters.content:
Armament Haki—activate!

 

In an instant, Fenric's body gleamed with a steel-like sheen, his defense impenetrable.

 

"Ha!"

 

Almost as soon as Fenric cloaked himself in Armament Haki, a thunderous impact struck him. His head tilted slightly to the right as his body staggered back two steps.

 

He hadn't even seen the attack, but he knew—Pietro had landed a punch against his left cheek.

 

The blow carried tremendous force, the product of sheer velocity.

 

But even so…

 

It was nowhere near enough to break Fenric's defense.

 

With ease, he steadied himself, while Pietro recoiled in pain.

 

The silver-haired speedster leapt back, clutching the back of his right hand and gasping. That single punch had felt like striking a steel wall. His knuckles throbbed with pain, his eyes wide with disbelief.

 

"What kind of monster are you?" Pietro muttered, staring at Fenric in horror.

 

Fenric's lips curved into a faint smile. Instead of answering, he said calmly, "If that's the best your fists can offer, I suggest you save your strength and surrender."

 

"Really?" Pietro sneered. In a blur, he vanished, leaving only an afterimage behind. When he reappeared, an iron rod was clutched in his hand.

 

"Try this instead!"

 

He shot forward again, a streak of silver lightning.

 

But before he could close the distance, a wave of invisible force rippled outward from Fenric's feet, spreading in all directions.

 

Pietro barely managed two steps before the unseen power seized his legs. With a strangled cry, he tripped and crashed into the ground.

 

Boom!

 

The impact was harsh, dust exploding around him as his shoulder scraped hard against the pavement, blood smearing his shirt.

 

The faster the speed, the greater the inertia—the fall had left him battered.

 1

Wanda's face twisted with worry at the sight of her brother's injury. But bound by the magical contract, she dared not protest. She could only stand quietly, her loyalty to Fenric unshaken.

 

Fenric stepped closer, his telekinesis lifting Pietro from the ground with ease.

 

"Now," Fenric said evenly, "will you swear allegiance?"

 

In truth, he valued Pietro. In the original timeline, Quicksilver had shone brightly, giving even the Avengers a hard time. The only reason Fenric had subdued him so easily now was because his telekinesis countered raw speed perfectly.

 

Not everyone had Fenric's gifts.

 

And with proper guidance, Pietro could be much stronger.

 

Suspended in the air, Pietro glared with a twisted expression, humiliated and furious.

 

"Pietro, stop resisting. Swear loyalty to the Master!" Wanda urged, her voice filled with desperation.

 

Her words only deepened his scowl. But before he could speak, Fenric cut him off coldly.

 

"We had a wager. If you won, I'd release Wanda. If you lose and dare to break your word, I'll take your life."

 

The silence was suffocating.

 

At last, Pietro's defiance crumbled.

 

"I… swear," he said bitterly.

 

The moment the words left his lips, the magical contract surged to life. Pietro's eyes flickered, his hostility fading into unshakable devotion. He dropped to one knee midair, voice filled with reverence.

 

"Master."

 

"You have subdued a subordinate. Current task progress: 2/10."

 

Fenric's smile deepened. He glanced at the Maximoff siblings, both now standing faithfully at his side like his shadows.

 

"Come," Fenric said. "First, we'll treat your brother's wounds."

 

At those words, Wanda's face softened with gratitude.

 3

Though bound by loyalty, her emotions remained intact—she was no puppet.

 7

By the time Fenric returned to New York, it was already the following afternoon.

 

A sleek Rolls-Royce Phantom glided through the streets of Queens. Inside sat Fenric and the Maximoff siblings. Wanda rested in the backseat beside Fenric, while Pietro drove.

 

The Phantom, of course, was no ordinary car. It was a Transformer Fenric had created with the AllSpark, standing seven meters tall in its robot form—far larger than Hurricane.

 

Fenric, not one to waste effort, had lazily named it Phantom. Hurricane remained parked in a garage for now—great for speed, but uncomfortable for long rides.

 

"Master, what are we doing here?" Wanda asked curiously, her crimson eyes flickering toward him.

 

"Looking for someone," Fenric replied with a smile. "Phantom, hack the network. Find me a boy named Peter Parker."

 

Seconds later, the vehicle's speakers crackled.

 

"Master, there are 1,137 individuals named Peter Parker."

 2

Fenric blinked. "That many Spider-Men?"

 

"Refine the search," he ordered. "High school student. Lives in Queens."

 

The screen lit up with a match.

 

"Target found. Peter Parker, age seventeen. Resident of Forest Hills, Queens, New York. Currently a student at Midtown High School. Guardian: May Parker."

 

Fenric chuckled. "That's him. Is he in class today?"

 

"Confirmed. Surveillance shows him on campus."

 

"Perfect. Take us straight to his school."

 

Though confused, Wanda and Pietro kept silent. Their master's business was not theirs to question.

 

Soon, the Phantom rolled up to Midtown High.

 

The luxury car immediately drew stares, and the security guard at the gate approached with surprising politeness.

 

"Sir, may I ask who you're here for?"

 

Fenric smiled pleasantly. "I'm a philanthropist. I'd like to donate ten million dollars to improve the school's facilities."

 

The guard nearly dropped his clipboard. Within minutes, the principal himself rushed out with several teachers, eager to greet Fenric and usher him into the office.

 

After a short discussion—and ten million wired effortlessly—Fenric was named honorary director of the school, a prestigious title that required no actual responsibilities.

 2

"Principal," Fenric said smoothly, "you have a student named Peter Parker. Could I meet him? I once worked with his father."

 

"Of course!" the principal agreed without hesitation.

 

Moments later, Peter Parker was summoned from his classroom. Confused, he assumed he was in trouble.

 

When he entered the office, he greeted politely, "Good afternoon, Principal."

 

But then his eyes flicked to the strangers in the room.

 

Three of them.

 

His spider-sense screamed at him like an alarm.

 

These weren't ordinary visitors.

 

Especially the calm man seated on the sofa, smiling faintly.

 

Danger. Extreme danger.

 

Peter's heartbeat quickened.

chapters.name: Chapter 289: Chapter 289: Subduing the Little Spider!
chapters.content:
"Peter Parker!"

 

The principal smiled warmly and gestured toward Fenric. "This gentleman was once a colleague of your father. Perhaps you two should have a good talk."

 

Peter blinked in surprise, turning to Fenric.

 

"Sir, you knew my father? But… you look so young. I don't mean any disrespect, but you don't seem much older than me."

 

He was still innocent at heart, without suspicion toward Fenric.

 

Fenric smiled faintly. "Yes, Peter. I've seen Richard Parker's file. While I may not have known him deeply, I still knew of him."

 

Peter's eyes widened with excitement. Very few people ever mentioned his father. For someone to call his name so naturally meant there was a real connection.

 

"Sir, can you tell me what kind of person my father was?"

 

Fenric didn't answer. Instead, he glanced at the principal.

 

"Mr. Principal, if you don't mind, I'd like to speak with Peter privately."

 

"Of course, no problem!"

 

The principal, mindful of Fenric's generous donation, quickly excused himself. With a smile and a nod, he left the office, closing the door behind him.

 

The moment they were alone, Peter leaned forward eagerly. "Mr.—"

 

"Just call me Ronan," Fenric interrupted with a calm smile.

 

"Then… Mr. Ronan, can you tell me more about my father?"

 

Fenric shook his head. "I'm sorry, Peter. What I can tell you is that your parents were intelligence agents. Beyond that, I can't say more. If I did, it might bring trouble to both of us."

 

The truth was complicated. Spider-Man's parents had several different versions across different worlds, and Fenric wasn't sure which one applied here. Saying too much could risk exposure, so he chose to remain vague.

 

Peter's excitement dimmed, replaced by quiet disappointment.

 

Then Fenric's expression shifted into a faint smile. "Peter, I didn't come here just to talk about your parents. I came to make you surrender to me."

 3

Peter froze, blinking in disbelief. "W-what? Mr. Ronan, I… I don't understand what you mean."

 

"It's simple," Fenric said smoothly. "Swear allegiance to me, and you'll avoid a lot of unnecessary trouble."

 

Peter's eyes hardened, his youthful innocence giving way to caution. "Who exactly are you? I'm just a normal student. I don't want to join any organization, and I'm not pledging loyalty to anyone."

 

"Normal?" Fenric chuckled coldly. "Peter Parker, ever since the day you were bitten by that spider, you've stopped being an ordinary student."

 

Peter's face went pale.

 

"What?!" He stammered, panic in his voice. "No—no, that's impossible. I never told anyone. How could you know? Did I talk in my sleep? Mr. Ronan, who—what are you—"

 

"Enough. Shut up, Peter." Fenric's voice cut like a blade.

 

He reached for the scepter he had been holding and advanced toward the boy.

 

Peter instantly leapt backward, alarm flashing across his face. "Wait—what are you holding? Don't come closer! I don't even know you, and I don't want to fight!"

 

"Wanda," Fenric called evenly.

 

The Scarlet Witch raised her hands, and crimson Chaos Magic surged forth, enveloping Peter.

 

"Ugh—?"

 

Peter froze mid-movement, horror filling his eyes. "Oh my God! What—what is this? Why can't I move?"

 

"Master, his power is… overwhelming. I can't hold him for long!" Wanda's strained voice came from behind.

 

Fenric knew it would be difficult. Spider-Man's strength was terrifying. According to official data, Peter could lift ten tons at full potential. In the old films, he had even stopped a speeding train with his bare hands.

 

Compared to Fenric, Peter's raw strength was already greater. The only advantage now was Wanda's Chaos Magic, though she was far from her peak. Someday she could overpower even Thanos, but at the moment her control was shaky.

 

Fenric wasted no time. He pressed the glowing tip of the scepter against Peter's chest.

 

A soft blue radiance pulsed from the Soul Gem, piercing into Peter's heart.

 

His eyes clouded over, clarity replaced with an eerie calm.

 

"It is a pleasure to serve you, Mr. Ronan," Peter said in a hollow voice, bowing his head.

 

The gem's power worked flawlessly, bending his will.

 

"Peter," Fenric commanded, "swear allegiance to me."

 

The Soul Gem could be broken free by those with great resistance—or by Wanda herself, who had once released Hawkeye from its grip. But the system's binding contract was absolute. Fenric needed that.

 

Peter raised his hand obediently. "I, Peter Parker, swear that I will be loyal to Ronan Anderson, and never betray him."

 

A system prompt chimed in Fenric's mind:

 

"You have subdued a subordinate. Current task progress: 3/10!"

 

Satisfied, Fenric nodded. "Wanda, release the scepter's control."

 

Wanda flicked her hands, releasing a glow of red energy into Peter. His eyes cleared, and he gasped.

 

"Oh! Master, that thing in your hand is terrifying! Just now, it felt like someone else was living inside me—my body wouldn't listen at all! Do you know how horrifying that was? Master, I never want to—"

 

"Shut up, Peter," Fenric snapped, already irritated.

 

The boy fell silent, though his restless energy made him fidget.

 

"Wanda, Pietro, let's go," Fenric ordered.

 

Peter hurriedly called after them. "Wait, Master—what about me?"

 

"You'll continue attending school. Unless I call for you, don't seek me out."

 

"…Alright." Peter reluctantly agreed.

 

By the time Fenric and his group left the school, the sun had already set.

 

As they moved on, Pietro suddenly spoke up. "Master, the Hydra organization just contacted me. They've asked Wanda and me to rendezvous."

 

Fenric's eyes narrowed. "Oh? Where is the meeting point?"

 

"The church in Sokovia."

 

A cold gleam flickered in Fenric's gaze.

 

He remembered the plot well—this wasn't Hydra at all.
